# goopg Design Documents

Design documents are **part of the deliverable** for this project, not scratch
notes. Every non-trivial subsystem must land alongside (or just before) its
design doc. See `.ralph/specs/GOAL_AND_REQUIREMENTS.md` §9 for the rules.

## Conventions

- Filenames use the form `<milestone-or-spec-id>-NNNN-short-slug.md`.
  `<milestone-or-spec-id>` is `root` for the foundational requirements spec
  and a milestone identifier such as `0002` for milestone-scoped docs.
  `NNNN` is a zero-padded sequence number within that identifier.
- Reserve a concrete filename before implementation work starts; do not
  leave bare `NNNN-*` placeholders in active plans.
- Each doc opens with a short metadata block: status, date, supersedes.
- Status values: `draft`, `accepted`, `superseded`, `historical`.
- When a new doc supersedes an older one, mark the older doc
  `superseded` and add a `superseded by:` link forward. Do not delete it.
- Cite upstream PostgreSQL with repository-relative paths
  (e.g. `postgres/src/backend/storage/buffer/bufmgr.c`).

## Design Bundles

- [fix-for-q5/README.md](fix-for-q5/README.md) - multi-file planner design set for making TPC-H Q5 choose the expected binary hash-join shape while keeping the rest of the TPC-H plan set stable.
- [bootstrap-procedure/README.md](bootstrap-procedure/README.md) - 12-file specification of every PG18 artefact goopg's `initdb` must produce **and** continuously maintain so a vanilla PG18 standby can attach via `pg_basebackup` at any time. Supersedes the reactive M0106-0010 step-3* loop (116+ docs). Covers ControlFile, WAL bootstrap, shared/local catalogs, BKI-derived catalogs, system views, relcache init files, streaming-replication readiness, a per-operation continuous-maintenance matrix, and a 35-task batched implementation roadmap.
- [perf-optimize/](perf-optimize/) - 10-chapter performance refactor design (00-overview, 01-memory-context `mctx`, 02-datum-pointer-free, 03-executor-concrete, 04-mvcc-procarray, 05-activity-perbackend, 06-bufpool-lockfree, 07-wal-fsm-insert, 08-runtime-internals, 09-migration-and-rollout). Targets c=10 SO 2 307→8 000 TPS, c=50 SU 347→2 000 TPS, c=100 SU SKIP→500 TPS, `gcBgMarkWorker` 63 %→<15 %, `runtime.futex` <8 %. All on-disk formats stay PG-compatible. Implemented under [M0107](../milestones/0107-performance-optimization-refactor.md); PG-compat invariants enumerated in [0107-0001-m0106-pg-compat-invariants.md](0107-0001-m0106-pg-compat-invariants.md).
- [wal-backend-flush/README.md](wal-backend-flush/README.md) - 7-chapter design (DESIGN ONLY, implementation not started) restructuring the WAL write path to PostgreSQL parity: committing backends perform the segment pwrite+fdatasync themselves under a `WALWriteLock` analog (`LWLockAcquireOrWait` tri-state; emergent group commit — the `flushGroup` queue and the dedicated writer goroutine are deleted), and the background walwriter becomes PG-equivalent (pre-writes completed pages; fsync throttled by a new `wal_writer_flush_after` GUC / delay-elapsed / segment completion). `commit_delay`/`commit_siblings` become real GUCs at PG defaults (0/5), replacing the hardcoded 1000 µs/5 loop-side sleep. 7-slice staged migration with per-slice gates; on-disk WAL format unchanged per [0107-0001](0107-0001-m0106-pg-compat-invariants.md). Supersedes (on implementation) 0098-0002, 0099-0002, wal_fsync_flow_primary §7, and 0107-0007ai's single-drainer assumption. Motivated by [analysis/perf-optimize2](../../analysis/perf-optimize2/README.md) (commit-flush-bound at c=50 after the CPU fixes).
- [mvcc-optimize/README.md](mvcc-optimize/README.md) - 2-document set covering MVCC visibility optimizations derived from `practice/pg_mvcc_internals.md`. M0115: heap tuple hint bit caching (read/write HEAP_XMIN_COMMITTED and related infomask bits; FrozenTransactionID fast path; hint-bit-only page dirty without WAL). M0116: multi-column Index-Only Scan key decoding (composite B-tree key decode; planner coverage check; extends the Visibility Map optimization to composite-PK tables).
- [leftdeep-joins/README.md](leftdeep-joins/README.md) - 10-chapter design bundle (DESIGN ONLY, 2026-08-02, amended 2026-08-03) restructuring join planning and execution to PostgreSQL's architecture with full PG fidelity: the join search emits **PG-shaped binary trees — left-deep chains plus bushy composite-composite joins** — exactly the shapes PG 18.3's `join_search_one_level` can produce (`standard_join_search`/`join_search_one_level` analogue over the dormant `path.go` `RelOptInfo`/`add_path` substrate, all three phases — clause joins at `joinrels.c:118`, bushy at `:141-198`, last-ditch at `:200-256`; join methods generated as costed paths INSIDE the search — no post-DP `rewriteJoinsToNLI`/MHJ-packing rewrites), and the executor's binary hash cascade is reworked until it matches `MultiHashJoin`'s execution profile (probe-seam de-materialisation incl. the deferred 0126-0004 slot chaining, `mergedKeySlot` hoist, single-pass single-map builds, PG-shaped multi-column hash keys retiring `reselectDegenerateHashKeys`, compiled key/residual eval) plus PG hybrid-hash spill (`ExecChooseHashTableSize`/nbatch analogue over `spillWriter`), streaming merge join, hash RIGHT/FULL fill, and a Materialize-under-NL operator — making both `MultiHashJoin` and the permanently-off `fusedHashJoinOp` deletable (S7 inventory estimated ~34 arms/18 files). **S7 deletions LANDED: P6.1 removed `fusedHashJoinOp`, P6.2 removed `MultiHashJoin` (42 non-test files — above the estimate), and P6.3 removed the old subset-bitmask DP itself (`bushy.go`, 2880 lines; the PG-shaped search is now the only join-order search) — all 2026-08-07; DS05 recorded plan shapes 99/99 identical across both P6.2 and P6.3, so the removals are behaviour-preserving by construction.** Only P6.4 (supersession stamps) remains open. Supersedes [0034-0001](0034-0001-bushy-join-planning.md)/[0038-0001](0038-0001-multi-way-hash-join.md) on implementation; successor to M0126's open tail (the Q9 804s/118s order blocker resolves via FK-aware selectivity + nbatch-honest build costing + the shape contract). Agent-reviewed 2026-08-03 (fusion panel + adversarial review; bushy phase re-admitted, P-LD→P-PG, relid-order canonical layout, `join_is_legal`-inference-dependent staging). Acceptance instrument amended 2026-08-05 (09 §4.1/§5.8, P5.6-g-iii): the S5 ratchet is **per-joinrel parity against the PG 18.3 reference** (joinrel identity = base-relation set, so different join orders still compare), not an absolute misestimate factor — PG itself trips the old 10³ tripwire on TPC-H Q18. First defect that instrument proved is closed (09 §5.9, P5.6-g-iv, 2026-08-05): goopg never ran PG's `canonicalize_qual`/`process_duplicate_ors` (prepqual.c), so a conjunct repeated in every arm of an OR — Q19's join clause — was priced once as the equi-join key and again per arm at DEFAULT_EQ_SEL; `internal/planner/qual_canonical.go` adds the pass and takes Q19's parity excess from 126.5× to 2.3×. TPC-DS SF0.5 discharged 2026-08-05 for all three ungated estimator commits (09 §5.10, P5.6-g-i): row counts and all 57 value checksums identical to the `ce027cee` baseline, while a four-arm whole-corpus `EXPLAIN` A/B (noise floor zero) attributes the churn as **P5.6-f-ii 74 of 99 plans, P5.6-g 1, P5.6-g-iv 4** — the nullable-key hypothesis that raised the sweep is measured false, and the corpus-wide re-ordering is the search finally reading the join key. That silence is now closed (09 §5.11, P5.6-g-i-b): the gate grew a **non-blocking plan-shape channel** — `scripts/tpcds-plan-diff.py` plus a `plans` subcommand / sweep tail stage that captures all 99 plans by `EXPLAIN` in 14 s and diffs them per query against the previous run, leaving row counts and checksums as the only thing that can fail the gate. Estimator amended 2026-08-05 (09 §5.12, P5.6-g-ii): **what crosses a grouping node is uniqueness, not statistics** — `examine_simple_variable`'s GROUP-BY/DISTINCT arm sets `isunique` and returns "cannot go further" without a statistics tuple, so `groupUniqueNDistinct` (joinkeyproof.go) answers a sole grouping key's distinct count as the grouped relation's own row count while `resolveBaseColumn` still refuses to walk the node; Q18's `× 0.5` punt goes 42 837× → 24 242×, and the arm exposed a pre-existing hole — `estimateJoin` had no outer-join arm, so LEFT/RIGHT/FULL took the INNER product and stopped before `calc_joinrel_size_estimate`'s non-nullable-input floor (TPC-DS Q77 estimated 885 rows for a join whose outer is 8 885; Q80 41 s → 14 s, Q40 16 s → 2 s, Q78 29 s → 17 s, DS05 rows identical). Attribution amended 2026-08-05 (09 §5.15, P5.6-f-iii): the DS05 gate's TIMEOUT **did not hop, it was moved** — the "sweep-tail confound" reading is refuted by an eight-vs-four-sweep step function, solo quiet-host runs reproducing the new regime outside any sweep tail (Q47 **523 s** where the hypothesis predicted ≈31 s), and a bisect against a COPY of the cluster pinning it to one commit, `ce027cee` (P5.6-f), whose per-pair **independence** fold collapses Q47's 5-pair join from a `Hash Join` to a condition-less `Nested Loop`; P5.6-f stays (net win, correctness unmoved) and the missing piece is PG's functional-dependency arm (`clauselist_selectivity`/`dependencies.c`), filed as P5.6-f-iv, with P5.6-f-v making the sweep diff the TIMEOUT **set** rather than its cardinality — `TIMEOUT=1` stayed byte-identical across a 17× re-pricing for four sweeps. Two attribution rules recorded: read a sweep header's `diff=` field before its commit subject (the boundary sweep was `29daeb72` + uncommitted WIP), and a summary count cannot detect a traded timeout. That last gap is now closed (09 §5.16, P5.6-f-v, 2026-08-05): the gate grew a second **non-blocking status-delta channel** — `scripts/tpcds-sweep-diff.py` plus a `delta` subcommand / sweep tail stage that diffs the per-query **status/runtime vector** against the previous full report and prints named lines (`TIMEOUT +Q47 -Q72`, plus any query that moved ≥2× above a 5 s floor, TIMEOUT readings excluded as caps rather than runtimes). Its input is the sweep report itself, so all ~90 archived reports are valid baselines: replayed over the 87 adjacent pairs of the corpus it names 17 verdict changes including §5.15's hidden Q72→Q47 trade and Q57's 5.4× — from artefacts that already existed the night it landed. **`estimate_num_groups` landed and the DS05 TIMEOUT set is empty** (09 §5.19, P5.6-f-vii, 2026-08-05): `estimateAggregate`'s `child/2` (and its unclamped single-key NDistinct) became `estimateNumGroups`, a port of `estimate_num_groups` (selfuncs.c:3449) — per-relation ndistinct products clamped to `rel->tuples` (÷10 above one variable), the Yao/Dell'Era restriction correction, and the closing clamp to `input_rows`. Filed as explicitly NOT load-bearing for Q47, it is what closed it: the 6-key `v1` body 3 626 → 7 252, its CTE-scan outer 6 → 12, the `Nested Loop rows=1958` became a `Hash Join rows=7252`, and **Q47 completes in 12 s** against a 300 s timeout — PASS 94 → 95, `TIMEOUT=0`, the first sweep with no timing-out query since §5.15, and no new estimate-audit violation (Q20 improved 30.2× → 24.9×). **The hash-join spill term landed** (04 §4.1 / 06 §5, P5.7-a, 2026-08-05): `hashJoinCost` calls `hashsize.Choose` — the executor's own geometry function — and applies PG's batch I/O charge verbatim when it answers `NBatch > 1` (costsize.c:4239-4248), replacing M0126-0013's unconditional `seq_page_cost × innerRows/100`, a stand-in for a page charge upstream does not make there and one that, being monotone in the row count, could not tell a 6 M-row build that fits `work_mem` from one that does not. The finding is which width crosses the sibling-path boundary: goopg's hash entry is a `[]Datum` of 48-byte structs, so its size follows the COLUMN count the executor passes, not the byte width `RelOptInfo.Width` carries — hence the new `RelOptInfo.NCols`. Deferred with 4 ledger rows (per-session `work_mem` never reaches the planner; `spillPages` prices the in-memory footprint, not the narrower batch-file encoding; `nbatch` unexposed on `Path` for EXPLAIN; the LIMIT `tuple_fraction` → P5.7-b). **That last deferral is closed** (04 §4.3, P5.7-b, 2026-08-05): `internal/planner/tuplefraction.go` ports `preprocess_limit` (planner.c:2577) and `get_cheapest_fractional_path` (planner.c:6617), and `searchCtx.finalPath()` — not `finalRel().CheapestTotal` — is now the value a caller hands `createPlanAtSearchRoot`, because reading the cheapest-total path silently discards the fraction. The finding is that `tuple_fraction` is **two mechanisms and only the pair moves a plan**: selection, and RETENTION via the new `RelOptInfo.ConsiderStartup` (`consider_startup`, relnode.c:211/707) enforced in `comparePathCostsFuzzily`'s two "different" arms (pathnode.c:178-183) — without the second the first has nothing to choose from, and goopg had neither, behaving as if `consider_startup` were permanently true (keeping fast-start paths PG prunes) and then always selecting on total cost. A 10 000-row joinrel offered a hash-shaped path (startup 500, total 900) and a loop-shaped one (startup 0, total 20 000) now chooses the hash with no LIMIT, the loop under `LIMIT 100`, and the hash again under `LIMIT 5000` — the fraction is honoured, not merely the presence of a LIMIT. **The search has a production caller as of 2026-08-05 (P5.9-b, 03 §6.3): `tryPGShapedJoinSearch` (`internal/planner/joinsearchseam.go`) is entered from the first line of `tryBushyDP`, so both join-search positions reach it through one door and the old DP stays the fallback the S5 rollback needs.** The seam owns the three questions the recursion does not: which statements enter the search (explicit-`JOIN` items and LATERAL items are declined, each for a correctness reason), which conjuncts survive it (the residual rule is a QUESTION PUT TO `buildRestrictInfos` rather than a re-derivation, because an OR-of-ANDs reaches two relations and must still stay in the `Filter`), and what the legacy passes may still do to what it built (08 §3's coexistence rule is now enforced for all seven `isSearchedTree` skips). `GOOPG_PGSHAPED_DP` stays OFF; the acceptance run and the flip are P5.9. **S5 run 1 (2026-08-05) is a documented NO-GO and its single blocker is now ATTRIBUTED and FIXED (P5.9-c, 09 §3.2):** the boundary map was built correctly and then rewritten by an **eighth** legacy pass, `remapTopProjection`, which finds the join tree to derive its posMap from by walking down past `*Project` wrappers — and the search boundary *is* a `*Project`, so it composed the search's own permutation on top of the boundary's and every column's value came back one relation-block from its name. 03 §10 gains a consumer-side amendment as a result: the producer-side tripwires all run before the passes that can damage the map, so the finished tree is re-checked at the tail of `Plan()` (`assertSearchedBoundariesIntact`) against the invariant that a boundary target names the very column it addresses. The re-run still waits on P5.9-d (value digests, not row counts) and P5.9-e (Q17). Amended 2026-08-05 (09 §3.6/§3.7, P5.9-h/-i): the `rows=1` estimate collapse run 3 named was minted AFTER the search by `EstimateRows`, which answered 1 for every index scan on the equality-probe convention — wrong for the bound-less full scan P5.4c-ii-b introduced (`parity_violations` 6 → 0), while the 7 TPC-DS plan-time aborts were the CHECKER's: `reresolveJoinByName`'s cross-side fallback could not tell a resolution MISS from an AMBIGUITY, and `(Name, SourceTableIdx)` is a column identity only WITHIN one scope, so three CTE arms' identically-named columns collide (DS05 under the flag `ERROR=7` → `PASS=6 … ERROR=0 TIMEOUT=1`). Neither fix moved a timing: what remained of S5 was a pure COST question (P5.9-h's full ordered index scan, P5.9-j's ~40× Q47). **Half of that is now closed** (09 §3.8, P5.9-j, 2026-08-05): Q47's 40× was one term charged on the wrong tuple count. The estimate everyone would have blamed is PG-faithful — the 1-row size for `{v1,v1_lag}` (four `DEFAULT_EQ_SEL`s over statistics-less CTE columns) is what **PG estimates too**, verified against the 65438 oracle on the same data — and PG escapes it only via a mechanism goopg lacks: its CTE scan publishes the WindowAgg's ordering as pathkeys, so PG merges at 375.55 with NO sort while goopg's merge must sort twice (1393.36), leaving hash (968.55) and plain nested loop (968.53) to decide it at a margin of **0.02**. `final_cost_nestloop` charges `cpu_per_tuple = cpu_tuple_cost + restrict_qual_cost.per_tuple` on `ntuples = outer_path_rows * inner_path_rows`, which PG comments in place as "number of tuples processed (not number emitted!)"; goopg splits that sum and the `cpu_tuple_cost` half was landing on the join's OUTPUT rows — an error smallest exactly on the plans the term exists to deter, since a nested loop is preferred when its output is small. `nestloopCost` now charges `cpuTupleCost * outerRows * innerRows` with PG's one-tuple clamp per side; the hash and merge siblings are deliberately untouched (PG charges those on `hashjointuples`/`mergejointuples`, which really are output counts). Q47 **8 m 40 s → 13 s**, DS05 subset under the flag `PASS=6 TIMEOUT=1` → **`PASS=7 TIMEOUT=0`**, flag-OFF arm unchanged with identical checksums. Two gaps ledgered rather than closed: CTE-scan pathkey propagation (P5.4c-ii) and the shared PG/goopg 7 193× under-estimate on stats-less CTE self-joins (§4.1's ratchet). **The other half — P5.9-h's TPC-H timing gap — is now closed too** (09 §3.9, P5.9-k, 2026-08-05), and the suspect P5.9-h named (`costIndexScan` at selectivity 1.0) was innocent: the defect was a MISSING term on the other side of the comparison. `costSortRun` implemented only `cost_sort`'s comparison half, on the stated premise that "TPC-H sorts are small dimension outputs" — which this phase invalidates, because a merge join sorts a JOIN INPUT and Q12's is 5 997 241 lineitem rows (~4.7 GB). Since P5.7-a the hash rival HAS been charged its spill, so the two candidates for one joinrel were billed **1 326 616** and **0** for spilling the same bytes through the same `work_mem` budget: the asymmetry ch. 04 §1 forbids, present as an entire term rather than a constant. `cost_tuplesort`'s disk branch is now reproduced term for term (`npages`/`nruns`/`log_runs` via `tuplesort_merge_order`, ¾-seq/¼-random page mix), sized through the same `hashsize.EntryBytes` model the hash side's `spillPages` uses so the two charges share one currency. Five TPC-H queries, one binary, both arms in one session: Q7 26.71→**16.29**, Q9 54.95→**15.86**, Q10 22.93→**5.65**, Q12 20.79→**9.82**, Q18 74.71→**29.79** s — **ON/OFF 2.61× → 1.007×**, every digest identical to run 3, Q12 back to Hash Join over two Seq Scans, §4 `parity_violations=0`, and the §5 audit's ON arm reduced to the OFF arm's single pre-existing Q18 violation. Ledgered rather than closed: goopg's merge operator sorts BOTH inputs unconditionally, so `tryMergeJoinPath`'s sort-skip credit is still a fiction at run time. **Run 4 executed 2026-08-06 (09 §3.10, HEAD `9e0cfe67`): five of the bar's six clauses PASS and the flip is held by the sixth, which has no instrument.** No defect in the run's evidence is attributed to the flag. Clause 1 PASS (23 MATCH; the lone VALUE-DIFF is the baseline's Q5, digests byte-identical to runs 2/3 so the PG adjudication carries), clause 2 **PASS 0.982×** — the ON arm is faster than the contemporaneous integer arm, where runs 1–3 read 1.36× — clause 3 PASS at a worst real query of 1.36× (Q9 15.83 s vs its named ≤ 170.9 s), clause 4 PASS with TPC-DS SF0.5 under the flag at `PASS=95 MISMATCH=0 CKMISMATCH=0 ERROR=0 TIMEOUT=0`, clause 5 PASS for the fourth consecutive run, and the §4 ratchet's `parity_violations` **6 → 0** on the ON arm. **Clause 6's missing instrument was built by P5.9-l-i 2026-08-06** (`internal/estimateaudit/spine.go`, rendered from `cmd/estimate-audit` on any run carrying a `--reference`; 09 §3.11) — the parity channel's `SHAPE (…-only joinrel)` labels compare relation SETS where clause 6 asks about PAIRINGS, so the spine channel computes each join node's child relsets instead; its first measurement refutes run 4's manual reading — the flag-ON arm goes bushy on six of the 22, not none, and on Q20 it chooses PG's bushy partition exactly, with two candidates (Q7, Q8) left for P5.9-l-ii's search-side enumeration provenance. Measured directly: PG 18.3 goes bushy on exactly Q7/Q8/Q20 of the 22 and goopg on none in either arm, which is not a failure by itself (the clause hard-fails only on a shape the search cannot express, and phase 2 is `joinrels.c:141-198` term for term) — but "enumerated and lost on cost" and "never enumerated" predict the same observable. **P5.9-l builds the pairing channel; P5.9 then re-runs clause 6 alone and flips or attributes.** **P5.9-l-ii added the SEARCH side of that channel 2026-08-06 (09 §3.12):** `internal/planner/joinsearchtrace.go` emits a `DPTRACE` block per join problem under `GOOPG_PGSHAPED_DP_TRACE=1` — every `(outer relset, inner relset, phase)` triple `makeJoinRel` was offered plus every pair the connectivity gate declined and why — and `internal/estimateaudit/enumtrace.go` parses it back through `estimate-audit --enum-trace <server log>`, adjudicating each §3.11 candidate as `OFFERED` (divergence is cost/stats, §4 admits it) / `DECLINED` / `SIDE-NOT-BUILT` / `NOT-ENUMERATED` (named gaps, §4 fails them) / `NO-TRACE` (a statement about the harvest, not the search). The two channels share one unit by construction: the trace's pair key is `SpineJoin.PairKey`'s string byte for byte and its relation names follow `leafRel`'s alias-first rule, without which Q7's two `nation` scans collapse on the search side while staying distinct on the plan side. goopg's own bushy pairings are derived as CONTROLS — each must come back `OFFERED` — and a failing control prints `VERDICT: HARNESS FAULT` and voids the run. Verified live on a throwaway cluster (bushy chosen plan recorded at `phase=2`, `created=0`, alias preserved, an unconnected partition reported as `SIDE-NOT-BUILT` with the side named); **and the measurement was taken 2026-08-06 (09 §3.13): clause 6 PASSES.** `PLAN_ONLY=1 DP_TRACE=1 PGSHAPED=1 scripts/tpch-estimate-audit-arm.sh 2026-08-06-p59lii-enum-on --queries 7,8,20` returns `enum_controls=2/2 enum_controls_oos=1 enum_candidates_offered=2/2 enum_problems=3 enum_malformed=0` — both PG-only bushy partitions (Q7's `{customer+lineitem+n2+orders} ⋈ {n1+supplier}`, Q8's `{lineitem+orders+part} ⋈ {customer+n1+region}`) were OFFERED to `makeJoinRel` at `phase=2` with `created=false`, so the search CAN express both shapes and lost them on cost, the reading §4's ratchet admits. Two instrument changes the run forced: **`estimate-audit --plan-only`** (plain `EXPLAIN`; §5 and the §4 parity column are OMITTED rather than printed empty, because a §5 table of `actual=? (no ANALYZE)` rows ends in a clean verdict — the one way the artifact could lie) which makes a planning-time question cost four minutes instead of a power run and, carrying no timing, exempts it from the arm's nightly-batch refusal; and the **`CROSS-QUERY-LEVEL`** verdict — goopg's Q20 plan prints `{nation+supplier} ⋈ {lineitem+part+partsupp}` across a SubPlan boundary that no join search of either engine ever partitioned, which the first run scored as `VERDICT: HARNESS FAULT` and voided a sound measurement. The classification is asymmetric on purpose: out of scope as a CONTROL (counted and printed, never silently dropped), a clause-6 FAILURE as a CANDIDATE (a partition PG reached inside one join problem is unreachable, not merely unchosen, when goopg did not flatten the sublink into the same problem), discriminated by positive evidence — a relation that entered no traced problem was planned elsewhere, whereas a log with no blocks at all is still `NO-TRACE` and still voids the run. **FLIPPED 2026-08-06** (`b92582fb`): `GOOPG_PGSHAPED_DP` is ON by default and `=0` is the opt-out; the post-flip DS05 arm (09 §3.15, M0127-P5.9-n) is green — `PASS=95 MISMATCH=0 CKMISMATCH=0 ERROR=0 TIMEOUT=0 SKIP=4`, zero verdict changes, zero runtime moves — while a FIXED-BINARY A/B of the two enumerators re-plans **86 of 99** TPC-DS queries, so the flip's correctness blast radius on this corpus is zero and its plan blast radius is 87%. The **COLLAPSE sub-flag stays OFF**: its acceptance pass ran 2026-08-06 (09 §3.18, M0127-P5.9-m) and every clause is green — TPC-H 24/24 MATCH at 0.984×, DS05 `PASS=95 MISMATCH=0 …`, one-variable plan A/B `same=99 changed=0` — but the same run measured the flag INERT end to end: `extractScans` descends `JoinTypeCross` only, so `tryPGShapedJoinSearch` declines every explicit-JOIN chain before `ctx.joinlist` is read, and goopg still reorders no `JOIN … ON` FROM clause at all. **Seam amended 2026-08-06 (09 §3.19, M0127-P5.9-r): `extractSearchLeaves` now descends INNER links and routes their `ON` quals into the search's clause list, so an explicit-JOIN chain IS searchable — and the re-run of §3.18's protocol is still `same=99 changed=0` under both collapse regimes, because the new `DPTRACE seam-decline reason=leaf-count` channel shows every one of the twelve TPC-DS JOIN queries (and TPC-H Q13) is topped by an OUTER link that stops the walk: 0 of 99 corpus queries are INNER-only (`TestNoCorpusQueryHasAnInnerOnlyJoinChain`). The blocker moved one level deeper — `joinlistItem` carries no join TYPE, so admitting an outer link would plan a LEFT JOIN as an INNER JOIN, and the leaf-count decline is what stands between that and a wrong answer; collapse stays default OFF.** Provenance tooling amended 2026-08-06 (09 §3.16, M0127-P5.9-q): the gates' `planner-flags:` stamp is GENERATED from the Go defaults it names (`internal/planner/flaglabels.go` → `cmd/gen-planner-flag-labels` → `scripts/planner-flags.env` → `scripts/planner-flags.sh`, sourced by both the SF0.5 gate and `tpch-spotcheck.sh`), after the same hand-written `unset(off)` label outlived two default flips (M0125-0005, M0127-P5.9) and mis-stamped the acceptance run of the second one; four unit guards, and the coverage guard's first finding was that six plan-shaping planner flags — including `GOOPG_PGSHAPED_DP` in the spot-check — were named by no artefact goopg had ever captured. EXPLAIN parity extended 2026-08-06 (09 §3.17, M0127-P5.9-o): a join's RESIDUAL qual now prints as upstream's `Join Filter:` line — in `ExplainNode`'s slot (after the Cond line, before the node's own `Filter:`) and split by the same `ExecHashKeyPlan`/`ExecMergeKeyPlan` the executor uses, so every conjunct appears exactly once — closing the gap where `ON a = b AND v < w` printed its second conjunct nowhere at all; byte-verified against PostgreSQL 18.3 on four join shapes, and it unpins `TestExplainQualifiesUpperFilter` onto the default enumerator. Outer-join spine peeled 2026-08-06 (09 §3.20, M0127-P5.9-s): `joinlistItem` carries a join TYPE, `makeRelFromJoinlist` REFUSES a pinned outer subproblem instead of searching it as an inner join, and `splitOuterSpine` peels pinned LEFT links off the top of a chain so the search plans the INNER PREFIX below them — the first change in the milestone to move a corpus plan (DS05 `same=97 changed=2` on exactly {Q72,Q75}, the predicted set, with every result cell identical and **Q72 163s→70s**), and the plan it moved exposed a pre-existing spill defect: `encodeDatum` never wrote a `KindTime` datum's `Flags`, so every DATE through a hash-join spill came back a bare timestamp (a spilled date still COMPARED correctly, which is why the round-trip test was green). Audited in 09 §3.21 (P5.9-u): the spill frame is goopg's ONLY Datum-level serializer — everywhere else a declared column type travels with the bytes — and it was broken three ways, not one. `flagDate` is retired for the structural `Datum.TimeSub` (carved out of the alignment pad; 48-byte layout unchanged), which also recovered a SECOND silent loss (a `timetz`'s UTC offset in `Datum.Scale`, so spilled timetz values sorted by local time — the guard's comparison flips +1→-1 with the fix reverted) and a loud one (`KindEnum`/`KindToastPointer` had no arm at all, so spilling an enum column failed outright). The fix is the CONTRACT: guards now walk `datumKindCount`/`timeSubtypeCount` and fail on any kind or subtype the codec has no arm for, and `decodeDatum` REJECTS an unknown subtype rather than quietly widening it to a bare timestamp; `Datum.Flags` stays unserialized because `flagBigNumeric` is representation state the decoder re-establishes. Regress-port run baseline-relative in a HEAD worktree: 56 tests, identical verdicts and diff sizes on both arms. RIGHT spines admitted 2026-08-06 (09 §3.22, M0127-P5.9-t), and the filing it closes was wrong twice over: upstream's `reduce_outer_joins` RIGHT→LEFT flip (prepjointree.c:3360) **cannot be represented** — `parser.FromExpr` is a `Base` range var plus a FLAT `[]JoinExpr`, so the flipped `d LEFT JOIN (a ⋈ b ⋈ c)` has no node, and flipping inside the planner's own tree would renumber every binding offset and reorder `SELECT *` (upstream escapes that only because its Vars are varno-addressed) — and the flip was never what the seam needed, because a left-deep chain puts a RIGHT JOIN's multi-relation side on the LEFT of the pin exactly where a LEFT JOIN's is. What differs is NULLABILITY: the prefix's ORDER is searchable either way (`deconstruct_recurse` builds a sub-joinlist for an outer join's nullable arm), but the `WHERE` is not pushable into it (`check_outerjoin_delay` delays any qual from above whose relids reach the nullable side), so `prefixNullable` scans the whole spine — one RIGHT link anywhere holds the entire `WHERE` in the residual above it — while the prefix's own `ON` quals, which originate below the join, are distributed as before. Measured, by reverting the guard: `… RIGHT JOIN rj_c … WHERE rj_a.id IS NULL` returns all three `rj_c` rows null-extended instead of the one. FULL stays declined (both inputs null-extended, and its USING coalescing names merged-var positions), as do outer links buried below an inner one; `reduce_outer_joins`' actual *reductions* — the strict-qual RIGHT→INNER proof that would let the qual push — are the ledgered follow-up, and are the half worth porting. Growth coverage restored on the DEFAULT enumerator 2026-08-06 (09 §3.23, M0127-P5.9-p): `TestExplainAnalyzeHashJoinReportsGrownBatches` had been blinding its own fixture (`SetRelationSizer(nil)`) and pinning the legacy arm, because a blind searched arm costs a nested loop rather than a hash join. The filed replacement — "a deliberately mis-estimated selectivity on the build side" — **cannot work**: the geometry sizes from `EstimateRows(buildNode)`, and for a searched scan the base restrictions ride on the scan node while `seqScanRows` returns the relation's row count and ignores them, so a `WHERE` on the build side moves the JOIN's estimate (priced in `makeJoinRel`: `rows=1840`→`rows=171`) while `Batches: 4` never budges. The lever that works is the WIDTH: `buildGeometry` passes `avgVarBytes = 0` (no per-column average-width statistic — ledger 2026-08-03 M0127-P3.1), so a text-heavy build is priced as if only its Datum array were resident — the one mis-estimate that leaves the ROW counts, and therefore the join algorithm, untouched. 400 rows of 2 kB text price at ~19 kB and occupy ~800 kB: `Batches: 32 (originally 4)` with the sizer installed and no flag pin, against a negative control at the ordinary 48-byte width that picks `Batches: 4` up front and never moves. The test is P3.1's grow-on-measured-overrun safety net under test, and carries the tripwire: populating `avgVarBytes` will make it fail with "nbatch never grew", which is the correct outcome to see. P5.6 CLOSED 2026-08-06 (04 §2.1, new): the roll-up's own residue — "re-evaluate M0125-0003 stage 3 against rows-once" — resolves to **stage 3 is not a fourth staged flag consumer**, because rows-once deletes the stage-2 seed consumer it would have shadowed; the placement is now `applyRelSizeFallback` at the search seam in `estimate_rel_size` → `set_baserel_size_estimates` order, a no-op S-cold (the reliability gate) and load-bearing post-restart (restored column stats with no `RowCount`). Acceptance re-read from the default-arm audit: Q9's final joinrel 6.3× against the ≤10² bar, `parity_violations=0`. P5.7 CLOSED 2026-08-06 (04 §4.4, new): the roll-up's residue was its own BAR — "PLAN, default arm ZERO diffs" — whose premise **expired between its sub-items landing (2026-08-05 12:20/12:47) and the read**, because P5.9 flipped `GOOPG_PGSHAPED_DP` ON by default at 2026-08-06 02:22; a zero-diff containment check on an inert search cannot be stated once the search is live and *supposed* to move plans, so what discharges P5.7 is that both halves were already in the tree the flip's own acceptance measured. The claim they rested on had spread: **28 files still carried `Still inert: GOOPG_PGSHAPED_DP is OFF … so they cannot change a plan` headers**, including `cost_funcs.go` where `hashJoinCost` lives — banners later loops read as gate-skip authority — each now corrected to verified post-flip reachability (`collapse.go` differs: its joinlist IS consumed; only the narrower `GOOPG_PGSHAPED_COLLAPSE` arm is off). P5.7-b's "no production PRODUCER of a fraction" ledger row is discharged (P5.9-b's `searchTupleFraction`), with the caller-fraction half re-filed. **The transferable lesson: a flag flip silently invalidates every comment, task justification and skipped gate that cited the old default, and none of them are in the flip's own diff.** PS6.1 first half landed 2026-08-06 (05 §6.1, new): the compiled key/residual seam (`compileExecExprs` off `initExecKeys`; key eval 9.91→7.32 ns/op, residual 150.3→139.0 ns/op, 0 allocs) — but the stage's substantive change turned out not to be dispatch. `evalFastExpr`'s `ColumnRef` arm had **no bounds check**, so moving the hash-join key/residual onto it would have re-armed the raw index panic that once escaped the build-side drain outside `ParallelGroup.Go`'s recover and closed the client socket (TPC-DS Q8); the guard now lives in `evalFastExpr` and covers filter/project/limit, latently exposed since M0107-0003. Two measurements worth carrying: a `widthSlot` capability assertion for that guard is an itab lookup costing ~1.4 ns/eval — alone enough to make the compiled arm SLOWER than the interpreter — so it is a concrete type switch that also removes the interface `Get`; and at ~150 ns the residual is dominated by `evalBinary`, not dispatch, so P2.2's NARROWING and not PS6.1's compilation is what makes an all-equijoin residual cheap. Third finding, a silent-wrong-answer class: a composite encode over an uncompiled node list does not error, it returns the EMPTY key and files every row under it, so `initExecKeys` now compiles on the plan-less path too. Amended 2026-08-06 (07 §4a): the join streams' composed-slot seam must build slots with `SlotFromRow`, never `asSlot` — absence travels as `EOF`, so a nil `Row` from `next()` is a ZERO-COLUMN tuple, and `asSlot`'s nil→nil arm turned it into a nil `TupleSlot` that the simple-query result loop dereferenced, **crashing the backend** on any join of two zero-column relations (the row-level analogue of [0122-0004](0122-0004-extended-zero-column-rows.md)'s schema-level nil/non-nil discriminator). Found by attributing the S7 gate's nightly regress failures, none of which turned out to be S5-attributable; guard is `TestPort_ZeroColumnJoinDoesNotCrashBackend` in `internal/testport`, because the `internal/executor` fixture yields non-nil zero-length Rows and passes against the unfixed code. **S7 gate record amended 2026-08-06 (09 §3.25):** the gate's "clean nightly cycle" was waiting on the 01:00 scheduler, not on evidence — `make nightly-batch` shares the same run lock and was run on demand (`20260806-191958`, 70 min), taking the batch from 18 action items to 10 with only `testport` red; 8 of the 10 are one `regress/suite-wedge` at `multirangetypes` and its truncated-output casualties, leaving `TestPort_IsolationEvalPlanQual` as the single engine-side blocker — a NEW failure (L696, `updwctefail`/`delwctefail`: PG's `TM_SelfModified` "tuple to be updated was already modified by an operation triggered by the current command" is not implemented), bisected to `276e7eda` (M0125-0052), which unmasked the latent gap rather than causing it.

- [parallel-query/README.md](parallel-query/README.md) - 11-file design (DESIGN ONLY, implementation not started) for **intra-transaction parallel query**: Parallel Seq Scan, Gather / Gather Merge, Partial+Finalize aggregation, and Parallel Hash Join, executed with goroutines rather than PG's worker processes. Motivated by the reference capture showing PG 18.3 parallelises **12 of 13 sampled TPC-H queries** (`Workers Planned: 2`) using exactly these node families (`Parallel Seq Scan` x26, `Gather`/`Gather Merge` x11 each, `Parallel Hash Join` x7, `Partial`/`Finalize` aggregates x18, `Parallel Index Scan` x0) while every parallel GUC in goopg is registered and explicitly inert (`internal/config/defaults.go:593-600`). Survey finding: the shared subsystems are ALREADY concurrency-safe (lock-free buffer pool, Lehman-Yao btree reads, pure MVCC visibility over an immutable snapshot value, RWMutex catalog) - the eleven blockers are per-operator scratch and missing plumbing, chief among them `mctx`'s single-owner contract whose per-page `Reset()` coincides exactly with the parallel block boundary. Takes PG as the semantic baseline (result identity, node labels, `Workers Planned/Launched`, GUC names and units, `compute_parallel_worker()`'s x3 size ladder, `proparallel` gating) while deliberately diverging on mechanism where process isolation is PG's reason and not goopg's: no DSM, no `shm_mq` tuple serialisation, no `aggserialfn`/`aggdeserialfn` (transition state crosses a channel directly), a hash-join build table shared by pointer behind a publish barrier instead of DSA, and goroutine startup in place of fork. Costing is a stats-gated size heuristic, not PG's `parallel_setup_cost` arithmetic, because goopg has no `(startup, total)` cost pair - EXPLAIN's `cost=0.00..0.00` is a hardcoded placeholder. v1 refuses SERIALIZABLE (SSI predicate locks are writes on the scan read path), all DML, parallel-unsafe functions, and non-decomposable aggregates. Also documents two GUC fidelity bugs found while surveying: `min_parallel_table_scan_size` renders `8GB` where PG renders `8MB`, and `min_parallel_index_scan_size` is off by the same 1024x (byte counts mislabelled as KB), plus `max_parallel_workers` missing entirely. P0-P8 roadmap with `race-gate` promoted to an acceptance criterion.

Supersedes-on-overlap [0058-0001](0058-0001-subplan-and-join-optimisation.md) (unimplemented remainder) and [0061-0001](0061-0001-exists-anti-semi-join-unnesting.md) follow-ups; absorbs [0063-0004](0063-0004-q21-anti-join-index-driven.md). Motivated by `analysis/tpch/goopg-pg-tpch-plan-compare-260718/` (on `origin/master`) and the in-bundle `evidence/` HEAD captures.
- [tpcds-section4.2-fixes/README.md](tpcds-section4.2-fixes/README.md) - Round-1 TPC-DS SF=1 fix bundle (2026-07-25) closing 8 of the 9 goopg-only errors reported in `analysis/tpcds-sf1-goopg-20260724.md` §4.2: analyzer alias-first `scopeRelMatches` (PG hides a FROM entry's table name once it is aliased) for Q47/Q57/Q58, `KindTime + KindInt` date arithmetic in `evalBinary` for Q72, `parseParenthesisedSelectStmt` in `parseRangeVar` plus `KwReturns` as an implicit alias for the FROM-subquery set operations in Q77/Q87, chained `WindowAgg` nodes for Q49's multiple window specs, ORDER BY derived-output-name resolution, and the COPY btree-index maintenance fix (`8ee4194b`) that restored 27 queries from 0 rows. Q8's INTERSECT crash was deferred and is picked up by the round-2 bundle below.
- [tpcds-round2-fixes/README.md](tpcds-round2-fixes/README.md) - Round-2 TPC-DS SF=1 bundle: root cause and fix design for every remaining goopg-only failure (2 errors, 6 row-count divergences, 16 timeouts) measured in `analysis/tpcds-sf1-goopg-20260726.md`. Headline finding: three of the four correctness classes are ONE defect class - eleven hand-written expression walkers in the planner, each a stale partial copy of the others, each silently passing through the `Expr` node kinds it does not enumerate (`plan.go` declares 32 types; the worst walker handles 11), so a skipped `IsNullExpr` leaves a stale `ColumnRef.Index` and the query returns the wrong answer instead of failing. Second, independent finding: `MultiHashJoin.Tables` is sorted by table OID while `MultiHashJoin.Filters` still carries FROM-cumulative column indices, and `pushSingleSourceFiltersIntoMHJTables` consumes the latter as if it were the former - on TPC-DS the two orders disagree and a `date_dim` predicate is evaluated against `store`. Designs a single shared `exprChildSlots` traversal primitive with a go/ast exhaustiveness gate (turning the class from silent wrong answers into a build failure), dual index+name attribution for MHJ filter push-down, `SetOp` coverage plus decline-on-unknown in `buildBindingsPosMap`, executor-side IN-list cross-kind coercion, and a flag-gated `estimate_rel_size` fallback for the timeout class. Includes a three-state (S-cold / S-warm / S-fallback) measurement protocol for the stats-and-plan-cache interaction.

- [../../analysis/cost-driven-second-try-200731/README.md](../../analysis/cost-driven-second-try-200731/README.md) - 14-file analysis bundle (DESIGN ONLY) evaluating the proposal to demote `MultiHashJoin` from a plan node to a runtime execution strategy so the planner emits only PG-shaped binary join trees. Verdict: adopt the goal, reject the proposed first mechanism — goopg's binary cascade re-materialises its probe input twice per level on two different execution paths, so the first move is de-materialising the join seam, not building a fusion operator. Carries the full semantic contract (C1-C15), the fail-closed qualification predicate (Q0-Q9), a risk register dominated by silent row-count regression (R1-R18), a staged plan with per-stage gates, three kill switches, and a two-independent-pass panel synthesis. PASSWORD` hashing (`auth.NewSCRAMSecretWithIterations` + `resolveScramIterations` reading the live session's `currentGUCResolver`) instead of always using the hardcoded default 4096 — `SET scram_iterations = N` now changes newly-derived verifiers' PBKDF2 cost, matching upstream `encrypt_password`/`scram_build_secret`. |
| root-0022 | [TOAST chunk_id restart durability](root-0022-toast-oid-restart-durability.md) | accepted | `executor.toastOIDCounter` is process-local (resets to 0 on restart) but the TOAST relation it writes into survives on disk, so the first TOASTed value written after any restart reissued `chunk_id 1`, colliding with a pre-restart value's still-resident chunk_id 1 and splicing unrelated rows' bytes together on detoast. Fix: `executor.SeedToastOIDCounter`/`MaxToastChunkIDInRel` scan every table's TOAST relation once at startup (`internal/initdb/open.go`, after `loadUserTablesFromHeap`) and advance the counter past the max chunk_id found, mirroring the existing catalog-OID-counter restart pattern (M0106-0013). Root cause of the WordPress `wp_options`/`wp_user_roles` neighbor-row corruption (deferral ledger 2026-07-02). Follow-up in the same doc: TOAST chunk inserts now route through `markHeapInsertDirty`/`LogHeapInsert` (same per-insert WAL discipline as the main heap-insert path) instead of a bare `MarkDirty`, closing a narrower unclean-crash gap where chunks 2+ into an already-dirty TOAST page produced zero WAL output. |
| root-0023 | [Statement / query logging (`GOOPG_LOG_STATEMENT`)](root-0023-statement-query-logging.md) | accepted | Env-var-controlled per-statement query log (`none`/`ddl`/`mod`/`all`, mirroring PG's `log_statement`), off by default. `server.Config.LogStatement` (from `GOOPG_LOG_STATEMENT` in `cmd/goopg`) parsed once in `server.New` into `Server.logStmtLevel`; `(*Server).logStatement` (`internal/server/statement_log.go`) logs at the simple-protocol choke point (`query.go:handleQuery`, before routing/parse like PG's `exec_simple_query`) and the extended path (`dispatch_extended.go:executeExtendedQueryViaExecutor`, at Execute), emitting `msg="statement"` with `proto`, `statement`, and (in an explicit txn with an assigned lazy xid) `xid`. | root-0024 | [Simple-query batch: CREATE TABLE/INDEX atomicity on abort](root-0024-simple-query-batch-ddl-create-atomicity.md) | accepted | A multi-statement simple-query message runs under one implicit mvcc transaction, so a LATER statement's failure must roll back an EARLIER successful `CREATE TABLE`/`CREATE INDEX` too — but `catalog.InMemory.RegisterTable` is non-transactional, so the registration survived while its `pg_class`/`pg_attribute` heap rows (written under the rolled-back tx) did not, permanently desyncing `pg_dump`-visible state (M0110-0001 DU-002 slice 444 discovery). Fix: `dispatchSimpleQueryViaExecutor` wires a message-scoped throwaway `*executor.BasicSession` for autocommit batches (so `RecordDDLCreate` has somewhere to record) and its abort defer now calls `executor.ProcessRollbackUndos` before `TxnMgr.Rollback`. `RecordDDLCreate`'s dead-code `inTx` guard removed (was unreachable pre-fix). Deferred: enum/composite-type creation and TRUNCATE/DROP-in-savepoint tracking remain explicit-transaction-only (touching `inTx` more broadly risks ~20 unrelated deferred-constraint/stats call sites). **Follow-up (loop #103):** the `CREATE TABLE; BEGIN; ...; ROLLBACK;` compound-batch residual (throwaway session's pending DDL-create list lost when replaced mid-batch) is now fixed — the `TxBegin` handler drains and replays the throwaway session's `pendingDDL` onto the newly-allocated real session before the hand-off. **Follow-up (2026-07-04):** found and fixed a more severe bug in this fix's own mechanism — `connTxState.Session()` returned a stale, permanently-reused session (never reset to nil by `End()`) instead of nil once a connection had ever run one explicit transaction, so every LATER autocommit statement on that connection got the wrong (long-lived) session instead of a fresh message-scoped throwaway one; a successful autocommit `CREATE TABLE`'s undrained `pendingDDL` entry then got incorrectly rolled back by a WHOLLY UNRELATED later aborting autocommit batch, dropping an already-committed table. Fixed by gating `Session()` on `c.active`. **Follow-up (2026-07-04):** enum/composite-type creation (`CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM/composite`, `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE/RENAME TO`) is now undo-aware for a single-message autocommit batch too — new `Session.TracksDDLUndo()` (true for both a real explicit transaction and a new `NewAutocommitUndoSession()`, without touching `inTx`/`InExplicitTransaction()` itself) gates the four `operators_ddl.go` record sites, and the abort defer now also calls the newly-exported `executor.UndoEnumDDLOnAbort`. Had to also guard `dispatch.go`'s `ectx.Pending*`→`connTx` write-back on `connTx.InExplicit()` to avoid leaking a committed autocommit type's pending-set entry into a later, unrelated aborting batch on the same connection (same collateral-damage class as the `connTxState.Session()` fix). **Follow-up (2026-07-04):** the mid-batch-`BEGIN` compound-batch combination, previously flagged as still open, is confirmed already resolved by the same write-back mechanism (it fires again right after `BEGIN` itself completes, by which point `connTx.InExplicit()` is already true) — no code change needed, only regression tests (`internal/server/dispatch_batch_atomicity_test.go`) and a design-doc correction. root-0024's first residual is now fully closed for enum/composite. **Follow-up (2026-07-04):** the TRUNCATE half of the first residual is now also closed — `truncateTableAndPartitions`'s `RecordTruncate` call site now gates on `TracksDDLUndo()` instead of `InExplicitTransaction()`, so `TRUNCATE t; SELECT 1/0;` in one autocommit message correctly restores `t`'s pre-truncate pages (`ProcessRollbackUndos` already drained/restored `TakePendingTruncates()` unconditionally — only the record-site gate was missing). The sibling `RecordDDLDrop` (DROP TABLE inside a savepoint) call site was audited and left as `InExplicitTransaction()`: it is additionally gated on `SavepointDepth() > 0`, and `SAVEPOINT` itself is structurally unreachable outside an explicit transaction (`25P01`), so widening that gate would be a no-op. root-0024's first residual is now fully closed — no open items remain. |
| root-0025 | [Auto-updatable views + WITH CHECK OPTION enforcement](root-0025-updatable-views.md) | accepted | INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against ANY view (planInsert/planUpdate/planDelete never checked `catalog.Table.View`) silently wrote through to storage keyed on the view's own OID — a location no SELECT ever reads back — reporting success (`INSERT 0 1`/`UPDATE 0`) while doing nothing, worse than the read-only-error the M0119-0004 slice-365 deferral assumed. Fix: `viewAutoUpdatableBase` (`internal/planner/view_dml.go`) detects a restricted "simple passthrough" subset (single base relation, no joins/aggregation/set-ops, unrenamed in-order full column list) and rewrites the DML onto the base table; anything outside that subset is rejected with `55000` (PG's `error_view_not_updatable`) instead of silently corrupting. `WITH CHECK OPTION` is enforced by `checkViewCheckOption` (`internal/executor/operators_fk.go`) against the finalized INSERT/UPDATE row, raising `44000` (`ERRCODE_WITH_CHECK_OPTION_VIOLATION`) on violation. Surfaced and fixed a latent, feature-independent bug along the way: `updateOp.updateViaIndex`'s initial B-tree scan never evaluated `o.pred` (only its EPQ-recheck path did), so a residual predicate folded into a `Filter`-wrapped `IndexScan` was silently dropped. **Same-date follow-up:** fixed at the root — `updateViaIndex` now evaluates `o.pred` on its initial scan, and `planUpdate` takes the index path unconditionally for view-target UPDATEs again (the earlier index-skip workaround is removed). **Later follow-up (view-of-view chaining, closes deferred item 2):** `viewAutoUpdatableChain` (renamed from `viewAutoUpdatableBase`) now recurses when a simple view's `FROM` relation is itself a simple auto-updatable view; `viewChainQuals` combines every level's own qual for the unconditional UPDATE/DELETE row-visibility restriction, and separately computes the CASCADED/LOCAL-aware subset for CHECK OPTION enforcement (mirroring `rewriteHandler.c`'s per-view propagation) — required correcting the eligibility check since `CreateView` marks every view (not just system-catalog virtuals) `Table.Virtual = true`. **Later follow-up (column subset/reorder/rename, closes deferred item 1):** `viewColumnMap` (replacing `viewTargetsPassthrough`) relaxes the eligibility check to "every target-list entry is a bare column reference to the `FROM` relation" (matching PG's `view_col_is_auto_updatable`) instead of requiring an unrenamed in-order full-column passthrough, returning a `colMap []int` (view ordinal → base ordinal) that `viewAutoUpdatableChain` composes down a chain; `viewProxyTable` builds a synthetic table with `base`'s exact physical column layout but the exposed ordinals renamed to the view's own names (unexposed ordinals hidden via an unmatchable empty name), which `planInsert`/`planUpdate`/`planDelete` pass to `singleBindingContext` in place of `base` so `SET`/`WHERE`/`RETURNING`/column-list resolution transparently uses the view's vocabulary while the plan node's actual scan/mutation target stays `base`; each chain level's own `WHERE` (`viewQualOnBase`) now resolves against its *immediate* `FROM`'s exposure rather than unconditionally against `base`. **Later follow-up (`UPDATE...FROM`/`DELETE...USING` a view, closes deferred item 3):** `planUpdate`/`planDelete` no longer reject `UPDATE...FROM`/`DELETE...USING` against a view unconditionally — the view's own qual is ANDed into `FromPred`/`UsingPred` so the cross-product path still restricts to rows the view exposes, and `WITH CHECK OPTION` is enforced in `updateWithFrom` (restricted to the base relation's own rows, matching the FROM-free path). Also fixed a previously-untested latent bug this surfaced: `viewProxyTable`'s synthetic table keeps `base`'s own name, so an unaliased qualified reference to the view by its own name (`UPDATE v SET x=1 WHERE v.id=1`) failed to resolve at every view-DML site; new `viewResolveAlias` helper falls back to the view's pre-rewrite name when no explicit alias is given. **Later follow-up (CHECK OPTION on partition/inheritance-child-routed rows, closes deferred item 5):** both `updateScanTables` (FROM-free `UPDATE`) and `updateWithFrom` gated the CHECK OPTION check to the base/parent table's own rows, but each already computes a `parentNewRow` in the base table's own column ordinal space before that gate (via `buildInheritColMap`/`remapChildRowToParent`/`remapParentRowToChild` for true inheritance children; PG requires a partition's columns to exactly mirror the parent's, so a partition-routed row needs no remap at all) — removed the gate and check `parentNewRow` unconditionally in both. New discovery, project-wide and view-independent, deliberately left unfixed: `updateViaIndex` has no partition/inheritance-child fan-out at all, so an index-eligible `UPDATE parent SET ... WHERE indexed_col = X` (no `ONLY`) silently skips a matching row living only in an inheritance child's own storage. **Later follow-up (`INSERT...ON CONFLICT` against a renamed view column, closes item 1's "Known residual"):** `planOnConflict` (`internal/planner/planner.go`) always resolved the conflict-target column list (`resolveArbiterIndex`), `DO UPDATE SET`/`WHERE`, and the `excluded` binding against `tbl` — already reassigned to `base` by the time `planInsert` calls it — instead of `resolveTbl` (the view's column-name proxy every other view-DML resolution site already substitutes); now threads `resolveTbl`/the view's pre-rewrite name through so a `scopeTbl`/`scopeAlias` pair resolves all three the same way `planUpdate`/`planDelete` already do. **Later follow-up (`WITH (check_option = ...)` reloption-form spelling, M0122-0004):** the pre-AS `WITH (...)` options loop in `internal/parser/ddl.go`'s `parseCreateViewTail` captured `security_barrier`/`security_invoker` but had no `check_option` case, silently dropping that spelling even though upstream's `DefineView` folds the trailing `WITH [CASCADED|LOCAL] CHECK OPTION` clause into the identical `check_option` reloption internally; added, with the same lenient (non-erroring, default-cascaded) handling as the sibling boolean options — no executor change needed since `execCreateView` already reads `s.CheckOption` regardless of which spelling set it. **Root-0025 is now fully closed** — no open items remain within this milestone's own scope; the `updateViaIndex` partition/inheritance-child fan-out gap, project-wide and view-independent, was resolved in a follow-up loop — see [root-0026](root-0026-update-via-index-inheritance-fanout.md). |
| root-0026 | [`updateViaIndex`/`indexScanOp` partition/inheritance-child fan-out](root-0026-update-via-index-inheritance-fanout.md) | accepted | Both goopg's UPDATE index fast path (`updateOp.updateViaIndex`) and its SELECT index fast path (`indexScanOp`, driven by the planner's `IndexScan` node) opened exactly one B-tree scoped to the named table's own storage, silently missing rows that live only in a plain-`INHERITS` child (`UPDATE`/`SELECT ... WHERE indexed_col = X`, no `ONLY`) — partitioned parents were unaffected (no storage/index of their own to match). Fix (UPDATE side): `updateOp.Next()` now builds the parent+children scan-target list before deciding whether to take the index fast path, taking it only when there are no children (falls through to the pre-existing, already-correct SeqScan+fan-out path otherwise); this landed via a reconciliation between two independent Ralph loops that picked up the same fix concurrently (kept one implementation, ported the other's extra test coverage). Fix (SELECT side, closes the twin gap the reconciliation surfaced): `planner.planIndexScanFromWhere`/`tryRangeIndexScan` (`internal/planner/planner.go`) gained an `enforceInheritanceFanout` guard — mirroring the pre-existing `PartitionKey` early-out — that refuses to attach an `IndexScan` node when the target has accessible inheritance children and the query isn't `FROM ONLY`, so the caller falls back to the plan shape `planScanRangeVar` already builds for that case (a `SetOp{All:true}` chain of per-table `SeqScan`s). Threaded from the SELECT call site only (`!fromOnly`, `fromOnly` capturing the FROM clause's `ONLY` flag); the `planUpdate`/`planDelete` call sites of the same function deliberately keep `enforceInheritanceFanout=false` since `updateOp`'s own executor-level gate already covers UPDATE and `deleteOp` never consults this plan node's index choice for its fan-out decision at all — done to keep this fix's diff disjoint from the concurrently-landing UPDATE-side fix rather than because a unified `true` everywhere would be incorrect. |
| root-0027 | [Nightly classifier: per-package resource-kill vs. regression (M-NIGHTLY follow-up)](root-0027-nightly-classifier-per-package-resource-kill.md) | accepted | Root-causes the `cmd/goopg`/`internal/amcheck` "units-timeout" mystery (open since the `20260715-010036` nightly, 3 prior investigation loops) as a classifier bug in `ci/batch/lib/summarize.py`, not a product hang. Reproduced the whole `units` package set failing identically under the exact nightly cgroup config (`GOMEMLIMIT=5GiB`/`MemoryMax=8G`/`GOFLAGS=-p=4`) in 16.5 minutes, confirming genuine multi-package resource contention. `cmd/goopg`/`internal/amcheck` die via a bare `signal: killed` (unambiguous cgroup/OOM per `ci/design/03` §C); `summarize.py`'s existing `looks_resource_killed(log) and "--- FAIL" not in log` resource-kill rule ran over the WHOLE combined ~40-package log instead of per-package, so `internal/wal`'s one genuine `--- FAIL` that same night flipped the guard for the entire `units` stage, misreporting the two pure resource-kills as regressions. The same bug, inverted, silently swallowed `race/internal/access/btree`/`race/internal/amcheck` (real, never-before-surfaced `-race` failures) into one uninformative whole-stage "resource kill" notice on every prior night. Fixed with `split_go_test_pkg_blocks` — per-package block-scoped classification instead of whole-log; new `ci/batch/lib/test_summarize.py` unit coverage; regenerated `ci/logs/action-items.md` from the real historical logs to confirm the fix's effect on production data. `internal/initdb`/`internal/mvcc` (ambiguous SIGQUIT-timeout-without-`signal:-killed` signature) and the two newly-surfaced `race` items remain open, correctly left as regression items pending real investigation — this fix makes the log honest, it does not by itself resolve them. |
| root-0028 | [amcheck real-tree stress test: leftover debug instrumentation caused nightly race-lane timeouts](root-0028-amcheck-realtree-stress-debug-instrumentation-cleanup.md) | accepted | Root-causes and fixes the two `race/internal/access/btree`/`race/internal/amcheck` items `root-0027` surfaced (never previously investigated). Both pass standalone (`btree` 23s, `amcheck` 148s) but reliably hung under the exact nightly race-lane cgroup config (`GOMEMLIMIT=5GiB`/`MemoryMax=8G`/`GOFLAGS=-p=4`) — traced to `TestVerifyBtreeEngineSilentOnRealConcurrentContended` (`internal/amcheck/verify_nbtree_realtree_test.go`), whose helper `buildRealTreeConcurrent` still had all 6 of the resolved M-NIGHTLY `AI-20260708-064334-001` investigation's debug-tracing flags (`DebugTraceInserts`/`DebugVerifyFastPathInserts`/`DebugTraceFlushes`/`DebugTraceReloads`/`DebugTraceContentMu`/`DebugTraceBufmap`) plus 2 pool-level flags (`DebugValidateCleanEvictions`/`DebugTraceSlotEvents`) permanently enabled — each funnels every pin/unpin/insert from 64 concurrently racing goroutines through shared mutex-guarded logs, harmless standalone but, combined with `-race` overhead and the nightly's memory-capped 4-package co-load, serialized this 200K-insert/64-writer stress test badly enough to exceed a 25-minute per-test timeout. `internal/access/btree`'s own nightly failure was pure collateral CPU starvation from sharing the box with amcheck's runaway test. Fix: removed all 8 flags/hooks (the investigation they served has permanent regression coverage elsewhere, `TestBufmapInsertSkipsPastTombstoneToExistingKey`) plus a now-permanently-dead `FastPathViolations()` diagnostic-log block. Standalone: the test 172.65s→7.05s (24x), full package 148s→11.4s (13x); re-verified clean under the exact nightly config that originally reproduced the hang. The now-unused `Debug*`/`Record*` instrumentation itself was left in place in `btree.go`/`bufpool.go` (zero-cost when unset, matching the codebase's existing pattern) as optional follow-up cleanup, not required for correctness. **Follow-up (2026-07-15):** re-ran the full 44-package nightly `units`-lane repro (identical cgroup config) now that the `amcheck` fix above is in place — `internal/initdb` (237.79s) and `internal/mvcc` (1.30s) both PASS cleanly, 0 `FAIL`, confirming their `AI-20260715-010036-001`/`-002` nightly timeouts were the same collateral resource-starvation class as `cmd/goopg`/`amcheck`'s classified resource kills, not an independent hang — closes the `20260715-010036` nightly triage thread. |
| root-0029 | [Nightly regress "wedge cascade": one hung case, 19 phantom regressions](root-0029-nightly-regress-wedge-cascade.md) | accepted | Root-causes the 26-item `20260725-011243` nightly action-item storm: 19 of the items were `regress/<case> (baseline pass) diverged: output mismatch; normalization rules need extension`, but 36 cases had simply consumed their full 120s budget and the harness diffed psql's **truncated** transcript against the full expected `.out`. A diff against a truncated file always differs, so the harness blamed the normalization rules. The wedge outlives the case (killing psql kills only the client; the goopg backend keeps executing and keeps holding whatever it holds), so the failures arrive in unbroken runs — 21 consecutive cases from `tid` in this run — and the existing `isAlive()` recovery hook never fired because a saturated server still answers `SELECT 1` in well under 5s (`server not responding` appears 0 times in the whole log). Three-layer fix: (1) `framework.ErrExecTimeout`/`RationaleExecTimeout` — `ClusterRegressExecutor.ExecuteSQL` now honours the caller's context deadline (it previously ignored the `context.Context` argument outright) and returns the partial output wrapped in a timeout error, which `RunRegressSubset` short-circuits *before* the diff; (2) a `clusterPoisoned` flag in the suite restarts the cluster after any timeout so the next case cannot inherit the orphan; (3) `summarize.py` collapses all timeout cases into a single `regress/suite-wedge` item naming the longest unbroken run and pointing the repro at its first case, with policy-excluded cases dropped from the contiguity scan. Replayed against the real nightly log: **26 action items → 17**; replayed against the unmodified log the classifier change is inert (26 items, 0 wedge items). The wedge's own root cause — orphaned backend vs. GOMEMLIMIT saturation — remains open (ledger row 2026-07-28); this change makes it report as one wedge instead of N phantom regressions. |
| root-0030 | [`lockRowsOp` kept drain state across a rescan — `EXISTS (… FOR UPDATE)` went FALSE on an EvalPlanQual recheck](root-0030-lockrows-rescan-state.md) | accepted | Closes nightly item AI-20260725-011243-004 (`TestPort_IsolationEvalPlanQual`, deterministic at HEAD). `lockRowsOp` buffers its whole result at first `Next` (`drainAndStamp` → `drained=true`, rows served from `pending[pos++]`), and its `Open` doubles as the operator's `ExecReScan` entry point — `classifySubPlan` maps any plan containing `LockRows` to `rescanCloseOpen` so row locks re-stamp per outer row. But `Close` cleared only `pending`, leaving `drained=true` and `pos` past the end, so the **second** `Open` produced an operator that answers `Next` with EOF without ever re-scanning. In eval-plan-qual's `wnested2` permutation the UPDATE's WHERE holds a correlated `EXISTS (… FOR UPDATE)`; on the EvalPlanQual recheck after the concurrent commit the sublink returned zero rows with zero `noisy_oper()` NOTICEs, `EXISTS` collapsed to FALSE, and `updateOp` dropped the row — a silently lost update (`checking` stayed `400` where PG has `-800`), not merely a missing NOTICE. Fix: reset `pending`/`pos`/`drained` at the top of `Open`, matching upstream `nodeLockRows.c`, which keeps no such buffer (`ExecLockRows` pulls one row at a time and `ExecReScan` resets the subtree). `drained` is unique to `lockRowsOp`, so there is no sibling path to change with it. Gates: the spec now passes (27.6 s), plus units, `./internal/executor/`, 21 row-lock + 14 FK/MERGE isolation specs, and `tpch-spotcheck.sh` (Q12=2, Q13=35). |
| root-0031 | [Table inheritance did not survive a restart (`pg_inherits` persistence)](root-0031-pg-inherits-restart-persistence.md) | accepted | Closes the surviving M-NIGHTLY `regress/errors` divergence left by root-0029. The prior triage read the failure as suite-ordering state leakage ("a case mutates the shared `test_setup` fixtures"), but bisecting the alphabetical prefix never converged — the same range failed once and passed three times. The variable is not which cases ran first, it is **whether the cluster restarted**: root-0029's `clusterPoisoned` recovery restarts after any 120 s timeout (frequent under nightly co-load, never in an isolated repro), and `pg_inherits` was a purely VIRTUAL catalog synthesized from `Table.InheritsParentOIDs` / `InMemory.inheritanceChildren`, written only by `CREATE TABLE … INHERITS` and reloaded by nothing. A restart therefore dropped every parent→child edge: `pg_inherits` went empty, `SELECT * FROM parent` stopped seeing child rows, and `renameatt`'s child name-collision recursion checked nothing — so `ALTER TABLE emp RENAME COLUMN salary TO manager` **succeeded**, leaving `emp` with two `manager` columns. Fix mirrors B5 Slice B's `pg_attrdef` treatment: `writeInheritsRow` appends canonical PG18 tuples to `base/<dbOid>/2611` from the `syncTableToCatalogHeap` funnel (1-based `inhseqno` preserves the `INHERITS (…)` order `pg_dump` re-emits), `deleteCatalogRowsForOID` stamps `xmax` on them, and a new standalone `loadInheritanceFromHeap` pass in `open.go` restores both the child's ordered parents and the parent→children registry. Three PG-fidelity bugs the restart had been masking are fixed with it: `RenameTable` reported the schema-qualified key (`relation "public.stud_emp" already exists`) where PG uses the bare name; `RENAME COLUMN` never checked the target relation's OWN columns (PG's `check_for_column_name_collision`, after the child recursion); and `DROP AGGREGATE newcnt (nonesuch)` silently succeeded because the name-keyed registry lookup preceded argument-type resolution — fixing which exposed a second bug it had been cancelling (`DROP AGGREGATE newcnt (float4)` dropped a `newcnt("any")`). Verified by a new non-vacuous `TestPort_InheritanceSurvivesRestart` (negative control: fails with the reload disabled) and by reproducing the nightly failure with a 63-case alphabetical **prefix** of the regress suite in ~3.5 min instead of the ~1 h full run: 8 divergent lines → PASS, in a run that took the restart path. |
