| 0003-0006 | [Date / Interval Arithmetic (M0003)](0003-0006-date-interval-arithmetic.md) | draft | `date 'YYYY-MM-DD'` / `timestamp 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'` typed-string-literal sugar (parser.TypedStringLit) and `interval 'N' unit` (parser.IntervalLit, units day/month/year). New Datum KindInterval with months+days fields. evalBinary handles `time ± interval` via Go's time.AddDate (upstream-aligned month overflow). EXTRACT(field FROM ts) added with year/month/day/hour/minute/second/dow/doy/quarter/epoch fields. Required for TPC-H Q1/Q4/Q5/Q6/Q7/Q8/Q9/Q12/Q14/Q15/Q20. **Follow-up (2026-07-06, M0122-0004):** `compareDatum` gained a `KindInterval` case (`<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=`/`ORDER BY`/`MIN`/`MAX` over intervals previously raised `42883`), mirroring upstream's `interval_cmp_value` 30-day-month linearization. **Follow-up (2026-07-06, M0122-0004, later loop):** `Datum.Format()`'s `KindInterval` case now renders upstream's actual `interval_out` shape (`"1 year 2 mons 3 days"`, `"-1 mons"`, `"00:00:00"` for zero) instead of the placeholder `"%d months %d days"`. **Follow-up (2026-07-06, M0122-0004, yet later loop):** `evalCast` gained an `"interval"` case so `'<n> <unit>'::interval`/`CAST('<n> <unit>' AS interval)` now parse into a real `KindInterval` (previously silently passed the string through unchanged); accepts the same day/month/year grammar as the `INTERVAL '<n> <unit>'` typed literal, raising `22007` for anything else (sub-day/multi-component strings remain a documented v0 scope limit). **Follow-up (2026-07-07, M0097-0004):** `justify_hours`/`justify_days`/`justify_interval` implemented for real (previously stubs returning the input unchanged) — `justify_days`/`justify_interval` normalize whole 30-day chunks of the day field into the month field via a new `justifyIntervalDays` helper, mirroring upstream's `interval_justify_days`/`interval_justify_interval`; `justify_hours` stays the identity since goopg's v0 interval has no time field for it to act on (matches upstream exactly, not an approximation). **Follow-up (2026-07-08, M0122-0018):** `evalIsFinite` now propagates a NULL argument to a NULL result (previously returned `FALSE`, since `isfinite` is a strict function per `pg_proc_seed_data.go` — no `NotStrict` marker on any of its 4 wired OIDs) — the non-NULL case is unchanged (always `TRUE`, since goopg v0 stores no infinity values). **Follow-up (2026-07-11):** `timestamp − timestamp → interval` now works — `evalBinary` gained a `KindTime − KindTime` branch (`subTimeTime`, microsecond delta justified into 24h days à la `timestamp_mi`+`interval_justify_hours`) plus `interval ± interval` (`addIntervalInterval`); the `KindInterval` carrier packs sub-day microseconds in the reserved `Datum.Hi` word (`IntervalMicrosValue`/`NewIntervalDatumFull`) and `formatInterval` was rewritten to render the `[-|+]HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]` time component mirroring `EncodeInterval` INTSTYLE_POSTGRES (**verified byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3**). Analyzer types temporal subtraction / `interval±interval` as `interval` (were `42725`/`42804`). Deferred: sub-day interval *literals* (parser) and `date−date→integer`. Tests: `interval_subday_test.go`. **Follow-up (2026-07-11, unimplemented_feat #5+#5(b), successive loops):** sub-day interval *literals* now parse (`interval '2 hours'`, Form-1/Form-2/cast), then fractional magnitudes (`interval '1.5 hours'`=01:30:00) + Form-1 SQL-typmod truncation (`interval '1.5' hour`=01:00:00), then **multi-field / HH:MM:SS bodies** (`interval '1 day 05:00:00'`, `interval '1 year 2 mons 3 days 04:05:06.789'`, bare `interval '05:00:00'`) — goopg can now re-parse its own `intervalout`. The interval-body math was hoisted into `internal/parser/interval.go` (`ParseIntervalMagnitude`/`IntervalUnitToParts`/`ParseIntervalBody`) as a *single tokenizer* shared by the typed-literal path (`evalIntervalLit`) and the `::interval`/CAST path (`parseIntervalCastString`, now a one-line delegate) so the sibling paths cannot diverge; `IntervalLit` carries pre-computed `PreMonths/PreDays/PreMicros`. Each field carries its own sign; abbreviations `mon(s)`/`min(s)`/`sec(s)`/`hr(s)` accepted. Still deferred: bare-number default-unit (`interval '5'`), week/decade/century, single-letter units. Byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3. Tests: `TestMultiFieldIntervalLiterals`, `TestParseIntervalBodySingleFieldMatchesUnitToParts`. **Follow-up (2026-07-11, unimplemented_feat #5(c)/(d-i)/year-month, successive loops):** coarse units week/decade/century/millennium/microsecond + abbreviations (`canonicalIntervalUnit`+`IntervalUnitToParts`); bare-number default-unit → seconds (`interval '5'`=00:00:05, accepted only as a single trailing field with the SECOND slot free, reproducing PG's `tmask&fmask` collision so `interval '1 2 days'`/`'5 5'` error); and the **SQL year-month hyphen field** (`interval '1-2'`=1 year 2 mons via new `parser.parseYearMonthField` → `years*12 ± months`, PG `DecodeInterval` DTK_NUMBER hyphen branch; month part bounded `0≤m<12` so `1-12`/`1--2`/`1-2-3` error; composes with trailing bare-seconds `1-2 3`=1yr2mon00:00:03). Still deferred: single-letter units (positional `m`), full typmod grammar (`HOUR TO MINUTE`/`SECOND(p)`), and PG field-mask collision cases goopg doesn't model (`1-2 3 mons`, `1 mon 2 mons`). Tests: `TestWeekDecadeCenturyIntervals`, `TestTrailingBareNumberDefaultsToSeconds`, `TestYearMonthHyphenIntervals`. **Follow-up (2026-07-11, unimplemented_feat #5(d-ii)):** single-letter interval unit forms `y/c/w/d/h/m/s` (seven `deltatktbl` keys added to `canonicalIntervalUnit`); the earlier "positional `m`" note was a misconception — `DecodeInterval` decodes units via `DecodeUnits`→`deltatktbl` where `m`=MINUTE unconditionally, so `interval '1 m'`=00:01:00 and `interval '1 y 2 m'`=1 year 00:02:00 (not months). `quarter`/`qtr`/`tz`/`timezone` are in `deltatktbl` but have no case in `DecodeInterval`'s per-unit switch → PG raises 22007, so goopg rejects them too. Still deferred: full typmod grammar (`HOUR TO MINUTE`/`SECOND(p)`), field-mask collision cases (`1-2 3 mons`), glued `1m` tokenizer forms. Tests: `TestWeekDecadeCenturyIntervals` (accepts) + `TestIntervalCastFromStringInvalidSyntax` (rejects). **Follow-up (2026-07-11, #5(d-iii)/(d-iii-rest), successive loops):** glued `<magnitude><unit>` forms + field-mask collisions (`interval '2h30m'`/`'1.5h'`/`'1y2mon3d'`, `expandIntervalFields`/`splitAlphaNumRuns` reproducing PG `ParseDateTime`'s digit↔letter split incl. the `datetktbl` gobble rule; `TestGluedIntervalLiterals`); then **ISO 8601 duration bodies** (`interval 'P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S'`/`'PT1H30M'`/`'P1.5D'`, alternative extended `'P0002-06-07T01:30:00'` + basic packed `'P00020607T013000'`, via a new `decodeISO8601Interval` fallback tried only when the free-form decoder fails — line-ported from `DecodeISO8601Interval`; `TestISO8601IntervalLiterals`); then the **year-month tokenizer quirks** `interval '1-'`=1 year (empty month tail = bare year) and `interval '1-2.5'`=1 year 2 mons 00:00:00.5 (new `splitYearMonthFraction` peels a `.`-led fractional run off an *unsigned* `<digits>-<digits?>` field, reproducing PG's `ParseDateTime` `DTK_DATE`+`DTK_NUMBER` split; a *signed* field stays whole → PG's `DTK_TZ` reject path, so `-1-2.5` errors; `TestYearMonthHyphenIntervals` +22 accepts/8 rejects). Still deferred: full typmod grammar (`HOUR TO MINUTE`/`SECOND(p)`), interval `±infinity`, and a bare unit-word glued to a year-month (`1-2h`). Byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3. **Follow-up (2026-07-11, #5(d-iii-rest), successive loops):** the glued/spaced year-month & time-field unit-word *absorption* (`interval '1-2h'`/`'1-2 h'`/`'12:00h'` → the unit is a no-op via a `prevAbsorbs` flag in `decodeIntervalFields` + a trailing-letter split in `splitYearMonthTrailer`/`expandIntervalFields`), then the **SIGNED** year-month glued form (`interval '-1-2h'` → -1 years -2 mons, `'+1-2h'`, `'-1-2mon3d'`, `'-1-h'` → -1 years) via a new `splitSignedTZTrailer` reproducing PG's DTK_TZ lexer (collects `digit|:|.|-`, stops at a letter, sign flows into both year and month). Still deferred: `+`-separated continuation (`-1-2+3`), typmod grammar, `±infinity`. Tests: `TestYearMonthTimeGluedUnitAbsorb`. **Follow-up (2026-07-11, #5(d-iii-rest), later loop):** the `+`-separated continuation now parses (`interval '-1-2+3'` → -1 years -2 mons +00:00:03; `'1-2+3d'`, `'-1-2+3:30'`, `'3h+2'`) — the field expander is re-entrant (`expandIntervalField`; `splitYearMonthTrailer`/`splitSignedTZTrailer`/`splitAlphaNumRuns` all stop at `+` and recurse, PG's "a sign always starts a fresh field" rule), plus two sign-lexer fidelity fixes: a sign must be followed by a digit (`+.5`/`-.5` now error as in PG) and whitespace soaks between a lone sign and its digits (`interval '- 3'` → -00:00:03, Form-1 `interval '- 3' day` → -3 days). Still deferred: typmod grammar incl. its range defaults (`interval '-1-2+3' day`), `±infinity`. Tests: `TestYearMonthTimeGluedUnitAbsorb` (79 accepts + 41 rejects vs live PG 18.3). **Follow-up (2026-07-11, #5(d-iv)):** the Form-1 interval typmod **range & precision grammar** — `interval '<mag>' <hi> TO <lo>` (`interval '5' hour to minute`=00:05:00, `'5' day to hour`=05:00:00, `'5' year to month`=5 mons) and `SECOND(p)` (`interval '1.23456789' second(2)`=00:00:01.23, round-half-away-from-zero). PG's `DecodeInterval` `switch(range)` + `AdjustIntervalForTypmod` both collapse a range to its LOW field (interpret+truncate there, higher fields kept), so `intervalRangeLowField` (validates the 7 legal pairs; invalid→syntax error) reuses the single-field `Qualified` path; `roundIntervalMicrosToPrec` line-ports the precision arm. Fixed a fidelity bug in passing: PLURAL/abbrev trailing words (`days`,`min`,`millisecond`) are NOT typmod keywords — PG parses `interval '5' days` as bare `interval '5'` (00:00:05) + column alias `days`; the singular-only rewrite (`tryIntervalTypmodQualifier`) makes them fall through to aliases (TPC-H uses only singular, unaffected). Deferred: complex body under a range (needs `range` threaded into `ParseIntervalBody`), `±infinity`, cast-form typmod. Tests: `TestIntervalTypmodRangeAndPrecision` + updated `TestParseIntervalLiteral`. **Follow-up (2026-07-11, #5(d-iv), later loop):** the **trailing-bare-number half of complex-body-under-range** now decodes — a multi-field Form-1 body whose final field is unitless resolves that number via the range's low field (`interval '1 day 5' hour to minute`=1 day 00:05:00, `'2 hour 5' hour to minute`=02:05:00, `'1 day 1.5' hour to minute`=1 day 00:01:00, `'-1 day 5' hour to minute`=-1 days +00:05:00). New `parser.ParseIntervalBodyWithDefault(body, defaultUnit)` threads PG's `DecodeInterval switch(range)` default field (= the range low field) into `decodeIntervalFields`'s trailing-unitless branch; `ParseIntervalBody` delegates with `"second"` so the `::interval`/CAST + Form-2 full-range siblings stay byte-identical. `evalIntervalLit` routes a Qualified non-magnitude body through it, then the existing `truncIntervalToUnit`/`roundIntervalMicrosToPrec` range truncation runs unchanged (matches `AdjustIntervalForTypmod`, which keeps higher-order day/month fields). Still deferred: a bare number to the **left** of a time/year-month word (`interval '1 2:03:04' day to second`=1 day 02:03:04; PG's right-to-left leftward carry, pre-exists at full range too), `±infinity`, cast-form typmod. Tests: `TestIntervalTypmodRangeAndPrecision` (+11 accepts, +1 deferred reject) vs live PG 18.3. **Follow-up (2026-07-11, #5(d-iv), later loops):** interval `±infinity` literals + arithmetic/ordering (`interval 'infinity'`, `interval_pl`/`interval_mi` sign pass-through, `infinity−infinity`→`interval out of range`), then **`EXTRACT(field FROM interval)` / `date_part`** — `evalExtractInterval` line-ports `interval_part_common` (no justification, integer fields→int8, second/ms/epoch→numeric, quarter from `interval->month`, ±infinity sentinels→±Infinity/NULL per `NonFiniteIntervalPart`); sibling `date_part('field', interval)` shares the helper. Deferred: `timestamp ± interval 'infinity'`, unary `- interval 'infinity'`, cast-form typmod, EXTRACT numeric-scale gap. Tests: `TestIntervalInfinityLiterals`/`TestIntervalInfinityArithmetic`/`TestExtractFromInterval` vs live PG 18.3. |

| 0003-0016 | [Join-Order Reordering (M0003)](0003-0016-join-order-reordering.md) | accepted | Cost-based pre-pass that permutes the comma-FROM list so small-cardinality tables join first when ANALYZE has supplied row counts. Greedy nearest-neighbour by cardinality with equality-edge preference, executed at parser-AST level so no resolved ColumnRef.Index needs remapping. Skips when stats missing, when an explicit JOIN clause is present, or when the result is the source order. | 0005-0001 | [Streaming Replication Architecture (M0005)](0005-0001-streaming-replication-architecture.md) | accepted | Process model (primary walsender(s) + standby walreceiver), wire-protocol surface (replication-mode startup, IDENTIFY_SYSTEM / CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT / START_REPLICATION SQL commands, MsgCopyBoth + WAL-data/keepalive/standby-status inner framing wire-compatible with upstream PG 18.3), state-transition diagram, replication-slot retention semantics, GUC surface, promotion path via control-socket PROMOTE, and the explicit hook list for each follow-up loop's implementation seam (protocol/server/control/wal/catalog touchpoints with file:line refs). **Follow-up (2026-07-08):** `parsePrimaryConninfoFull` now parses `sslmode` (in addition to host/port/application_name/user); `DialWalReceiver`'s new `checkSSLMode` accepts `disable`/`allow`/`prefer`/unset (goopg has no TLS, so these all connect in plaintext) and rejects `require`/`verify-ca`/`verify-full` before dialing instead of silently downgrading an operator's explicit encryption request. `password` remains unparsed/unconsumed — the replication handshake never reads an auth challenge (v0 is trust-only), so there's nowhere for it to go yet. |
| 0005-0002 | [Standby Recovery and Replay (M0005)](0005-0002-standby-recovery-and-replay.md) | accepted | Continuous standby-side WAL replay. Refactors `wal.ReplayRecords` into a per-record `wal.ApplyRecord` kernel and adds a streaming `wal.StreamReplayer` driven by a `wal.RecordIterator`, applying each record as it lands via the writer's flush-event subscription. | 0007-0001 | [WAL Segment Preallocation (M0007)](0007-0001-wal-segment-preallocation.md) | accepted | `wal.Config.Preallocate` (driven by the new `wal_init_zero` GUC, default `on`) zero-fills new segments to `SegmentSize` and fsyncs them at creation time, plus the parent directory, so subsequent commit-path syncs don't pay for inode metadata or filesystem allocations on the hot path. The encoded zero header (`len=0 && crc=0`) is reserved as the EOS sentinel: `Writer.Append` rejects empty payloads (`ErrEmptyPayload`); `decodeRecord` callers stop on `isZeroHeader`. `detectWritePos` now scans the last segment record-by-record (via `scanLastSegmentEnd`) so it works for both legacy short-tail segments and full-size preallocated tails. `cmd/goopg start` threads the GUC through `initdb.Open(OpenOptions{WALInitZero})`. `fdatasync` switch (0007-0002) and `wal_recycle` land separately. **Follow-up (2026-07-08):** preallocation counters landed — `walBufferCounters` gains `segmentsPreallocated`/`preallocatedBytes` (per-P sharded `stats.Counter`, bumped once in `state.openSegment`'s `wasNew` branch), exposed via `Writer.SegmentsPreallocated()`/`PreallocatedBytes()` and two new `pg_stat_wal_io` columns (`wal_segments_preallocated_total`, `wal_init_zero_bytes_total`). **Follow-up (2026-07-09):** eager next-segment lookahead landed (M0122-0007) — `openSegment(segNo)` now kicks off a background `eagerPreallocSegment(segNo+1)` (temp-file + `os.Link`-no-clobber, mirroring upstream `XLogFileInit`) so a real rollover usually finds the next segment already zero-filled instead of paying for it synchronously; `state.eagerWG`/`close()` ensure no goroutine outlives the writer. The adapter (`aioEngineAdapter` + `aioFileAdapter` + `aioHandleAdapter`) lives in `internal/initdb/open.go` to keep storage free of the aio import; `WriteAt` on the file adapter panics because PrefetchBlock is read-only. `Runtime.Close()` closes the engine AFTER the storage manager so in-flight prefetches drain cleanly. `cmd/goopg start` reads the `io_method` / `io_workers` / `io_max_concurrency` GUCs via new `stringGUC` / `intGUC` helpers; `io_uring` is silently downgraded to `worker` with a warn-level log line (`event=aio_method_fallback`) until the io_uring runtime probe lands. Heap-scan caller integration also lands in this same doc: `Pool.SetPrefetchEnabled(bool)` + `Pool.Prefetch(tag)` (warms the kernel page cache via Manager.PrefetchBlock, drops the AIO handle, atomic-load fast-path when disabled), and `seqScanOp.refillPrefetchWindow` keeps `seqScanLookahead=4` blocks ahead of curBlock prefetched. Tests: TestPrefetchBlockSyncFallback (no engine — pre-completed handle yields read bytes), TestPrefetchBlockUsesAttachedEngine (recording engine sees the right offset; bytes round-trip), TestPrefetchBlockOutOfRange (past-EOF surfaces ErrShortRead via Wait, matches ReadBlock), TestOpenAttachesAIOEngineWhenMethodSet (Runtime.AIO non-nil after AIOMethod="sync"), TestOpenLeavesAIONilWithoutMethod (no AIOMethod → no engine, existing synchronous paths unchanged), TestPoolPrefetchDisabledIsNoOp, TestPoolPrefetchEnabledFiresThroughEngine, TestSeqScanFiresPrefetchesAcrossBlocks (600-row scan; recording engine sees `[1, nBlocks]` submits). Bitmap-heap-scan / direct read-stream-driven seqScan + checkpointer + WAL writer caller integrations remain follow-up slices. |

EOF is excluded from `errored` per the engine's "EOF is expected" semantics. **Per-I/O (`pg_aios`):** layered on per-handle tracking added to `aio.Engine` in the same slice. Engine gained `nextID` (atomic.Uint64), `inflight map[uint64]inFlightEntry` guarded by `inflightMu sync.RWMutex` (acquired only on Submit/completion — never on the hot path), and Handle gained `id` + `submittedAt`. New `Engine.finishHandle(h, r)` replaces the previous `completionBookkeeping(r)` — combines counter bumps, inflight-map removal, and `Handle.finish(r)` in one call. `Engine.InFlight() []InFlightInfo` returns a sorted copy (sort key: ID, monotonic by submission order). | 0009-0006 | [AIO io_uring method (M0009)](0009-0006-aio-io-uring.md) | accepted | Linux-only `io_uring` AIO method matching upstream `pgaio_uring.c`. `internal/aio/method_iouring_linux.go` talks to the kernel directly via syscall 425 (`io_uring_setup`) + 426 (`io_uring_enter`) — no third-party wrapper. `newMethodIOUring` runs the probe inline: any errno returns the sentinel `errProbeFailed`, which `NewEngine` matches via `errors.Is` and uses to silently fall back to `MethodWorker` (matches upstream's behaviour when the kernel can't honour `io_uring`: ENOSYS, sysctl `io_uring_disabled=1` EPERM, EINVAL on too-old kernels, ENOMEM under locked-memory limits). The non-Linux stub (`method_iouring_other.go`) returns the same sentinel on every other GOOS. Submission model: SQ/CQ rings + SQE array are mmap'd from the byte offsets the kernel returned (3× `mmap MAP_SHARED\|MAP_POPULATE`); SQE/CQE Go structs (`ioSqe` 64 B, `ioCqe` 16 B) mirror the kernel UAPI byte-for-byte. `Submit` serialises SQE writes under `submitMu` (io_uring's SQ is single-producer), release-stores the new tail, calls `io_uring_enter(submit=1)`. A dedicated reaper goroutine blocks in `io_uring_enter(0, min_complete=1, GETEVENTS)` and drains CQEs into the per-handle map (`pending[userData]`); idle ring costs one parked goroutine, no busy spin. `Close` wakes the reaper out of GETEVENTS by submitting an `IORING_OP_NOP` SQE with sentinel user_data `0xFFFF...FFFF` — closing the ring fd alone doesn't reliably unblock the syscall on every kernel. Slot semaphore caps in-flight at `min(MaxConcurrency, sqEntries)`; `MaxConcurrency=0` defaults to `sqEntries=32`. `Engine.FallbackFrom() (requested, reason)` reports any io_uring → worker fallback; `cmd/goopg start` logs `event=aio_method_fallback requested=io_uring actual=worker reason=...` post-Open so an operator triaging "but I asked for io_uring" can grep for it. Fd exposure: optional unexported interface `fdHaver { Fd() uintptr }`; `*os.File` satisfies it, and `storage.relFile` / `initdb.aioFileAdapter` / `initdb.walAIOFileAdapter` add forwarding methods so storage and WAL caller chains preserve fd visibility. In-memory test files don't satisfy `fdHaver` and Submit runs the I/O inline via `runOp` (correct, just no kernel acceleration). Tests: `TestNewEngineIOUringConstructs` (cross-platform — io_uring always constructs, FallbackFrom reports correctly), `TestEngineIOUringReadWriteRoundTrip` (Linux-only — pwrite-then-pread round-trips bytes through the kernel ring; per-direction counters bump; in-flight gauge returns to zero), `TestEngineIOUringParallel` (Linux-only — 64 concurrent writes + 64 reads verify no slot collisions in the userData→Handle map). Both Linux-only tests `t.Skip` when the engine fell back so the suite passes on any Linux host regardless of `io_uring_disabled` / seccomp. Registered files, SQPOLL, linked ops, fixed buffers, and io_uring-specific latency histograms remain follow-up slices. **2026-07-08 fixes**: the raw-fd path bypassed `File.WriteAt`/`ReadAt` entirely, silently skipping `storage.relFile`'s checksum stamp/verify on a checksummed cluster — fixed via optional `aio.ChecksumFile{PrepareWrite,VerifyRead}`, which `Submit`/`completeOne` now call when `op.File` implements it (`TestEngineIOUringChecksumFileHooks`, `TestChecksumRelFilePrepareWriteVerifyRead`). The related but separate per-(rel,block) same-tag ordering gap (`storage/aio-relfile-mu-bypass`) is also now fixed: `relFile.lockBlock` (`internal/storage/smgr.go`) is a per-block in-flight registry that `readBlock`/`writeBlock`/`PrefetchBlock`/`WriteBlockAIO` all consult, released via a new `AIOSubmitOp.OnComplete` hook wired to `aio.Op.Callback` (fires at real I/O completion, independent of `Wait` timing) — see the design doc's updated section and `TestBlockLatchSerializesAIOAgainstSync`. |
| 0010-0001 | [WAL direct-I/O write path (M0010)](0010-0001-wal-direct-io-write-path.md) | accepted | Linux O_DIRECT WAL writes for the primary writer + walreceiver, gated by a new `wal_direct_io` GUC (`TypeBool`, default `off`, `ContextPostmaster`). **Phase 1 (probe + plumbing)**: `wal.Config.DirectIO` plumbing, `probeDirectIO(walDir)` runs once at construction when DirectIO=true (opens `<walDir>/.wal_direct_io_probe` with `O_RDWR\|O_CREAT\|O_DIRECT`, observes EINVAL / EOPNOTSUPP, removes the sentinel; success returns empty reason, EINVAL/EOPNOTSUPP returns a human-readable fallback reason). `Writer.DirectIORequested()` / `Writer.DirectIOFallbackReason()` are stable for the writer's lifetime. `cmd/goopg start` logs `event=wal_direct_io_active` (probe ok) or `event=wal_direct_io_fallback reason=...` (probe rejected) — mirrors M0009 `event=aio_*` shape. **Phase 2 (alignment-safe writes)**: `state.directIOActive = directIORequested && fallback==""`. `enableDirectIO(f)` uses `fcntl(F_SETFL, flags\|unix.O_DIRECT)` to flip the flag on the live fd AFTER preallocation finishes (preallocation's 64-KiB heap-buffer zero-fill can't satisfy O_DIRECT alignment, so the flip is post-preallocation). `state.writeAt` dispatches to `state.writeAtDirectIO`: per-write RMW (pread aligned region into per-state mmap'd scratch → overlay user bytes → pwrite full aligned region back). `directIOScratchCap=1 MiB`; outsized writes loop through the scratch. Aligned scratch lazy-allocated via `unix.Mmap(MAP_PRIVATE\|MAP_ANONYMOUS)` (mirrors `internal/storage/arena.go`); freed in `state.close`. Block size hard-coded at 4 KiB (every modern Linux DIO-capable FS satisfies this; STATX_DIOALIGN-driven detection deferred). AIO+DirectIO bypasses the engine and uses synchronous RMW — engine-side aligned-copy is a perf-only follow-up (`Phase 2.b` in the design doc). Walreceiver's WAL-persist path inherits via the shared writer fd (`wal.Writer.Append` → `state.writeAt` → the same O_DIRECT-aware code path; no separate code path). On non-Linux GOOS the probe always falls back so directIOActive=false; the buffered legacy path runs unchanged. Tests: TestDirectIODisabledByDefault, TestDirectIOEnabledProbesFilesystem, TestDirectIOFallbackReasonStable (Phase 1); TestDirectIORoundTripWithPreallocation (three appends + flush + ReadAll round-trip via RMW; SegmentSize=4 KiB), TestDirectIORecordSpanningBlocks (12 KiB payload across ~3 block boundaries — every byte round-trips). Phase 2 tests `t.Skip` on probe fallback. Crash-restart correctness rides on the existing `TestPreallocatedSegmentRecoversCleanly` (the byte stream is identical under O_DIRECT vs buffered, so the M0007-0001 EOS-sentinel decoder sees no difference). The walsender in-memory WAL handoff (M0010-0002) and `pg_stat_wal_io` observability surface (M0010-0003) remain follow-up slices. |
| 0010-0002 | [Walsender in-memory WAL handoff (M0010)](0010-0002-walsender-in-memory-wal-handoff.md) | accepted | Bounded in-memory WAL byte ring backing walsender's `RecordIterator` so streaming replication doesn't depend on OS page-cache residency — pairs with M0010-0001's `wal_direct_io=on` (writes bypass the cache, so the ring is the cache replacement for sender reads). New `wal_sender_memory_buffer` GUC (`TypeInt`, default 16 MiB / 16777216, range `[0, 1 GiB]`, `ContextPostmaster`); 0 disables the ring. New `wal.MemRing`: fixed-size `[]byte` ring keyed by 0-based LSN-byte position. `Append(pos, data)` mirrors writer bytes (called from `state.append` AFTER `state.writeAt` succeeds — a failed pwrite must not appear in the ring). `ReadAt(pos, out)` returns `(n, true)` on full hit, `(0, false)` on miss (no partial-overlap stitching — caller fetches the whole range from disk in one go). Single `sync.RWMutex`: writers Lock during memcpy + head/tail advance, readers RLock during their own memcpy so a concurrent eviction can't free bytes mid-read. `hits` / `misses` are atomic counters bumped per `ReadAt`; observable via `MemRing.Hits()` / `Misses()` (M0010-0003's `pg_stat_replication.send_buffer_*` surface reads these). Eviction is FIFO: when `tail - head > cap`, head advances to `tail - cap`. Reset path handles post-recovery first-Append at non-zero `writePos`; oversized Appends keep only the trailing `cap` bytes. Iterator integration: `RecordIterator.readBytesAt` consults `it.writer.MemRing().ReadAt(pos, out)` first; on hit returns from RAM (zero syscalls), on miss falls through to the legacy per-segment pread loop. `cmd/goopg start` reads the GUC into `OpenOptions.WALSenderMemoryBuffer` → `wal.Config.SenderMemoryBuffer`; logs `event=wal_sender_memory_buffer_attached capacity_bytes=N` at startup when configured. Lagging senders that fall outside the retention window cleanly miss and resume from disk without dropping the connection — protocol semantics unchanged. Tests: TestMemRingNilSafe (NewMemRing(0)=nil; every method nil-safe), TestMemRingRoundTripWithinCap, TestMemRingEvictsOldBytesOnOverflow, TestMemRingPartialOverlapMisses, TestMemRingWraps (cross buffer-boundary write), TestMemRingWriteLargerThanCap, TestMemRingConcurrentReads (4 readers vs 100 writes — pins the lock-during-memcpy invariant); TestIteratorReadsFromMemRing (ring on + segment file deleted post-Append → iterator still streams, proving RAM source; Hits()>0), TestIteratorFallsBackToDiskWithoutRing (ring off + segment intact → pread succeeds, legacy path unchanged). Walsender's `pg_stat_replication.send_buffer_*` counters surface (M0010-0003) and the AIO+ring composition remain follow-up slices. |

| 0011-0001 | [B-tree NUMERIC key ordering (M0011)](0011-0001-btree-numeric-key-ordering.md) | accepted | Sortable byte encoding for NUMERIC B-tree keys: `EncodeNumericKey(mantissa, scale) []byte` produces a scale-invariant byte string such that bytewise compare matches numeric order. Layout: `sign(1) \|\| biased exp(4 BE) \|\| normalized digits \|\| terminator(1)`. Sign byte (`0x00` neg, `0x01` zero, `0x02` pos) settles cross-sign cases; exponent is biased-uint big-endian (inverted for negatives so larger E sorts smaller); digits are stripped of trailing zeros and emitted as ASCII (inverted `9-d` for negatives); terminator is `0x00` (positives) / `0xFF` (negatives) so prefix-equal-but-shorter sorts on the correct side of the digit run. Zero is the single-byte sentinel `[0x01]`. Numerically-equal inputs (e.g. `(10,1)` and `(100,2)`, both `1.0`) produce identical bytes — required for UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY equality. `CompareKeys` switched to straight `bytes.Compare` (length-first compare was wrong for variable-length keys; int4 keys are all 4 bytes so the change is a no-op for the existing path). Decoding is intentionally not provided — index probes always re-encode from the live datum. Bound: encoding length ≤ 25 bytes (1 sign + 4 exp + ≤19 digits + 1 term). Tests: TestEncodeNumericKeyZeroIsSingleByte, TestEncodeNumericKeyScaleInvariance (1 == 1.0 == 1.00 == 1.000 etc.), TestEncodeNumericKeySignOrder (every neg < zero < every pos), TestEncodeNumericKeyMonotone (sort 23-element representative slice numerically, assert encoded slice sorts identically under CompareKeys), TestEncodeNumericKeySamePrefixDifferentLengths (terminator behaviour for 1.9 vs 1.99 and the negative mirror), TestEncodeNumericKeyMinInt64 (int64-min edge case via uint64 absolute-value path). DDL acceptance, backfill, and HammerDB TPC-H validation are M0011-0002 / M0011-0003 follow-ups. |

ON ... (col numeric)` no longer aborts with `btree v0 only supports int4 keys`. Four changes: (1) `BTPageOpaque.HighKey` becomes `[]byte` in memory and a 32-byte variable-length slot (`MaxHighKeyLen=32`, with a 2-byte length prefix at offset 14 replacing `_padding`) on disk; opaque area grows from 24 to 48 bytes; `btreeVersion` bumps from 2 to 3 (older btrees error with `ErrNotABTree` — pre-GA, no migration tooling). (2) Split path's `len(rightItems[0].key) != len(op.HighKey)` length-equality guard is replaced by a `MaxHighKeyLen` upper bound; the right page's first item just becomes the new HighKey verbatim. (3) `createSingleColumnBTreeIndex` accepts `numeric`/`decimal` via a new `isSupportedBTreeKeyType` predicate (still rejects everything else with `0A000`). `backfillSingleColumnBTree` switches the dedup map from `map[int32]struct{}` to `map[string]struct{}` keyed on the encoded byte form so `(10,1)` and `(100,2)` collapse into one UNIQUE entry. (4) `indexScanOp.lookupKey` calls the same helper, so probe keys land on the same bytes backfill produced. | 0012-0001 | [Lock manager architecture (M0012)](0012-0001-lock-manager-architecture.md) | accepted | PostgreSQL-style SQL lock manager core surface — relation-level lock tags, mode-compatibility matrix, holder/waiter tracking, Acquire/Release/ReleaseAll API. New `internal/lockmgr` package. Eight lock modes (`AccessShareLock` … `AccessExclusiveLock`) with numeric values matching upstream's `lockdefs.h` so log lines and future SQL views share the vocabulary. `conflictTab[1..8]` is a verbatim port of `LockConflicts[]` from `postgres/src/backend/storage/lmgr/lock.c` (lines 65-104), encoded as a `[9]Mask` with slot 0 unused so 1-based indexing matches. `LockTag{DB, Rel}` is the v0 tag granularity (forks intentionally collapsed — relation lock covers heap and indexes, matching upstream). Per-tag `lockState` carries `holders map[BackendID]Mask`, `waiters []*Waiter`, and a cached `granted` mask; lazy-allocated on first Acquire and GC'd to nil when both holders and waiters drain. `Acquire(ctx, b, t, m)` grants immediately when no conflict against `grantedExcept(b)` AND no waiters queued (the second check enforces strict head-of-line FIFO so a strong waiter doesn't starve behind a stream of compatible-with-current-holders newcomers); otherwise enqueues a `Waiter{b, m, signal}` with a buffered chan and parks on `<-signal`. Cancellation splices the waiter out under `lm.mu` and handles the rare race where Release promoted us between context cancel and lock acquisition (releases the just-granted bit, runs another wake-pass). `Release` runs the wake-pass head-first and stops at the first non-promotable waiter (FIFO). `ReleaseAll(b)` drops every mode held by backend `b` across every tag — the executor's commit/rollback hook. `ConflictsWith(m, held)` is exported so the M0012-0002 deadlock detector can ask the same question against the lock table. Single coarse `lm.mu sync.Mutex` — per-tag striping deferred. Self-conflict is impossible: `grantedExcept(b)` excludes the requester's own holdings so a backend can stack modes (e.g. `RowExclusive` + `AccessShare` for `INSERT … SELECT`). Race-clean (`go test -race`). The deadlock sub-case is subsumed by the `grantedExcept` conflict check. New tests: TestLockManagerEarlyGrantAheadOfWaiter, TestParseModeRoundTrip. | 0012-0002 | [Deadlock detection algorithm (M0012)](0012-0002-deadlock-detection-algorithm.md) | accepted | Wait-for graph + cycle detection + victim selection on top of M0012-0001's lock manager. New `internal/lockmgr/deadlock.go` (`runDeadlockCheck`, `CheckDeadlocksNow`, `findCycle`, `cancelVictimLocked`). Wait-for graph derivation: for every parked Waiter `w` on tag `t`, emit edge `w.Backend → h` for every holder `h` of any conflicting mode (`ConflictsWith(w.Mode, holders[h])`); self-edges excluded. Cycle detection: iterative three-colour DFS (white/grey/black); a grey-on-grey edge is a back-edge → cycle reconstructed via parent pointers. Victim selection: youngest backend in the cycle (max `BackendID`) — matches upstream's "cancel youngest xact" heuristic. Cancellation contract: `Waiter` grew a second `victim chan struct{}`; the detector splices the victim out of its parked queue under `lm.mu`, sends on `victim`, and runs the wake-pass so backends queued behind the victim get a chance to advance. The victim's `Acquire` selects on `signal` / `victim` / `ctx.Done()` and on `victim` returns `ErrDeadlockDetected` (sentinel exported for higher layers to translate to SQLSTATE `40P01`). The Acquire goroutine then calls `lm.ReleaseAll(b)` outside the mutex so survivor backends' wake-passes fire. Scheduling: every parked Acquire arms a `time.AfterFunc(deadlockTimeout, lm.runDeadlockCheck)` (default 1s, matches upstream's `deadlock_timeout` GUC; tunable per-manager via `SetDeadlockTimeout`). Concurrent timer fires serialise on `lm.mu` and the detector is idempotent. Tests: TestDeadlockDetectsTwoSessionCycle (classic A↔B), TestDeadlockYoungestBackendIsVictim (BackendID 5 vs 9 → 9 cancelled), TestDeadlockDetectsThreeSessionCycle (A→B→C→A multi-edge cycle, exactly 1 cancellation), TestDeadlockNoCycleNoCancel (linear wait chain → false-positive guard), TestDeadlockTimerSchedulesCheck (20ms timeout, no synchronous trigger — pins the AfterFunc wiring), TestDeadlockSurvivorMakesProgress (post-cancellation survivor's blocked Acquire returns nil). All race-clean. Out of scope: `lock_timeout` (separate from deadlock_timeout), predicate-deadlock / SSI, soft-cancel retry, cross-database locks. Executor integration (M0012-0003) maps `ErrDeadlockDetected` to a `*ExecError{Code:"40P01"}` and routes it back to the client. |

| 0021-0012 | [Tuple-lock FIFO wiring (row-lock waiter fairness) (M-NIGHTLY AI-20260712-020530-002)](0021-0012-tuple-lock-fifo-wiring.md) | landed (loop #91) | Fixes the flaky `TestPort_IsolationTuplelockUpgradeNoDeadlock` (perm `s1_share s2_for_update s3_for_update …`: `s3` completed before `s2`, `s2` timed out). Root cause (loop #90): `Context.LockMgr` is nil in the production server by design, so `acquireTupleLock`/`tryAcquireTupleLock` were TOTAL NO-OPS — including `lockRowsOp`'s FOR UPDATE ExclusiveLock — and all row-lock serialisation instead rode `mvcc.WaitForXID`'s single `commitCond.Broadcast()`, which wakes every waiter and lets Go scheduling (non-FIFO) pick the winner. Landed fix: `acquireTupleLock`/`tryAcquireTupleLock` (`internal/executor/context.go`) route to the always-on `tableLockMgr` under the per-statement `BackendID` when `c.LockMgr == nil`, but — refining the original design sketch — the tag is acquired **lazily**, only at the three "about to sleep" sites in `stampLockInner` plus the DML write-path's `waitForConflictingRowLock` (mirroring `heap_acquire_tuplock`'s placement immediately before `XactLockTableWait`/`MultiXactIdWait`), never up-front; a non-conflicting request never touches the tag, avoiding a reintroduced upgrade-deadlock. `tupleLockHwMode` ports PG's four-mode `tupleLockExtraInfo` hwlock matrix (`AccessShareLock`/`RowShareLock`/`ExclusiveLock`/`AccessExclusiveLock`) instead of the old two-mode collapse, so FOR KEY SHARE never wrongly queues behind an unrelated no-key UPDATE holder. `selfIsLockMember`/`selfRowLockMember` port `current_is_member` to skip the tag on an upgrade. `executor.ReleaseTupleLocks` releases per-statement holdings from `dispatch.go`'s Query-message defer. Validated: 20× strict standalone loop zero flakes; full isolation suite (121 specs) clean except three confirmed pre-existing unrelated failures; race-gate + `tpch-spotcheck.sh` (Q12=2/Q13=33) + pgbench CI-parity smoke all green. `postgres-oracle-target-inventory.csv` flipped `defer`→`pass`; test re-promoted to `runIsoSpecStrict`. |
| 0021-0011 | [Tuple-level locking step 4: multi-holder FOR SHARE via lockmgr modes (M0021 follow-up)](0021-0011-tuple-locking-for-share-multi-holder.md) | accepted (multi-holder FOR SHARE without MultiXact infrastructure; persistent xmax bookkeeping deferred) | Fixes the hidden bug where two concurrent SELECT FOR SHARE sessions on the same row serialised because lockRowsOp.stampLock acquired ExclusiveLock regardless of strength. Achieves upstream's "multiple FOR SHARE holders coexist" semantics WITHOUT introducing MultiXact infrastructure: the lockmgr's existing conflict matrix already supplies what we need — RowShareLock is compatible with itself and conflicts with ExclusiveLock. New `lockRowsOp.tupleLockMode()` picks RowShareLock for HeapXmaxShrLock / HeapXmaxKeyShrLock strengths; ExclusiveLock for HeapXmaxExclLock. Mapping table: FOR UPDATE → ExclusiveLock (single writer), FOR SHARE → RowShareLock (compatible with self), FOR KEY SHARE → RowShareLock, UPDATE/DELETE foreign-lock detection → ExclusiveLock (waits for all holders). Transaction-scoped ReleaseAll(backendID) via the existing dispatch.go hook cleans every holder up at commit/abort. On-page xmax bookkeeping note: with multiple holders, second session's stamp overwrites first's xmax bytes — harmless because (a) visibility short-circuits on HeapXmaxLockOnly without consulting xmax value, (b) lockmgr tracks each holder by backend ID independently, (c) WAL records each lock emission with its own (xid, lockStrength). The remaining gap (accurate post-crash reconstruction of holder set) is what MultiXact would solve; v0 defers because lockmgr is in-memory only so all locks are lost on crash anyway. New TestForShareCompatibleMultipleHolders runs two sessions concurrently taking FOR SHARE on the same row (second succeeds without blocking; verifies both backends appear in lm.Holders[tag]), then a third session UPDATE blocks waiting for both, and unblocks only after BOTH holders release — pins both the multi-holder property and the UPDATE-conflicts-with-shared-holders property. Full `go test ./...` green; race-mode targeted runs across executor + lockmgr all green. Lock-strength promotion (FOR SHARE → FOR UPDATE upgrade) + persistent MultiXact identifier in xmax + tuple-level NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED + streaming per-row stamping + pg_locks introspection all stay deferred. |
| 0021-0010 | [Tuple-level locking step 2d: UPDATE/DELETE via IndexScan path (M0021 follow-up)](0021-0010-tuple-locking-index-update-path.md) | accepted (planner emits IndexScan for UPDATE/DELETE WHERE indexed_col=key; executor handles both shapes; foreign-lock detection continues to fire) | Closes the seqScan-only restriction on the write side. planUpdate/planDelete now mirror planSelect's `planIndexScanFromWhere` arm — when `WHERE indexed_col = key` matches the single-column equality shape with a constant/param rhs, the planner picks IndexScan; otherwise falls through to Filter(SeqScan). `ctx.cat = cat` set on the singleBindingContext so subquery resolution inside the index key works. extractScanAndPredicate extended to accept *planner.IndexScan and *planner.Filter wrapping IndexScan. New `indexScanPredicate(ix)` synthesises a `<indexed_col> = key` equality predicate from the IndexScan node — lhs is a fresh ColumnRef pointing at the table's output ordinal for the indexed column; rhs is the IndexScan's already-resolved Key. For Filter(IndexScan) the outer predicate AND the synthesised key predicate combine. The runtime's scanMatching is inherently sequential — treating IndexScan as "SeqScan with a synthesised key predicate" is correct (the predicate filters the same tuples the index would have probed) but does not exploit the index for fast access; that's a follow-up optimisation. Crucially, scanMatching's per-tuple foreign-lock detection from step 2b is unchanged: every tuple the seq-scan visits (including those passing the synthesised `=` predicate) goes through lockedByForeign + acquireTupleLock. Index-driven UPDATE/DELETE optimisation (probe instead of seq-scan) + tuple-level NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED through UPDATE/DELETE + MultiXact + streaming stamping all stay deferred. |

| 0021-0008 | [Tuple-level locking step 2b: blocking enforcement (M0021 follow-up)](0021-0008-tuple-locking-blocking-enforcement.md) | accepted (UPDATE/DELETE block on foreign lock-only xmax via lockmgr tuple tags; NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED at tuple level deferred) | Closes the gap between steps 1/2a/3 (data on the page) and actual blocking. lockmgr.LockTag grew Block + Offset uint32 fields — both zero is the historic relation-level tag (every existing caller continues to work via Go's struct-literal zero-init), both non-zero is the new tuple-level tag. | 0021-0007 | [Tuple-level locking step 2a: producer wiring (M0021 follow-up)](0021-0007-tuple-locking-producer-wiring.md) | accepted (lockRowsOp stamps + emits WAL; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE conflict detection deferred) | The producer side of tuple-level locking. New `LogHeapLockFunc` + `Pool.LogHeapLock()` accessor + `PoolConfig.LogHeapLock` field mirroring the existing LogHeapInsert / LogHeapDelete pattern. `initdb.Open` wires a closure that calls `wal.EncodeHeapLock` + `walWriter.Append`. New `seqScanOp.currentTID()` returns the (rel, ItemPointer) of the most recently emitted row by reading curBlock + curSlot-1 (curSlot is incremented post-fetch). `findSeqScan(op)` walks past Project / Filter wrappers to surface the leaf seqScanOp; nil return (IndexScan, Values, CTEScan) falls through to pass-through Next with only relation-level lock applied. `lockRowsOp` switched to a two-pass drain-then-stamp protocol — necessary because seqScanOp holds the page's RLock continuously across Next() calls (RUnlock fires only at page exhaustion / Close), so the slot's write Lock() for xmax stamping would deadlock against the scan's reader. First Next() drains the entire child chain capturing (rel, ItemPointer, row) per row inline (after child.Next() returns and before the next child.Next() so curSlot is authoritative), then runs the stamp pass after EOF (when seqScan has released all page RLocks): pin page, write-Lock, PageSetHeapTupleLockOnly, MarkDirtyChangeRecord(LogHeapLock), unlock, unpin. Subsequent Next() calls yield from buffer. Lock-strength selection: `o.plan.Locks[0].Strength` → ExclLock for FOR UPDATE, ShrLock for FOR SHARE; multi-clause merge under strongest-wins deferred. Full `go test ./...` green. | 0017-0003 | [UPSERT executor: conflict detection + DO UPDATE apply (M0017)](0017-0003-upsert-executor-concurrency-and-locking.md) | accepted (Stage A executor slice) | Runtime for `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (cols) DO {NOTHING \| UPDATE SET ... [WHERE ...]}`. New `upsertOp` in `internal/executor/operators_upsert.go` consumes the planner state from M0017-0002 and: (1) reorders source row → target column order; (2) encodes conflict key via existing `encodeBTreeKeyForColumn` (NULL-key rows fall through to plain insert per upstream's NULL-never-matches rule); (3) probes the arbiter btree via `RangeScan(key, key, callback)` and applies `mvcc.TupleVisible` on each matching ItemPointer — invisible tuples skipped, first visible match becomes the conflict; (4) on no-conflict: writeHeapRowReturning + arbiter Insert so subsequent rows in the same statement see the new entry; (5) on conflict + DO NOTHING: skip silently, no rowsAffected bump (upstream rule); (6) on conflict + DO UPDATE: build merged 2N-wide row (existing 0..N-1, inserted N..2N-1 — planner ColumnRef Index values address this layout), evaluate UpdateWhere (non-true → skip), evaluate each non-nil UpdateSet[i] (nil slots inherit existing[i]), stamp xmax on conflicting tuple via `PageSetHeapTupleXmax` + `markHeapDeleteDirty`, writeHeapRowReturning the updated tuple, maintainArbiter inserts (key, newPtr) — old (key, oldPtr) entry stays in place since btree.Insert allows duplicates, future probe's visibility filter rejects the dead one. Refactor: `writeHeapRow` split into `writeHeapRow` (void wrapper) + `writeHeapRowReturning` (surfaces inserted tuple's `(block, slot)` ItemPointer); existing INSERT/UPDATE callers unchanged. Stage A scope guard at `upsertOp.Open`: any UpdateSet expression targeting a conflict-key column ordinal rejects with 0A000 — without it, the arbiter index entry for the original key would point at a tuple whose actual key bytes differ; future probes would land on the wrong row. Multi-column arbiters surface 0A000 at runtime — v0 btree only handles single-column composite encoding (extension is M0017-0004). Tests in operators_upsert_test.go: 6 end-to-end scenarios through parser→analyzer→planner→executor — TestUpsertNoConflictInsertsRow (new key path), TestUpsertConflictDoUpdate (replace existing label), TestUpsertConflictDoNothing (RowsAffected=0), TestUpsertDoUpdateMixingExistingAndExcluded (`SET label = label \|\| '/' \|\| excluded.label` pins merged-row layout), TestUpsertDoUpdateWithWhereSkipsRow (predicate false → silent skip), TestUpsertConflictKeyModificationRejected (0A000 guard). Test fixture seeds rows THEN creates the unique index so backfill picks up the seeded tuples — required because v0 doesn't maintain non-arbiter indexes on plain INSERT (pre-existing limitation; M0017's arbiter is the only index UPSERT itself maintains). Concurrency hardening (speculative insert + cleanup on conflict, MVCC-correct under contention) deferred to follow-on slice; under concurrent UPSERTs both writers may believe they're winning the insert race until the next CREATE INDEX rebuild surfaces the duplicate. Fixed via depth-tracked `planHasEscapingOuterRef`. A second, independent bug (`splitEqualityForHash` not recognising AND-of-equalities, forcing Nested Loop against an expensive derived-table join side) was found and fixed in the same investigation. Q20: 1200s+ timeout → 2.55s, rows=92 (matches real PostgreSQL 18.3). **Follow-up (2026-07-09, M0122-0011):** non-correlated `x NOT IN (subquery)` — previously hard-rejected by `isUnnestableNonCorrelatedIn` and stuck on the slower runtime-cache path — now unnests to a new `Join.NullAware` `JoinTypeAnti` hash join. The naive relax (just dropping the `Negated` guard) would have reused the pre-existing NOT-EXISTS-shaped Anti join's "NULL probe key never matches → keep" rule, which is wrong for NOT IN's three-valued-NULL semantics and would have silently over-returned rows; the executor's `openLazyHashJoin`/`nextLazy` (`internal/executor/operators_join_agg.go`) instead special-case `NullAware` with build-side NULL/emptiness tracking. Correlated NOT IN's matching gap (same missing `NullAware`) was found but deliberately left open — see the doc body's new Follow-up section and the deferral ledger. **Follow-up (2026-07-09, M0122-0011 follow-up):** non-correlated IN's LHS operand no longer has to be a bare `*ColumnRef` — `isUnnestableNonCorrelatedIn` was only enforcing the restriction because `unnestNonCorrelatedInExpr` reconstructed a fresh `ColumnRef` by copying fields; since `Join.LeftKey`/`RightKey` are already general `Expr` and the hash-join executor evaluates them with `evalExpr`, the operand (e.g. `f(x)`, `a + b`) is now used directly. Closes the matching `unimplemented_feat.json`/M0069-0005 entry. **Follow-up (2026-07-09, M0122-0011 follow-up #2):** found and fixed a real (pre-existing, bigger-than-flagged) correctness bug in correlated-IN unnest — `unnestInExpr`'s correlated branch built its join key purely from the subquery's correlation predicate, never from `in.Operand`, so a correlation column differing from the IN operand/select column produced a silently wrong join for both `IN` and `NOT IN` (demonstrated: `x IN (SELECT y FROM t2 WHERE z = outer.w)` matched on `w = y` alone). New `correlatedInOperandSafeToUnnest` gate requires operand/select-column identity with the correlation pair before unnesting; this also proves the previously-flagged "correlated NOT IN needs per-group NullAware tracking" moot for every case still unnestable post-fix (no NULL/mismatch can survive the now-required identity). See the doc body's new Follow-up section. **Follow-up (2026-07-09, M0122-0011 follow-up #3):** re-investigated the previously-deferred "Q16's real join shape does not unnest" observation — could not reproduce it against any committed planner revision (with or without realistic indexes/stats); most likely a stale/un-rebuilt binary at the original observation time, not a planner defect. Closed as refuted with a permanent regression guard (`internal/planner/q16_unnest_test.go`). See the doc body's new Follow-up section. |

SET TABLESPACE` now resyncs the heap row immediately. Live-verified via a real `goopg stop`/`goopg start`. TABLESPACE` in the post-restart session succeeds (previously `42704`); a `DROP TABLESPACE` before restart stays gone. **2026-07-09 physical-relocation follow-up (M0122-0007):** closed the last-named "tablespace physical relocation" residual. `storage.RelFileNode` gained `TblOid`; `Manager.relPath`/`RelPath` route through `pg_tblspc/<TblOid>/<version dir>/<dbOid>/` when non-zero; `catalog.InMemory.RelFileNode`/`IndexRelFileNode` (the sole two table/index→RelFileNode conversion sites) now set it from `Table.Tablespace`/`Index.Tablespace`. `ALTER TABLE/INDEX ... | 0097-0036 | [CREATE TEMP VIEW/SEQUENCE parser dispatch (M0097)](0097-0036-create-temp-view-parser-dispatch.md) | accepted | `parseCreate` (`internal/parser/ddl.go`) consumed the `TEMP`/`TEMPORARY` prefix then unconditionally called `parseCreateTableTail`, so `CREATE TEMP VIEW`/`SEQUENCE`/`MATERIALIZED VIEW` were mis-parsed as tables — `CREATE TEMP VIEW` produced no `*CreateViewStmt`, so no view landed in the catalog and a later `DROP VIEW` failed with "view does not exist". Now dispatches on the object keyword after `TEMP`: VIEW → `parseCreateViewTail` (`Temporary=true`), MATERIALIZED VIEW → `parseCreateMatViewTail`, SEQUENCE → `parseCreateSequenceTail(temp=true)`, else TABLE. `CreateViewStmt` gains a `Temporary` field. Known limitation: PG reorders merged USING columns to the front (`using-cols, left-rest, right-rest`); goopg keeps left-table order, which agrees whenever the USING column is the leading column of the left table (every affected regress case). | 0097-0036c | [TID input validation, normalization, and output (M0097)](0097-0036c-tid-input-validation.md) | accepted | goopg's `'…'::tid` cast was a no-op string passthrough (`evalCast` fell through to the unknown-type return in `internal/executor/expr.go`), so `'(-1,0)'::tid` printed `(-1,0)` instead of PG's unsigned `(4294967295,0)`, out-of-range `'(4294967296,1)'`/`'(1,65536)'` were silently accepted, and `pg_input_is_valid`/`pg_input_error_info` mis-reported `tid` as always valid. | 0097-0003b | [SERIAL pseudo-types type-check as their integer base (M0097)](0097-0003b-serial-pseudotype-integer-typecheck.md) | accepted | `SERIAL`/`BIGSERIAL`/`SMALLSERIAL` are not real types — PostgreSQL resolves them to `int4`/`int8`/`int2` (`pg_typeof` reports `integer`). goopg stores `"serial"` as the catalog type (the INSERT auto-increment path keys off the name) and the codec already aliases serial→int4, so reads/`pg_typeof` worked — but the analyzer/planner type system did not know the aliases, so `serial_col = 1` raised `42804 "operator = has incompatible operand types \"serial\" and \"int8\""` and `serial_col + 1` raised `"operator + requires numeric operands"`, blocking any comparison/arithmetic on a serial column with an integer literal (e.g. `WHERE id = N` on a serial PK; the first blocker in `copyselect`). Root cause: three predicates omitted the aliases — analyzer `isNumericTypeName` (gates comparison via `isComparable` AND arithmetic via `isNumericLike`), planner `isIntegerLikeType` and `promoteIntType` (arithmetic result-type promotion). The planner's NUMERIC/DECIMAL-only `isNumericTypeName` was intentionally left untouched. Fix: add `"serial"`/`"bigserial"`/`"smallserial"` as integer aliases (serial→int4, bigserial→int8, smallserial→int2), mirroring `codec.go`'s alias-list style — purely additive, storage/INSERT untouched. Sibling-path class [[pattern_sibling_paths_must_agree]] (codec canonicalised serial but type-checking did not). `copyselect` still defers on a separate parser bug (trailing `ORDER BY 1` greedily attached to the right set-op branch, where positional 1 hits the `*` target). Tests: `TestSerialPseudotypeIntegerTypeCheck` (`internal/analyzer/coerce_test.go`, incl. serial-vs-text still-errors negative case), `TestPromoteIntTypeSerialFamily` (`internal/planner/planner_test.go`). |

(1) `isColumnFunctionallyDetermined` (`internal/planner/planner.go`) accepted both primary-key *and* unique indexes when deciding whether a column may pass through a GROUP BY, but PostgreSQL's `check_functional_grouping` (`src/backend/catalog/pg_constraint.c`) recognises only PRIMARY KEY — never unique constraints (deferrable; nullable admits multiple NULLs). So `GROUP BY body`/`GROUP BY title` on UNIQUE columns wrongly passed (state-dependent on whether the inline-UNIQUE index was registered at plan time, producing a nondeterministic spurious `relation "fdv1" already exists` in the shared-cluster run). (2) `execCreateView` (`internal/executor/operators_ddl.go`) validates the view body via `planner.Plan` but returned the raw `*planner.PlanError`, whose `Error()` renders `"<code>: <msg> (byte <pos>)"` — diverging from the simple-query path that extracts `.Code`/`.Message`. | 0097-0024c | [Reject COPY (SELECT … INTO …) with the PG-compatible message (M0097)](0097-0024c-copy-select-into-rejection.md) | accepted | `copy (select t into temp test3 …) to stdout` must fail with `ERROR:  COPY (SELECT INTO) is not supported`. Fix: `parseCopy` splits direction handling on source form — query form accepts only `TO`, else `errSyntaxAtCur()` (new bare `syntax error at or near "TOKEN"` helper, no `(got X)` suffix); removes the old post-hoc check. | 0097-0024e | [COPY in multi-statement simple-query batches: psql `\;` (M0097)](0097-0024e-copy-in-multi-statement-batch.md) | accepted | psql's `\;` joins commands into one Query message; the server runs them in order with one CommandComplete each + one trailing ReadyForQuery. goopg mishandled embedded COPY: a batch starting with COPY hit `expected exactly one COPY statement` (whole message routed to the single-COPY path), and a batch reaching a COPY via the multi-statement dispatcher leaked the internal `planner.Copy has no executor path yet` (`0A000`). Fix: (1) `handleQueryOrCopy` routes any query with an internal `;` to the multi-statement dispatcher even when it starts with `COPY ` (single COPY keeps the `copyInState` fast path); (2) the dispatch loop intercepts `*parser.CopyStmt` before the executor via new `runInlineCopy`, which streams COPY TO (and server-side COPY FROM file) within the batch's shared txn, writing only CommandComplete. CopyFail/decode errors → `writeQueryError(57014/…)` + `errQueryErrorSent` aborts the batch. Safe because the main read loop is parked in `handleQueryOrCopy` (no second consumer of `r`). Tests: `TestCopyFromStdinInMultiStatementBatch`, `TestCopyFromStdinInBatchAbortsOnFail`. Verified live: the STDIN-batch block matches PG byte-for-byte (`select * from test3` → rows 1, 2). Remaining `copyselect` (2 lines): query-form bare legacy CSV options (`… to stdout csv header force quote t`) — parser stops at `csv`, plus CSV HEADER/FORCE_QUOTE TO-output rendering. | 0100-0005y | [`tableoid` system column for partition + non-partitioned scans (M0100)](0100-0005y-tableoid-system-column.md) | accepted | `rangeBinding.tableOidColIdx` plus a new `TableOidExpr` plan expression let `resolveColumnRefAt` (planner) and `resolveColumnRefTypeAt` (analyzer) recognise the `tableoid` system column. Fix: (a) add `case *setOp: return v` in `findScanLeaf` — `setOp` now implements `currentTIDProvider`; (b) `setOp.currentTID()` delegates to `findScanLeaf(active_child)` (left while `!leftDone`, right once `leftDone`), reaching the correct leaf `seqScanOp`. Without the fix, `upsertOp.findInProgressConflict` Case 3 (lock-only xmax) never fired for `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on a partitioned table, causing `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` to proceed without waiting. | 0106-0010 step 3ct | [pg_database heap row matches PG18 Form_pg_database (M0106-0010 step 3ct)](0106-0010-step3ct-pg-database-pg18-row-layout.md) | accepted | Closes the `TRAP: failed Assert("j > attnum"), File: "heaptuple.c", Line: 642` PG-standby user-backend abort surfaced by Step 3cs's note. Root cause: `bootstrapPostgresDatabase` wrote a 16-column pre-PG15 schema (missing `dathasloginevt` + `daticurules`; `daticulocale` not renamed to `datlocale`; `datcollate`/`datctype` typed as `name` not `text`) and never stamped `HEAP_HASVARWIDTH` in `t_infomask`. PG18 reads the row through `formrdesc`-baked `Desc_pg_database` (18 cols) — schema drift was fully invisible to local tests but produces immediate FATALs on every standby connect once the syscache lookup succeeds. The missing `HEAP_HASVARWIDTH` flag is the actual trigger: `nocachegetattr` (heaptuple.c:520) skips its var-width early-exit guard when the bit is unset, falls through to the fast path, breaks the fixed-prefix loop at the first attlen<=0 attribute, and asserts `j > attnum`. `CheckMyDatabase`'s `SysCacheGetAttr(DATABASEOID, tup, Anum_pg_database_datcollversion)` (attnum 17) is the first path that hits this. Regression pins (new in `internal/initdb/pg_database_pg18_schema_test.go`): `TestPgDatabaseAttrsMatchesPG18FormPgDatabase` (strict 18-attr fixture against pg_database.h) and `TestBootstrapPostgresDatabaseTupleHasVarWidthAndNullBitmap` (end-to-end pin asserting `HEAP_HASVARWIDTH | HEAP_HASNULL` and `t_natts == 18` on both template1 + postgres heap tuples). Verified: `go build ./...` PASS; targeted `go test -run 'TestPgDatabaseAttrs\|TestBootstrapPostgresDatabaseTuple' ./internal/initdb/` PASS; `go test -count=1 ./internal/initdb/` — same 15 baseline failures as Step 3cs (no new regressions, baseline-diff confirmed via `git stash`); cross-package smoke `go test -count=1 ./internal/executor/ ./internal/server/ ./internal/storage/ ./internal/catalog/ ./internal/mvcc/` PASS; `GOOPG_RUN_BLOCKED_M0102_E2E=1 TestE2E_FailoverGoopgToPG/async` re-run confirms the `Assert("j > attnum")` TRAP is gone. Next blocker (Step 3cu): first standby FATAL is now `FATAL: XX000: could not open relation with OID 2964` (pg_db_role_setting) raised by `process_settings(MyDatabaseId, GetSessionUserId())` immediately after `CheckMyDatabase` returns; cascading `invalid attalign value:` FATALs on follower backends are the Step 3cs catcache-stale pattern and disappear once the first FATAL is closed. |

| 0106-0010 step 3cr | [pg_class.reltablespace for shared catalogs (M0106-0010 step 3cr)](0106-0010-step3cr-pg-class-reltablespace-shared.md) | accepted | Closes the FATAL `could not open file "base/5/2672"` that PG-standby user backends hit immediately after Step 3cq let them past InitPostgres. Root cause: `bootstrapPgClassTuples` wrote `reltablespace = 0` for every nailed rel — including the eight shared heaps and their indexes — but PG's `RelationInitPhysicalAddr` (relcache.c:1347-1354, with explicit comment "we do not look at relisshared here") routes file paths purely from `pg_class.reltablespace`: shared catalogs must store GLOBALTABLESPACE_OID = 1664 to resolve to `global/<relfilenode>`, otherwise `spcOid = MyDatabaseTableSpace` and the path becomes `base/<MyDatabaseId>/<relfilenode>`. `formrdesc` sets reltablespace=1664 in memory at Phase 2 (relcache.c:1948), but Phase 3 then overrides rd_rel with the on-disk pg_class row, so the on-disk value must match. Second, independent layer of the bug: `relcache_init.go::flattenRels` created each index from `idxSpec` with `IsShared = false` (struct zero value) regardless of the parent heap's flag, so shared-catalog indexes (e.g. pg_database_oid_index OID 2672) were encoded with relisshared=false too. Fix: (a) `flattenRels` now propagates `IsShared` from `heaps[0]` to each emitted `indexNailed` entry; (b) new helper `pgClassReltablespaceFor(isShared)` returns 1664 for shared and 0 for local, called from `pgClassRow` at the reltablespace Datum slot; (c) `buildPgClassBlob` writes 1664 at struct offset 92 for shared rels in the init-file encoder too, keeping the two paths in sync. New file `internal/initdb/pg_class_reltablespace_test.go` pins: `TestPgClassRowSharedReltablespaceIsGlobalTablespaceOID` (Datum value), `TestPgClassRowSharedReltablespaceInEncodedPayload` (bytes [92:96] LE uint32 == 1664 after `EncodeRowPG`), `TestFlattenRelsPropagatesIsSharedToIndexes` (every `RelKind='i'` in `nailedSharedRels` has `IsShared=true`; every such entry in `nailedLocalRels` has `IsShared=false`). Verified: `go build ./...` PASS; targeted `go test -run 'TestPgClassRowShared\|TestFlattenRelsPropagatesIsSharedToIndexes' ./internal/initdb/` PASS (3/3); `go test -count=1 ./internal/initdb/` — same 15 baseline failures as Step 3cq (no new regressions, baseline-diff confirmed via `git stash`); cross-package smoke PASS. Next blocker (Step 3cs): pursue whichever FATAL surfaces next now that `global/2672` is reachable. |

Wired into `Init` immediately after `bootstrapPgAttributeTuples` so it overwrites the v0 layout `bootstrapSystemCatalogs` wrote earlier. Regression pins (all new in `pg_type_bootstrap_test.go`): `TestPgTypeColDefsLayoutMatchesPG18` (probes int4 / OID 23 — byte 128 == 'i', byte 129 == 'p'), `TestPgTypeInitialEntriesCoverNailedAttrTypeOIDs` (strict guard — every TypeOID a nailedAttr references must have a `pgTypeCanonical` entry), `TestPgTypeRowCanonicalTypalignByte` (every entry encoded via `EncodeRowPG` has `payload[128] == e.Align`, `payload[129] == e.Storage`), `TestBootstrapPgTypeTuplesWritesCanonicalHeap` (end-to-end heap walk asserts byte 128 ∈ {c,s,i,d}, byte 129 ∈ {p,e,x,m} for every tuple at both base/1 and base/5). | 0106-0010 step 3ba | [multi-leaf btree leaf P_HIKEY uses firstright, not lastleft (M0106-0010 step 3ba)](0106-0010-step3ba-multi-leaf-btree-hikey-firstright.md) | accepted | Closes the `FATAL: cache lookup failed for attribute 2 of relation 3593` PG-standby boot blocker that has been firing on every backend `InitPostgres` since Step 3az silenced the multi-leaf btree assertion. The error fires from `RelationGetIndexAttOptions → get_attoptions(3593, 2)` (relcache.c:6008 → lsyscache.c:1074) while opening `pg_shseclabel_object_index` (OID 3593). Direct page dumps confirm the underlying heap row exists at `base/{1,5}/1249` (block 0, offset 60) and `pg_attribute_relid_attnum_index` (OID 2659) has the corresponding entry at leaf 1 slot 407. But that entry sits at the **leaf boundary**: leaf 1 ends at (3593, 2) and leaf 2 starts at (3593, 3). PG's `_bt_compare` (nbtsearch.c:806–831) for a forward-direction scan key against a heapkeyspace pivot with `keysz == ntupatts && heapTid == NULL && scantid == NULL` returns 1 (strictly greater), and `_bt_moveright` then steps right to leaf 2 where the key doesn't exist. Step 3az set the P_HIKEY's source tuple to `group[len(group)-1]` (= lastleft); PG's `_bt_truncate` (nbtutils.c:3776) instead uses **firstright** — the first data tuple of the *next* leaf. Fix: `pgBuildBtreeBulkLoad` now sources the pivot from `leafGroups[li+1][0]`. With HIKEY = (3593, 3), the scankey (3593, 2) compares strictly less in the second key (2 < 3), `_bt_compare` returns -1, and the search stays on leaf 1. Pivot encoding helper (`pgBuildBtreeLeafHighKey`) is unchanged. `TestPgBuildBtreeBulkLoadTwoLeafLayoutMatchesPG18` updated to read firstright (`tuples[maxTuplesPerNonRightmostLeaf]`) instead of lastleft. Safe for every currently bulk-loaded index because they're all UNIQUE — consecutive keys are distinct, so PG's `_bt_keep_natts` returns `nkeyatts` (no heap-TID tiebreaker needed, no suffix truncation). `GOOPG_RUN_BLOCKED_M0102_E2E=1 TestE2E_FailoverGoopgToPG/async` advances past the cache-lookup blocker; new blocker surfaces as `could not open relation with OID 2328` (= pg_db_role_setting) — out of scope, Step 3bb territory. |
| 0106-0010 step 3az | [multi-leaf btree leaf P_HIKEY pivot + P_NONE sentinel fix (M0106-0010 step 3az)](0106-0010-step3az-multi-leaf-btree-hikey-and-pnone.md) | accepted | Closes the `TRAP: failed Assert("_bt_check_natts(...)") nbtsearch.c:707` PG-standby boot blocker that has been firing on every backend startup since Step 3aw activated the multi-leaf bulk-load path for `pg_attribute_relid_attnum_index` (OID 2659). Two independent encoding bugs in `internal/initdb/btree_index_bootstrap.go` had to be fixed in lockstep: (1) `pgBuildBtreeBulkLoad` set every non-rightmost leaf's P_HIKEY to a verbatim copy of the leaf's last data tuple, but PG18 V4 heapkeyspace btrees require leaf high keys to satisfy `BTreeTupleIsPivot()` (INDEX_ALT_TID_MASK in t_info, BT_IS_POSTING clear). New helper `pgBuildBtreeLeafHighKey(dataTuple, nkeyatts)` allocates a fresh buffer, ORs INDEX_ALT_TID_MASK into t_info preserving size bits, and writes `nkeyatts` into ip_posid with zero status bits (no BT_PIVOT_HEAP_TID_ATTR). (2) The `pNone` package constant was declared `0xFFFFFFFF` with a comment conflating `P_NONE` with `InvalidBlockNumber`; PG's `#define P_NONE 0` (nbtree.h) and `#define InvalidBlockNumber 0xFFFFFFFF` (block.h) are distinct sentinels. Writing `0xFFFFFFFF` into `btpo_next` of the "rightmost" leaf made `P_RIGHTMOST(opaque)` false, so PG's `P_FIRSTDATAKEY` macro treated slot 1 as a high-key pivot — the actual non-pivot data tuple there failed the same `_bt_check_natts` heapkeyspace pivot branch. Fix: `pNone uint32 = 0`. The single-leaf fast path was unaffected because `pgBuildBtreeLeafRootPage` never wrote btpo_prev/btpo_next (zero-fill from `make([]byte, BlockSize)` was already correct P_NONE). New regression pin `TestPgBuildBtreeLeafHighKeyMatchesPGPivotEncoding` (pins helper's byte layout including no-mutation invariant); `TestPgBuildBtreeBulkLoadTwoLeafLayoutMatchesPG18` updated to demand pivot encoding instead of verbatim equality. `GOOPG_RUN_BLOCKED_M0102_E2E=1 TestE2E_FailoverGoopgToPG/async` advances past 0 TRAPs to a new blocker: `cache lookup failed for attribute 2 of relation 3593` (`pg_shseclabel_object_index`) — out of scope, Step 3ba territory. |

Slow path (> 407 tuples) emits PG18 nbtsort format: metapage at block 0, N BTP_LEAF pages with `btpo_prev`/`btpo_next` sibling links and P_HIKEY at slot 1 on every non-rightmost leaf (rightmost slid left per `_bt_slideleft`), root at block N+1 with `BTP_ROOT` + `btpo_level=1` + N downlinks. Leftmost downlink is the 8-byte zero-attribute "minus infinity" pivot (nbtsort.c:1001–1008); subsequent downlinks copy the corresponding leaf's first data tuple with `INDEX_ALT_TID_MASK = 0x2000` set in `t_info`, `ip_blkid` = child block (struct-order `bi_hi`/`bi_lo` halves, same trap as Step 3s heap TIDs), `ip_posid` = `nkeyatts & BT_OFFSET_MASK = 0x0FFF` per `BTreeTupleSetDownLink` / `BTreeTupleSetNAtts` (nbtree.h:563/603). New method `Pool.MarkDirtyLogicalChange(s, emitter)` always runs the logical `emitter` and additionally emits the FPI on first-dirty-in-epoch, in WAL order: logical first (LSN_log) then PageImage (LSN_fpi > LSN_log). | 0103-0032 | [M0103-0007 rung 9 — PG-publisher → goopg-subscriber TRUNCATE replication](0103-0032-m0103-0007-rung-9-pg-to-goopg-truncate.md) | accepted | Closes rung 9 of M0103-0007. Rungs 1–8 covered every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE shape across pgoutput proto_version=1 but never the `'T'` (TRUNCATE) frame; the apply worker dispatched only on B/R/I/D/U/C and fell through to the `default` arm of `ApplyMessage` for `'T'`, returning `"applyworker: unsupported pgoutput kind \"T\""` and stalling the slot. Rung 9 closes the gap end-to-end: decoder gains a `case pgoTruncate` arm in `internal/wal/pgoutput_decoder.go::DecodeMessage` and two new `DecodedMessage` fields (`TruncateRels []uint32`, `TruncateOption byte`); `ApplyWorker.ApplyMessage` gains a `case 'T'` branch routing to `applyTruncate`, which walks the relid list, resolves each via the existing relation cache, and calls the existing `truncateRelation(ctx, rel)` primitive to stamp `xmax = currentTx.XID` on every visible tuple — transactional with the surrounding apply xact, symmetric with `applyDeleteByKey`. Soft-truncate semantics (no physical file shrink) are intentional: `Pool.Manager().TruncateRelation(rel)` is non-transactional and would diverge subscriber durability from publisher xact rollback. Both pgoutput option bits (`TRUNCATE_CASCADE`/`TRUNCATE_RESTART_SEQS`) are publisher-side decisions — CASCADE expansion already populates the relid list before the publisher emits `'T'`, RESTART IDENTITY is a no-op on goopg's apply path which has no replicated sequence state — but the byte is recorded for future rungs. Unknown-relid rejection mirrors `applyDelete`/`applyUpdate` (catalog drift surfaces with `event=apply_error`, `kind=T`). Pinned by: decoder unit `TestPgoutputDecoderTruncateMessage` (4 sub-tests), apply-worker units `TestApplyWorkerTruncate` + `TestApplyWorkerTruncateUnknownRelOid`, live E2E `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgTruncate` (publisher INSERT×3 → TRUNCATE → INSERT×2; subscriber must show only the two post-truncate rows). Verification: live E2E PASS (~2.0 s); all 9 `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopg*` together → PASS (~15.4 s); race-tested regression on `executor/wal/catalog/pubsubcluster` → green. pgbench against PG publisher with `pgbench_history` polling, proto_version=2 streaming subxacts, and `kill -9` + libpq multi-host reconnect remain future rungs. |
| 0103-0031 | [M0103-0007 rung 8 — PG-publisher → goopg-subscriber multi-table interleaved DML](0103-0031-m0103-0007-rung-8-pg-to-goopg-multi-table.md) | accepted | Closes rung 8 of M0103-0007. Rungs 1–7 all exercised a single published table `public.t (id int PRIMARY KEY, v text)`; the apply worker's relation cache (`internal/executor/applyworker.go`) only ever held one entry, the relOid was constant for the slot's lifetime, and the per-relation dispatch path was untested at that level. Rung 8 publishes two tables with deliberately different column shapes — `public.users` (2 cols: `id int PK, name text`) and `public.orders` (3 cols: `id int PK, user_id int, amount int`) — and interleaves INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against both inside one top-level transaction plus a follow-up autocommit phase. The load-bearing property pinned is the **multi-relation dispatch contract**: the apply worker's relation cache must keep both `R` messages live across the `B…C` block, every change must route to the matching `*catalog.Table` on the subscriber, and per-table primary-key index maintenance (`maintainUniqueIndexesForInsert`) must run against the right table so subsequent fresh-session PK IndexScans find each row. Column-index drift between the wire tuple and the subscriber's `catalog.Table.Columns` would surface either as a parse error (text into int4 at the same ordinal across tables) or as the per-row identity assertions failing. Expected final state on the subscriber: `count(users)=2` with `id=1 name='alice-updated'` + `id=3 name='carol'`; `count(orders)=3` with `id=10 user_id=1 amount=99` + `id=12 user_id=1 amount=50` + `id=13 user_id=3 amount=75`. Per-table count assertion catches cross-relation dispatch leaks; per-id identity assertions catch UPDATE-routing bugs. No code change needed — rungs 1–7's machinery already covered both `applyRelation` map keying and per-table `*catalog.Table` resolution. Pinned by `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgMultiTable` (`internal/testport/pgoutput_interop_test.go`). Verification: targeted test → PASS (~1.7 s); all 8 `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopg*` together → PASS (~13.4 s); race-tested regression on `executor/wal/server/catalog/pubsubcluster` → green. pgbench against PG publisher with `pgbench_history` polling, DDL replication shapes, proto_version=2 streaming subxacts, and `kill -9` + libpq multi-host reconnect remain future rungs. |
| 0103-0030 | [M0103-0007 rung 7 — PG-publisher → goopg-subscriber SAVEPOINT subxacts](0103-0030-m0103-0007-rung-7-pg-to-goopg-savepoint-xact.md) | accepted | Closes rung 7 of M0103-0007. Rungs 1–6 covered single-statement autocommit (1–5) and explicit multi-DML single-xact (6); this rung scales another dimension — **subtransactions**. At `proto_version=1` (goopg's default, set in `internal/server/logicalreceiver.go:149-151`) subxact boundaries are NOT streamed: the publisher's reorder buffer filters rolled-back subxact rows before emission, and the wire carries only the committed net effect of the top-level transaction as one `B…C` block. This rung pins the contract end-to-end with a SAVEPOINT-heavy workload (`SAVEPOINT s1 → INSERT + UPDATE → ROLLBACK TO s1`; `SAVEPOINT s2 → INSERT → RELEASE`; top-level INSERT; `SAVEPOINT s3 → DELETE → ROLLBACK TO s3`). Expected final state: `count(*)=3`, `id=1 v='one'` (s1 UPDATE rolled back), no `id=2` (s1 INSERT rolled back), `id=3 v='three'` (s2 RELEASE merged + s3 DELETE rolled back), `id=4 v='four'` (top-level INSERT). Each assertion fail-fasts on a distinct potential regression (publisher leaks rolled-back inserts → count=4/5; UPDATE leaks through → wrong `v`; ROLLBACK TO of DELETE fails → no `id=3` row). No code changes needed — the publisher does the work at buffer-flush time and the apply worker's existing one-TxnMgr-per-`B…C` machinery handles the resulting block exactly as rung 6 did. `proto_version=2+` streaming subxacts (with `Y`/`A` frames + parent-XID linkage) is out of scope here; promoting the default requires apply-worker subxact tracking and is a later rung. Pinned by `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgSavepointXact` (`internal/testport/pgoutput_interop_test.go`). Verification: targeted test → PASS (~1.7 s); all 7 `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopg*` together → PASS (~12.0 s); race-tested regression on `executor/wal/server/catalog/pubsubcluster` → green. pgbench against PG publisher with `pgbench_history` polling, DDL replication shapes, proto_version=2 streaming, and `kill -9` + libpq multi-host reconnect remain future rungs. |
| 0103-0029 | [M0103-0007 rung 6 — PG-publisher → goopg-subscriber multi-DML single transaction](0103-0029-m0103-0007-rung-6-pg-to-goopg-multi-dml-xact.md) | accepted | Closes rung 6 of M0103-0007. Rungs 1–5 ran every publisher DML in its own implicit autocommit xact (one pgoutput `B…C` per statement); this rung scales vertically — one explicit `BEGIN; INSERT×3; UPDATE; DELETE; COMMIT;` block on the publisher, one pgoutput xact on the wire, one `txnMgr.Begin/Commit` pair on the subscriber. No code change was required for this rung — the machinery landed across rungs 1–5 and the broader MVCC effort already supports the shape; the new `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgMultiDMLXact` asserts it end-to-end via fresh `database/sql` sessions (PK IndexScan path): `count(*) = 2`, `id=1 v='one'`, `id=2 v='two-prime'` (INSERT-then-UPDATE in same xact), `id=3` → 0 (INSERT-then-DELETE in same xact). | 0103-0028 | [M0103-0007 rung 5 — PG-publisher → goopg-subscriber unchanged-TOAST ('u') decode](0103-0028-m0103-0007-rung-5-pg-to-goopg-toast-unchanged.md) | accepted | Closes rung 5 of M0103-0007. | 0103-0025 | [M0103-0007 rung 2 — PG-publisher → goopg-subscriber full DML round-trip](0103-0025-m0103-0007-rung-2-pg-to-goopg-full-dml.md) | accepted | Closes rung 2 of M0103-0007 (Scenario A). Mirrors the M0103-0008 closure shape: the new `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgFullDML` drives a full INSERT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE round-trip through the pubsubcluster harness (PG publisher + goopg subscriber, pre-created slot since goopg's CREATE SUBSCRIPTION doesn't yet auto-create), then asserts fresh-session visibility on the goopg subscriber via PK IndexScan: `WHERE id = 2 AND v = 'updated'` returns 1, `WHERE id = 1` returns 0, `count(*)` returns 1.
