| 0103-0024 | [Apply-Worker Index Maintenance for Fresh-Session Visibility (M0103-0007 rung 1)](0103-0024-apply-worker-index-maintenance.md) | accepted | Closes the M0103-0006 fresh-session-visibility caveat (the one carried into M0103-0007 Scenario A as a runtime gap). The caveat hand-waved the cause as "the apply worker writes outside the dispatcher's MVCC view," but the actual root cause is narrower: `ApplyWorker.applyInsert` called `writeHeapRow` only, with no index maintenance. SeqScan and `id::text='1'` / `id=1::int4` predicates worked correctly; bare `WHERE id = 1` fell back to IndexScan, probed an empty PK btree, and returned 0 rows. Dispatcher INSERTs into the same table were matched fine, isolating the gap to the apply path. Fix: pipe the freshly-written tuple's `storage.ItemPointer` from `writeHeapRowReturning` through to `maintainUniqueIndexesForInsert` from inside `applyInsert`; mirror the same change in `applyUpdateByKey` (signature gains `*catalog.Table` so it can resolve `IndexesOnTable`). Pinned by `TestPubSubClusterSmokePGToGoopgFreshSessionVisibility` (`internal/testutil/pubsubcluster/cluster_test.go`): drives the full PG-publisher + goopg-subscriber harness, asserts `count(*) WHERE id = 1` returns 1 after the apply commit. Before the fix: fails at the 10 s `WaitForRow` deadline. After: passes in ≈ 2 s. UPDATE old-tuple / DELETE index-entry deletion and non-unique secondary indexes are documented follow-ups (orphan index entries are tolerated by goopg's IndexScan re-fetch + re-visibility-check loop). |
| 0103-0033 | [M0103-0007 rung 10 — PG-publisher → goopg-subscriber column-order remap](0103-0033-m0103-0007-rung-10-pg-to-goopg-column-order.md) | accepted | Closes rung 10 of M0103-0007. Rungs 1–9 covered every DML/TRUNCATE pgoutput shape but assumed publisher and subscriber tables shared identical physical column ordering. `decodePgoutputTupleAsRow` indexed `localCols[i]` with the remote ordinal `i` and wrote `row[i] = d`, so a swapped-order subscriber table either crashed with a parse error (text into int4) or installed silently-corrupted heap rows (values landed in the wrong slots, `id` and `v` swapped). Fix: the decoder now builds a per-call `localIdx[]` map by matching `remoteCols[i].Name` to `localCols[j].Name` (PG's apply worker behaviour). The `Row` is sized to `len(localCols)` and indexed by LOCAL position; the `unchanged` mask stays in lockstep. Unmatched remote columns return an explicit error (catalog drift surfaces early instead of silently dropping values). Subscriber columns missing on the publisher remain `NullDatum` — DEFAULT-value handling for that asymmetric case stays out of scope. Pinned by unit tests `TestApplyWorkerDecodeRemapsReorderedColumns` + `TestApplyWorkerDecodeRejectsUnmatchedRemoteCol` (`internal/executor/applyworker_test.go`) and the live E2E `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgColumnOrderMismatch` (`internal/testport/pgoutput_interop_test.go`: PG publisher `(id int PK, v text)` + goopg subscriber `(v text, id int PK)`, workload INSERT×2 + no-key-touch UPDATE + DELETE, asserts via fresh `database/sql` sessions through PK IndexScan). Verification: targeted unit + E2E PASS (~2.0 s); all 10 `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopg*` together → PASS (~17.2 s); race-tested regression on `executor/wal/catalog/pubsubcluster` → green. |

Rungs 1–11 verified the apply worker against REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT (rungs 1–3, 6–11) and FULL (rung 4); USING INDEX on a non-PK unique index was untested. Before this rung, the no-OldTuple UPDATE branch resolved through `primaryKeyOnlyRow(cat, tbl, newRow)`, which walked the subscriber catalog for `idx.Primary == true`. That dropped the UPDATE silently when (a) the subscriber declared no PK at all (USING INDEX subscriber matches the publisher's no-PK shape) or (b) the subscriber PK columns differed from the publisher's identity-index columns. Fix: add `replicaIdentityKeyRow(remoteCols, localCols, newRow) Row` consulting the wire's per-column `LOGICALREP_IS_REPLICA_IDENTITY` bit (bit 0 of `DecodedAttr.Flags`) instead of any catalog lookup; `applyUpdate`'s no-OldTuple branch calls it first, falls back to `primaryKeyOnlyRow` only when no flags are set (older or corrupt streams). Symmetric with rung 2's hot path because REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT sets the flag on PK columns, so the helper produces the same key. Pinned by unit tests `TestReplicaIdentityKeyRow` (four sub-cases: PK columns flagged, non-PK composite identity, no-flags returns nil, row-length mismatch returns nil) in `internal/executor/applyworker_test.go` and the live E2E `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgReplicaIdentityUsingIndex` (publisher `t (k int NOT NULL, v text)` with UNIQUE index `t_k_uniq` and `ALTER TABLE … REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX t_k_uniq`; subscriber `t (k int, v text)` with no constraints; workload INSERT×3 + no-key-touch UPDATE + DELETE; asserts via fresh `database/sql` sessions). Verification: targeted unit + E2E PASS (~1.7 s); all 11 `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopg*` together → PASS (~21 s); regression sweep on `executor/wal/catalog/pubsubcluster` → green. |
| 0103-0036 | [M0103-0007 rung 13 — PG-publisher → goopg-subscriber subscriber-extra column DEFAULT evaluation](0103-0036-m0103-0007-rung-13-pg-to-goopg-subscriber-extra-default.md) | accepted | Closes rung 13 of M0103-0007. Rung 11 preserved subscriber-only column values across replicated UPDATEs by copying from the matched heap row; the symmetric INSERT case was deferred — every replicated INSERT silently installed `NullDatum` into every column the publisher's Relation message did not claim, including columns with a CREATE TABLE DEFAULT clause. Slots without a DEFAULT stay NullDatum (NOT NULL violations surface loudly). Pinned by parser test `TestParseCreateTableDefaultExpr` (four DEFAULT shapes — string, int, bool, NULL), unit tests `TestApplyDefaultsForMissingFillsSlots` + `TestApplyDefaultsForMissingIgnoresFalseMask` (`internal/executor/applyworker_test.go`), and the live E2E `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgSubscriberExtraDefault` (publisher `(id, v)`, subscriber `(id, v, note text DEFAULT 'auto', bare text)`; two INSERTs replicate; assertions: `note='auto'` for both rows, `bare IS NULL`, exactly 2 rows). Verification: targeted unit + E2E PASS (~2.0 s); all 12 `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopg*` together → PASS (~23.7 s); parser/catalog/executor regression green. |
| 0103-0037 | [M0103-0007 rung 14 — dispatcher INSERT DEFAULT-expression evaluation](0103-0037-m0103-0007-rung-14-dispatcher-insert-default.md) | accepted | Closes rung 14 of M0103-0007 by lifting rung 13's apply-worker DEFAULT-fill into goopg's regular dispatcher INSERT path. Fix split across parser + planner: new sentinel AST node `parser.DefaultMarker` (zero-field, satisfies `Expr`); `parseValuesRow` accepts `KwDefault` as a complete cell and emits the marker; `Plan()` runs new `rewriteInsertDefaultMarkers(s, cat)` BEFORE `analyzer.Analyze` for `*parser.InsertStmt` — it walks each VALUES row, maps row position → target column ordinal via the same logic `planInsert` uses, and substitutes each `*DefaultMarker` with the column's catalog `DefaultExpr` (or `*parser.NullConst` when the column has no DEFAULT). The substituted expression flows through `resolveExpr` and the executor unchanged, so neither the analyzer nor the executor ever observes a `DefaultMarker`. Mirrors upstream's `rewriteValuesRTE` pass. | 0103-0041 | [M0103-0007 rung 18 — zero-arg time functions in DEFAULT expressions](0103-0041-m0103-0007-rung-18-default-time-funcs.md) | accepted | Closes rung 18 of M0103-0007 by adding `*parser.FuncCall` evaluation for the zero-arg time functions (`now`, `current_timestamp`, `transaction_timestamp`, `statement_timestamp`, `current_date`) in the catalog DEFAULT-eval slow path. Wall-clock is read per call rather than threaded through `ctx.Now` to avoid a signature change touching three callers — documented bounded-skew divergence from upstream's statement-scoped `statement_timestamp`. Unknown niladic functions stay at NullDatum so unevaluable DEFAULTs surface as NOT NULL violations loudly. Star args / non-`pg_catalog` schemas / non-string arg-types / overflow errors all fall through to NullDatum so unevaluable DEFAULTs surface as NOT-NULL violations loudly rather than silently NULL-ing the row. | 0103-0045 | [M0103-0007 rung 22 — SIGKILL + libpq multi-host reconnect (PG → goopg)](0103-0045-m0103-0007-rung-22-kill-and-reconnect.md) | accepted | Closes rung 22 of M0103-0007 by lifting `Kill()` onto `pubsubcluster.ReplPeer` and adding a `PubSubCluster.MultiHostConninfo(applicationName)` helper so client redirection from a SIGKILLed PG publisher to the (always-writable) goopg subscriber can be exercised end-to-end. `pgPeer.Kill()` delegates to the existing `pgcluster.Cluster.Kill()` (`pg_ctl -m immediate -w stop`); `goopgPeer.Kill()` delegates to `cluster.Cluster.Kill()` (direct SIGKILL of the server process). `MultiHostConninfo` returns the libpq-style `host=<pub>,<sub> port=<pp>,<gp> user=<u> dbname=<db> [application_name=<an>]` shape (PG18 libpq-connect §32.1.1) with the publisher listed first; libpq walks the host list in order, so after `Publisher.Kill()` the dead host is connect-refused and libpq falls through to the surviving subscriber. | 0103-0046 | [M0103-0007 rung 23 — pgbench-shape kill mid-flight + async DoD bracket (PG → goopg)](0103-0046-m0103-0007-rung-23-pgbench-kill-async.md) | accepted | Ties rungs 1–22 together end-to-end against M0103-0007's Scenario A async DoD bracket `count(*) ∈ [killCommitted - asyncLossBound + 1, killCommitted + 1]` (asyncLossBound=50). Two Go-driven writer goroutines hold their own `*sql.DB` handles to the PG publisher and run a throttled (5 ms/INSERT/client → ~400 commits/s total) INSERT loop into `public.bench_log(client int, src text)` — no PK because INSERT-only doesn't need REPLICA IDENTITY. An `atomic.Int64 committed` counter is bumped AFTER each successful commit returns and the ctx.Err() check sits at the TOP of the loop, so an in-flight INSERT always runs to completion before the goroutine exits — eliminating the "committed-on-server-but-not-counted" race that would break the bracket's upper bound. Sequence: replication-is-alive gate (≥1 row on goopg within 30 s), 1500 ms workload hold, `workCancel + wg.Wait`, `killCommitted := committed.Load()`, 200 ms walsender drain window, `psc.Publisher.Kill()` (rung 22 plumbing), multi-host post-failover INSERT (`client=-1, src='post'`) via the in-tree `psql` with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=postgres/local_install/lib`, poll subscriber count until stable for 1 s, assert async DoD bracket + `src='post'` row presence. Pinned by `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgPgbenchKillAsync` (`internal/testport/pgoutput_interop_test.go`); also lands a shared `waitForCountStable` helper for the apply-buffer drain detection. Throttle rationale: unthrottled the workload sustains ≈10 k commits/s which exceeds goopg's apply throughput and piles thousands of rows in the walsender's TCP buffer + apply queue; PG dying drops that buffer and observed loss balloons past any fixed asyncLossBound. Drain rationale: 200 ms is empirically enough on the in-tree local_install build for the throttled workload's steady-state apply lag to drop below 50 rows. Out of scope: `sync_remote_apply` mode (zero-loss invariant, separate rung), `pgbench` as workload driver (rungs 20/21 already cover, no atomic counter from a subprocess), apply-path crash (different failure mode). Deferred within M0103-0007: sync_remote_apply subtest, proto_version=2 streaming subxacts, `filler char(N)` bpchar padding. |

The live E2E `TestPort_PgoutputInteropPGToGoopgPgbenchKillSyncRemoteApply` in `internal/testport/pgoutput_interop_test.go` carries the full sequence (publisher + subscriber bring-up, sync-state wait, sustained workload with per-session remote_apply, mid-flight SIGKILL, multi-host fall-through INSERT, count-stabilisation poll, strict equality assertion) but is currently `t.Skip` with the verbatim PG18 diagnosis quoted in its docstring: `pg_stat_replication` consistently reports `sync_priority=0 / sync_state=async` for goopg's logical walsender despite GUC=`pg2g_ksync` (or `'*'`), `state=streaming`, `application_name` matching by `pg_strcasecmp`, `pg_is_in_recovery()=false`, and `pg_terminate_backend()`-triggered reconnects all reproducing the priority=0 state — per PG18's `SyncRepGetCandidateStandbys` line 798 a priority-0 walsender is skipped from the candidate list so `SyncRepReleaseWaiters` never fires and any session-level `remote_apply` commit hangs. Most likely cause is a per-process `SyncRepConfig` lifecycle quirk for logical walsenders. Closing requires either (a) understanding PG18's `SyncRepConfig` ordering well enough to drive `SyncRepInitConfig` into setting `MyWalSnd->sync_standby_priority > 0` (principled fix, rung 26), or (b) replacing the publisher-side `SyncRepReleaseWaiters` dependency with a goopg-side polling invariant on `pg_stat_replication.apply_lsn ≥ commit_lsn` (natural fallback). Out of scope (deferred within M0103-0007 in order): rung 26 to close the priority puzzle, proto_version=2 streaming subxacts, column-ref-typed `nextval` args, binary-format pgoutput, Scenario A milestone closure rung. |

After `Publisher.Kill()` the subscriber `count(*)` equals `killCommitted` exactly; the multi-host failover INSERT then adds 1 → strict `count(*) == killCommitted + 1`. Subscriber QueryScalar serialised across goroutines via a small `subMu sync.Mutex` since `goopgPeer.QueryScalar` dials per call and concurrent dispatcher state isn't specifically goroutine-tested. | 0104-0003 | [SIREAD Predicate-Lock Substrate (M0104-0003)](0104-0003-predicate-lock-substrate.md) | accepted | Lands the M0104-0003 SIREAD predicate-lock substrate that M0104-0004/0005's read-path / write-path SSI hooks will sit on top of. `PredicateLockTag` (`internal/mvcc/predlock.go`) is the goopg analogue of PostgreSQL's `PREDICATELOCKTARGETTAG` (`src/include/storage/predicate_internals.h`) — a four-field `(DB, Rel, Page, Offset)` struct with granularity (relation / page / tuple / invalid) encoded in sentinel fields (`Page == InvalidBlockNumber` ⇒ relation, `Offset == 0` ⇒ page, otherwise tuple); constructors `RelationLockTag` / `PageLockTag` / `TupleLockTag` panic on invalid inputs so callers commit to a granularity at construction time. `PredicateLockTag.Covers(other)` captures the implicit-coverage hierarchy: a relation-level lock covers every page/tuple in that relation, a page-level lock covers every tuple on that page, a tuple-level lock covers only itself, with O(1) short-circuit on `(DB, Rel)` mismatch. `SerializableXact.predicateLocks` becomes a `map[PredicateLockTag]struct{}` (replacing the M0104-0002 forward-declared empty placeholder) so coverage checks and coarsening pruning are O(holdings) without slice reshuffling; nil until first acquire so M0104-0002's zero-cost RC/RR contract holds. `Manager.predicateLocks` (`predicateLocksRegistry`) holds the global inverted index `targets map[PredicateLockTag]*predicateLockTarget` (target → holder set of `SerializableXact` handles) that M0104-0005's conflict-out hook will walk to discover concurrent SIREAD readers when a serializable writer touches a target. Empty target slots are evicted on the last release so the global map size tracks live (target, holder) pairs exactly. `Manager.AcquirePredicateLock(handle, tag)` is the single entry point: reject invalid tag, no-op for non-SERIALIZABLE handles (RC/RR/finished xacts pass silently), idempotent under existing coarser coverage (no maps touched), prune every owned tag the new tag covers (e.g. acquiring a relation lock prunes its tuple/page sub-locks), install the new tag in both maps, then run the coarsening cascade. `coarsenAfterAcquireLocked` runs three stages finest-first — per-page (tuple count on the same page > `PerPage` → page-level promotion), per-relation (page count on the same rel > `PerRelation` → relation-level promotion), per-xact ceiling (total holdings > `PerXact` → promote the busiest `(db, rel)` footprint, tie-breaker `(db, rel)` ascending for deterministic test behaviour under randomised map iteration). `promoteToPageLocked` / `promoteToRelationLocked` are the two primitive promotions; both detach every covered tag from both maps before attaching the coarser tag so the substrate-wide invariant "an xact never holds two tags where one covers the other" holds at every transition. `Manager.releasePredicateLocksLocked(handle)` is called from `releaseSerializableLocked` *before* `FinishedAt` is stamped — the `SerializableXact` is still addressable via the registry while the release runs, so future tooling can rejoin both pieces. Three GUCs registered in `internal/config/defaults.go` (`max_predicate_locks_per_xact` BootVal=64 range=[10, 1<<30] ContextPostmaster; `max_predicate_locks_per_relation` BootVal=-2 range=[-1<<30, 1<<30] ContextSigHup; `max_predicate_locks_per_page` BootVal=2 range=[0, 1<<16] ContextSigHup) mirror `postgres/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c` so existing postgresql.conf templates / pgbench setups / parameter probes keep working; PG's `-N` shorthand for per-relation is surfaced verbatim and the server-side bridge into `Manager.SetPredicateLockLimits` (lands when M0104-0004 wires the read-path hook through the executor) is the only resolver into positive thresholds. `Manager.SetPredicateLockLimits` accepts partial overrides — non-positive values are ignored field-by-field so tests can adjust one dimension without resetting the others. Regression pins (`internal/mvcc/predlock_test.go`): `TestPredicateLockTag_Granularity`, `TestPredicateLockTag_Covers`, `TestPredicateLock_AcquireOnlyForSerializable`, `TestPredicateLock_AcquireAndReleaseOnCommit` (table-driven over commit + rollback), `TestPredicateLock_IdempotentUnderCoarserOwnership`, `TestPredicateLock_AcquireCoarserPrunesFiner`, `TestPredicateLock_PerPageCoarsening`, `TestPredicateLock_PerRelationCoarsening`, `TestPredicateLock_PerXactOverflowCoarsens`, `TestPredicateLock_GlobalTargetHoldersTrackMultipleXacts`, `TestPredicateLock_InvalidTagRejected`, `TestPredicateLock_LimitsRoundTrip`; plus `internal/config/guc_test.go::TestPredicateLockGUCDefaults` (boot values 64 / -2 / 2 + range gates including PG's `per_xact >= 10` floor). Out of scope (deferred to M0104-0004..0006): read-path / write-path hooks that call `AcquirePredicateLock` and traverse the holder set; rw-edge bookkeeping (`inConflicts` / `outConflicts` remain empty placeholders on `SerializableXact`); post-commit retention for finished xacts whose locks must still participate in dangerous-structure detection (substrate currently releases on finish; M0104-0006 will revisit retention once the conflict graph exists, switching the release path to a deferred-cleanup queue keyed on `FinishedAt` without changing the Acquire/Holds/Release/Count API surface); index-am-specific predicate-target shapes (B-tree page-range locks, GIN/GiST nuances — index-range coverage will piggyback on page-level coverage when the read-path hooks land). |
| 0104-0004 | [Read-Path SSI Conflict-In Hook (M0104-0004)](0104-0004-ssi-conflict-out-hook.md) | accepted | Lands the read-path half of M0104's rw-conflict edge machinery, the goopg analogue of `CheckForSerializableConflictOut` in `postgres/src/backend/storage/lmgr/predicate.c`. New `Manager.CheckForSerializableConflictOut(readerHandle, writerXID)` (`internal/mvcc/ssi_conflict.go`) is called by the read path when a SERIALIZABLE reader observes a tuple version whose xmin/xmax was written by another xact: if both reader and writer are in `ssiState.xacts`, install an rw-conflict edge R→W in both directions (`reader.outConflicts += writer`, `writer.inConflicts += reader`). Returns true iff the edge was new — idempotent on repeat calls so the executor can call once per visible tuple without dedup logic. No-op (returns false) when: writerXID is Invalid/Bootstrap/Frozen (system writers skip SSI), readerHandle is not in `ssiState.xacts` (RC/RR/finished readers skip), reader's own XID matches writerXID (self-modify is not a conflict), or writerXID resolves to no live SerializableXact (RC/RR writer, or already-finished writer — retention is M0104-0006's concern). Writer lookup via `serializableXactByXIDLocked` does a linear scan of `ssiState.xacts` — the in-flight SERIALIZABLE set is bounded by `max_connections` so a dedicated XID-keyed map adds allocation/sync cost without measurable benefit at the current scale; if profiling later shows the scan dominates, the substrate's attach/lifecycle code is the natural place to maintain a parallel `xid → *SerializableXact` index. Edge installation via polarity-agnostic `registerRWConflictLocked(from, to)` — M0104-0005's write-path hook will reuse the same helper with the polarity reversed (writer discovers reader via SIREAD lock holder set instead of via tuple xmin/xmax); both must produce the same R→W edge orientation. Critical correctness invariant lands in `releaseSerializableLocked` (`internal/mvcc/ssi.go`): every release now calls `removeSerializableXactFromPeersLocked(sx)` *before* nulling its own slices and removing from `ssiState.xacts`, scrubbing references to the dying xact from every peer's in/outConflicts slices. Without scrub, surviving peers retain dangling pointers to xacts that are no longer in the registry, breaking the M0104-0006 dangerous-structure walker and leaking memory. `removeSerializableXactFromSlice` does the in-place compaction and zeros the released tail so the dying xact's pointer is eligible for GC. Diagnostic helpers `OutConflictCount`, `InConflictCount`, `HasRWConflict` expose the slices for tests and future tooling; the M0104-0006 walker will use package-internal accessors directly so the public diagnostics never become a critical path. Regression pins (`internal/mvcc/ssi_conflict_test.go`): `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_RegistersEdgeBetweenSerializable` (happy path — both directions installed, reverse direction NOT installed so edges are directed), `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_IdempotentEdgeInstall` (second call returns false, counts stay at 1), `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_NoOpForRCReader` + `_NoOpForRRReader` (non-SERIALIZABLE readers never install edges), `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_NoOpForRCWriter` (RC writer never appears in `ssiState.xacts`), `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_NoOpForSelfXID` (reader's own XID skipped), `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_NoOpForReservedXIDs` (Invalid/Bootstrap/Frozen all skipped), `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_NoOpForFinishedWriter` (writer committed before the call — silent no-op until M0104-0006 retention lands), `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_NoOpForUnknownReader` (defensive — bad handle returns false without panicking), `TestSerializableXact_PeerEdgesScrubbedOnCommit` + `_OnAbort` (after one side finishes, the surviving side's slice no longer contains the dying pointer), `TestCheckForSerializableConflictOut_MultiplePeersDistinctEdges` (one reader vs three writers, reader's outConflicts grows to 3, each writer's inConflicts stays at 1). Out of scope (deferred to M0104-0005..0007): write-path `CheckForSerializableConflictIn` (M0104-0005 — reuses `registerRWConflictLocked` with reversed polarity); pre-commit `Doomed` evaluation and SQLSTATE 40001 abort on dangerous-structure detection (M0104-0006); post-commit retention so committed writers stay conflict-relevant until in-flight readers finish (M0104-0006 — release path moves to a deferred-cleanup queue keyed on `FinishedAt` without changing the public API surface); call-site wiring at every executor read path (M0104-0007 promotes deferred D-002 isolation tests, forcing real integration through this hook). |
| 0104-0005 | [Write-Path SSI Conflict-In Hook (M0104-0005)](0104-0005-ssi-conflict-in-hook.md) | accepted | Lands the write-path half of M0104's rw-conflict edge machinery — the goopg analogue of `CheckForSerializableConflictIn` in `postgres/src/backend/storage/lmgr/predicate.c`. New `Manager.CheckForSerializableConflictIn(writerHandle, tag)` (`internal/mvcc/ssi_conflict.go`) is called by the write path when a SERIALIZABLE writer is about to modify the target identified by `tag`: if the writer is in `ssiState.xacts`, walk the predicate-lock holder set on the exact tag plus every covering ancestor (`tuple → page → relation`), and for each holder ≠ writer install an rw-conflict edge `R → W` via the polarity-agnostic `registerRWConflictLocked` helper M0104-0004 introduced — same edge orientation, same idempotence semantics, same in/outConflicts slices, so the M0104-0006 dangerous-structure walker sees a single consistent graph regardless of which side discovered the conflict first. Returns true iff at least one new edge was installed; existing edges (idempotent calls) and self-references (a SERIALIZABLE xact may legitimately read a tuple before writing it) do not count. No-op (returns false) when: tag is invalid (Rel == 0), writerHandle is not in `ssiState.xacts` (RC/RR/finished writers skip), `m.predicateLocks.targets == nil` (zero predicate locks ever acquired — single-probe short-circuit keeps the cost zero for SERIALIZABLE workloads that have not read anything yet), or no holder is found on the exact or any covering tag (the most common hot-path case, designed to make executor wiring safe to leave on for non-SERIALIZABLE workloads too). Coverage discovery via `coveringPredicateLockTags(tag)` returns `[tuple, page, relation]` for tuple tags, `[page, relation]` for page tags, and `[relation]` for relation tags — finest-first ordering is observable in tests but never load-bearing for correctness because `registerRWConflictLocked` is idempotent. Finer descendants are deliberately not included — PostgreSQL's `CheckForSerializableConflictIn` uses the same upward-only pattern via `GetParentPredicateLockTag`, and goopg's heap workload writes at the finest granularity, so the descendant case does not arise. Self-conflict handling: the loop's `holder == writerHandle` guard skips the writer's own SIREAD when present (distinct from the read-path's `reader.XID == writerXID` guard — the write-path discovers holders by handle, so the comparison is on handle, not XID). No new lifecycle code in this slice — the M0104-0004 invariant in `releaseSerializableLocked` (`removeSerializableXactFromPeersLocked` runs before nulling own slices and removing from `ssiState.xacts`) already covers edges installed via the write-path because both sides use the same in/outConflicts slices; `TestCheckForSerializableConflictIn_PeerEdgesScrubbedOnReaderCommit` pins this from the symmetric counterpart angle. Regression pins (`internal/mvcc/ssi_conflict_test.go`): `TestCheckForSerializableConflictIn_RegistersEdgeForExactSIREADHolder` (happy path, both directions, reverse not installed), `_IdempotentEdgeInstall` (second call returns false), `_FiresOnPageLockHoldingForTupleWrite` (page-level holder fires for tuple write), `_FiresOnRelationLockHoldingForTupleWrite` (relation-level holder fires for tuple write), `_NoOpForFinerDescendantHolder` (unrelated reader tuple lock on same page does NOT fire), `_NoOpForDifferentRelation` (relation-level reader on a different relation stays disjoint), `_NoOpForRCWriter` (RC writer never appears in `ssiState.xacts`), `_NoOpForSelfHolder` (writer holding its own SIREAD on the target it then writes is not a self-conflict), `_NoOpForInvalidTag` (defensive against caller bugs), `_NoOpForUnknownWriter` (defensive — bad handle returns false without panicking), `_NoHoldersIsSilentNoOp` (hot path, no allocation when no concurrent reader covers), `_MultipleReadersDistinctEdges` (one writer, three readers covering at tuple/page/relation granularities — all three receive distinct edges in a single call), `_PeerEdgesScrubbedOnReaderCommit` (lifecycle invariant from M0104-0004 covers write-path-installed edges too). Out of scope (deferred to M0104-0006..0007): pre-commit `Doomed` evaluation and SQLSTATE 40001 abort on dangerous-structure detection (M0104-0006); post-commit retention so committed readers stay conflict-relevant until in-flight writers finish, paired with the finished-writer retention deferred from M0104-0004 (M0104-0006 — release path moves to a deferred-cleanup queue keyed on `FinishedAt` without changing the public API surface); index-am-specific predicate-target shapes (B-tree page-range locks, GIN/GiST nuances — substrate currently uses heap page/tuple targets only); call-site wiring at every executor write path — `executor.heapInsert` / `heapUpdate` / `heapDelete` and the index-AM mutators (M0104-0007 promotes deferred D-002 isolation tests, forcing real integration through this hook). |
| 0104-0006 | [Pre-Commit Dangerous-Structure Detection (M0104-0006)](0104-0006-precommit-dangerous-structure-detection.md) | accepted | Closes the enforcement gap left by M0104-0003..0005: the rw-conflict graph is populated but nothing acts on it. New `Manager.PreCommitCheckForSerializationFailure(handle)` (`internal/mvcc/ssi_precommit.go`) runs the goopg analogue of PostgreSQL's `PreCommit_CheckForSerializationFailure` (`postgres/src/backend/storage/lmgr/predicate.c`) over the rw-conflict graph reachable from the committing SERIALIZABLE transaction: if `me.Doomed` is set, return `*SerializationFailureError` (SQLSTATE `40001`, reason "Canceled on identification as a pivot, during commit attempt"); otherwise walk `me.inConflicts` for each pivot, walk pivot's `inConflicts` for each Tin candidate, and set `pivot.Doomed = true` when (Tin == me) — the 2-cycle write-skew case — or when (Tin is in-flight and not doomed) — the 3-cycle generic dangerous structure case. The committing xact itself is never doomed by its own scan, mirroring upstream's "letting it commit ensures progress" policy. Hook lives in `Manager.finish` at the top of the SERIALIZABLE + XactCommit branch, running BEFORE the WAL xact-marker hook, BEFORE `releaseSerializableLocked`, BEFORE `delete(m.active, handle)`. On detection the transaction stays in `m.active` and the caller MUST invoke `Manager.Rollback(tx)` to drive the actual abort (the executor's existing `execRollback` path is reused once M0104-0007 surfaces the typed error as `ExecError{Code: "40001"}`). Doom-the-pivot semantics match upstream's `SXACT_FLAG_DOOMED`: the pivot continues executing, only its next commit attempt fails — this is what makes the progress guarantee work, because aborting the pivot synchronously would let it retry and re-fail on the same anomaly while the committing xact's writes are still uncommitted. New typed error `mvcc.SerializationFailureError` (`Reason string`, `Error() string`, `SQLSTATE() string` returning `"40001"`) plus convenience predicate `mvcc.IsSerializationFailure(err error) bool` (errors.As wrapper) so executor callers can recognise the failure without type-asserting through the mvcc package. Test-only mutators `Manager.MarkDoomedForTest` / `Manager.IsDoomedForTest` expose the internal Doomed bit so the "self already doomed" branch can be pinned without driving a full 2-cycle setup; production callers must reach the bit through the pre-commit scan, never directly. Zero footprint for RC/RR (never registered in `ssiState.xacts` — single map probe exits) and for read-only SERIALIZABLE workloads (empty inConflicts slice — outer for-loop iterates zero times). Regression pins (`internal/mvcc/ssi_precommit_test.go`): `TestPreCommitCheck_NoOpForRC` (RC commit cleanly), `_NoOpForReadOnlySerializable` (empty-graph SERIALIZABLE commits cleanly — no false positive), `_AlreadyDoomedReturns40001` (MarkDoomedForTest + scan + SQLSTATE check + Commit propagates + Rollback drains active set), `_WriteSkewDoomsPivot` (canonical 2-cycle via write-path hook end-to-end through Manager.finish — pins the M0104 DoD anomaly pattern at the mvcc layer), `_ThreeNodeCycleDoomsPivot` (3-node `T0 -rw-> Pivot -rw-> Me` dooms Pivot on Me's commit; T0 commits cleanly; Pivot's later commit returns 40001), `_LinearChainIsSafe` (already-committed T0's edges scrubbed by M0104-0004 invariant; Me's scan finds nothing to doom; all three xacts commit cleanly — pins no false-positive on linear chains), `_FinishedPivotIgnored` (defensive — manually-stamped FinishedAt makes scan skip the pivot), `_IdempotentDoomedPivot` (second scan on same graph is no-op; pivot stays doomed; doomed pivot's commit still returns 40001). Out of scope (deferred to M0104-0007/beyond): executor read/write-path call-site wiring for `Manager.CheckForSerializableConflictOut` / `Manager.CheckForSerializableConflictIn` (currently public but no executor caller — M0104-0007 promotes deferred D-002 isolation specs and forces real integration); executor-level conversion of `*SerializationFailureError` to `ExecError{Code: "40001"}` in `execCommit` (the mvcc-level contract is the load-bearing piece; converting the wrap is mechanical); upstream's `OnConflict_CheckForSerializationFailure` per-edge synchronous check from `FlagRWConflict` (pre-commit scan is sufficient for the M0104 DoD; per-edge variant is a pure addition that the polarity-agnostic `registerRWConflictLocked` helper is the natural injection point for, with `SerializationFailureError.Reason` already future-proofed for the upstream "Canceled on conflict out to pivot %u" phrasing); post-commit retention so committed xacts stay conflict-relevant past `FinishedAt` (current first-slice substrate scrubs at finish; the scan is correct under that policy because it runs WHILE the committing xact is still addressable and BEFORE peer-scrub — boundary-case false negatives at "T0 commits, then Me's scan would have walked into T0" are acceptable because the structure required for that miss is already caught by the first-committing xact's own scan); READ ONLY distinct lifecycle (upstream's READ-ONLY-Tin optimisation skipped — conservative absence is only false positives, never false negatives); 2PC `PREPARE TRANSACTION` interactions (goopg has no 2PC yet — upstream's `SxactIsPrepared` branch is not relevant). |
| 0104-0007 | [Executor SSI Hook Wiring (M0104-0007)](0104-0007-executor-ssi-wiring.md) | accepted | Lands the executor-side wiring that turns the M0104-0003..0006 SSI substrate into actual SERIALIZABLE enforcement at the executor layer. New `internal/executor/ssi.go` exports three helpers — `ssiActive`, `ssiRecordTupleRead`, `ssiRecordTupleWrite`, `ssiPreCommitCheck` — each guarded by an inline isolation-level test so RC/RR readers/writers/commits pay one comparison and never touch the mvcc registry. The read-path helper calls `mvcc.Manager.AcquirePredicateLock(handle, TupleLockTag(...))` then `CheckForSerializableConflictOut(handle, writerXmin)`; the write-path helper calls `CheckForSerializableConflictIn(handle, TupleLockTag(...))`. Both filter `block == InvalidBlockNumber || slot == 0` before `mvcc.TupleLockTag` to absorb the slot-0 edge case seqScanOp surfaces via `curSlot - 1`. `ssiPreCommitCheck` wraps `mvcc.SerializationFailureError` as `*ExecError{Code: "40001"}` with the upstream "could not serialize access due to read/write dependencies among transactions" prefix. Wiring sites — read path: `seqScanOp.Next` post-visibility before decode (uses curSlot-1); `indexScanOp.Next` post-HOT-resolution after page RLock release (target = actualSlot, not the index-pointed slot). Write path: `insertOp.Next` for both non-partitioned and partition-routed paths after `writeHeapRowReturning` returns the new tuple's ItemPointer; `updateOp.Next` at a single post-EPQ-loop site so HOT and non-HOT both fire with the converged `pu.slot` (the rw-conflict target a concurrent SERIALIZABLE reader would have predicate-locked); `deleteOp.Next` after the `epqSkipDel` filter so concurrent-abort victims do not register a phantom rw-edge. Commit path: `transactionOp.execCommit` runs `ssiPreCommitCheck` AFTER the deferred-FK check and BEFORE `TxnMgr.Commit`; on detection it drives `TxnMgr.Rollback` + `EndExplicitTransaction` + `clearCtxTransaction` before returning the 40001 ExecError so the session exits the explicit-transaction state with rollback semantics and no commit record is burned. Out of scope (deferred to M0104-0008/beyond): non-user-facing visibility-check sites (FK enforcement, DDL scans, ANALYZE, MERGE, ON CONFLICT, apply-worker, TOAST chunk fetch — predicate-locking these would inflate the SIREAD set on every internal MVCC reader); index-target predicate locks for btree range-boundary phantom detection (the heap-grain wiring is sufficient for the M0104 DoD 2-cycle pattern); end-to-end SQL-driven write-skew tests through two concurrent sessions (staged for M0104-0008 oracle isolation-test promotion which owns the multi-session harness); upstream's `OnConflict_CheckForSerializationFailure` per-edge synchronous check (the polarity-agnostic `registerRWConflictLocked` helper is the natural injection point if latency-sensitive workloads need the earlier abort). Regression pins (`internal/executor/ssi_test.go`, 8 tests): `TestSSI_RecordTupleRead_NoOpForRC`, `_NoOpForRR`, `_AcquiresPredicateLockForSerializable` (read-path acquire + peer SERIALIZABLE write through write-path helper → R→W edge installed end-to-end), `_InvalidTagFiltered` (InvalidBlockNumber/slot==0 absorbed before TupleLockTag panics), `_ZeroHandleSkipped` (Handle==0 short-circuits even when isolation tag is SERIALIZABLE), `TestSSI_ExecCommit_ReturnsSerializationFailureWhenDoomed` (BEGIN SERIALIZABLE + MarkDoomedForTest + COMMIT → ExecError{Code:"40001"} + session cleared + ActiveCount==0), `TestSSI_ExecCommit_NoOpForRC`, `TestSSI_ExecCommit_HappyPathForSerializable` (no false positive on isolated SERIALIZABLE). |
| 0104-0008 | [SSI Oracle-Test Promotion & M0104 Closeout (M0104-0008)](0104-0008-ssi-promotion-and-closeout.md) | accepted | Closes M0104 by promoting applicable deferred SERIALIZABLE/SSI tests in `internal/testport` and evidencing DoD #2/#4. Lands `internal/testport/ssi_write_skew_test.go` — four pass-required multi-session SQL-driven Go tests that enact the canonical simple-write-skew permutations against a live goopg cluster: `TestPort_SSI_WriteSkew_NoOverlap_BothCommit` (sequential SERIALIZABLE — both commit), `_Overlap_SecondCommitterAborts` (rwx1 rwx2 c1 c2 → c2 returns SQLSTATE 40001), `_Overlap_FirstCommitterAborts` (rwx1 rwx2 c2 c1 → c1 returns SQLSTATE 40001), `_RC_NoSerializationFailure` (READ COMMITTED + REPEATABLE READ control — overlap shape MUST NOT trip 40001; guards the `ssiActive` short-circuit). Why focused Go tests instead of promoting upstream spec files: `framework.IsolationRunner` only runs spec-declared `permutation` directives — auto-permutation generation (the upstream `isolationtester.c` default) is not implemented, so `simple-write-skew.spec` and SSI-adjacent neighbours that omit explicit permutations cannot be driven through `TestPort_IsolationSuite` without a runner upgrade that itself owns the D-002 infrastructure; the focused Go tests express the same end-to-end shape against the wire protocol. Four load-bearing gap fixes uncovered by the new tests: (1) **`BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL <level>` was silently ignored on the simple-query path** — `internal/server/dispatch.go` `TxBegin` branch called `connTx.Begin(ctx.Tx)` on the placeholder RC tx allocated at dispatch entry, bypassing `transactionOp.execBegin` where M0096-0002's isolation-level parsing lives; fix promotes the placeholder by rolling it back and `Begin(parsedLvl)`-ing a fresh tx + snapshot when `txNode.IsolationLevel != ""` and the parsed level differs. (2) **`COMMIT` bypassed `ssiPreCommitCheck` on the simple-query path** — the same dispatcher called `TxnMgr.Commit(connTx.Tx())` directly without the pre-commit dangerous-structure walk; fix gates the dispatch-side commit on `PreCommitCheckForSerializationFailure(handle)` for SERIALIZABLE explicit transactions and translates a hit to wire-protocol SQLSTATE 40001 with the upstream wording, mirroring the executor path. (3) **`scanMatching` (UPDATE/DELETE inner scan) didn't fire the SSI read hook** — `updateOp` / `deleteOp` use a separate heap-page walk (`internal/executor/operators_storage.go`) that never went through seqScanOp.Next where M0104-0007 added `ssiRecordTupleRead`; fix invokes the hook immediately after visibility (before predicate filter) so the SIREAD covers every tuple the UPDATE/DELETE ever observed, matching upstream `predicate.c` semantics. (4) **`ssiRecordTupleRead` only checked the visible writer's xmin** — original wiring missed the write-skew shape where the reader's MVCC snapshot hides the concurrent writer's new version and the OLD version it sees carries the concurrent writer's XID in `tuple.Header.Xmax`; fix extends helper signature to take `writerXmax storage.TransactionID` and invokes `CheckForSerializableConflictOut(handle, xmax)` whenever `xmax != xmin`. Three call sites (seqScanOp, indexScanOp, scanMatching) pass `tuple.Header.Xmax` alongside `tuple.Header.Xmin`. Together the fixes close the 2-cycle write-skew end-to-end: s1's UPDATE seqScan installs SIREAD on every tuple observed (including slot=1 'apple'); s2's UPDATE writes slot=1, which fires `CheckForSerializableConflictIn` and installs the s1→s2 edge; s2's UPDATE seqScan reads slot=2 whose `xmax = s1.XID` because s1 marked it for update, which fires `CheckForSerializableConflictOut(s2, s1.XID)` and installs the s2→s1 edge; pre-commit on the second committer walks `me.inConflicts`, finds the 2-cycle through the pivot's `inConflicts`, and the second committer's `Doomed` flag is set so its `COMMIT` returns SQLSTATE 40001. Files touched: new `internal/testport/ssi_write_skew_test.go`; `internal/executor/ssi.go` (helper signature + xmax conflict-out); `internal/executor/operators_storage.go` (scanMatching read hook + seqScanOp.Next xmax); `internal/executor/operators_index.go` (indexScanOp.Next xmax); `internal/executor/ssi_test.go` (existing call sites updated to pass `storage.InvalidTransactionID` for xmax — no behaviour change to MarkDoomedForTest-driven pins); `internal/server/dispatch.go` (TxBegin isolation-level promotion + TxCommit SSI pre-commit check). Regression gates: `go test ./internal/executor/ ./internal/mvcc/ ./internal/server/` all green; `go test -run TestPort_SSI_WriteSkew ./internal/testport/` 4/4 pass. Out of scope: auto-permutation in `framework.IsolationRunner`; `SHOW transaction_isolation` GUC tracking the active transaction's isolation level (currently always reads the session-default GUC; new tests do not depend on it — SQLSTATE assertion is load-bearing); READ-ONLY DEFERRABLE optimisation; `OnConflict_CheckForSerialization`; index-target predicate locks for btree range-boundary phantoms (staged per M0104 milestone doc's "Out of Scope" section). |
| 0104-0001 | [Serializable (SSI) Foundation and GUC Parity (M0104)](0104-0001-serializable-ssi-foundation.md) | accepted | M0104-0002 landed 2026-05-14: `mvcc.SerializableXact` introduced in `internal/mvcc/ssi.go` as the goopg analogue of PostgreSQL's `SERIALIZABLEXACT` (`src/include/storage/predicate_internals.h`). `mvcc.Manager` gains an embedded handle-keyed `ssiState` registry (lazy-init: RC/RR workloads stay zero-cost) plus a monotonic `CommitSeqNo` allocator. `Manager.Begin` registers a fresh `SerializableXact` for `IsolationSerializable` only (RC/RR skip), `Manager.AssignXID` stamps the new top-level XID onto `SerializableXact.XID` so future conflict-detection paths can look up xacts by writer XID, and `Manager.finish` releases on both commit and abort by stamping `FinishedAt` with a dense, monotonically-increasing `CommitSeqNo`. Empty placeholder slots for `inConflicts` / `outConflicts` / `predicateLocks` keep the struct shape stable so M0104-0003..0005 can fill them in without changing the lifecycle API. Regression pins (`internal/mvcc/ssi_test.go`): `TestSerializableXact_BeginRegistersAndCommitReleases`, `TestSerializableXact_RollbackAlsoReleases`, `TestSerializableXact_AssignXIDStampsTopXid`, `TestSerializableXact_NotRegisteredForRCorRR`, `TestSerializableXact_CommitSeqNoMonotonic`. M0104-0001 landed 2026-05-14: `mvcc.IsolationSerializable` is now a distinct enum constant from `IsolationRepeatableRead`, `ParseIsolationLevel("serializable")` returns it without aliasing, and `mvcc.Manager.Begin` + `executor.BasicSession.SetIsolationLevel` accept the new tag so BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE / SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE round-trip the new isolation onto the open transaction (`Transaction.Isolation == IsolationSerializable`). Snapshot acquisition still reuses the RR pinned-snapshot branch deliberately — this is the SI half of SSI; the predicate-lock + rw-edge overlay lands in M0104-0003..0005 without changing snapshot semantics. `default_transaction_isolation` and `transaction_isolation` GUCs already accepted `"serializable"` (PG EnumOptions parity). Regression pins: `internal/mvcc/manager_test.go::TestParseIsolationLevel` + `TestSerializableDistinctFromRepeatableRead` and `internal/executor/transaction_test.go::TestTransactionBeginSerializableSession`. Establishes PostgreSQL-aligned SERIALIZABLE delivery scope for goopg: canonical GUC naming (`default_transaction_isolation`, `transaction_isolation`), separation from REPEATABLE READ runtime, predicate-lock (SIREAD) target model, rw-conflict tracking hooks, and pre-commit dangerous-structure abort policy with SQLSTATE 40001. References `guc_tables.c`, `xact.c`, and `predicate.c` as the upstream oracle for naming and SSI semantics. |

| 0107-0012 | [WAL drain-safety: LSN-0 idle sentinel + Path A appendMu discipline (M-NIGHTLY)](0107-0012-wal-drain-lsn0-sentinel-and-pathA-lock.md) | accepted | Fixes the `race/internal/wal` nightly REOPEN (AI-20260717-010601-001): a genuine data race in `TestDrainSafetyStress` where the drain goroutine's `writeAt` reads WAL ring bytes a fast-path stripe writer's `writeReserved` is still writing. A deterministic assertion (`writeReserved` panics when `lsn < tail`) exposed **two** root causes. (1) `insertionTracker`'s idle sentinel `lsnIdle` was `0`, which aliases the legitimate byte-LSN-0 first reservation on a fresh/reset `walBuffer` — `lowestActiveLSN` treated the LSN-0 stripe as idle, so the tail publisher advanced the drain watermark past a still-being-written record; fixed by `lsnIdle = -1` (never a valid byte-LSN) with the constructor explicitly initialising every slot. (2) `appendPGCompat` Path A (direct file write, bypassing the ring, not reserving its LSN range in the tracker) **released** `appendMu` across its `writeAt` despite its comment claiming otherwise; concurrent RLock stripe writers then reserved into Path A's range and published a tail that the trailing `walBuf.reset(end)` rewound — landing a `writeReserved` below the rewound tail; fixed by holding `appendMu.Lock()` across the whole Path A section. Verified: 0/60 below-tail writes (was 25/25 pre-fix-1, ~55/60 after fix-1 alone), `TestDrainSafetyStress` 40/40 under `-race`, whole-package `-race` 3/3, unit + vet clean, pgbench smoke PASS. Distinct from the test-only [[0107-0011]]. |

| 0107-0007e | [Phase D4 — `selectFSMCandidatePage` Heap-Insert Page-Selection Helper (M0107-0007, slice C executor consumer foundation)](0107-0007e-select-fsm-candidate-page.md) | accepted | Combines slice C foundations (1) `FSM.GetCandidates` and (3) `Pool.SlotPinCount` into the read-only selection step of parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §3's `selectInsertPage`. Asks the FSM for up to four candidate pages with enough free space, then walks them probing `Pool.SlotPinCount` and returns the candidate with the lowest live pin count; short-circuits on the first pin-0 hit (the common case costs one `bufmap.Lookup`); returns `(0, false)` when no candidate qualifies or every candidate is ≥ `hotPinThreshold` so the caller falls through to the heap-extend path instead of re-pinning a hot page. No locks held across the body — `FSM.GetCandidates` takes its own RLock for the scan and returns a fresh slice; `SlotPinCount` is the lock-free seqlock `bufmap.Lookup` + `state.Load` from [[0107-0007d]]. Nil-safe (`fsm == nil \|\| pool == nil → (0, false)`) so the heap-insert path can call it before FSM is initialised (catalog bootstrap before `pg_init`). Decouples selection (pure, unit-testable, no on-disk effect) from the call-site rewrite of `writeHeapRowReturning` / `writeHeapRowReturningPG` — the rewrite plus the batched-extend fallback via [[0107-0007c]] `Pool.ExtendRelationBatch` lands in the next loop together with the PG-compat WAL byte-diff gate from the parent milestone. Slice B (8-stripe `wal.Writer.appendLocks` per parent §2) stays deferred — splitting `state.appendMu`'s four invariants is multi-loop scope. Regression coverage in `internal/executor/heap_insert_select_test.go` (five tests against a real `storage.Manager`+`Pool`+`FSM` fixture, no mocks): `TestSelectFSMCandidatePageNilInputs` (nil-safe early returns); `TestSelectFSMCandidatePageEmptyFSM` (no FSM candidate ≥ minFreeBytes → fall-through); `TestSelectFSMCandidatePageRanksByPinCount` (three FSM entries pin counts 2/0/1 → block 1); `TestSelectFSMCandidatePageShortCircuitsOnPinZero` (block 0 unpinned, block 1 over-`hotPinThreshold` pinned, helper deterministically returns block 0); `TestSelectFSMCandidatePageRejectsHotCandidates` (all four candidates ≥ `hotPinThreshold` → `(0, false)`); `TestSelectFSMCandidatePagePicksAmongModeratelyPinned` (pin counts 3/1/2 → pin=1 block, independent of zero-short-circuit). Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestSelectFSMCandidatePage' ./internal/executor/` PASS (1.03 s); `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/executor/` PASS (2.79 s). PG-compat — none (read-only in-memory helper; FSM on-disk format / bufmap layout / WAL / catalog / wire all unchanged; not yet on any production code path until the call-site rewrite lands). |
| 0107-0007d | [Phase D4 — `Pool.SlotPinCount` Lock-Free Pin-Count Probe (M0107-0007, slice C foundation 3 of 3)](0107-0007d-pool-slot-pin-count.md) | accepted | Adds `Pool.SlotPinCount(tag BufferTag) int32` to `internal/storage/bufpool.go` — third and final primitive parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §3 needs for the FSM-driven heap-insert path. Returns the live pin count of `tag`'s slot or 0 if `tag` is not currently mapped / valid / current-generation; helper spec from [[06-bufpool-lockfree]] §4 ("Helper: `Pool.SlotPinCount`"). The `!stateValid` guard catches eviction-window slots before the gen comparison (cheaper primary check). Isolating bit-layout knowledge behind the helper keeps future `slotState` re-packings (`slotPinMask` / `slotGenShift` / `slotValidBit`) from rippling into FSM ranking code. PG-compat — none (in-memory bufpool API addition; bufmap on-disk format / WAL / catalog / wire all unchanged; helper is read-only). |

| 0107-0007b | [Phase D4 — `FSM.GetCandidates` Top-K Free-Space Query (M0107-0007, slice C foundation)](0107-0007b-fsm-get-candidates.md) | accepted | Adds `(*FSM).GetCandidates(rel, minFreeBytes, n) []BlockNumber` to `internal/storage/fsm.go` — one of the three primitives parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §3 needs to break the c=100 simple-update tail-page convergence. | 0107-0008k | [Phase D5 — WAL Drain Byte Counters via `stats.Counter` (M0107-0008, loop 11)](0107-0008k-wal-buffer-drain-stats-counter-wiring.md) | accepted | Fifth concrete consumer of [[0107-0008f]] (after [[0107-0008g]] btree, [[0107-0008h]] MemRing, [[0107-0008i]] AIO totals, [[0107-0008j]] AIO per-direction): `walBufferCounters.overflowDrainBytes` and `.flushDrainBytes` in `internal/wal/writer.go` move from `atomic.Uint64` to `stats.Counter`. `drainBufferBytes` runs under `state.appendMu` and is therefore single-writer-at-a-time, but the writer P is whichever client backend acquires `appendMu` next — every cross-backend handoff bounces the shared counter line. Public accessors (`Writer.WALBuffersOverflowDrainBytes() uint64`, `.WALBuffersFlushDrainBytes() uint64`) preserved verbatim via `uint64(.Sum())` casts at the boundary; the `c.overflowDrainBytes.Add(uint64(n))` / `.flushDrainBytes.Add(uint64(n))` call sites in `drainBufferBytes` switch to `.Add(n)` directly (the local `n int64` matches `stats.Counter.Add(int64)`). `internal/initdb/wal_io_views.go` reads through the public accessors and observes identical types and values. Memory cost is 32 KiB per server (2 × 16 KiB Counter; exactly one walBufferCounters allocation per Writer per server). | 0107-0003d | [Parser token allocation: GC-safety of the `tokenSlicePool` fast path (M0107-0003 Phase C.3)](0107-0003d-token-pool-gc-safety.md) | accepted | Closes the Phase C.3 token-arena attempt that crashed the regress suite (`found pointer to free object`, reverted in `adfb935`). Documents two independent reasons the mctx arena fast path is *fundamentally* GC-unsafe, not merely buggy: (1) an mctx slab is a `[]byte` **noscan** span, so `Token.Value` string pointers stored in an arena-backed `[]Token` are invisible to the GC mark phase; (2) the cross-session plan cache retains some `Value` strings by reference (`SchemaColumn.Name`/alias, `StringConst.Value`, `SeqScan.Alias`), so arena release would dangle live cached plans. Decision: the heap-backed `tokenSlicePool` is the canonical, already-allocation-free fast path; `parser.Token` is permanently barred from mctx arenas (guardrail added to `AllocSlice` doc). | 0100-0006b | [UPSERT DO UPDATE: HOT-equivalent index-key reuse (M0100-0006b)](0100-0006b-upsert-hot-index-key-reuse.md) | accepted | Final fix of M0100-0006b. PG's `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` is a HOT update when no indexed column changes: it inserts zero index tuples and never re-evaluates a non-unique expression index. goopg (no HOT) re-inserted every index entry on `applyUpdate`, re-evaluating `blurt_and_lock_4(key)` → 2 extra NOTICEs after `s2_commit`. | 0100-0011 | [BEFORE/AFTER Trigger Inline Firing During UPDATE/DELETE Scan (M0100-0011)](0100-0011-evalplanqual-trigger-before-trigger-inline-firing.md) | accepted | PG fires BEFORE ROW triggers per-row during the UPDATE scan (after each row's WHERE passes, before moving to the next row). goopg's two-phase `updateOp` (Phase 1: scan all rows; Phase 2: fire BEFORE triggers, write) fired BEFORE triggers after all WHERE-condition NOTICEs for all rows, diverging from PG's interleaving order. Fix: Phase 1 inline EPQ fires BEFORE triggers immediately after EPQ resolution for all isolation levels (not RC-only). RR/SSI frozen-snapshot infinite-retry fixed via `HasAbortedXID` global check. Concurrent-delete detection fixed: goopg leaves CTID at `{InvalidBlockNumber,0}` on INSERT (never sets self-pointer), so DELETE detection uses `ctid.Block == storage.InvalidBlockNumber` rather than a self-pointer check. AFTER INSERT/BEFORE UPDATE/AFTER UPDATE triggers added to `upsertOp` ON CONFLICT paths. `TestPort_IsolationEvalPlanQualTrigger` now passes (21/21 RC isolation tests). |

Remaining index-reloptions gap tracked separately. **Follow-up (later loop):** the index-reloptions gap just named is now closed too — see "index reloptions never survived a restart either" — which also uncovered and fixed a `pg_index` heap-mirroring bug that had silently defeated index heap-scan recovery (`loadUserIndexesFromHeap`) entirely in real deployments, and a dual catalog-key registration bug: `RegisterIndexDuringRecovery`/`UnregisterIndexDuringRecovery` (unlike `RenameIndexDuringRecovery` above, which already used the slice-443 `lookupIndexLocked` helper) still did a bare `key(...)` probe, so the two recovery drivers could register the same index under different keys — switched both to `lookupIndexLocked` too, fixing a `TestRenameIndexSurvivesRestartViaWAL` regression the `pg_index`-mirror fix exposed. Partition-child index reloptions inheritance remains a separate, still-open gap (ledger). **Follow-up (later loop):** that partition-child gap is now closed too — `createPartitionChildIndexes` copies the six WITH-clause fields onto each auto-created child index (and resyncs its heap row), propagating correctly through multi-level partition recursion since the same top-level `CreateIndexStmt` is threaded down; see the design doc's "partition-child index reloptions" section. **2026-07-06 addendum:** the guard test now also probes the actual dump+restore round trip; fixed the `xmloption` GUC gap it found, and discovered the real remaining blocker is that `catalog.InMemory` has no per-database namespace at all (milestone-scale, see design doc's "DU-002 round-trip probe" section + deferral ledger). **Slice 446 (2026-07-06):** `CREATE TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION (PARSER = ...)` + `ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION ... ADD MAPPING FOR ... WITH ...` now round-trip through `pg_dump`, verified byte-for-byte against real PG 18.3; new `pg_ts_config`/`pg_ts_config_map` virtual catalogs plus a `ts_token_type(oid)` FROM-clause SRF back the dump query. Restart/WAL persistence, 42710 duplicate-mapping detection, and every other `ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION` form stay deferred (ledger). **Slice 437/446 restart-persistence follow-up (2026-07-06):** closes the restart/WAL-persistence deferral for both slices — `CREATE`/`DROP TEXT SEARCH DICTIONARY` and `CREATE TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION`/`ALTER ... ADD MAPPING`/`DROP TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION` now survive a restart via 5 new WAL record kinds (104-108, `internal/wal/recovery.go`) + two new recovery drivers (`internal/initdb/tsdict_ddl_recovery.go`, `internal/initdb/tsconfig_ddl_recovery.go`) wired into `open.go` after `replayConversionDDLRecords`, mirroring the CAST/TRANSFORM/CONVERSION/COLLATION precedent exactly. 42710 duplicate-mapping detection and the other `ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION` forms remain deferred. **Slice 446 duplicate-mapping follow-up (2026-07-06):** verified against a scratch PG 18.3 instance that re-`ADD MAPPING`ing an already-mapped token type actually raises `23505` unique_violation on `pg_ts_config_map_index` (mapseqno restarts at 1 per call), not the `42710` this milestone's ledger rows had guessed; `catalog.InMemory.AddTSConfigMapping` now detects the collision and `execAlterTSConfigAddMapping` raises PG's exact message/detail. Other `ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION` forms remain deferred. **Slice 446 RENAME/SET SCHEMA/DROP MAPPING follow-up (2026-07-06):** `ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION name {RENAME TO|SET SCHEMA|DROP MAPPING [IF EXISTS] FOR tok [, ...]}` now all work (previously discarded as a compat no-op); `AlterTSConfigAddMappingStmt` generalized to `AlterTSConfigStmt` with an `Action` field; 3 new catalog methods + 3 new WAL record kinds (109-111) + recovery-driver wiring give the same restart persistence CREATE/ADD MAPPING/DROP already have; also fixed a pre-existing bug where this whole statement type had no `ddlTag` case at all (silently tagged bare `"OK"` instead of `"ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION"`). Only `ALTER MAPPING REPLACE`/`OWNER TO`/the `CONFIGURATION = source_config` COPY form remain deferred. **Slice 446 `ALTER MAPPING REPLACE` follow-up (2026-07-06):** `ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION name ALTER MAPPING [FOR tok [, ...]] REPLACE olddict WITH newdict` now works (previously discarded as a compat no-op alongside `OWNER TO`); mirrors `MakeConfigurationMapping`'s replace path — an unconditional scan-and-substitute that silently no-ops on zero matches, not a lookup; new `catalog.ReplaceTSConfigMappingDict` + WAL record kind 112 give it the same restart persistence as its siblings; also fixed a latent `AddTSConfigMapping` aliasing bug where a multi-token-type `ADD MAPPING` call shared one `DictOIDs` backing array across every named token type, so an in-place `REPLACE` mutation on one token type corrupted its siblings. Only `OWNER TO` remains deferred (considered acceptable, not a gap). **Slice 437 `ALTER TEXT SEARCH DICTIONARY` follow-up (2026-07-06, this loop):** `ALTER TEXT SEARCH DICTIONARY name {RENAME TO|SET SCHEMA|( key [= value], ... )}` now all work (previously the whole statement fell through to the discarded compat no-op, unlike CONFIGURATION's already-implemented ALTER forms); the options-merge form mirrors `AlterTSDictionary`'s real remove-then-maybe-add-per-key semantics (a bare `key` deletes, `key = value` replaces/adds), needing a new `catalog.SerializeTSDictOptions`/`DeserializeTSDictOptions` pair since `InitOption` is stored pre-serialized with no parallel structured list; 3 new WAL record kinds (114-116) give it the same restart persistence as the CONFIGURATION siblings. Only `OWNER TO` remains deferred. **2026-07-08 addendum**: `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN col RESET (...)` now clears the named per-column attribute options (parser + executor), matching the pre-existing `SET (...)` side. **2026-07-09 follow-up (M0122-0007, foreign-server registry restart durability, `unimplemented_feat.json` DU-002-376/DU-002-378 closed)**: `catalog.InMemory.foreignServers` now survives a restart via new `wal.RecordKindCreateForeignServer`/`RecordKindDropForeignServer` (126/127) + `internal/initdb/foreignserver_ddl_recovery.go`, mirroring the tablespace-registry follow-up above; a design-review pass caught and fixed a real gap the naive port would have left — `DROP SERVER`/`DROP FOREIGN DATA WRAPPER ... CASCADE` are now gated on the durable `foreignServers` registry instead of the non-durable `compatObjects` bookkeeping, so a WAL-recovered server can be dropped/cascaded again after a restart. Live-verified via a real `goopg stop`/`start`. `CREATE USER MAPPING` restart durability remains a separate, still-open gap (ledger row). **Follow-up (2026-07-09, same day): user-mapping registry restart durability** — closes that gap. New `wal.RecordKindCreateUserMapping`/`RecordKindDropUserMapping` (128/129) + `internal/initdb/usermapping_ddl_recovery.go`, mirroring the foreign-server follow-up exactly (no correctness gap found this time — `DROP USER MAPPING` already gated on the durable `userMappings` registry, not `compatObjects`). Live-verified via a real `goopg stop`/`start` (twice): a `CREATE USER MAPPING` survives the first restart with the same `umid`/`srvid`, and a subsequent `DROP USER MAPPING` survives the second restart too (0 rows, not just the create side). **M0122-0024 addendum**: Slice 374's "per-column option/constraint form ... rejected, not supported" deferral is now half-resolved — `CREATE TABLE name OF type (col WITH OPTIONS column_constraint, ...)` genuinely parses and applies NOT NULL/DEFAULT/CHECK/etc. onto the composite-derived columns (new shared `parseColumnConstraintList` + `CreateTableStmt.OfTypeColumnOptions`); the sibling `table_constraint` form in the same paren list (PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE/CHECK/FOREIGN KEY at table level) remains explicitly rejected, tracked in the deferral ledger. **Addendum 2 (2026-07-10):** the table_constraint half is now implemented too, via a shared `parseTableConstraintElement` helper extracted from the ordinary CREATE TABLE column-list dispatch — both grammar halves interleave freely, matching PG's own mixed doc example. **Follow-up (2026-07-15, M0119-0004): CAST-target multi-word type names (DU-002)** — `parseTypeNameAfterCast` (`internal/parser/select.go`), the shared type-name parser for both `x::typename` and `CAST(x AS typename)`, now calls the existing `parseMultiWordTypeName` helper so multi-word built-in type names (`character varying`, `double precision`, `bit varying`, `timestamp/time [with\|without time zone]`) parse as CAST targets, not just as column/domain base types; unblocks the DU-002 probe past a `CREATE DOMAIN ... DEFAULT 'na'::character varying` syntax error. New deferral: the probe now hits a cross-database `CREATE FUNCTION` name-collision gap, the same collision shape the M0122-0007 4e series already fixed for type registries — next DU-002 resume point. |

The MVCC/attribute + TOAST tiers of 004 corrupt PG's `varatt_external` layout (goopg-divergent chunk-relation TOAST) and are not faithfully portable; `003_check`/`005_opclass_damage` remain deferred under CSV `AC-003`. **2026-07-07:** `002_nonesuch`'s last residual (`UPDATE pg_database SET datconnlimit = -2` invalid-database filter) is now also ported — `catalog.InMemory` gained a runtime `datconnlimit` read/write path (`SetDatabaseConnLimit`/`DatabaseConnLimit`) and `updateOp` gained a dedicated `nextVirtualPgDatabase()` execution path for this one storage-less Virtual table (the generic UPDATE executor assumes a physical heap to scan/rewrite, which `pg_database` doesn't have). `002_nonesuch.pl` now has zero remaining residuals; see this doc's "Former deferred residual — now closed" section for the full writeup. **2026-07-07 follow-up:** the still-deferred connect-time half of that residual (a client could still open a session against a `datconnlimit = -2` database) is now closed too — `catalog.DatconnlimitInvalidDB` + a new `databaseConnLimitRegistry` interface gate a check in `Server.handleStartup` (`internal/server/server.go`) right after the existing "database does not exist" gate, rejecting with the real PG FATAL `55000` `cannot connect to invalid database "..."` (mirrors `postinit.c`'s `database_is_invalid_form` check). **2026-07-07, same day, residual #2:** positive-limit connection-count throttling is now also landed — `activity.ActivityRegistry.CountByDatName` (`internal/activity/registry.go`) scans live backend slots for a matching `DatName` (no new mutable state; correct by construction since it runs after `Server.handleStartup`'s existing `reg.Register` call, giving the same self-inclusive count PG's `CountDBConnections` relies on), and a new check in `handleStartup` rejects a non-superuser connection once that count exceeds `DatabaseConnLimit`, mirroring `postinit.c`'s `CheckMyDatabase` (`ERRCODE_TOO_MANY_CONNECTIONS`/53300, `!am_superuser` bypass). `002_nonesuch`'s `datconnlimit` coverage is now fully closed, both sentinel and positive-limit halves. See this doc's "Follow-up: residual #2 — positive `datconnlimit` connection-count throttling" section. **2026-07-07, same day, AC-003 cluster unblocked:** `verify_heapam`/`bt_index_check` now report synthetic `pg_toast_<oid>`/`pg_toast_<oid>_index` relations as healthy-empty (via the pre-existing `catalog.InMemory.ToastParentTable` helper) instead of raising 42P01 — these OIDs have no real backing storage by design, so real `pg_amcheck`'s default whole-table walk (which always checks a table's TOAST relation too) no longer poisons every "pre-corruption baseline is clean" gate. `TestPort_PgAmcheck004VerifyHeapam`, `TestPort_PgAmcheckAllTables`, `TestPort_PgAmcheckBtreeIndexCheck` now genuinely PASS (previously always skipped); the four corruption-injection AC-003 tests advance past this gate but hit a new, distinct blocker (cluster restart timeout after a manually-removed relation file) — see this doc's "Follow-up (2026-07-07): AC-003 cluster unblocked" section and the deferral ledger. **2026-07-07, same day, restart-timeout blocker closed:** root cause was `internal/wal/xlog_emit.go`'s `extractRecordBytes` allocating `cap(stream)` (the entire remaining WAL input, often most of a 16 MB segment) per record instead of `wantBytes` (a single header/body, tens of bytes) — `initdb.Open` runs several independent full-WAL replay passes, so this turned a handful of small records into 20-40s of allocation+memclr, blowing the test harness's 20s restart timeout. Fixed to allocate `min(wantBytes, len(stream))` (CPU-profiled: `initdb.Open` on the repro data dir dropped from 23.57s to 0.18s); new regression test `TestExtractRecordBytesCapBoundedByWantBytes` (`internal/wal/xlog_emit_test.go`). **AC-003/AC-004 are now fully unblocked — all four corruption-injection tests pass, no open blockers remain.** See this doc's "Follow-up (2026-07-07): AC-003 restart-timeout blocker closed" section. **2026-07-08, `DatabaseConnLimit` unset-default fix:** `DatabaseConnLimit(name)` returned the Go zero-value `0` (means "reject all" in PG) instead of `-1` ("no limit") for any database without an explicit `SetDatabaseConnLimit` override — i.e. every database in a fresh cluster — so every non-superuser role's first-ever connection anywhere was rejected with `too many connections`. Fixed via the map's comma-ok lookup; `TestConnectNonSuperuserFirstConnectionUnlimitedDatabaseAccepted` added. WHERE amproc = ...` corruption-injection statement actually takes effect instead of silently affecting 0 rows; also fixed an adjacent bug found while testing this (a bare builtin proc name cast to `regproc`/`regprocedure`, e.g. `'int4eq'::regproc`, wrongly raised 42883 since the cast only checked `Routines()` and not `catalog.LookupBuiltinProc`'s builtin fallback). **Still deferred**: the btree AM has no per-index comparator dispatch at all, so a corrupted `amproc` remains unobservable to `pg_amcheck` — `005_opclass_damage.pl` needs that separate, larger index-AM change before it can pass end-to-end. See this doc's "Follow-up (2026-07-08): `005_opclass_damage.pl` UPDATE-path prerequisite" section. |

| 0110-0005 | [verify_heapam page-structural verification engine (M0110)](0110-0005-verify-heapam-engine.md) | accepted (partial) | Lands the reusable, fully-unit-tested **core** of amcheck's `verify_heapam()` — the page-structural integrity checker (`postgres/contrib/amcheck/verify_heapam.c`) — as a standalone `internal/amcheck` package (`VerifyHeapPage`), decoupled from any SQL/SRF wiring (engine-first, mirroring the M0102-0010 checksum engine). Tier 1 only: line-pointer bounds/alignment, redirect-target validity, and tuple-header `t_hoff` consistency — deterministic functions of the raw 8 KiB page bytes (no clog/TupleDesc/toast). Corruption messages are mirrored verbatim from upstream so the later SRF + `004_verify_heapam` port reuse them. 11 unit tests (clean empty/new/tuple pages → no reports; targeted corruptions → exact upstream message). Deferred (with resume points): the HOT-chain tier, the MVCC/attribute tier (xmin/xmax/multixact/TOAST), and the SQL surface (`CREATE EXTENSION amcheck` + the `verify_heapam` SRF) that promotes `AC-002` (`002_nonesuch`) — the SQL surface waits for a clean working tree (current uncommitted gen-column WIP across parser/planner/executor/catalog). Keystone blocker for the four deferred pg_amcheck TAP tests. Loop #55 adds the index-side companion `verify_nbtree.go` (`VerifyBtreePage`): the page-structural `palloc_btree_page` tier — metapage magic/version + leaf/internal page-level consistency, verbatim upstream messages, reading goopg's B-tree layout through new exported `btree.ParseMeta`/`ParseOpaque` accessors (single source of truth); 10 unit tests. PG-divergent high-key-as-item and `MaxIndexTuplesPerPage` checks documented as not-ported. Loop #56 adds the second index tier `VerifyBtreeItemOrder` — `bt_target_page_check`'s page-local item-order (strict ascending) + high-key invariant (`<=` leaf / `<` internal) checks, verbatim upstream messages, via new exported `btree.PageItemKeys` (one separator key per line pointer, collapsing posting lists) + `CompareKeys`; negative-infinity empty key and rightmost gating handled; 10 amcheck tests + 1 btree `TestPageItemKeys`. Loop #57 adds the third index tier — the item-count ceiling folded into `VerifyBtreePage` (`palloc_btree_page`'s `maxoffset > MaxIndexTuplesPerPage` check): a page whose line-pointer count exceeds what can physically fit is corrupt. The bound is goopg's own per-item footprint, exported as `btree.MaxItemsPerPage` = `(BlockSize - SizeOfPageHeaderData) / (4 + itemPrefixSize)` = 680 (goopg stores items unaligned; single source of truth beside `itemPrefixSize`), with upstream-verbatim message. 5 new tests (constant pin, at/over ceiling, damaged pd_lower, deleted-page suppression). Loop #58 adds the first **cross-page** index tier `VerifyBtreeLevelSiblingLinks` — the sibling-link checks `bt_check_level_from_leftmost` performs walking one level left-to-right: left-link/right-link agreement (`left link/right link pair … not in agreement`), per-level `btpo_level` uniformity, and circular-chain detection (visited-set, subsumes upstream's immediate `current==leftcurrent` check + bounds longer cycles), plus deleted-page-reached-via-sibling. Takes a minimal `PageSource func(BlockNumber)(Page,error)` seam (the SQL surface fills it from smgr; tests use an in-memory map) so it stays new-file/additive; 10 tests. Loop #59 adds the **cross-level** index tier `VerifyBtreeParentDownlinks` — `bt_child_check`'s per-downlink checks: follows every downlink of an internal parent to its child (via the same `PageSource` seam + new exported `btree.PageDownlinks` decoding `(separator key, child block)` entries) and enforces downlink-to-deleted (`downlink to deleted page found`), child-level-one-down (`downlink points to block … whose level is not one level down`), and the down-link lower-bound invariant (`down-link lower bound invariant violated`). goopg-faithful divergences: an **inclusive** lower bound (`childKey >= K_i`, since `findChildBlock` routes to the rightmost item `<=` key, so children cover `[K_i, K_{i+1})`) vs upstream's strict heapkeyspace `<`, and skipping the internal child's empty negative-infinity item (item 0 only). 10 tests. Loop #62 closes the **heap** engine's last update-chain tier — the clog-dependent HOT-chain checks (`verify_heapam.c:759-833`): in-progress→committed xmin, aborted→in-progress/committed xmin, and the heap-only-root-of-chain check, all via a new `VerifyHeapPageWithXminStatus` entry point taking an injected `XidStatusFunc` commit-status callback (keeps the engine off the contaminated `internal/mvcc`; bootstrap/frozen xids resolve to committed directly; nil callback leaves the page-bytes-only paths byte-for-byte unchanged). 10 new tests (3 positive cross-link cases isolated, heap-only-root positive, + 6 false-positive guards incl. nil-callback regression + frozen resolution). The heap engine is now logic-complete; only the MVCC/attribute tier (xmin/xmax numeric bounds, multixact, goopg-divergent TOAST) and the SQL surface remain. Loop #23 (2026-06-14) adds the heap **xmin numeric-bounds tier** — `check_tuple_visibility`'s future / cluster-min / rel-min xid-range checks driven by `get_xid_status` (three verbatim messages), consuming three new `RelDesc` fields (`NextXid`/`OldestXid`/`RelFrozenXid`) the SQL surface supplies; gated on `NextXid != 0` so all page-bytes-only callers are byte-for-byte unchanged; plain-unsigned (epoch-0) comparisons vs upstream's wraparound-aware FullTransactionId; 8 new tests. Remaining MVCC/attribute work: xmax numeric bounds + multixact membership. Deferred now: the SQL surface (waits for a clean tree). 2026-07-08 update: `VerifyBtreeItemOrder`'s item-order tier was found too strict — corrected from strictly-ascending to non-decreasing (equal adjacent keys are legitimate; goopg's `CompareKeys` has no heap-TID tiebreak anywhere in the engine, so same-key duplicates are not TID-ordered) after it produced false-positive corruption reports under duplicate-key churn (M-NIGHTLY AI-20260708-064334-001); see the design doc's new dedicated subsection for the full story. |
| 0110-0006 | [amcheck Bloom filter (heapallindexed primitive) (M0110)](0110-0006-amcheck-bloom-filter.md) | accepted (partial) | Ports upstream's space-efficient Bloom filter (`postgres/src/backend/lib/bloomfilter.c` + `.h`) into `internal/amcheck` as `bloomfilter.go` — the foundational primitive for the last remaining B-tree verification tier, `heapallindexed` (`bt_check_every_level` fingerprints every index tuple into the filter, then asserts each visible heap tuple's index tuple is present; an absent result is a genuine "heap tuple not represented in index" corruption). Standalone data structure (no clog/TupleDesc/catalog/SQL coupling), so it lands engine-first/wire-later in new files only, touching none of the contaminated gen-column WIP. Every part is upstream-verbatim — `bloomCreate`/`bloomAddElement`/`bloomLacksElement`/`bloomPropBitsSet`/`myBloomPower`/`optimalK`/`kHashesValues`/`modM`, including the 1MB-floor/512MB-cap power-of-two sizing and enhanced double hashing — with a **single documented divergence**: the underlying hash. Upstream seeds from `hash_any_extended` (Jenkins lookup3, mirrored as the unexported `pgHashBytesExtended` in `internal/executor`); importing that would entangle amcheck with executor (a contaminated package), and since the no-false-negatives contract holds for any shared hash, the port uses a self-contained seeded FNV-1a + MurmurHash3 `fmix64` finalizer (both 32-bit halves well-avalanched for the double-hashing split). 8 unit tests: no-false-negatives (load-bearing), realistic-regime FP rate < 5%, seed-distinguishes-FPs, sizing-invariants, empty/variable-length elements, and the `myBloomPower`/`optimalK`/`modM` helpers. Deferred (resume points): the heapallindexed heap scan + index-tuple formation (needs heap relation + index `TupleDesc`), the `CREATE EXTENSION amcheck` + SRF SQL surface (blocked on a clean tree; promotes `AC-002`), and hash unification once Jenkins can be shared without cross-package entanglement (distribution-only). |
| 0110-0007 | [amcheck heapallindexed verification tier (M0110)](0110-0007-amcheck-heapallindexed.md) | accepted (partial) | Ports the heapallindexed logic of `bt_check_every_level`/`bt_tuple_present_callback` (`postgres/contrib/amcheck/verify_nbtree.c`) into `internal/amcheck` as `heapallindexed.go` (`VerifyBtreeHeapAllIndexed`) — the last B-tree tier, consuming the Bloom primitive from [0110-0006](0110-0006-amcheck-bloom-filter.md). Pure function over two `btree.LeafEntry` slices: fingerprints every index leaf entry into a filter sized to the exact count, then probes the index tuple each live heap tuple would form; emits one `BtreeReport` (verbatim `heap tuple (b,o) from table "T" lacks matching index tuple within index "I"` + heap block) per lacking entry. Sound because the filter has no false negatives — a healthy heap tuple is never flagged; false positives only mask a `<2%` fraction of real misses, never invent corruption. One `fingerprintLeafEntry` (`TID.Block` big-endian ++ `TID.Offset` ++ key bytes) runs both phases, so present entries hash identically on both sides (sibling-path invariant). New exported `btree.PageLeafEntries` is the canonical leaf reader the wire-later fingerprint phase uses — expands posting-list items to one entry per heap TID (unlike `PageItemKeys`, which collapses to one separator key), beside `PageItemKeys`/`PageDownlinks` as single source of truth against v3→v4 layout drift. Divergences: no `bt_normalize_tuple` step (goopg does not TOAST index keys, so leaf and heap-formed key bytes are already one canonical `EncodeXxxKey` form), and the seed is a parameter (caller randomizes per run, tests pin it). 6 amcheck tests (no-false-negatives load-bearing at n=100k, missing-tuple detection w/ exact message, TID-distinguishes, empty index/heap, shared-key-distinct-TIDs) + 1 btree `TestPageLeafEntries`. Deferred (resume points): the lazy heap scan + index-tuple formation via index `TupleDesc` (catalog coupling), the `CREATE EXTENSION amcheck` + `bt_index_check(…, heapallindexed => true)` SQL surface (blocked on a clean tree; promotes `AC-002`), and hash unification (distribution-only). |
