Execute-ready plan for the `CREATE EXTENSION amcheck` + SRF SQL surface that wires the committed `internal/amcheck` engine to the wire protocol and promotes the deferred `AC-002`…`AC-005` pg_amcheck TAP tests. Captures (once, instead of loops #62/#63 re-deriving it) the three exact client queries `pg_amcheck.c` issues: the per-database `pg_extension`⋈`pg_namespace` install probe (`amcheck_sql`), the `verify_heapam(relation, on_error_stop, check_toast, skip, startblock, endblock)` heap SRF returning `SETOF (blkno,offnum,attnum,msg)`, and the void-returning `bt_index_check`/`bt_index_parent_check` index SRFs (corruption raised as errors). Records the one missing catalog relation (`pg_extension`; `pg_namespace` already exists) and a **scope refinement loop #63 missed**: `002_nonesuch` is almost entirely client-side pattern resolution and exercises only `CREATE EXTENSION amcheck` + the install probe — *not* real `verify_heapam` corruption — so Slices S1+S2 alone promote `AC-002` (the SRFs need only *exist* in `pg_proc`). Five independently-committable slices (S1 DDL → S2 `pg_extension`+probe → S3 verify_heapam SRF → S4 bt_index_check SRFs → S5 port TAP tests), contaminated-file map, and `git add -p` separability vs the foreign M0100-0010 gen-column WIP. No code changed this loop (documentation only); resume point is Slice S1 once the tree is clean. |
| 0110-0009 | [B-tree split: relink the old right sibling's prev-link (M0110-0007)](0110-0009-btree-split-rightsibling-prevlink.md) | accepted | Fixes a B-tree split bug the real-producer amcheck harness ([0110-0005](0110-0005-verify-heapam-engine.md)) uncovered: on a **non-rightmost** split, `insertIntoBlock` spliced the new right page between `L` and its old right sibling `S` but never updated `S.btpo_prev` (it kept pointing at `L`), leaving the doubly-linked sibling chain half-relinked on any non-append insert pattern (random PKs, UUIDs, secondary indexes). Sorted/append inserts split only the rightmost page (no `S`), so the bug was invisible until shuffled inserts forced middle splits. `btpo_prev` is load-bearing — page deletion (`btree_vacuum.go`) reads `op.Prev` and WAL-logs `RightSibNewPrev` to relink siblings. Fix mirrors PostgreSQL `_bt_split`: relink `S.btpo_prev = rightBlk` under the **same atomic split WAL record**, which now carries an optional third page (`btreeSplitHeaderSize` 18→22 with a `SibBlk` field; `replayBtreeSplit` WriteBlocks it). Lock order strictly left→right (`blk → rightBlk → oldNext`), deadlock-free. On-disk page format unchanged (only the WAL record format changed). Detection test flipped to a silence assertion (`TestVerifyBtreeEngineSilentOnRealShuffledInt4`); new 3-page replay + encode/decode tests. Gates: `-race` on btree/wal/mvcc/storage, amcheck/executor/initdb, full build, TPC-H spotcheck (Q12=2/Q13=33) all PASS. |
| 0110-0010 | [B-tree vacuum: relink the live siblings when deleting adjacent empty leaves (M0110-0010)](0110-0010-btree-vacuum-adjacent-leaf-relink.md) | accepted | Fixes a B-tree page-deletion bug the real-producer amcheck page-deletion harness ([0110-0005](0110-0005-verify-heapam-engine.md)) uncovered: when `VacuumIndexPages` empties an **adjacent run** of leaves in one pass (the common case for a range `DELETE` + `VACUUM`), `unlinkEmptyLeaf`/`unlinkEmptyLeafFPI` relinked neighbours from pointers captured at PHASE-1 scan time (`emptyLeafInfo.prev`/`.next`), before any unlink. For `L0→L1→L2→L3→L4` with `L1,L2,L3` emptied, the survivors `L0.next` and `L4.prev` ended up pointing at a block deleted in the same pass — a structurally broken leaf sibling chain the engine's sibling-link tier (correctly) flagged "points to deleted block". `btpo_prev`/`btpo_next` are load-bearing (backward scans, future relinking). Fix mirrors PostgreSQL `_bt_unlink_halfdead_page`: a new `liveSibling` walk skips any `BTDeleted`/`BTHalfDead` page (PHASE 1 stamps every target leaf before any unlink, and `recycleBlock` does not wipe pages, so the chain stays navigable) and relinks the nearest LIVE left/right sibling — order-independent, so `CompleteDeferredDeletions` (post-crash, block-order) is correct too. No WAL format change (the `BtreeUnlinkPage` record already carries arbitrary sibling blocks; only the computed values changed). Detection test flipped to silence (`TestVerifyBtreeEngineSilentAfterAdjacentLeafDeletion`); new storage-layer `TestVacuumIndexPagesAdjacentLeafRunRelinksLiveSiblings`. Gates: `-race` on btree/amcheck/wal/mvcc/storage, full build, TPC-H spotcheck all PASS. |
| 0110-0011 | [LEFT JOIN inner-only pushdown shift/classify completion (M0110-0003)](0110-0011-leftjoin-inner-pushdown-shift-completion.md) | accepted | Generalizes [0097-0023](0097-0023-leftjoin-inner-in-pushdown-shift.md). The LEFT JOIN inner-only ON-conjunct pushdown depends on two sibling helpers staying in lockstep — `classifyConjunctSide`→`walkColumnRefs` (`pushdown.go`) decides a conjunct is inner-only and pushable; `shiftColumnRefsBy` (`planner.go`) rebases its `ColumnRef.Index` by `-leftWidth`. Both hand-enumerate `Expr` kinds in a `switch`, and several sub-expression-bearing kinds were missing from one or both, leaving the same latent `index out of range` panic class. Concrete trigger: **pg_amcheck's exclude-pattern anti-join** (`--exclude-relation`/`--exclude-schema`/`--exclude-table`) panicked the backend — M0110-0003 residual #2. In the `toast` exclusion CTE, the conjunct `('pg_toast' ~ ep.nsp_regex OR ep.nsp_regex IS NULL)` over a 5-col `exclude_pat` VALUES build relation: the `~` ref classified it `sideRight` (pushed + shifted) but the `IS NULL`'s inner ref was an `*IsNullExpr` that `shiftColumnRefsBy` left at combined index 43 → `MaterializedSlot.Get(43)` on a width-5 row → panic via `joinOp.Open→drainRowsCtx→filterOp.Next`. Fix: add `*IsNullExpr`/`*IsBoolExpr`/`*IsDistinctFromExpr`/`*CollateExpr`/`*RowExpr` to `shiftColumnRefsBy` and the same set plus `*CastExpr` to `walkColumnRefs` (the `*CastExpr` add is the dangerous-direction twin — before it, `cast(outer.col)=inner.col` hid the outer ref so a mixed conjunct was wrongly pushed below the LEFT JOIN). Verified end-to-end: the live anti-join CTE + real `pg_amcheck --exclude-relation`/`--exclude-schema` both run with no panic (exit 0). Sibling-path class [[pattern_sibling_paths_must_agree]]. Test: `planner/shift_colrefs_in_test.go` `TestShiftColumnRefsByIsNullExpr`. |
| 0110-0012 | [CREATE SCHEMA durability across restart (WAL-record mechanism) (M0110-0003)](0110-0012-create-schema-wal-durability.md) | accepted | Makes `CREATE/DROP SCHEMA` survive a server restart. Previously schema registration was an in-memory-only side effect (`InMemory.schemas`, backing `pg_namespace` + schema-qualified resolution); on restart only the three bootstrap namespaces (`pg_catalog`/`pg_toast`/`public`) were rebuilt, so user schemas silently vanished — a `pg_amcheck --schema s1` run clean before a restart reported `no relations to check` after (recurring M0110-0003 003_check blocker). Mirrors the **CREATE/DROP DATABASE WAL-record mechanism** (M0054-0001), not the `pg_class` heap-append: two new physical-replay-no-op record kinds `RecordKindCreateSchema`=34 (`kind\|oid\|nameLen\|name`, OID carried so recovery restores the same identifier) / `RecordKindDropSchema`=35, a verbatim-mirror recovery driver `replaySchemaDDLRecords` (`internal/initdb/schema_ddl_recovery.go`) wired into `open.go` after the database-DDL replay, and idempotent catalog hooks `Register/UnregisterSchemaDuringRecovery`. Emitted at all three execution routes: parsed `CompatNoopStmt{schema}` in `ddlOp.execCompatNoop`, the parser-rejected compat-no-op branch in `dispatchSimpleQueryViaExecutor`, and `DROP SCHEMA` in `execDropCompat`; all guarded by `WAL != nil`. Non-transactional (like CREATE DATABASE). PG-standby visibility (pg_namespace heap row + 2684/2685 indexes) is explicitly out of scope — goopg resolves schemas via the in-memory registry, not the index. Tests: wal codec round-trip, initdb Open→append→Close→Open replay (CREATE survives w/ OID, CREATE+DROP cancels), and the e2e `TestPort_CreateSchemaSurvivesRestart` (live cluster, over-the-wire CREATE/DROP across two restarts). |
| 0110-0013 | [User-schema table durability across restart (relnamespace OID round-trip) (M0110-0003)](0110-0013-user-schema-table-durability.md) | accepted | Follow-up to [0110-0012](0110-0012-create-schema-wal-durability.md): makes a *table created inside a user schema* reload under its schema after a restart. Two sibling paths disagreed on how a user table's schema is encoded in `pg_class.relnamespace` — the **write side** `namespaceOIDForSchema(schema)` collapsed every non-`public` schema to the `pg_catalog` OID (11), so `s1.t` was written `relnamespace=11` and the **read side** `loadUserTablesFromHeap` reloaded it as `pg_catalog.t`; after a restart `pg_amcheck --schema s1` found no relations (the recurring 003_check symptom). Fix makes both halves agree on the **real schema OID** from the registry that 0110-0012 restores: `namespaceOIDForSchema(cat, schema)` resolves a registered user schema via `cat.SchemaOID` (system schemas keep fixed OIDs; unregistered/nil falls back to `pg_catalog`); `loadUserTablesFromHeap`/`loadUserIndexesFromHeap` reverse-map a non-system `relnamespace` via the new `cat.SchemaNameForOID`; `replaySchemaDDLRecords` is moved **before** table load in `open.go` so the registry is populated when the reverse-map runs; `SchemaOID` promoted onto the `Catalog` interface. No new durability machinery — only corrects the value written to an existing column so the existing heap-scan recovery is lossless. PG-standby user-schema visibility (pg_namespace heap row) stays out of scope. [[pattern_sibling_paths_must_agree]]. Tests: `TestSchemaOIDNameRoundTrip`, `TestNamespaceOIDForSchemaResolvesUserSchema`, e2e `TestPort_PgAmcheck003SchemaScoped` (corrupt s1.t across a restart, assert `pg_amcheck --schema s1` reports it). |
| 0111-0001 | [PG-Format Codec Parity (varlena decode, type coercion, TOAST) (M0111)](0111-0001-pg-format-codec-parity.md) | draft | Fix three PG-format codec bugs: (A) `DecodePhysicalPGRow: truncated varlena` under concurrent UPDATE, (B) complete `encodeValuePG` string→numeric/float coercion for float4/float8, (C) TOAST write/read round-trip where `NBlocks` returns 0 for freshly-extended TOAST relation. Unblocks UPDATE-based pgbench workloads and ~40 regress tests. |
| 0111-0002 | [Heap-Tuple Row Format Unification (single PG-physical format) (M0111)](0111-0002-heap-tuple-format-unification.md) | draft | Collapse the two coexisting heap-tuple row formats (goopg legacy `EncodeRow`/`decodeGoopgRowIntoMctx` vs PG-physical `EncodeRowPG`/`decodePhysicalPGRowIntoMctx`) into one PG-physical format, and replace the format-**guessing** decode (`decodeRowIntoMctx` tries PG then legacy; `DecodeRowIntoMctxPGTuple` guesses when `natts==0 && bitmap==nil`) with a deterministic header-driven dispatcher: `natts>0 \|\| bitmap!=nil` ⇒ PG-physical, else legacy. Eliminates the cross-acceptance corruption class where a legacy `int4` byte (e.g. 15=`0x0f`, 28=`0x1c`) parses as a valid PG varlena and decodes to wrong data (root cause of the ANALYZE `15/28→0` bug fixed in `ce422ec`; latent in ~16 bare-`DecodeRow` sites). Staged: S1 deterministic decode (16 call sites → `DecodeHeapTupleRow` helper) → S2a pgoutput physical decode → S2 always-PG-physical writes (user DML + TOAST, drop `LogCanonical` encode branch, unconditional `SetNatts`) → S3 delete legacy encoder/decoder/guessing + dead projection code. Out of scope: `catalog/codec.go` (virtual tables, never heap-decoded), BTree keys, WAL redo (opaque). Migration: data-dir re-init. |
| 0111-0004 | [PG-Format Decode Gap for Fixed-Width Types (int8 / name / temporal) (M0111)](0111-0004-pg-format-decode-fixed-width-gap.md) | accepted | `decodePhysicalPGValueMctx` in `internal/executor/codec.go` had no case for `int8`/`bigint`/`bigserial`, `name`, `regproc`, `xid`/`xid8`, `timestamp`/`timestamptz`, `date` even though `encodeValuePG` writes them — the encode/decode switches drifted out of sync since M0106-0010. An int8 (or name) value encoded fine but failed both the physical and legacy decoders, so the seqscan silently dropped the row: a plain `INSERT INTO t(bigint) VALUES (5)` reported `INSERT 0 1` yet `SELECT *` returned 0 rows, and `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT count(*) … GROUP BY` stored nothing (`count(*)`/`sum()` are int8). Added the missing fixed-width decode arms, each mirroring the encoder byte-for-byte. Recovers `select_implicit` + `portals_p2` regress tests (`failed → pass`) and improves `name` (97 → 77 diff lines). Also removed leftover `GOOPG_DIAG_OVF` debug code + unused `os` import in `expr.go` that broke the build. Pinned by `TestDecodePhysicalPGInt8RoundTrip`, `TestDecodePhysicalPGNameRoundTrip`, `TestDecodePhysicalPGRowInt8DoesNotDropRow`. INSERT-side string-literal coercion for timestamp/date/xid and `KindNumeric → int8` remain separate (out of scope). |
| 0111-0005 | [int2 Storage-Encode Out-of-Range Message Parity (M0111)](0111-0005-int2-encode-out-of-range-message.md) | accepted | `encodeValuePG`'s int2/smallint arm in `internal/executor/codec.go` emitted a bare `fmt.Errorf("smallint out of range")` — the `int2pl`/`int2mul` *arithmetic* wording — when a string literal coerced into an int2 column overflowed (the `int2in` input-function path, e.g. `INSERT INTO INT2_TBL(f1) VALUES ('100000')`). PostgreSQL reports `value "100000" is out of range for type smallint` (22003) there; the bare wording is reserved for arithmetic overflow, which goopg already raises in the expression evaluator before the storage-encode path. The sibling int4 arm directly below already did this; the two arms had drifted. Now mirrors int4: a 22003 `*ExecError` with `value %q is out of range for type smallint` over `strings.TrimSpace(d.StringValue())`. Recovers the `int2` regress case (`failed`, 4 diff lines → **pass**). Pinned by `TestEncodeValuePGInt2OutOfRangeMessage` (`internal/executor/codec_int8_name_pg_test.go`); arithmetic wording still asserted by `phase_c_test.go` `int2_*_overflow` cases. |
| 0111-0006 | [PG-Format Float Decode Returns KindString (numeric sort regression) (M0111)](0111-0006-pg-format-float-decode-kind.md) | accepted | `decodePhysicalPGValueMctx` in `internal/executor/codec.go` lumped `float4`/`float8`/`real`/`double precision` into the shared `text`/`varchar` decode case, which returns a `KindString` Datum. goopg stores floats as varlena text (M0111-0002), and this PG-native decoder became the primary heap-read path in M0111-0001 — so float columns compared byte-lexicographically rather than numerically (`SELECT f1 FROM TEMP_FLOAT ORDER BY f1` produced `-1234` ahead of `-2147483647`). The legacy `decodeValue`/arena decoders had always parsed float text back to `KindNumeric` (M0097-0003 "for correct ORDER BY numeric sort"); the PG-native path lost it. Fix: dedicated float case that parses the varlena-text payload to `KindNumeric` (NaN/Inf fall back to `KindString`), mirroring the legacy decoders byte-for-byte. Display stays correct because float8 output formatting is keyed on the column type (`%.15g`), not the Datum kind, so `1.2345678901234e+200` round-trips. Recovers the `numerology` regress case (`failed`, 60 diff lines → **pass**); `float4` 680→676, `float8` 1031→1027; no previously-passing case regressed. Pinned by `TestDecodePhysicalPGFloatKind` (`internal/executor/codec_int8_name_pg_test.go`), which asserts the decoded `Kind` and a `compareDatum(-1234, -123456) > 0` numeric-ordering proof. Same decode-arm-drift class as [[0111-0004]]; lesson: after a codec change audit that each type's decode produces the **Kind** the comparison/sort layer expects, not just the same bytes. |
| 0111-0007 | [PG-Format Name Encode Skips NAMEDATALEN-1 Truncation (M0111)](0111-0007-pg-format-name-encode-truncation.md) | accepted | `encodeValuePG`'s `name` arm in `internal/executor/codec.go` copied the full input string into the fixed 64-byte `NameData` buffer with **no** NAMEDATALEN-1 = 63 truncation, so a 64-char input filled all 64 bytes (no NUL terminator) and `decodePhysicalPGValueMctx` read it back as 64 chars. PostgreSQL's `namein()` truncates `name` to 63 bytes; the sibling `encodeValueStorage` path already did (`if len(s) > 63 { s = s[:63] }`, M0097-0003) but the PG-native encoder — primary heap path since M0111-0001 — had drifted. The off-by-one widened `name` columns by one (64-dash header underline), kept a trailing byte that PG clipped, and corrupted `WHERE` row counts (stored values weren't truncated, so equality matched a different row set: `(7 rows)`/`(0 rows)` vs PG's `(5 rows)`/`(1 row)`). Fix: clip to 63 bytes before `copy`, mirroring storage-encode (plus its KindBytes/KindInt handling). Recovers the `name` regress case (`failed`, 77 diff lines → **pass**) — the **last** of the 6 M0106-0010 codec regressions. Pinned by `TestEncodePhysicalPGNameTruncation` (`internal/executor/codec_int8_name_pg_test.go`). Encode-side analogue of the [[0111-0004]]/[[0111-0006]] decode drifts; lesson: audit that `encodeValuePG` and `encodeValueStorage` agree on type-specific normalization (length clip, padding, error wording), not just round-trip bytes for short values. |
| 0107-0007f | [Phase D4 — Heap-insert call site: pin-aware FSM consultation (M0107-0007, slice C call-site part 1)](0107-0007f-heap-insert-fsm-pin-aware.md) | accepted | First half of the slice C call-site rewrite: `writeHeapRowReturning` and `writeHeapRowReturningPG` in `internal/executor/operators_storage.go` swap the single-block `ctx.FSM.GetPageWithFreeSpace(rel, minFreeBytes)` for the slice-C executor consumer `selectFSMCandidatePage(ctx.FSM, ctx.Pool, rel, minFreeBytes)` from [[0107-0007e]]. Identical `(BlockNumber, bool)` signature, so the change is a one-liner per call site; the surrounding `if ctx.FSM != nil` wrapper is removed because the helper handles nil-FSM / nil-Pool itself. Under low concurrency the selected block is unchanged (`GetCandidates` returns blocks in free-space-desc with lowest-block tie-break, matching the FSM scan order that `GetPageWithFreeSpace` used; the first pin-0 short-circuit picks the same candidate). Under high concurrency every backend's `Pool.SlotPinCount` probe biases it away from the hot tail page, so backends spread across cold FSM candidates instead of converging on one slot's content lock. Per-record WAL emission is byte-identical — the only thing that changes is the block-reference number embedded in `XLOG_HEAP_INSERT` for a given workload, which PG standby replay handles per-record (no "expected next block" invariant). The batched-extend half of slice C (replacing `PinNew` with `Pool.ExtendRelationBatch` per [[0107-0007c]] + FSM registration for the extras) and slice B (8-stripe `wal.Writer.appendLocks` per parent §2) both stay deferred — those need the parent milestone's WAL byte-diff integration gate. Verified: `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/executor/ ./internal/storage/ ./internal/wal/ ./internal/server/` all PASS (≈17 s total); the six existing `TestSelectFSMCandidatePage*` helper tests in `internal/executor/heap_insert_select_test.go` exercise the pin-aware ranking and the broader executor/server suites exercise the wiring end-to-end through every existing `writeHeapRowReturning` caller (planner, lockrows, upsert, merge, apply-worker, partition). PG-compat — none for this slice (per-record WAL bytes unchanged; only the selected target block diverges under contention, which is part of the parent milestone's scope and gated separately). |
| 0107-0007g | [Phase D4 — Heap-insert call site: adaptive batched-extend tail (M0107-0007, slice C call-site part 2)](0107-0007g-heap-insert-batched-extend.md) | accepted | Second (and final) half of the slice C call-site rewrite, closing parent §3 steps 5–6 in `internal/executor/operators_storage.go`. New constant `extendBatchSize = 8` and helper `batchExtendAndRegisterFSM(pool, fsm, rel)` in `heap_insert_select.go`: one `Pool.ExtendRelationBatch` call appends eight empty pages in one syscall and FSM-registers blocks `[firstBlk+1 .. firstBlk+7]` at empty-page free space; `firstBlk` is intentionally left out of the FSM (the caller's `markHeapInsertDirty → FSM.RecordFreeSpaceForPage` records the post-insert remainder, matching the existing single-page path). `lockHeapExtend(rel, procNum)` signature changes from `unlock` to `(unlock, contended bool)`: `TryLock` first, fall through to blocking `Lock()` on failure with `contended=true`. Both heap-insert call sites add a post-lock FSM re-consult via `selectFSMCandidatePage` (cross-stripe pickup of fresh candidates registered by a sibling stripe's just-completed batch) followed by an adaptive tail — `contended==true` → `batchExtendAndRegisterFSM` + `tryAppendToBlock`; `contended==false` → original `Pool.PinNew` fast path (preserves single-INSERT one-page semantics that HOT-update / VACUUM / LockRows tests rely on, mirrors PG's `RelationExtensionLockWaiterCount`-driven `extraBlocks` heuristic in `RelationGetBufferForTuple`). Three new tests pin the batched-extend half (`TestBatchExtendAndRegisterFSMAppendsAndRegistersExtras`, `…NilFSM`, `…SecondCallContinuesAndRegisters`); two new assertions in `extend_lock_stripe_test.go` pin the `contended` contract (first acquirer of a stripe sees `false`; a peer who had to wait sees `true`). Verified: `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/executor/ ./internal/storage/ ./internal/wal/ ./internal/server/` all PASS. PG-compat — per-record WAL bytes unchanged; the on-disk relation grows by 8 blocks per contended extend event vs. 1 in the uncontended path. Empty pre-extended extras that never receive a tuple are never WAL-touched, so PG standby replay only extends to cover blocks referenced by replayed records, identical to PG's own batched-extend recovery model. Slice B (8-stripe `wal.Writer.appendLocks` per parent §2) remains deferred — multi-loop scope splitting `state.appendMu`'s four invariants — and is the last outstanding piece of M0107-0007 before the pgbench c=100 SU TPS ≥ 500 gate. |

| 0107-0007u | [Phase D4 — `stripeAppend` writer-side composer (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 14)](0107-0007u-wal-stripe-append.md) | accepted | Fourteenth slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2. Adds `stripeAppend(locks, posTracker, insertTracker, walBuf, memRing, procNum, record) (start, prev uint64, err error)` in new file `internal/wal/stripe_append.go`. Performs one stripe-locked WAL append by composing seven writer-side primitives in the order the slice B contract requires: (1) `appendLockSet.lockByProcNum` ([[0107-0007i]]) acquires one of eight stripe mutexes selected by `procNum & 0x7`; (2) `insertPosTracker.reserveAndPublish` ([[0107-0007p]]) jointly advances `(curr, prev)` and publishes the stripe's active LSN under `posMu` — closing the pre-reserve race documented in [[0107-0007m]] §"Pre-reserve race"; (3) `walBuffer.writeReserved` ([[0107-0007l]]) lands bytes into the bytes-side ring at the reserved LSN; (4) `MemRing.WriteReserved` ([[0107-0007o]]) lands bytes into the walsender mirror at the same LSN; (5) `insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(stripe, lsnIdle)` ([[0107-0007m]]) publishes the END marker so the drain-side `tailPublisher` stops capping `safeTail` at this stripe's start LSN; (6) the stripe mutex is released. Steps (5) and (6) are deferred so LIFO ordering runs END-marker → unlock — matching the lock-ordering tier documented at the end of [[0107-0007t]]. Cross-segment crossings are handled by the `insertPosTracker.onCrossSegment` hook fired under `posMu` inside step (2); the slice B call-site rewrite will install [[0107-0007s]] `emitSegmentPad` as that hook so a reservation that straddles a segment boundary automatically gets a well-formed XLOG_NOOP pad record dropped into the gap, and the reservation lands at the post-boundary LSN with the xl_prev chain preserved. Symmetric counterpart of [[0107-0007t]] `publishVisibility` (drain-side composer): stripeAppend lands bytes without advancing visibility; publishVisibility advances visibility without writing bytes. The two composers together cover the full slice B write/publish lifecycle so the call-site rewrite can install each as a one-liner at its natural site. Error handling and END marker. If `walBuf.writeReserved` or `memRing.WriteReserved` returns an error (e.g. `errWALBufferReservedOutOfRange` from a caller-side range bug), the composer still publishes the END marker before unlocking the stripe so the drain's `tailPublisher` is not frozen — leaving the stripe slot stuck at the failed reservation's start LSN would permanently cap `safeTail`. The error is returned verbatim from the failing primitive so callers can pattern-match (`errors.Is(err, errWALBufferReservedOutOfRange)`); `start, prev` are returned even on error for forensic logging. Nil-safety contract: `locks` / `posTracker` / `insertTracker` are required (nil → structured errors `errStripeAppendNilLocks` / `errStripeAppendNilPosTracker` / `errStripeAppendNilInsertTracker` before any side effect; nil insertTracker would re-open the pre-reserve race); `walBuf` / `memRing` are individually nil-safe (skip the corresponding `writeReserved` so the composer works under `Config.WALBuffers == 0` and/or `wal_sender_memory_buffer == 0`). Empty record rejected with `errStripeAppendEmptyRecord` rather than silently no-oping: (a) `reserveAndPublish(0, …)` panics on size == 0 by design — we want a structured error not a panic for a benign empty case; (b) the slice B caller has no useful "empty WAL insert" semantics; (c) early rejection avoids acquiring the stripe lock for a definitively-no-op call. Concurrency: two `stripeAppend` calls with procNums hashing to different stripes proceed fully in parallel — only the per-stripe mutex serialises within a stripe. PG counterpart: `XLogInsertRecord` in `postgres/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c` calls `WALInsertLockAcquire(MyProcNumber % NUM_XLOGINSERT_LOCKS)` → `ReserveXLogInsertLocation` (with `WALInsertLockUpdateInsertingAt` under the same insert lock) → `CopyXLogRecordToWAL` (into `XLogCtl->pages`) → `WALInsertLockRelease` (which resets `insertingAt` to `InvalidXLogRecPtr`). goopg's `stripeAppend` fuses the equivalent five steps into one composer so the call-site rewrite stays a one-liner. Lock-ordering tier: `stripeAppend → appendLockSet.lockByProcNum → insertPosTracker.reserveAndPublish (posMu held: reserveLocked + insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(start); posMu released, with rare cross-segment onCrossSegment hook → emitSegmentPad) → walBuffer.writeReserved (no lock; leaf) → MemRing.WriteReserved (memRing.mu read-lock) → insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(stripe, lsnIdle) → drop stripe lock`. Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite mounts `appendLockSet` + `insertPosTracker` + `insertionTracker` on `Writer` and switches `state.append`'s body to call `stripeAppend`; foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] / [[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]] / [[0107-0007g]]) and the thirteen earlier slice B foundations ([[0107-0007h]] / [[0107-0007i]] / [[0107-0007j]] / [[0107-0007k]] / [[0107-0007l]] / [[0107-0007m]] / [[0107-0007n]] / [[0107-0007o]] / [[0107-0007p]] / [[0107-0007q]] / [[0107-0007r]] / [[0107-0007s]] / [[0107-0007t]]). Regression coverage in `internal/wal/stripe_append_test.go` (15 tests): `TestStripeAppendHappyPathWritesBothRings` (single insert, both rings get bytes, END marker fires, publishVisibility makes them visible); `TestStripeAppendNilLocksReturnsError` / `TestStripeAppendNilPosTrackerReturnsError` / `TestStripeAppendNilInsertTrackerReturnsError` (defensive nil-guards return structured errors); `TestStripeAppendEmptyRecordReturnsError` (empty / nil record rejected before any side effect, pos tracker / insertion tracker untouched); `TestStripeAppendNilWalBufStillWritesMemRing` (`Config.WALBuffers == 0` path); `TestStripeAppendNilMemRingStillWritesWalBuf` (`wal_sender_memory_buffer == 0` path); `TestStripeAppendWalBufOutOfWindowReturnsErrorAndClearsStripe` (walBuf range violation surfaces error AND END marker fires so drain isn't frozen); `TestStripeAppendMemRingOutOfWindowReturnsErrorAndClearsStripe` (symmetric for memring); `TestStripeAppendSelectsStripeByProcNum` (procNum & 0x7 stripe selection; per-stripe slot back to idle after every call); | 0107-0007r | [Phase D4 — `walBuffer.tail` upgraded to `atomic.Int64` (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 11)](0107-0007r-wal-buffer-tail-atomic.md) | accepted | Promotes `walBuffer.tail` from plain `int64` to `atomic.Int64` so a single drain goroutine's `publishTail` (foundation 10, [[0107-0007q]]) and concurrent stripe writers' tail readers (resident / readForDrain / readAt) coexist without a data race. Five production sites rewritten: `reset` (Store), `resident` (Load), `append` (Load+Store, single-goroutine), `readAt` (single-Load snapshot for both `pos >= tail` guard and avail computation), `publishTail` (Load → if safeTail > cur → Store, monotonic). Tests updated: 11 reads via `.Load()`, 3 direct writes via `.Store(...)`; new `TestWALBufferTailIsAtomicInt64` (compile-time pin via `*atomic.Int64 = &b.tail`) and `TestWALBufferPublishTailObservedByConcurrentReader` (100 K iterations: reader observes monotonic non-regressing values and never exceeds writer's last-Stored ceiling by more than 1). PG counterpart: `XLogCtl->LogwrtResult.Write` accessed via `pg_atomic_read_u64`. Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite — atomicity becomes load-bearing once the drain goroutine begins calling `publishTail` outside `state.appendMu`. |
| 0107-0007q | [Phase D4 — `walBuffer.publishTail` bytes-side tail-publication primitive (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 10)](0107-0007q-wal-buffer-publish-tail.md) | accepted | Tenth slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2. Adds `(*walBuffer).publishTail(safeTail int64) int64` in new file `internal/wal/wal_buffer_publish_tail.go` — the bytes-side mirror of [[0107-0007o]] `MemRing.PublishUpTo`. Under the slice B 8-stripe writer model a stripe lands bytes via [[0107-0007l]] `walBuffer.writeReserved` without touching `tail`; the drain goroutine — after consulting [[0107-0007n]] `tailPublisher` for the safe watermark — calls `publishTail` to monotonically advance `tail` so the freshly-published bytes become drainable (visible to `resident` / `readForDrain` / `readAt`). Without this primitive the call-site rewrite cannot promote bytes from "written but invisible" to "drainable" without holding the global `state.appendMu` that slice B is trying to retire. Contract: nil-safe (`b == nil` returns 0, matching [[0107-0007l]] / [[0107-0007o]]'s nil-safe convention for `Config.WALBuffers == 0`); monotonic store (`safeTail <= b.tail` short-circuits as a no-op — regressing values from a stale `tailPublisher` snapshot are silently ignored); returns the resulting tail value (post-update). Does NOT mutate `head` or `base` — drain remains solely responsible for head/base advances via `advanceHead` after `writeAt` confirms bytes are persisted. No head-eviction. Unlike `MemRing.PublishUpTo` (which auto-evicts oldest residents when `safeTail - head > cap`), `walBuffer.publishTail` must NOT auto-advance head when resident exceeds cap — pending writes are not yet on disk, so silently evicting them would lose data. The contract instead requires the caller (drain) to keep resident ≤ cap by `advanceHead`-after-`writeAt`; today's Path A satisfies this via overflow-drain-then-append in `state.append`, and the slice B call-site rewrite satisfies it by running drain on a dedicated goroutine and pausing publication when the ring is full. The `TestWALBufferPublishTailDoesNotEvictPendingWrites` test pins this contract: a deliberate caller-side overflow (`publishTail(96)` on a cap-64 buffer with head=0) leaves head at 0 — the primitive does not paper over the caller's bug by data-losing eviction. Monotonic-store contract: `safeTail` is expected to come from `tailPublisher.publishUpTo` (itself monotonic per [[0107-0007n]]); the `<=` defends against stale snapshots that callers may hold; under the drain goroutine's typical pattern (`safeTail := tailPublisher.publishUpTo(...); walBuffer.publishTail(safeTail)`) a regression cannot happen in practice, but the no-op is the right response if it does — matches the equivalent guard in `MemRing.PublishUpTo`. Concurrency: this foundation lands the API surface only. `b.tail` remains a plain `int64` for now; the eventual atomicity upgrade (so a drain goroutine's `publishTail` and stripe writers' tail readers — via `resident`, `readForDrain`, `readAt` — can coexist without a data race) is a separate follow-on foundation, deliberately decoupled so the call-site rewrite can wire `publishTail` in lock-step with the atomic upgrade. Under today's single-goroutine usage (`state.append` holding `appendMu`), `publishTail` is trivially safe — every call is on the writer goroutine that holds the lock. The concurrent-scenario test drives 8 stripe writers + a publisher goroutine serialising `publishTail` calls under -race so the API surface is exercised under the stripe-concurrent pattern without yet asserting field-level atomicity. PG counterpart: `XLogCtl->LogwrtResult.Write` advance in `postgres/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c` after `WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish` returns; downstream readers consult the published watermark before issuing reads. Lock-ordering tier after foundation 10: stripe writer `appendLockSet.lockByProcNum → insertPosTracker.reserveAndPublish → walBuffer.writeReserved → MemRing.WriteReserved → insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(stripe, lsnIdle) → drop stripe lock`; drain side `safeTail := tailPublisher.publishUpTo(upperBound, insertionTracker) → walBuffer.publishTail(safeTail) → walBuffer.advanceHead(safeTail - prior) → MemRing.PublishUpTo(safeTail)` — `publishTail` sits immediately before `advanceHead` in the drain chain because `resident()` derives from `tail - head` and drain wants to see all newly-published bytes before issuing the write batch. Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite consumes it; foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] / [[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]] / [[0107-0007g]]) and the nine earlier slice B foundations ([[0107-0007h]] / [[0107-0007i]] / [[0107-0007j]] / [[0107-0007k]] / [[0107-0007l]] / [[0107-0007m]] / [[0107-0007n]] / [[0107-0007o]] / [[0107-0007p]]). Regression coverage in `internal/wal/wal_buffer_publish_tail_test.go` (11 tests): `TestWALBufferPublishTailAdvancesFromBase` (first publish on a freshly-reset buffer advances tail and returns it; head/base untouched); `TestWALBufferPublishTailMonotonicIgnoresRegression` (second publish with a lower value is a no-op; return value is the existing tail); `TestWALBufferPublishTailEqualIsNoop` (boundary case `safeTail == tail` is a no-op; the `<=` guard matches `MemRing.PublishUpTo`); `TestWALBufferPublishTailDoesNotMutateHeadBase` (series of monotonic publications leaves head/base untouched); `TestWALBufferPublishTailNilReceiver` (nil-safe convention; returns 0); `TestWALBufferPublishTailExposesWriteReservedBytesToReadAt` (end-to-end pairing: bytes written via `writeReserved` are invisible to `readAt` until `publishTail` covers them — pins the publication-is-the-visibility-edge invariant); `TestWALBufferPublishTailMakesResidentTrackTailMinusHead` (`resident()` reflects only published bytes; an unpublished `writeReserved` leaves `resident()` at zero); `TestWALBufferPublishTailComposesWithAdvanceHead` (drain pattern `publishTail → readForDrain → advanceHead` interleaves correctly; a second cycle confirms `publishTail` extends from the post-advance tail); `TestWALBufferPublishTailDoesNotEvictPendingWrites` (deliberate caller-side overflow leaves head at 0; the primitive does not auto-evict — matches the no-data-loss contract that differs from `MemRing.PublishUpTo`); `TestWALBufferPublishTailMonotonicUnderSerialisedAdvances` (scripted sequence of monotonic/regressing requests; tail follows the cumulative max); `TestWALBufferPublishTailRaceFreeWithDisjointWriters` (8 writers × 50 records × 16 bytes via `writeReserved`; a serialiser goroutine forwards max-LSN requests to `publishTail`; race-clean under `-race`; final `readAt` confirms every record landed in the right slot; body extracted to `runPublishTailDisjointWritersScenario` so the watchdog can re-run it); `TestWALBufferPublishTailWatchdog` (5-second watchdog on the concurrent scenario — surfaces deadlock regressions before the package-level timeout; mirrors foundation 7 / 9's pattern). Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestWALBufferPublishTail' ./internal/wal/` PASS (1.02 s); `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/` PASS (3.12 s). PG-compat — none (in-memory primitive; WAL record / file format / catalog / wire all unchanged; lock geometry mirrors PG's published-watermark advance in `xlog.c`). Out of scope (later slice B foundations and call-site rewrite): upgrading `b.tail` to `atomic.Int64` so a single drain goroutine's `publishTail` and stripe writers' tail readers can coexist without a data race (mechanical but ripples to 5 production sites + the existing test that pokes `b.tail` directly; lands in its own loop so this foundation's footprint stays minimal); mounting `publishTail` on `Writer` and consuming it from the drain/flush goroutine (multi-loop because `state.append` currently advances `walBuf.tail` and `memRing.tail` synchronously inside `appendMu`; the rewrite splits the four invariants — writePos / walBuf / memRing / writeLSN — into per-stripe local state vs. shared state); drain coordination with concurrent stripe writes (`drainBufferBytes` currently runs under `appendMu` — the rewrite must let drain run concurrently with stripe writes by consuming `tailPublisher.publishUpTo`'s return as drain ceiling for `walBuffer.publishTail` / `walBuffer.advanceHead` / `MemRing.PublishUpTo`); deciding whether `lsnAllocator` ([[0107-0007h]]) becomes dead-code-removed once the call-site converges on `insertPosTracker` + `insertionTracker` + `tailPublisher` + `reserveAndPublish` + `publishTail` — `reserve` remains in the API as a callable primitive without a tracker. |
| 0107-0007p | [Phase D4 — `insertPosTracker.reserveAndPublish` joint-atomic reserve + stripe-publish (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 9)](0107-0007p-wal-reserve-and-publish.md) | accepted | Ninth slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2. Adds `(*insertPosTracker).reserveAndPublish(size uint64, stripe int, tracker *insertionTracker) (start, prev uint64)` in new file `internal/wal/insert_pos_publish.go`, and refactors `insert_pos.go`'s `reserve` to share a private `reserveLocked(size)` helper so the (curr, prev) update logic lives in exactly one place. Closes the pre-reserve race documented in [[0107-0007m]] §"Pre-reserve race" and re-cited in [[0107-0007n]] and [[0107-0007o]]: under the slice B per-stripe insert contract, `insertPosTracker.reserve` advances `curr` and then the caller separately calls `insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(stripe, start)`; a drain reader that calls `tailPublisher.publishUpTo(upperBound, tracker)` between those two steps observes `lowestActiveLSN == lsnNoActive` for the in-flight reservation and may advance the published watermark past still-being-written bytes — a soundness bug that would let `walBuffer.advanceHead` or `MemRing.PublishUpTo` reclaim ring slots an unfinished `writeReserved` is still memcpying into. Closure (option A from [[0107-0007m]]'s "Pre-reserve race" alternatives): move both updates under a single `posMu` critical section so they appear to all observers as one indivisible action. Any thread that subsequently acquires `posMu` (notably `insertPosTracker.load`, used by a drain reader to obtain `upperBound`) observes both the advanced `curr` and the published `insertionTracker[stripe]` together; the `setInsertingAt` Store is sequenced-before the `posMu.Unlock` that releases the lock. PG implements the same pattern: `ReserveXLogInsertLocation` is followed inside the same WAL insert lock by `WALInsertLockUpdateInsertingAt` in `postgres/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c`. Why not option B (pre-reserve marker — write a floor LSN before calling `reserve`, then refine after): it requires the caller to know `curr` ahead of time (defeating the point of having `posMu` be authoritative over `curr`), and adds a second atomic write per insert where option A adds zero (the `setInsertingAt` happens regardless of which option is chosen; option A just moves it inside `posMu`). Contract: `size` must satisfy `0 < size <= segSize` (matches `reserve`); `tracker` MUST be non-nil — if the call site has no insertion tracker (e.g. legacy non-striped path), it calls `reserve` instead, panics on nil rather than silently skipping publication since silent degradation would defeat the foundation's purpose; `stripe` must satisfy `0 <= stripe < appendLockStripes` (matches `insertionTracker.setInsertingAt`'s panic semantics). Cross-segment crossings publish the **new reservation's start** (post-boundary LSN), NOT the gap's start: the pad record at `[gap, boundary)` is a gap-fill emitted synchronously under `posMu` via the `onCrossSegment` hook, not a stripe reservation; the reservation that triggered the crossing lands at `boundary` with `prev = gap`, and `boundary` is what the stripe slot publishes — matching PG's behaviour. The END `setInsertingAt(stripe, lsnIdle)` is **NOT** part of this primitive — it remains a separate call by the caller, sequenced after the byte write; closing the race only requires sealing the BEGIN side under `posMu`. Cost: one additional `atomic.Int64.Store` under the existing posMu critical section; does not extend the critical section meaningfully (single instruction on amd64/arm64); cost dominated by the existing `posMu` Lock/Unlock pair. No new locks introduced. Lock-ordering tier after foundation 9: `appendLockSet.lockByProcNum → insertPosTracker.reserveAndPublish (posMu held: reserveLocked + tracker.setInsertingAt(start); posMu released) → walBuffer.writeReserved → MemRing.WriteReserved → insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(stripe, lsnIdle) → drop stripe lock`; drain side `tailPublisher.publishUpTo(upperBound, insertionTracker) → walBuffer.advanceHead → MemRing.PublishUpTo`. Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite consumes it; foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] / [[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]] / [[0107-0007g]]) and the eight earlier slice B foundations ([[0107-0007h]] / [[0107-0007i]] / [[0107-0007j]] / [[0107-0007k]] / [[0107-0007l]] / [[0107-0007m]] / [[0107-0007n]] / [[0107-0007o]]). Regression coverage in `internal/wal/insert_pos_publish_test.go` (10 tests): `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishBasic` (single reservation publishes to named stripe; others remain idle; startCurr=1 avoids the lsnIdle=0 sentinel collision); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishMultiStripe` (three reservations on distinct stripes populate independent slots; `lowestActiveLSN` returns the minimum); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishCrossSegmentPublishesNewStart` (the published stripe value is the post-boundary reservation start, not the pad-record start; onCross hook still fires with the expected `(gap, boundary, gapPrev)` payload); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishInvalidSizePanics` (`{0, segSize+1, 2·segSize}` panic); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishNilTrackerPanics` (nil tracker panics — no silent degradation); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishInvalidStripePanics` (bad stripe indices on the write path panic); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishInteropWithReserve` (mixing `reserve` and `reserveAndPublish` on the same tracker preserves (curr, prev) chain integrity; the tracker only reflects `reserveAndPublish` calls); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishConcurrentChain` (32 goroutines × 100 × 16 B; starts form a contiguous permutation; every goroutine pairs its `reserveAndPublish` with a matching `setInsertingAt(idle)`, so `lowestActiveLSN` returns to the sentinel at the end); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishConsistentSnapshot` (the main race-closure test — 8 writers × 2000 reservations; a reader takes `posMu` directly (legal in-package), reads `curr` and every stripe slot inside the critical section, asserts every non-idle slot value v satisfies `v < curr` and `(v - startCurr) % size == 0`; under the old un-coupled reserve + setInsertingAt sequence the reader would observe `curr advanced + stripe still idle` for an in-flight reservation, breaking the invariant; with `reserveAndPublish`, the BEGIN edge is sealed under `posMu` so the snapshot is consistent); `TestInsertPosTrackerReserveAndPublishWatchdog` (5-second watchdog on the concurrent race-closure scenario — surfaces a deadlock regression before the package-level test timeout). Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestInsertPosTracker' ./internal/wal/` PASS (1.04 s); `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/` PASS (3.15 s). PG-compat — none (in-memory primitive; WAL record / file format / catalog / wire all unchanged; lock geometry mirrors PG's `ReserveXLogInsertLocation` + `WALInsertLockUpdateInsertingAt` together under WAL insert lock). Out of scope (later slice B foundations and call-site rewrite): mounting `reserveAndPublish` on `Writer` and rewriting `state.append` to consume it (multi-loop work because `state.append` currently advances `walBuf.tail` and `memRing.tail` synchronously inside `appendMu`; the rewrite splits `state.appendMu`'s four invariants — writePos / walBuf / memRing / writeLSN — into per-stripe local state vs. shared state); the END-edge race (publishing idle) — the END `setInsertingAt(idle)` is intentionally outside `posMu` because the END only needs the stripe lock for synchronisation; the publication-walker invariant the END must respect is "no observation of lsnIdle without observing the preceding byte writes," which the atomic Load on the slot already provides under Go's memory model; no further sealing needed on the END side; drain coordination with concurrent stripe writes (`drainBufferBytes` currently runs under `appendMu` — the rewrite must let drain run concurrently with stripe writes by consuming `tailPublisher.publishUpTo`'s return as drain ceiling for both `walBuffer.advanceHead` and `MemRing.PublishUpTo`); deciding whether `lsnAllocator` ([[0107-0007h]]) becomes dead-code-removed once the call-site converges on `insertPosTracker` + `insertionTracker` + `tailPublisher` + `reserveAndPublish` — `reserve` remains in the API as a callable primitive without a tracker. |
| 0107-0007o | [Phase D4 — `MemRing.WriteReserved` + `MemRing.PublishUpTo` stripe-concurrent in-memory mirror (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 8)](0107-0007o-wal-mem-ring-write-reserved.md) | accepted | Eighth slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2. Adds two methods to the existing `MemRing` (`internal/wal/mem_ring.go`, M0010-0002 walsender in-memory mirror) plus the sentinel error `errMemRingReservedOutOfRange`, all in new file `internal/wal/mem_ring_concurrent.go`. `WriteReserved(pos int64, data []byte) error` writes `len(data)` bytes at LSN byte position `pos` without advancing head or tail; the bytes become readable via `ReadAt` only after a subsequent `PublishUpTo` advances tail past `pos+len(data)`. `PublishUpTo(safeTail int64)` advances tail monotonically to `safeTail`, evicting the oldest residents (advancing head) when `safeTail - head > cap`. Problem: the existing `MemRing.Append(pos, data)` has a sequential-writer contract that *resets the ring* on non-`tail` `pos` ("the existing residence is no longer trustworthy"). Under the slice B 8-stripe writer model, peer stripes reserve and write disjoint LSN ranges out-of-order — feeding such writes through `Append` would reset the ring on every other call, destroying the walsender RAM cache. The slice B writer-side needs a primitive matching the [[0107-0007l]] `walBuffer.writeReserved` shape: disjoint-LSN writes with no implicit tail advance, plus a separate publication step driven by [[0107-0007n]] `tailPublisher`. Errors: `errMemRingReservedOutOfRange` if `[pos, pos+len(data))` escapes the ring's currently-allocated `[head, head+cap)` window — covers both `pos<head` (already evicted by prior `PublishUpTo`) and `pos+n>head+cap` (write target outside the ring's address range); exact boundary `pos+n==head+cap` is accepted. Empty data is a no-op returning nil; runs *before* the range check so a zero-length "reservation" with out-of-window `pos` is benign — eliminates a class of spurious errors from defensive callers. Nil receiver is a no-op returning nil for both methods (matches the `MemRing.Append` nil-safe convention so the slice B call-site rewrite can leave the ring unset under `wal_sender_memory_buffer == 0` without an extra nil-guard at every write site). Concurrency: `WriteReserved` holds the read lock for the memcpy duration; multiple `WriteReserved`s at disjoint LSN ranges (and hence disjoint ring-slot ranges, since each reservation is smaller than the 16 MiB default cap) run in parallel under the read lock. `PublishUpTo` takes the write lock and excludes everything — this is required because head advance reclaims ring slots that an in-flight `WriteReserved` at a low LSN might still be mid-memcpy on. (The slice B call site further constrains: `tailPublisher`'s `safeTail` can never exceed any stripe's active reservation LSN, so a well-behaved drain never advances past an active write; the lock here is defence in depth for misbehaving callers and the bootstrap window.) Overlapping LSN ranges from two concurrent `WriteReserved`s are a contract violation producing undefined ring contents (overlapping copy regions race); the slice B call site makes this structurally impossible via [[0107-0007k]] `insertPosTracker`'s joint-atomicity of `(curr, prev)` under `posMu`. PG counterpart: PG does not have a separate "memring" — its equivalent is the shared WAL buffer `XLogCtl->pages` that `CopyXLogRecordToWAL` writes into under WAL insert locks, with `XLogCtl->LogwrtResult.Write` as the published watermark; goopg's MemRing exists for a different reason (M0010-0001's direct-IO write path bypassing the OS page cache), but under stripe-concurrent writers both rings need identical publication discipline. Coexistence: `Append` and `WriteReserved`+`PublishUpTo` describe two writer modes; they take the same `mu` correctly so coexistence is mechanically safe, but in practice a given `Writer` will use one or the other after the call-site rewrite. Lock-ordering tier (leaf reader on the write side; leaf publisher on the drain side): writer chain `appendLockSet.lockByProcNum → insertPosTracker.reserve → insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(start) → walBuffer.writeReserved → MemRing.WriteReserved → insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(idle) → drop stripe lock`; drain `tailPublisher.publishUpTo(upperBound, insertionTracker) → walBuffer.advanceHead(published - prior) → MemRing.PublishUpTo(published)`. Pre-reserve race carry-over from [[0107-0007m]] and [[0107-0007n]]: the observed `lowestActiveLSN` (which `tailPublisher` consumes and feeds to `MemRing.PublishUpTo`) can temporarily exceed the true minimum between `insertPosTracker.reserve` returning and the matching `setInsertingAt(stripe, start)`; closing this race is the call-site rewrite's job (option A: move `setInsertingAt` under `posMu`; option B: emit a pre-reserve marker), not this foundation's. Dead code until slice B's call-site rewrite mounts these methods on `Writer` and consumes them from `state.append` + the drain/flush goroutine; foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] / [[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]] / [[0107-0007g]]) and the seven earlier slice B foundations ([[0107-0007h]] / [[0107-0007i]] / [[0107-0007j]] / [[0107-0007k]] / [[0107-0007l]] / [[0107-0007m]] / [[0107-0007n]]). Regression coverage in `internal/wal/mem_ring_concurrent_test.go` (15 tests): `TestMemRingWriteReservedAtHeadNoWrap` (write at `pos==head==0`, head/tail untouched, bytes at `buf[:5]`); `TestMemRingWriteReservedAtNonZeroOffset` (LSN→slot arithmetic at non-zero offset; pre-marker fill detects any leakage outside target range); `TestMemRingWriteReservedWrapsAcrossRingBoundary` (write straddles cap boundary, split across `[pos%cap, cap)` and `[0, n-first)`); `TestMemRingWriteReservedRejectsBelowHead` (after `PublishUpTo` advances head, pre-head pos rejected); `TestMemRingWriteReservedRejectsPastWindow` (exact boundary `pos+n==head+cap` accepted; `pos+n>head+cap` and `pos==head+cap` rejected); `TestMemRingWriteReservedEmptyIsNoop` (nil/empty data short-circuit *before* range check; out-of-window empty write still returns nil; head/tail untouched); `TestMemRingWriteReservedNilReceiver` (nil receiver returns nil for both methods); `TestMemRingWriteReservedDoesNotMutateHeadTail` (8 writes leave head/tail exactly as before); `TestMemRingPublishUpToAdvancesTail` (tail tracks `safeTail`; head stays at 0 when residency fits in cap); `TestMemRingPublishUpToMonotonic` (regressing or equal `safeTail` is a no-op); `TestMemRingPublishUpToEvictsWhenOverCap` (`safeTail-head>cap` advances head; pinned across two evictions); `TestMemRingPublishUpToNilReceiver` (defensive nil-safety on publisher side); `TestMemRingWriteReservedReadbackViaReadAt` (end-to-end: ReadAt misses before publication, hits after with same bytes); `TestMemRingWriteReservedConcurrentDisjoint` (8 goroutines × 50 records × 16 bytes in disjoint LSN ranges, race-clean under `-race`, every stripe's marker bytes land in the right slot after final `PublishUpTo`); `TestMemRingPublishUpToAndWriteReservedSerialise` (8 writers × 100 records race while publisher goroutine continuously advances tail using min-across-writers progress to mimic `tailPublisher`'s discipline; final ReadAt of every written LSN range succeeds with the right bytes). Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestMemRing' ./internal/wal/` PASS (1.02 s); `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/` PASS (3.13 s). PG-compat: none (in-memory primitive; WAL record / file format / catalog / wire all unchanged). Out of scope (later slice B foundations and call-site rewrite): mounting `MemRing.WriteReserved` + `PublishUpTo` on `Writer` and rewriting `state.append`'s current `MemRing.Append` call (multi-loop work because `state.append` currently advances `walBuf.tail` and `memRing.tail` jointly inside `appendMu`; the rewrite splits the two and lets drain run concurrently); closing the pre-reserve race ([[0107-0007m]] §"Pre-reserve race") — owned by call-site rewrite; drain coordination with concurrent stripe writes (`drainBufferBytes` currently runs under `appendMu` — the rewrite must let drain run concurrently with stripe writes by consuming `tailPublisher.publishUpTo`'s return as the drain ceiling for both `walBuffer.advanceHead` and `MemRing.PublishUpTo`); deciding whether `lsnAllocator` ([[0107-0007h]]) becomes dead-code-removed once the call-site converges on `insertPosTracker` + `insertionTracker` + `tailPublisher`. |
| 0107-0007n | [Phase D4 — WAL `tailPublisher` publication watermark (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 7)](0107-0007n-wal-tail-publisher.md) | accepted | Seventh slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2. Adds `tailPublisher` to new file `internal/wal/tail_publisher.go`: `atomic.Int64 published` + `newTailPublisher()` + `load() int64` + `publishUpTo(upperBound int64, tracker *insertionTracker) int64`. Computes `candidate = min(upperBound, tracker.lowestActiveLSN())` and CAS-loops the published watermark monotonically; returns `min(currentPublishedWatermark, upperBound)` so a peer that pushed the watermark past the caller's request does not leak a drain-eligible LSN beyond the caller's view (matches PG's `WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish(upTo)` return contract). PG counterpart: PG splits the role across `WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish` (walks `WALInsertLock[i].insertingAt` and waits) + `XLogCtl->LogwrtRqst.Write` (monotonic watermark) in `postgres/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c`; goopg merges them because `atomic.Int64.CompareAndSwap` makes the monotonic-publish loop trivial and the wait-vs-poll policy belongs to the caller. The publisher is non-blocking by construction. Why monotonic publication: two concurrent calls may observe different `lowestActiveLSN` depending on which stripes happen to be idle when each call reads; without monotonicity a published value could regress, racing readers (drain, walsender, `readAt`) against fresh inserts below the prior watermark — exactly the hazard that prompted [[0107-0007l]] `walBuffer.writeReserved` to leave `tail` untouched. Sentinel composition: when every stripe is idle, `lowestActiveLSN == lsnNoActive == math.MaxInt64` and the min collapses to `upperBound`; the sentinel cannot leak into the published value because only `candidate` (≤ upperBound) is ever stored. nil-safety: nil receiver returns 0, nil tracker behaves as "all idle" (safeTail = upperBound) — mirrors the foundation-level nil-safety arguments from [[0107-0007h]] / [[0107-0007l]] and lets a future `Writer` constructor leave the publisher unset under `Config.WALBuffers == 0`. Lock-ordering tier (leaf reader): `appendLockSet.lockByProcNum → insertPosTracker.reserve → insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(start) → walBuffer.writeReserved → insertionTracker.setInsertingAt(idle) → drop stripe lock`; then separately on the drain goroutine `tailPublisher.publishUpTo(upperBound, insertionTracker) → walBuffer.advanceHead(published - prior)`. Pre-reserve race carry-over from [[0107-0007m]]: between `insertPosTracker.reserve` returning and the matching `setInsertingAt(stripe, start)` the observed `lowestActiveLSN` can temporarily exceed the true minimum; the publisher cannot close this race by itself — it is the call-site rewrite's job (option A: move `setInsertingAt` under `posMu`; option B: emit a pre-reserve marker). Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite mounts the publisher on `Writer` and drives it from the drain/flush goroutine; foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] / [[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]] / [[0107-0007g]]) and the six earlier slice B foundations ([[0107-0007h]] / [[0107-0007i]] / [[0107-0007j]] / [[0107-0007k]] / [[0107-0007l]] / [[0107-0007m]]). PG-compat — none (in-memory primitive; WAL record / file format / catalog / wire all unchanged; identical role to PG's `WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish` + `XLogCtl->LogwrtRqst.Write` pair). |
| 0107-0007m | [Phase D4 — WAL `insertionTracker` per-stripe insertion-in-progress LSN slot (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 6)](0107-0007m-wal-insertion-tracker.md) | accepted | Sixth slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2. Adds `insertionTracker` to new file `internal/wal/insertion_tracker.go`: `[appendLockStripes]atomic.Int64 inserting` per-stripe slot array + sentinels `lsnIdle = 0` (zero value of `atomic.Int64`, exploits the constructor's no-init contract) and `lsnNoActive = math.MaxInt64` (sentinel for "all stripes idle" — composes with `safeTail = min(upperBound, lowestActiveLSN())` without a branch in the publication-walker hot path). API: `newInsertionTracker()`, `setInsertingAt(stripe int, lsn int64)`, `insertingAt(stripe int) int64`, `lowestActiveLSN() int64`. PG counterpart: `WALInsertLock[i].insertingAt` + `WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish` in `postgres/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c` — each stripe publishes its current insert start LSN under the stripe lock; the flush coordinator computes a publication watermark from the per-stripe slots. goopg lands the slot machinery here so it can be exercised in isolation; the publication walker (computing `safeTail` and advancing `walBuffer.tail`) lands in its own later foundation once the wait policy is settled. Per-stripe contract: stripe takes `appendLockSet.lockByProcNum(procNum)` → `insertPosTracker.reserve(size)` → `setInsertingAt(stripe, start)` (publish active LSN, sequenced-before the byte write) → `walBuffer.writeReserved(start, bytes)` → `setInsertingAt(stripe, lsnIdle)` (publish idle, sequenced-after byte write) → drop stripe lock. Per-slot `atomic.Int64.Store` / `.Load` gives the happens-before pairing Go's memory model requires: a walker that observes `lsnIdle` for stripe i also observes every byte the stripe sequenced before going idle (sequential-consistency on amd64/arm64; per-slot acquire on weaker memory platforms is sufficient because cross-stripe ordering is not required for tail safety). The tracker itself acquires no locks — each stripe writes only its own slot. Known pre-reserve race (between `insertPosTracker.reserve` returning and `setInsertingAt` publishing the active LSN): documented in the design doc §"Pre-reserve race (future-loop concern)" with two closures — pre-reserve marker (write floor LSN before reserve, refine to exact start after) and reserve-and-publish hook (callback under `posMu`). Both are forward-compatible with this foundation; the call-site rewrite picks one. Why not couple this into `insertPosTracker`: that primitive is a single-writer abstraction over the LSN axis; stripe identity is a separate concern owned by `appendLockSet`. Keeping them split lets each be unit-tested in isolation and lets future call-site rewrites compose them differently (e.g., a non-striped fallback path reuses `insertPosTracker` without an `insertionTracker`). Out-of-range stripe panics on both Set and Get — silent neighbour-slot corruption is a worse failure mode than a fast crash at the bad index. Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite mounts the tracker on `Writer`; foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] / [[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]] / [[0107-0007g]]) and the five earlier slice B foundations ([[0107-0007h]] / [[0107-0007i]] / [[0107-0007j]] / [[0107-0007k]] / [[0107-0007l]]). Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestInsertionTracker' ./internal/wal/` PASS; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/` PASS. Out of scope (future slice B foundations): the publication walker itself (computing `safeTail` and advancing `walBuffer.tail`); the pre-reserve race closure (pre-reserve marker vs reserve-and-publish hook — owned by call-site rewrite); mounting `insertionTracker` on `Writer` and wiring begin/end around the byte write (multi-loop scope); `memRing` mirror handling under stripe-concurrent writes; drain coordination with concurrent stripe writes; deciding whether `lsnAllocator` ([[0107-0007h]]) becomes dead-code-removed once the call-site converges on `insertPosTracker` + `insertionTracker`. PG-compat — none (in-memory primitive; WAL record / file format / catalog / wire all unchanged; identical slot geometry to PG's `WALInsertLock.insertingAt` field). |
| 0107-0007l | [Phase D4 — `walBuffer.writeReserved` concurrent-stripe bytes-write primitive (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 5)](0107-0007l-wal-buffer-write-reserved.md) | accepted | Fifth slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2. Adds `(*walBuffer).writeReserved(lsn int64, record []byte) error` to `internal/wal/wal_buffer.go`. Copies `record` into the ring at the offset corresponding to absolute byte LSN `lsn` without mutating `head`, `tail`, or `base`. This is the bytes-write counterpart to [[0107-0007k]]'s LSN reserve: a stripe holds `appendLocks[i]` (from [[0107-0007i]]), reserves `[lsn, lsn+n)` atomically via `insertPosTracker.reserve` ([[0107-0007k]]), then lands bytes here while peer stripes write into disjoint LSN ranges in parallel. PG counterpart: `CopyXLogRecordToWAL` in `postgres/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c` writes into the shared `XLogCtl->pages` buffer at the previously-reserved offset; PG's `WALInsertLocks` serialise writes WITHIN a stripe's LSN range, ACROSS stripes the writes proceed concurrently because the LSN reservations are disjoint. Errors: `errWALBufferNil` if receiver is nil (matches the `s.walBuf != nil` guard pattern in `state.append`, makes the 8-stripe call-site rewrite safe against `Config.WALBuffers == 0`); `errWALBufferReservedOutOfRange` if `[lsn, lsn+len(record))` extends below `base` or past `base+cap` (catches caller contract violation; `insertPosTracker` is supposed to keep reservations inside the window). Empty record is a no-op (matches `state.appendRaw`'s `len == 0` short-circuit) — runs before the range check so a zero-length out-of-range reservation is still a no-op. Concurrent safety: two writers writing into disjoint LSN ranges of the same buffer are safe under Go's memory model (Go's `copy` on disjoint byte slice regions is data-race free); overlapping ranges is a contract violation that produces undefined byte contents (not detected — would need per-byte ownership map). Tail publication (advancing `tail` so resident bytes become visible to drain/readers) is deliberately a separate slice B foundation: it can't advance past LSN X until *every* reservation strictly below X has had its bytes written by its owning stripe (needs either a `publishedLSN` atomic walking `prev` chains, or PG-style `WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish(LSN)`). Wrap branch mirrors `walBuffer.append`'s wrap-aware copy verbatim; under the current contract (`lsn+len ≤ base+cap`, `cap == len(buf)`) the wrap branch is structurally unreachable from valid callers — the LSN window equals the ring capacity — but is retained for symmetry with `append`/`readAt` and robustness against future contract changes. Lock-ordering tier for the future call-site rewrite: `appendLockSet.lockByProcNum` → `insertPosTracker.reserve` (briefly under `posMu`) → (rare on segment crossings) `buildSegmentPadRecord` → `walBuffer.writeReserved` (no lock; leaf of chain). Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite mounts these primitives on `Writer` and rewrites `state.append` / `state.appendRaw` to use them — foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] / [[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] all landed before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]] / [[0107-0007g]] consumed them) and the four earlier slice B foundations ([[0107-0007h]] / [[0107-0007i]] / [[0107-0007j]] / [[0107-0007k]]). Regression coverage in `internal/wal/wal_buffer_write_reserved_test.go` (nine tests): `TestWALBufferWriteReservedAtBaseNoWrap` (write at `lsn==base`, bytes at `buf[0..n]`, head/tail/base unchanged); `TestWALBufferWriteReservedAtNonZeroOffset` (LSN→ring-offset arithmetic at non-zero offset; neighbouring bytes untouched); `TestWALBufferWriteReservedRejectsBelowBase` (`lsn<base` rejected); `TestWALBufferWriteReservedRejectsPastEnd` (`lsn+n>base+cap` and `lsn=base+cap` both rejected; `lsn+n==base+cap` exactly accepted); `TestWALBufferWriteReservedEmptyIsNoop` (`nil`/`[]byte{}` short-circuit before range check; head/tail/base unmodified); `TestWALBufferWriteReservedNilReceiver` (nil receiver returns `errWALBufferNil`); `TestWALBufferWriteReservedConcurrentDisjoint` (8 goroutines × 50 records × 16 bytes in disjoint LSN ranges; race-clean under `-race`; `readAt` confirms every stripe's marker bytes land in the right slot after manual tail publication); `TestWALBufferWriteReservedReadbackViaReadAt` (bytes written at LSN X read back identically via `readAt(X)`); `TestWALBufferWriteReservedDoesNotMutateTailHeadBase` (series of writes leaves `base`/`head`/`tail` exactly as before — pins the publication-is-separate contract). Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestWALBufferWriteReserved' ./internal/wal/` PASS (1.02 s); `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/` PASS (3.12 s). Out of scope (later slice B foundations): tail publication primitive; mounting `appendLockSet` + `insertPosTracker` + `writeReserved` on `Writer` and rewriting `state.append` / `state.appendRaw` (the full call-site rewrite that splits `state.appendMu`'s four invariants — writePos / walBuf / memRing / writeLSN — into per-stripe local state vs. shared state); `prevRecPtr` chain integrity under per-stripe writers; `memRing` mirror handling under stripe-concurrent writes; drain coordination with concurrent stripe writes; deciding whether `lsnAllocator` ([[0107-0007h]]) becomes dead-code-removed once the call-site converges on `insertPosTracker`. PG-compat — none (in-memory primitive; WAL record / file format / catalog / wire all unchanged; identical bytes-write geometry to PG's `CopyXLogRecordToWAL` writing into `XLogCtl->pages`). |
| 0107-0007k | [Phase D4 — WAL `insertPosTracker` PG-compat prevRecPtr chain (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 4)](0107-0007k-wal-insert-pos-tracker.md) | accepted | Fourth slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2. Adds `insertPosTracker` to new file `internal/wal/insert_pos.go`: `sync.Mutex posMu` + `uint64 curr` + `uint64 prev` + immutable `segSize` + optional `onCrossSegment(start, boundary, prev uint64)` callback. `reserve(size) (start, prev uint64)` holds `posMu` for the joint (curr, prev) update — matching PG's `ReserveXLogInsertLocation` which advances `XLogCtl->Insert.CurrBytePos` + `PrevBytePos` under one spinlock (`postgres/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c`). Segment crossings fire `onCross` synchronously under `posMu` so the gap `[gapStart, boundary)` is observed once per crossing; the reservation that triggered the crossing lands at `boundary` with `prev = gapStart` so the xl_prev chain remains unbroken across the boundary (the pad record built by [[0107-0007j]] `buildSegmentPadRecord` will be stamped with the inherited `gapPrev`). Why a mutex instead of CAS: two atomics cannot be CAS-updated together; the (curr, prev) joint atomicity is *required* (a peer must never observe `curr` past LSN X without `prev` set to the start of the record that reserved X); PG faces the identical constraint and picks a spinlock — we follow with `sync.Mutex` because 128-bit CAS is non-portable in Go. Uncontended cost ~10 ns vs ~2 ns for atomic CAS, but at the per-stripe rate (≤ 8 backends ever race here because the 8 stripe locks above this primitive cap concurrency) contention is bounded. Lock-ordering tier for the future call-site rewrite: `appendLockSet.lockByProcNum` → `insertPosTracker.reserve` (briefly under `posMu`) → (rare, only on crossings) `onCrossSegment` hook → e.g. `buildSegmentPadRecord` + WAL-buffer write. Coexists with [[0107-0007h]] `lsnAllocator` (a CAS-fast-path reserve without prev tracking, suitable for callers that don't need the xl_prev chain); the WAL append path needs the chain so it consumes this primitive. Dead code until the slice B call-site rewrite mounts it on `Writer`; foundation-first pattern matches slice C ([[0107-0007b]] / [[0107-0007c]] / [[0107-0007d]] before [[0107-0007e]] / [[0107-0007f]] / [[0107-0007g]]). Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestInsertPosTracker' ./internal/wal/` PASS (1.02 s); `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/` PASS (3.13 s). Out of scope: mounting `insertPosTracker` on `Writer` + rewriting `Append` to take a stripe lock + reserve here (call-site rewrite, multi-loop scope); splitting `state.appendMu`'s four invariants (writePos / walBuf / memRing / writeLSN); deciding whether `lsnAllocator` becomes dead-code-removed once the call-site converges on `insertPosTracker` (independent later decision). PG-compat — none (in-memory primitive; WAL record / file format / catalog / wire all unchanged; identical lock geometry to PG's `insertpos_lck` spinlock). |
| 0107-0007j | [Phase D4 — WAL segment pad-record builder (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 3)](0107-0007j-wal-segment-pad-record.md) | accepted | Third slice B foundation for parent chapter [[07-wal-fsm-insert]] §2's cross-segment slow path.
