Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestPredictEmittedSize' ./internal/wal/` PASS (~2 s); `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/` PASS (~4 s); `go vet ./internal/wal/` clean. PG-compat — none (pure size-prediction mirror; produces no bytes, does not interact with on-disk WAL). |
| 0107-0007ai | [Phase D4 — WAL buffer head/base atomic upgrade + async drain: appendPGCompat Path B lock-free (M0107-0007, slice B)](0107-0007ai-wal-buffer-head-base-atomic-async-drain.md) | accepted | Closes the last Lock()-on-hot-path bottleneck: (1) upgrades `walBuffer.head` and `walBuffer.base` to `atomic.Int64` (parallel of [[0107-0007r]]'s tail upgrade) so concurrent stripe writers' `free()`/`writeReserved` reads are race-free against the drain goroutine's `advanceHead` stores; (2) removes `appendMu.Lock()/Unlock()` from `appendPGCompat` Path B — drain runs without any outer lock; stripe append takes its own stripe lock via `AppendXLogPayload`. Safety: drain reads `[head, head+need)`, stripe writes at `lsn ≥ tail ≥ head+need` (disjoint); `advanceHead` is single-writer (state-loop goroutine only); `advanceHead` stores base-first-then-head to prevent false `errWALBufferReservedOutOfRange` from concurrent `writeReserved` range checks. State-loop bookkeeping (`writePos`, `writeLSN`) unchanged (state-loop-only fields); `writeLSNMirror` uses `storeMaxLSN` (CAS-max) consistent with [[0107-0007ah]]. Four new tests in `wal_buffer_head_base_atomic_test.go` (compile-time pins + concurrent drain/read race-freedom); two new integration tests in `append_pgcompat_async_drain_test.go`. Verified: `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/ ./internal/executor/ ./internal/storage/ ./internal/mvcc/ ./internal/server/ ./internal/access/btree/` all PASS. |
| 0107-0007aj | [Phase D4 — WAL buffer reservation must cover the segment-crossing pad footprint (M0107-0007; surfaced by M0118-0001)](0107-0007aj-wal-segment-cross-reservation.md) | accepted | Fixes `errWALBufferReservedOutOfRange` that tripped the `multiple-row-versions` isolation spec's 1,000,000-row bulk-insert setup ~50% of runs. Both buffered append paths (`state.tryAppend` fast path, `state.appendPGCompat` Path B) reserved only `conservativeSize` (`paddedLen+64`) ring bytes, but a record whose stripe reservation straddles a WAL segment boundary occupies up to `2*conservativeSize`: `reserveEmittedAndPublish` emits an `XLOG_NOOP` pad over the gap `[curr, boundary)` (a `writeReserved` via `emitSegmentPad`) AND re-lands the record at the boundary (a second `writeReserved`); near-full, the second write left the `[head, head+cap)` window. Crossing predicate gives `gapLen < total ≤ conservativeSize`, so `footprint < 2*conservativeSize` is a strict, `curr`-independent (race-free) upper bound. Fix reserves `reserveSize = 2*conservativeSize` in `tryReserve`/`canHold`/`needsDrain`/Path-B `need`/`releaseReservation`. Single writers never tripped it (they take the all-draining Path A before a crossing can overflow); the overflow needs concurrency (`reservedBytes` from peer stripes, or Path B in the state loop). Negligible cost (extra ~record-sized headroom on a multi-MiB ring). Regression: `internal/wal/segment_cross_reservation_test.go` `TestConcurrentAppendAcrossSegmentBoundariesNoOverflow` (8×6000 concurrent appends, 32 KiB segments, 12 000-byte near-full ring) — fails 3/3 when reverted to `conservativeSize`, green under `-race -count=5`. Verified `go test -race ./internal/wal/` PASS. **2026-07-07 (AI-20260707-000712-001)**: the "Concurrency correctness" proof missed that `appendPGCompat` Path B's own headroom recheck (as opposed to the Path A/B gate) never subtracted `reservedBytes`, so a concurrent `tryAppend` fast-path claim could still overflow the ring past Path B's stale `free()`-only check; fixed by having Path B claim/release its `reserveSize` via the same `tryReserve`/`releaseReservation` CAS pair `tryAppend` uses (looping drain+claim until the reservation succeeds) instead of a plain comparison. Reproduces reliably at `GOMAXPROCS=2`/`-cpu=2` (~1/15 at `-count=1`, every time at `-count=15`); fix verified 15/15 plus a separate 8/8 clean, revert-confirmed non-vacuous. |
| 0107-0007y | [Phase D4 — `stripeAppendBuild` encode-after-reserve composer (M0107-0007, slice B foundation 16)](0107-0007y-stripe-append-build.md) | accepted | Adds the encode-after-reserve sibling of [[0107-0007u]] `stripeAppend` so the slice B call-site rewrite can materialise PG-compat record bytes using the prev LSN that [[0107-0007k]] `insertPosTracker.reserveAndPublish` returns. `stripeAppend` takes a pre-encoded `record []byte`; that contract is structurally insufficient for PG-compat records (`encodeRecordXLog`) because `XLogRecord.Prev` (`xl_prev`) carries the immediately-preceding record's start LSN — known only AFTER the reservation. Pre-encoding with a stale prev breaks the chain under concurrent stripe writers; patching the encoded record in place after reservation forces cross-stripe coupling that slice B is eliminating. The clean fix is to invert the order: reserve first, then encode with the assigned prev, then write. New function `stripeAppendBuild(locks, posTracker, insertTracker, walBuf, memRing, procNum, size, build func(prev uint64) ([]byte, error)) (start, prev uint64, err error)` in `internal/wal/stripe_append.go` slots `build(prev)` between `reserveAndPublish` and the byte writes, all under the stripe lock — `build` runs after posMu is released so multi-stripe encoders cannot serialise on the same posMu. Contracts: `size > 0` (zero panics inside reserveAndPublish), `build != nil`, `len(build(prev)) == size` (mismatch corrupts peer stripes — over — or publishes zeros — under), build errors propagate verbatim and END marker fires via defer (publication never freezes). New `(*stripeWriterCore).AppendBuilt(procNum, size, build)` wraps it. Cross-segment crossings are transparent: build observes the prev that points at the pad record, not the pre-pad record. Regression coverage in `internal/wal/stripe_append_build_test.go` (11 tests): two-record happy path pins prev=0 → prev=start1 chain; nil-guards on all four pointer args + build; size ∈ {0, -1} → `errStripeAppendEmptyRecord`; build error propagation with END-marker assertion; size-mismatch (15, 17 vs 16) → `errStripeAppendBuildSizeMismatch`; independent nil-safety per ring; 128-byte segment cross with two 80 B records pins build receiving prev=80 (pad LSN) and rec #2 landing at LSN 128; 8×50 concurrent disjoint stripes with all 400 starts distinct; `core.AppendBuilt` end-to-end through reserve→build→publish→read-back; nil receiver guard. Verified: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestStripeAppendBuild\|TestStripeWriterCoreAppendBuilt' ./internal/wal/` PASS (1.04 s); `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wal/` PASS (3.18 s); `go vet ./internal/wal/` clean. PG-compat — none (in-memory composer; the encoded record bytes the build closure returns are identical to what the legacy `state.append` path emits via `encodeRecordXLog`, just produced under a stripe lock instead of `state.appendMu`). Out of scope (deferred to slice B call-site rewrite parts 2/3): mounting `core.AppendBuilt` as the body of `state.append` for the PG-compat path; mounting `core.PublishUpTo` in the drain goroutine's prelude; 8-byte MAXALIGN of record sizes in the Append pre-amble (already satisfied by `encodeRecordXLog`'s `maxAlignXLog(realLen)` padding); group-commit fast path (`tryAppend`) reroute; walreceiver replay (`appendRaw`) does not need stripeAppendBuild — its bytes arrive pre-encoded so plain `core.Append` (foundation 14) is the right primitive for that site. |
| 0097-0075 | [UPDATE … FROM … RETURNING projects FROM-table columns (M0097)](0097-0075-update-from-returning-projection.md) | accepted | `planUpdate` resolves RETURNING expressions against a combined `[target_cols..., from_cols...]` binding context (planner.go:4977), so column references to a joined FROM table carry indices past `len(tgtCols)`. The executor's `updateWithFrom` (`internal/executor/operators_storage.go:2645`) carried the full `combinedRow` through nested-loop FROM-pred evaluation correctly, but `pendingUpdate` only stored target-only `newRow`, and `appendUpdateRetRow(pu.newRow)` evaluated RETURNING against a target-only slice — out-of-range FROM-column references returned NULL silently. The first divergent case in the `returning` regress test (`UPDATE foo SET f3 = f3*2 FROM int4_tbl i WHERE foo.f1 + 123455 = i.f1 RETURNING foo.*, i.f1 as "i.f1"`) returned `NULL` for `i.f1` instead of `123456`. Fix is 3-part: (1) split `appendUpdateRetRow` into a wrapper + `appendUpdateRetRowWithFrom(newRow, fromPortion Row)` that builds `evalRow = [newRow..., fromPortion...]` before evaluating; (2) `pendingUpdate` gains a `fromPortion Row` field cloned from `combinedRow[tgtColCount:]` at recursion leaf (cloning required because the recurse reuses backing storage); (3) the pending-apply loop calls the new helper. Non-FROM `updateOp` callers (`updateViaIndex`, `Next[2]`) continue to use the legacy wrapper which forwards `fromPortion == nil`. `returning` regress diff 553→545 lines (-8); next blockers are DELETE USING parser, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN DEFAULT backfill, INHERITS row propagation, RETURNING OLD/NEW. Sibling-path class [[pattern_sibling_paths_must_agree]] (planner-resolved schema vs executor evaluation row shape). |
| 0097-0076 | [DELETE … USING clause (M0097)](0097-0076-delete-using-clause.md) | accepted | `parseDelete` had no USING branch, so `DELETE FROM foo USING int4_tbl WHERE foo.f1 + 123455 = int4_tbl.f1 RETURNING foo.*, int4_tbl.f1` silently no-op'd on the next divergent `returning` regress line after [[0097-0075]]. Fix mirrors the existing UPDATE … FROM path in four layers: (1) parser — `DeleteStmt` gains `Using []RangeVar`; `parseDelete` consumes an optional `USING` keyword after the target and parses a comma-separated `parseRangeVar` list before WHERE. (2) analyzer — `analyzeDelete` appends each USING table to the scope's `rels` list with its alias (or table name when none is given) so `WHERE`/`RETURNING` references type-check; also now analyzes `s.Returning` (mirroring `analyzeUpdate`). Without the analyzer extension `resolveColumnRefType` raises 42P01 *missing FROM-clause entry for table "a"* before the planner runs. (3) planner — `Delete` gains `UsingTables`/`UsingScans`/`UsingSchema`/`UsingPred` fields; `planDelete` adds an early branch when `len(s.Using) > 0` that builds a combined `rangeBinding`s context with monotonically increasing `sourceIdx` (1, 2, …) and `offset` advancing by each table's column count; WHERE resolves to `UsingPred`, RETURNING resolves against the same context so projecting USING-table columns works the same way as UPDATE FROM RETURNING. (4) executor — `deleteOp.Next` dispatches to a new `deleteWithUsing` when `len(o.plan.UsingTables) > 0`. Mirrors `updateWithFrom`: collect all rows of each USING table, scan target with no predicate, do recursive nested-loop cross-product against cached USING rows, each combination evaluated against `UsingPred`. Each target slot recorded at most once (`seen` set keyed by `(block, slot)`) matching PG's semantics that a single qualifying row deletes the tuple even when multiple cross-product rows match. `appendDeleteRetRowWithUsing(oldRow, usingPortion)` builds `evalRow = [oldRow..., usingPortion...]` before RETURNING evaluation; plain-DELETE path's `appendDeleteRetRow` forwards `usingPortion == nil` for backwards compatibility. EvalPlanQual retry chain intentionally skipped — concurrent xmax conflicts skip the victim rather than chasing the update chain (acceptable for v0; full EPQ for DELETE USING is M0097-0020 follow-up scope). Coverage: `TestParseDeleteUsing` pins parser; `TestPlanDeleteUsing` pins analyzer+planner column-binding for USING-table refs in WHERE and RETURNING. Sibling-path class [[pattern_sibling_paths_must_agree]] (parser, analyzer, planner, executor must all agree on the same DML-with-extra-tables shape). |
| 0097-0078 | [Inheritance-aware UPDATE/DELETE column remapping (M0097)](0097-0078-inheritance-dml-column-remapping.md) | accepted | UPDATE/DELETE on inherited tables were applying SET/WHERE/RETURNING expressions using parent column ordinals against child row layouts. Fix adds `buildInheritColMap`/`remapChildRowToParent`/`remapParentRowToChild` helpers; the seq-scan, UPDATE...FROM, and DELETE...USING loops detect inheritance children, remap child rows to parent space for predicate+SET evaluation, and remap results back to child layout for writes. RETURNING uses parent-aligned rows. `returning` regress: 479→394 diff lines. |
| 0097-0077 | [ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN … DEFAULT fast default / attmissingval (M0097)](0097-0077-add-column-default-fast-default.md) | accepted | Next in-order `returning` regress divergence after [[0097-0076]]: `ALTER TABLE foo ADD COLUMN f4 int8 DEFAULT 99` added the column but recorded no default, and the heap decoder emitted `NullDatum` for every column beyond the row's stored `natts`, so rows written before the ALTER surfaced NULL instead of the declared DEFAULT — PG instead records the constant as `pg_attribute.attmissingval` and fills it at decode time (the PG 11 "fast default", no table rewrite). Fix mirrors attmissingval: (1) catalog — `Column` gains `MissingValue any` holding an `executor.Datum`, typed `any` to avoid the catalog→executor import cycle; `nil` keeps the prior decode-as-NULL fallback. (2) DDL — `execAlterTableAddColumn` evaluates `DefaultExpr` once at ALTER time via new `constDefaultDatum(expr, type)` (handles int/numeric/string/bool/NULL literals + unary `-` over numeric literals, coerced to the column type; scientific-notation/non-constant → `(_, false)` leaving `MissingValue` nil) and stores the Datum on the column when constant and non-NULL. (3) decoder — `DecodeRowIntoMctxPGTuple`'s `i >= storedNatts` branch surfaces `c.MissingValue.(Datum)` when present, else `NullDatum` (single read site). Bundled inheritance recursion: `addColumnRecursive(tbl, col, …, isRoot)` applies `AddColumn` to the table then recurses over `InMemory.InheritanceChildren(tbl.OID)`; a duplicate-column error on the root (`isRoot==true`) is a real user error → `42701`, on a recursed child it's PG's silent column-merge no-op. The `isRoot` flag fixes a draft bug where root vs child was distinguished by `tbl.Name == act.Column.Name` (table name vs column name — never matches), which silently swallowed the root-table 42701; `TestDDLAlterTableAddColumnDuplicateErrors` guards it. Coverage: `TestDecodeRowIntoMctxPGTuple{Uses,No}MissingValue*`, `TestConstDefaultDatumLiteralCases`, `TestDDLAlterTableAddColumnDefaultBackfillsExistingRows`. Only constant defaults become fast defaults — volatile/expression defaults still decode missing rows as NULL (PG rewrites for those; deferred). |

The `Aborted` array is rebuilt empty on restart (it is not the durable commit log), so after a restart a recovered rolled-back row could read as committed at runtime — recovery consults the CLOG when re-scanning the heap but the runtime snapshot path did not. Sub-`OldestClogXid` XIDs skip the consult (wraparound-safe `storage.XIDPrecedes`, M0117-0001). | 0117-0003 | [`pg_subtrans` restore-on-restart (M0117-0003)](0117-0003-pg-subtrans-restore-on-restart.md) | accepted | M0117 added a write path to a PG-byte-compatible `pg_subtrans` SLRU mirror (`SubtransSLRU.SetParent`, opted in via `SubxactMap.EnablePersistence`) but nothing read it back on startup, and the `Manager`'s runtime subxact store (`subxactParents`) never touched the SLRU — so the persistence machinery was dead in production and subxact parentage was lost across a restart (gap G5 read path). Deliberately diverges from PG's `StartupSUBTRANS` zero-on-startup (G5 consumers — standby/2PC/post-backend-exit readers — need durable parentage); conservative (parentage only redirects a sub-XID to its top-level ancestor, never makes a tuple more visible). Implemented in isolated worktree `m0117-0003-pg-subtrans-restore` off `b3d5b448` to avoid entangling the foreign M0100-0010 catalog WIP. |
| 0117-0005 | [CLOG incremental flush + group commit (M0117-0005)](0117-0005-clog-incremental-flush-group-commit.md) | accepted | `CLog.flush` rewrote the *entire* `global/pg_xact` flat file with `os.WriteFile` on every single-XID `setStatus` (O(N) bytes per commit), and `setStatus` issued one `f.Sync()` per committing XID through `mirrorToSLRUUnlocked` (no amortisation under concurrency) — gap G7. Part A makes the flat write incremental: `setStatus` records the touched 8 kB flat page (`clogFlatPageSize`, always wholly inside one bank since `xidsPerBank` is a multiple of it) in a `dirtyPages` set and the durable write replays only those pages with `WriteAt` (still no fsync — the fsynced `pg_xact/` SLRU stays the source of truth, `MarkUnknownAsAborted` repairs the flat cache after a crash); the bulk/relayout callers (`InitializeAsCommitted`, `MarkUnknownAsAborted`, `TruncateCLOG`) keep the whole-file rewrite, which now takes `flushMu` and clears `dirtyPages`. Part B (`clog_groupcommit.go`) is a faithful Go port of `clog.c:TransactionGroupUpdateXidStatus`: concurrent committers CAS-push a `{xid,status,done}` node onto a Treiber stack (`atomic.Pointer` head ≙ `ProcGlobal->clogGroupFirst`); the first arrival becomes the leader, takes `flushMu`, `Swap`s the whole stack to nil in one atomic op (ABA-free, ≙ `pg_atomic_exchange`), applies the batch durably (one incremental flat-page pass + one `f.Sync()` per touched SLRU *segment* instead of one per XID, OR lane semantics ≙ `TransactionIdSetStatusBit`), drops the lock, then wakes every follower's `done` channel. goopg serialises all durable writes on one `flushMu`, so PG's same-page grouping restriction is dropped (the leader batches across pages/segments freely — strictly more batching). All new `CLog` fields are zero-value-ready, so `&CLog{}`/`OpenCLog` need no constructor change. Pinned by `internal/mvcc/clog_groupcommit_test.go` (concurrent committers → durable re-open + SLRU decode). Implemented in isolated worktree `m0117-0005-clog-incremental-flush-group-commit` off `f6d3d36c` to avoid entangling the foreign M0100-0010 catalog WIP. |
| 0117-0004 | [`SUB_COMMITTED` (0x03) CLOG lane (M0117-0004)](0117-0004-clog-sub-committed-lane.md) | accepted | goopg's PG-byte-compatible `pg_xact/` SLRU mirror knew only three of PG's four 2-bit lane values; the `0x03 = TRANSACTION_STATUS_SUB_COMMITTED` lane (`postgres/src/include/access/clog.h:30`) was never written and `loadFromSLRU` decoded any `0x03` it found as `Committed` with a defensive OR-artifact comment — conflating PG's real "subxact committed, resolve via parent" state with corruption and leaving the mirror unable to round-trip a sub-committed subtransaction (gap G5 `SUB_COMMITTED`, blocking durable subxact resolution for an attached PG standby / 2PC / post-backend-exit readers). Adds `TxnStatusSubCommitted = 3` (raw byte matches the on-disk lane so flat-file and SLRU agree) + `pgClogStatusSubCommitted = 0x03`; teaches the write seam (`mirrorToSLRUUnlocked` + batched `mirrorTerminalRangeBatchedUnlocked`) to emit `0x03` and the read seam (`loadFromSLRU`) to decode it back to `SubCommitted`; new public primitive `CLog.SetSubCommitted(xid)` mirrors `SetCommitted`/`SetAborted` through `setStatus` (flat file + SLRU). Resolution helper `CLog.DidCommit(xid, parentOf)` mirrors `transam.c TransactionIdDidCommit`: `Committed→true`, `Aborted/Unknown→false`, `SubCommitted→` recurse on the parent link supplied by the M0117-0003 `SubxactMap` (nil/zero parent → false, PG's missing-`pg_subtrans`-entry branch). OR mirror semantics are deliberately kept (not switched to PG's clear-then-set): OR preserves a durable committed bit against a stale in-memory abort, and the `0x03` it can produce resolves identically to the old "treat as committed" intent. Visibility (`SeesCommittedXID`, M0117-0002) only flips on a positive `Aborted`, so a bare `SubCommitted` read stays conservatively "assume committed" — the change cannot make a live tuple less visible. Non-goal: `SUB_COMMITTED→COMMITTED` finalisation (PG's two-pass tree write) is deferred — resolution-via-parent makes it unnecessary until a runtime CLOG commit path exists; no live caller wires `SetSubCommitted` yet (encode/decode + resolution machinery only, like the M0117-0002/0003 primitives). Pinned by the extended `internal/mvcc/clog_dual_store_consistency_test.go` (all four lane values round-trip flat-file ↔ SLRU + `DidCommit` parent resolution). Implemented in isolated worktree `m0117-0004-clog-sub-committed` off `24b09523` to avoid entangling the foreign M0100-0010 catalog WIP. |
| 0117-0006 | [CLOG SLRU buffer pool / 2-bit collapse — Part A+B+C (M0117-0006)](0117-0006-clog-slru-buffer-pool.md) | accepted (Part A + B + C landed; C landed 2026-07-01) | goopg's `CLog` keeps the entire commit-log status array resident as per-bank byte slices (`clogBank.data`, one *byte* per XID — `internal/mvcc/clog.go:53`), so memory scales linearly with `NextXID` (16× denser in PG, which packs 4 XIDs/byte into a bounded SLRU buffer pool sized by `transaction_buffers`) — gap G6. This Effort-L memory-model rewrite of the highest-blast-radius subsystem is decomposed; **Part A (this slice)** lands the GUC + the standalone, fully-tested buffer-pool component without touching any live CLOG path (blast radius nil), deferring the risky `GetStatus`/`setStatus` swap (Part B) and the resident-bank removal / flat-file drop (Part C) to a dedicated session that can run the full TPC-H/visibility gate. Adds: (1) the `transaction_buffers` GUC (`defaults.go` + `postgresql.conf.sample`, PGC_POSTMASTER, boot_val 0, max 1GiB/BLCKSZ; registered unit-less as a raw buffer count == PG's `GUC_UNIT_BLOCKS` stored value); (2) `EffectiveCLOGBuffers` — faithful port of `clog.c:CLOGShmemBuffers + SimpleLruAutotuneBuffers` resolving the GUC to a resident-page budget; (3) `clogBufferPool` (`internal/mvcc/clog_bufferpool.go`) — a bounded LRU page cache over the 2-bit SLRU representation backed by the `pg_xact/` segment files: faults a `BLCKSZ` page in on access (missing/short file ⇒ zero = in-progress, ≙ PG faulting an unwritten page), evicts the LRU slot when full (writing back if dirty), reads/updates a single 2-bit lane with PG's clear-then-set (`TransactionIdSetStatusBit`), and `flushDirty` fsyncs each touched *segment* once. Pinned by `internal/mvcc/clog_bufferpool_test.go`, including a **sibling-path encode↔encode equivalence** test (`TestCLOGBufferPoolEncodingMatchesSLRUMirror`) asserting the pool's segment bytes are byte-identical to the existing `mirrorToSLRUUnlocked` writer, so the new store cannot drift from the canonical on-disk format a PG standby reads. Implemented in isolated worktree `m0117-0006-clog-slru-buffer-pool` off `5fcdb27b` to avoid entangling the foreign M0100-0010 catalog WIP; PENDING HUMAN MERGE of the stacked chain m0117-0001 → … → -0006. **Part B LANDED 2026-06-29 (loop #11):** the pool is now the live in-memory store (`CLog.pool atomic.Pointer`, promoted by `EnablePGSLRUMirror` after the backfill); `GetStatus`/`setStatus`, the group-commit leader (`applyGroupBatchLocked`→`pool.flushDirty`), and the bulk callers (`InitializeAsCommitted`/`MarkUnknownAsAborted`/new `highestSLRUXID`-backed `HighestKnownXID`/`TruncateCLOG`→new `pool.invalidateBelow`) all route through it; the never-fsynced goopg-legacy `global/pg_xact` flat file is retired (SLRU is the single durable store, basebackup already excluded it, PG has no such file). The prior "gates SKIP in the autonomous loop" deferral reason was empirically disproven — standby-attach + checksum-streaming E2E, `-race` mvcc/wal (incl. xlog_replay), and the TPC-H Q12=2/Q13=33 spot-check all RUN+PASS. **Part C LANDED 2026-07-01 (loop #47):** the resident `banks`/legacy flat-file store is fully removed — `OpenCLog` no longer reads its path argument, `EnablePGSLRUMirror` creates the pool directly with no backfill round-trip, and `IsEmpty()` is rewritten to a disk-truth check (`highestSLRUXID() == 0`) instead of a process-local flag (a flag would have misreported "empty" on every restart of a populated cluster). ~20 test functions plus 5 direct `loadFromSLRU` callers migrated/rewritten to preserve sibling-path-independence. Full gate suite (`-race` mvcc+wal, initdb+server suites, standby-attach + checksum-streaming E2E, TPC-H Q12=2/Q13=33) PASS; one accepted, deliberate compatibility cut recorded in the ledger (a pre-Part-B data dir's never-mirrored flat-file bytes are now silently unrecoverable — not a PG-fidelity gap, since PG itself has no such dual-store distinction). |
| 0117-0007 | [CLOG async-commit LSN tracking — Parts A–C (M0117-0007)](0117-0007-clog-async-commit-lsn.md) | landed (Parts A–C complete; residual redo-pointer-sampling race deferred, see doc's Part C) | goopg's CLOG has no LSN association — every status change is durably fsynced inline — so there is no "safe to flush to here" LSN per transaction and no way to defer the per-commit WAL fsync under a future `synchronous_commit=off` path without a torn durability guarantee (gap G8). PostgreSQL tracks, per 32-XID group sharing a CLOG page, the highest commit-record LSN (`group_lsn`) and `XLogFlush`es up to it immediately before the page is written back, so a CLOG page never reaches disk claiming a commit whose WAL is not yet durable. This slice (**Part A**) lands that tracking on the M0117-0006 buffer pool as composing infrastructure with **nil live blast radius** (the pool is not yet the live store — M0117-0006 Part B is deferred): (1) per-LSN-group constants `clogXactsPerLSNGroup = 32` / `clogLSNsPerPage = clogXactsPerPage/32 = 1024` and `lsnIndexInPage(xid)` (= PG `GetLSNIndex` minus the `slotno*CLOG_LSNS_PER_PAGE` term, since each `clogPageSlot` carries its own `groupLSN [1024]uint64` rather than a flat cross-slot array); (2) `setStatusWithLSN(xid,status,lsn)` bumps `groupLSN[lsnIndexInPage(xid)] = max(…, lsn)` (≙ `TransactionIdSetPageStatusInternal`; `setStatus` is now `setStatusWithLSN(…,0)`, byte-identical for LSN-free callers; `lsn==0` ≙ `InvalidXLogRecPtr`, a no-op matching PG's recovery branch); (3) `groupLSNFor(xid)` read side (≙ the `*lsn` out-param of `TransactionIdGetStatus`); (4) an injected `flushWAL func(uint64) error` hook (nil ⇒ off, the default) that `writePageToDisk`/`flushDirty` call with the page's max group LSN **before** writing the page out — the async-commit ordering barrier, wired to `wal.Writer.FlushUpTo` only when the pool goes live (Part B). `groupLSN` is in-memory only (zeroed on fault-in ≙ PG never persisting it — an on-disk page's WAL is already durable). **Part B (landed 2026-07-02, loop #49):** wires the barrier to the live WAL writer (`CLog.SetFlushWALHook` ← `walWriter.FlushUpTo`), adds `mvcc.Manager.CommitAsync` (threads a new `waitLocalFlush bool` through `finish`/the `xactMarker` hook, which skips its inline `FlushUpTo` and calls the new `CLog.SetCommittedWithLSN` instead of `SetCommitted` when false), and reads `synchronous_commit` for the local-flush decision for the first time via `executor.Context.AsyncCommit` + `Context.CommitTransaction`, wired at every live interactive commit call site. **Does not yet reduce commit latency**: M0117-0005's `groupUpdate` still flushes the CLOG page synchronously on every commit, so the barrier fires immediately regardless of `waitLocalFlush` — genuinely cutting latency needs a lazy-write-back path for async commits plus a checkpoint-driven CLOG flush (`CLog` implements no `wal.DirtyPageFlusher`), a separate follow-up recorded in the doc's "Still open" and the ledger. **COPY's own 4 commit call sites are now also wired (loop #50)**: `dispatchCopyViaExecutor` threads a new `sess *config.SessionRegistry` param to compute `asyncCommit`/set `ectx.AsyncCommit` and calls `ectx.CommitTransaction` for its `CopyTo`/file-`CopyFrom` branches; the two `copyInState`-based streaming `COPY FROM STDIN` commits go through a new `commitCopyTx` helper keyed off a new `copyInState.asyncCommit` field. Pinned by `internal/mvcc/clog_bufferpool_lsn_test.go` (Part A), `internal/mvcc/clog_asynccommit_test.go` + `TestCommitAsyncPassesWaitLocalFlushFalse` (manager_test.go) + `TestContextCommitTransactionRespectsAsyncCommit` (executor) + `TestSessionAsyncCommit` (server) (Part B), `TestCommitCopyTxRespectsAsyncCommit` (server, COPY follow-up). **Part C (landed 2026-07-02, loop #51) closes the latency gap:** `CLog.setStatusWithLSN` now skips the eager `groupUpdate` durable write-back whenever `lsn != 0` (async commit only — every sync caller still passes `lsn==0`, unaffected byte-for-byte), leaving the page dirty; write-back is deferred to a later sync commit's group flush, LRU eviction, or the new `CLog.FlushAll()` (a thin `pool.flushDirty()` wrapper structurally satisfying `wal.DirtyPageFlusher`) registered via a new `wal.CheckpointerConfig.FlushCLOGFn` hook wired at `internal/initdb/open.go` (`FlushCLOGFn: clog.FlushAll`), called in the checkpoint's flush phase before the redo LSN is sampled — and, unlike `PostCheckpointFn`/`TruncateCLOGFn`, a `FlushCLOGFn` error fails the checkpoint rather than being swallowed. Crash-safety rests on the pre-existing `replayCLogFromWAL` backstop (recovery re-derives CLOG status from WAL records after the last checkpoint's redo LSN regardless of what reached disk); `TestReplayCLogFromWAL_RecoversUnflushedAsyncCommit` (`internal/initdb`) pins this end to end. Pinned by `TestCLogSetCommittedWithLSNDefersFlush`/`TestCLogFlushAllBeforePoolExistsIsNoop` (mvcc), `TestCheckpointerCallsFlushCLOGFn`/`TestCheckpointerFlushCLOGFnErrorFailsCheckpoint` (wal). Gates: `-race` mvcc+wal, `internal/initdb`/`internal/executor`/`internal/server` suites, `TestE2E_PhysicalReplication{,Sync}`/`TestE2E_StandbyAttachRetainsUpstreamRowsAfterRestart`/`TestE2E_ChecksumStreamingGoopgToPG` (`-race`), TPC-H spot-check — all PASS. One residual gap deferred to the ledger: the checkpoint's redo LSN is sampled after (not before) the flush phase, a narrow theoretical race shared symmetrically with the heap pool's own checkpoint flushing, not CLOG-specific — closing it needs a whole-checkpoint-subsystem redo-pointer redesign, out of scope here. |
| 0117-0009 | [Batched CLOG→SLRU backfill on mirror enable (startup fsync storm)](0117-0009-clog-slru-backfill-batched-startup.md) | accepted | `CLog.EnablePGSLRUMirror`'s startup backfill projected the resident commit-status banks into the `pg_xact/` SLRU mirror by calling `mirrorToSLRUUnlocked` **once per committed/aborted XID** — each call an `open`+`ReadAt`+`WriteAt`+`f.Sync()`+`Close` cycle, i.e. ~`NextXID` fsyncs. On the 6M-row bench data dir (~1.5M XIDs) on WSL2's slow fsync this took **>6 min** (still stuck on segment `0000`), so the server never reached `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh`'s 60 s readiness window and the mandated executor/planner gate infra-FAILED — which blocked the entire M0117 CLOG-live-path tail (loops #7/#8 reported BLOCKED solely because the populated-data Q12/Q13 gate could not run). The per-XID `f.Sync()` is the live per-commit durability barrier and is unnecessary for the backfill (a one-shot re-projection of in-memory state that is itself re-derived from the flat file on every start, so a crash mid-backfill just re-runs it). Fix: the backfill now calls the existing batched range writer `mirrorTerminalRangeBatchedUnlocked(FirstNormalTransactionID, nBanks*xidsPerBank)` (added by M0110-0004 for the byte-identical `pg_resetwal` sweep pathology) — it builds each segment's page buffer in memory (read-first + strict-OR per XID via `GetStatus`, identical lane arithmetic) and fsyncs **once per segment**, collapsing ~1.5M fsyncs to ≈2. Byte-equivalent to the per-XID writer it replaces; the live per-commit `mirrorToSLRUUnlocked` path is untouched, so commit durability is unchanged; nil query/format/visibility blast radius. **Empirically clears the blocker:** a fresh spotcheck start on the 2.2 GB / ~1.5M-XID dir reached *ready* in **~35 s** (vs the prior >6-min hang) and proceeded past readiness. New regression `TestCLogEnableMirrorBackfillBatched` (writes a mixed committed/aborted/sub-committed page-boundary-spanning set with the mirror disabled, then `EnablePGSLRUMirror` and asserts the SLRU-derived view matches every XID — reaching the drift surface via the backfill, which `TestCLogDualStoreConsistency` did not). Gates: `go test -race ./internal/mvcc/ ./internal/wal/` PASS; `go build`/`go vet` clean; pgbench pre-commit smoke. |
| 0117-0010 | [TPC-H spot-check gate: persistent-data-target fallback (M0117 enabler)](0117-0010-tpch-spotcheck-target-fallback.md) | accepted (enabler) | The mandated executor/planner pre-commit gate `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` (fresh restart + Q12/Q13 canonical row-count check) was **silently SKIPping on a fully-loaded 2.2 GB data dir** even after [0117-0009](0117-0009-clog-slru-backfill-batched-startup.md) cleared the startup fsync storm. Root cause is a goopg persistence property the gate surfaced: `CREATE ROLE`/`CREATE USER` are registered **in memory only** (`internal/server/role_ddl.go`, M0095-0006 v0) and the `tpch` *database* is likewise not durable, so the `user=tpch / db=tpch` HammerDB load identity **does not survive the fresh restart** the gate performs — but the loaded tables persist in the **`postgres`** database (the only user database goopg keeps across restart; verified `select count(*) from lineitem` = 5,999,786). The probe failed with `role "tpch" does not exist`, whose `does not exist` substring matched the *table*-missing SKIP heuristic, so the gate reported "schema not loaded" and never ran — meaning the populated-data Q12/Q13 gate had effectively never run, the very thing loops #7/#8 cited as the M0117-tail blocker. Fix (test-infra/script only, nil engine blast radius): the gate now probes the configured `tpch` target first, and on a `(role|database) ... does not exist` error specifically falls back to the **superuser + `postgres` database** persistent target and re-probes (a genuine `relation ... does not exist` there is the real not-loaded SKIP), then runs the Q12/Q13 runner against the *resolved* target and echoes `data target = <user>@<db>`. Verified end-to-end on the bench dir: fresh start → falls back to `postgres@postgres` → **Q12=2, Q13=33, RESULT=PASS** (matches `spotcheck_expected.env` exactly, also confirming HEAD has no row-count regression). Combined with 0117-0009 this removes the last *gate-runnability* blocker; M0117-0006/0007 Part B remain dedicated-full-gate-session work (they additionally need PG-standby E2E + `-race` mvcc/wal + crash-replay per [0117-0006](0117-0006-clog-slru-buffer-pool.md)). Follow-up context: durable role/database persistence is a real goopg feature gap, tracked in the doc (not in any milestone's actionable band). |
| 0117-0008 | [Persist `datfrozenxid` in the on-disk `pg_database` tuple (M0117-0008)](0117-0008-datfrozenxid-persistence.md) | accepted (Part A + Part B landed 2026-07-02) | goopg bootstraps `pg_database` (heap `global/1262`) once at initdb with a hard-coded `datfrozenxid = 3`; PostgreSQL advances it at every VACUUM end via `vac_update_datfrozenxid`'s in-place `heap_inplace_update`. **Crucially bounded:** goopg's own CLOG truncation reads the in-memory `cat.DatFrozenXID()` directly, *not* the on-disk row, so this is purely external (standby/tooling) parity, never goopg's own visibility/truncation. **Part A (DONE via chain M0117-0004):** dual-store consistency for all 4 CLOG status codes (`clog_dual_store_consistency_test.go`). **Part B LANDED 2026-07-02:** `vacuumOp.Next` now calls `persistDatFrozenXID` (new `internal/executor/operators_vacuum_datfrozenxid.go`) unconditionally at VACUUM end, guarded so a failure never aborts the client statement. New `catalog.SharedCatalogRelFileNode`/`PgDatabaseColumnsPG18`/`PgDatabaseRelationOID` (`internal/catalog/pg_database_schema.go`) are shared between initdb's bootstrap encode and the runtime decode/re-encode (`bootstrapPostgresDatabase` now calls the shared column-list function instead of duplicating it). The live tuple is located by scanning `global/1262` for the row whose raw oid matches `catalog.InMemory.DBOID()` (same liveness/oid check as initdb's `detectCatalogDBOID`), fully decoded via the existing `DecodeRowIntoMctxPGTuple`, mutated, and re-encoded via `EncodeRowPG` — sidesteps hand-deriving a byte offset. The in-place overwrite (`storage.PageReplaceItemRaw`, pre-existing primitive) is WAL-logged via a new `catalog.PgCanonicalHeapInplace`/`BuildCanonicalHeapInplacePayload` pair using the real `XLOG_HEAP_INPLACE` opcode (`0x70`) and FPI strategy (mirrors `PgCanonicalHeapInsert`); `internal/wal/recovery.go`'s replay dispatch gained a matching `xlogHeapInplace` case. | 0118-0001 | [Isolation spec port strategy: runner, normalization, promotion workflow (M0118-0001)](0118-0001-isolation-spec-port-strategy.md) | accepted (initial slice) | Anchors how M0118 ports upstream isolation specs: runner execution, output normalization to the `expected/*.out` oracle, and the per-spec promotion workflow (CSV → `pass`, regenerate coverage/inventory/port-status docs). Records the two engine fixes the first slice needed. (1) **Auto-permutation generation** — most SSI anomaly specs declare no explicit `permutation` lines, so upstream `isolationtester.c run_all_permutations` runs every interleaving of the per-session step sequences; the goopg runner previously left `IsolationSpec.Permutations` empty for those specs and ran zero permutations, mis-reporting every declared step as `unused step name`. `framework/isolation.go generateAllPermutations` now mirrors `run_all_permutations_recurse` (pick the next unconsumed step from each session in declaration order, recurse, emit when all piles exhausted), byte-identical to upstream order (the 6 interleavings of `simple-write-skew` match `expected/simple-write-skew.out` exactly). (2) **SSI `40001` wire-message parity** — `predicate.c` emits a bare errmsg + a separate `Reason code:` DETAIL + a retry HINT, and isolationtester/psql print only the primary errmsg; goopg's commit-path abort built `"<errmsg>: " + SerializationFailureError.Error()` and `Error()` itself appends the reason in parens, doubling and inlining the reason. `mvcc.SerializationFailureError` now exposes `PrimaryMessage()` (bare errmsg) + `Detail()` (`Reason code: <reason>.`); both wire seams (`executor/ssi.go`, `server/dispatch.go` explicit-COMMIT) emit the clean primary message with the reason as DETAIL and the retry HINT, matching the existing during-write site in `operators_storage.go`. Promotes `simple-write-skew.spec`, then `two-ids.spec` (committed-xact retention + `OnConflict` at edge creation), then `total-cash.spec` (mid-statement read-path reader-kill surfaced via `CheckForSerializableConflictOutReportingFailure` threaded through the three scan operators, plus an index-UPDATE `ssiRecordTupleWrite` sibling-path fix) to `pass`. Later slices (§3–§13) promoted the rest of the SSI write-skew family — `project-manager`/`classroom-scheduling` (phantom/empty-range predicate locking), `read-only-anomaly-2`, the `read-write-unique` family, `temporal-range-integrity`/`classroom-scheduling` (date / timestamptz B-tree key types), `partial-index` (parenthesised `INSERT` source) and `referential-integrity` (§13: index-only-scan per-tuple conflict-out against a visible tuple's `xmax`, an executor-only fix so a reader of a row an in-flight peer `DELETE`d installs the reader→deleter rw-edge) — §15 lands `serializable-parallel` (the `read-only-anomaly-2` cycle with a parallel-worker read-only `s3`; reuses the §9 per-tuple SIREAD locks and needed only the no-op `debug_parallel_query` developer GUC), and §16 lands `serializable-parallel-2`/`-3` (write-free `RO_SAFE` read-only workloads whose outcome is anomaly-free regardless of goopg's lack of a parallel executor — the only blocker was the setup DDL `ALTER TABLE … SET (parallel_workers = N)`, now parsed and applied via a `CREATE TABLE WITH`-lock-step `SET`/`RESET (reloptions)` merge with validate-then-apply atomicity), bringing the isolation pass count to 29, and §17 lands `read-only-anomaly-3` (the O'Neil read-only anomaly with a `SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE` `s3`: `Manager.waitForSafeSnapshot` defers the reader's first snapshot until every concurrent declared-read-write SERIALIZABLE xact drains — goopg's minimal `GetSafeSnapshot` — so `s3r` blocks then commits with no abort; needed the `KwDeferrable` keyword-token parser fix in `parseBeginModes` and the `SerializableXact.ReadOnly`/`Deferrable` mode plumbing via `Manager.MarkSerializableModes`), bringing it to 30, and §18 lands `matview-write-skew` (write skew between a SERIALIZABLE `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` and a reader/writer of the matview's parent: the refresh rewrites the matview heap via the low-level `writeHeapRow` path that never runs the per-tuple `ssiRecordTupleWrite` hook, so the four read-before-refresh permutations formed no reader→refresher rw-edge; fixed with `Manager.CheckTableForSerializableConflictIn` — a relation-wide all-granularity conflict-in mirroring upstream's `CheckTableForSerializableConflictIn` for TRUNCATE/DROP — invoked from `execRefreshMatView` via the new `ssiRecordTableWrite` hook, plus runner `MM-DD-YYYY` date rendering and libpq `PQprint` content-based right-justification), bringing it to 31, and §19 lands `receipt-report` (the daily-receipts read-only anomaly with a declared `SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY` `s3`: goopg over-aborted 48-vs-6 by modeling every SERIALIZABLE xact as read-write, so the read-only `s3` closed dangerous structures it can only appear to precede; fixed with de-facto READ ONLY SSI modeling mirroring `predicate.c` — a `SnapshotSeqNo` watermark captured at the first-statement snapshot (the `lastCommitBeforeSnapshot` analogue) + a `committedBeforeSnapshot` predicate, the `checkForSerializableConflictOutLocked` skip that records no rw-conflict for a READ ONLY reader of a committed writer unless the writer holds an out-conflict committed before the reader's snapshot, and the `!ReadOnly` guards on `onConflictCheckLocked` Cases 2/3 + the `PreCommit` far-conflict scan), bringing the isolation pass count to 32, and §20 lands `index-only-scan` (the two-table `SELECT min(id)` write skew through index-only scans — a zero-SSI-change promotion needing only a floating-point GUC parser fix in `parseSetValueAtoms`, the per-setup-block submission runner fix so multiple global `setup {}` blocks no longer overwrite each other and `VACUUM FREEZE ANALYZE` runs standalone in its own implicit transaction, and the inert `cpu_tuple_cost`/`cpu_index_tuple_cost`/`cpu_operator_cost` real GUCs), bringing the isolation pass count to 33. `multiple-row-versions` also now passes (the WAL-buffer race fix of 0107-0007aj held across 3/3 uncached ~65s runs), so every spec in the M0118-0001 SSI-anomaly group is green. The M0118-0003 row-locking slice then lands `nowait` (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` fail-fast): a parser fix accepting a trailing `LIMIT` after the locking clause (`parseSelectLimitClauses` invoked at both grammar sites), plus cross-statement row-lock conflict detection in `stampLockInner` via the persisted lock-only xmax (goopg's lock manager is statement-scoped, so the durable heap-page lock bit — not the lockmgr — carries the conflict across sessions) returning the relation-qualified `55P03` for NOWAIT only (blocking / SKIP LOCKED paths untouched), bringing the isolation pass count to 34. The next M0118-0003 slice lands base `skip-locked` (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT n`): the planner lifts the `LIMIT` *above* the `LockRows` (`Limit → LockRows → Sort`, scoped to `SKIP LOCKED` so existing `FOR UPDATE` plans are unchanged) and caps the executor drain at `LIMIT` *successfully-locked* rows; `stampLock`/`stampLockInner` silently drop rows held by another active xact (the `epqSkipped` path via the lockmgr tuple-lock probe + the same persisted lock-only-xmax signal NOWAIT reads); and `sortOp` now preserves the per-row `ctid` side-channel through its in-memory sort (the prior blocker — a `Sort` between `LockRows` and the scan dropped the TID so nothing was ever locked), bringing the isolation pass count to 35. The next slice lands `nowait-3` (a *blocking* `FOR UPDATE` on a row whose lock-only xmax is held by another active session now waits via `WaitForXID` and re-stamps on the holder's COMMIT, while a concurrent `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` still fails fast with `55P03`; `stampLockInner`'s lock-only branch now honours the wait policy instead of overwriting the holder), bringing it to 36, and then `update-locked-tuple` (the non-conflicting corner of the row-lock matrix: s1's FK-induced `KEY SHARE` lock on a `users` row is compatible with s2's concurrent no-key `UPDATE` of that row, and the FK-key-unchanged update-chain traversal commits with no `40001` under `REPEATABLE READ` — a zero-engine-change promotion confirming goopg's FK row-locking + update-chain path), bringing it to 37, and then `lock-committed-keyupdate` (the *conflicting* mirror of `lock-committed-update`: a `FOR KEY SHARE` locker meeting a committed *key*-update waits behind the in-progress `UPDATE` then follows the CTID chain to the successor under READ COMMITTED, or raises `40001` under REPEATABLE READ / SERIALIZABLE — a pure promotion on the cumulative lock-only-xmax + `WaitForXID` + CTID-chain infrastructure with no new engine code), bringing it to 38. A further M0118-0001 zero-engine-change promotion lands `insert-conflict-do-nothing-2` (multi-row `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` under REPEATABLE READ / SERIALIZABLE: DO-NOTHING skips the duplicate without writing, so it records no conflict-in edge and never raises `40001` — all eight permutations match PG 18.3 on goopg's existing M0100-0002 arbiter path), bringing it to 39. Deferred siblings (`nowait-2`..`-5`, `lock-nowait`, `skip-locked-2` multixact / `-3` cross-statement tuple-lock wait queue / `-4` EvalPlanQual advisory chain; `tuplelock-conflict` full lock matrix + multixact, `tuplelock-update` advisory locks, `tuplelock-partition` ON CONFLICT partition tuple lock, `lock-update-traversal`/`lock-update-delete`/`propagate-lock-delete`/`aborted-keyrevoke`/`delete-abort-savept` all multixact or subxact-lock-restore) are tracked in the deferral ledger. |

[[pattern_sibling_paths_must_agree]]. **Hot-path wiring slice 12 landed** this loop — two **non-row-lock-engine** divergences fixed to promote `tuplelock-update` (`TestPort_IsolationTuplelockUpdate`): (1) a shared planner `defaultMarkerReplacement` helper rewrites an explicit `DEFAULT` keyword on a `SERIAL`/identity column (whose catalog `DefaultExpr` is nil) to a synthesized `nextval('<table>_<col>_seq')` call instead of `NULL` — so `INSERT INTO pktab VALUES (1, DEFAULT)` / `UPDATE pktab SET data = DEFAULT` no longer collapse to NULL and trip the `SERIAL NOT NULL` constraint (mirrors PostgreSQL where SERIAL's default IS `nextval`); all three substitution sites (INSERT row cell, UPDATE single-column, UPDATE tuple-form) route through it, pinned by `TestPlanInsertValuesDefaultSerialSubstitutesNextval`/`TestPlanUpdateSetDefaultSerialSubstitutesNextval`; (2) the isolation runner now honours `BlockerStepComplete` step-name annotations (e.g. `s1_advunlock1(s2_update)`) via `reportStepGatedOnBlockers` — it renders the immediately-completing unlock step in `<waiting ...>`/`<... completed>` format with its report gated behind the referenced pending blocker step, matching upstream isolationtester's stable ordering (zero blast radius: only six upstream specs use parenthesised step blockers and all but this one are still `failed`). The row-lock engine itself was unchanged. **Hot-path wiring slice 13 landed** this loop — `tuplelock-partition` (`TestPort_IsolationTuplelockPartition`, isolation pass 73→74) promoted via two fixes in the upsert `applyUpdate` path (`operators_upsert.go`): (1) `onConflictUpdateTouchesKeyColumn` stamps `HEAP_KEYS_UPDATED` on the conflicting tuple when the `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` `SET` list assigns a unique/primary-key column — set-list based per PG `ExecUpdateLockMode`/`ExecGetAllUpdatedCols`, not value comparison (so `SET key=1` with an unchanged key still makes a concurrent `FOR KEY SHARE` wait, while a no-key `SET col1/col2` does not), distinct from the value-based plain-`UPDATE` path; (2) `applyUpdate` now links the old tuple to the new version via `stampOldCtid` (ON CONFLICT never moves partitions) so the waiting `FOR KEY SHARE` follows the `t_ctid` chain to the live successor instead of short-reading a self-pointing ctid. **Hot-path wiring slice 14 landed** this loop — `propagate-lock-delete` (`TestPort_IsolationPropagateLockDelete`, all 8 permutations, isolation pass 50→51) promoted with **no new engine code**: goopg does not model the FK check as a heap row-lock that must be *propagated* across the `UPDATE`'s version chain; instead the parent `DELETE`'s `enforceFKOnDelete`→`fkChildWaitForInFlightInsert` (M0100-0005w) detects the still-in-flight child `INSERT`s directly on the child relation and `WaitForXID`s on them, then after they commit the refreshed snapshot makes `assertNoChildRows` raise `23503`, so there is no parent-side lock to lose across `s3`'s intervening `UPDATE` (the aborted-savepoint variant keys off the same child inserter xids). |
| 0118-0003 | [Transaction-scoped `LOCK TABLE` heavyweight locks (M0118-0003 slice 15)](0118-0003-txn-scoped-lock-table.md) | landed | Promotes the `lock-nowait` isolation spec — the first M0118-0003 spec to exercise *relation-level* (not tuple-level) heavyweight locking. `LOCK TABLE … IN <mode> MODE [NOWAIT]` now takes a **real, transaction-scoped** heavyweight lock so a conflicting `LOCK` in another session blocks until `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` (previously `execLockTable` only recorded the lock in the `pg_locks` display registry and never waited). The `lockmgr` package already had every primitive — conflict matrix, blocking `Acquire`, non-blocking `TryAcquire` (`NOWAIT`), and `canGrantImmediately`'s `JoinWaitQueue` early-grant rule written explicitly for this spec — but `lockmgr.New()` had **no production caller** (`server.Config.LockMgr` is always `nil`, so all `acquireRelLock`/`acquireTupleLock` are no-ops and cross-statement row blocking rides `xmax`/`WaitForXID` instead — [[lockmgr_locks_are_statement_scoped]]), and the lock lifecycle was statement-scoped (`dispatch.go` mints a fresh `BackendID` per `Query` and `ReleaseAll`s it at statement end). Fix: a **dedicated, always-on** `executor.tableLockMgr` singleton touched by nothing but explicit `LOCK` statements (so the blast radius of real heavyweight locking is confined to `LOCK TABLE` — scans/DML/DDL keep the `nil` global manager and are unaffected), plus a stable per-connection `connTxState.LockBackendID` (minted once from the same monotonic counter, threaded onto each `Context` as `TxnLockBackendID` only while `connTx.InExplicit()`) under which `execLockTable`→`acquireRelLockTxn` acquires; the per-statement `ReleaseAll` leaves it untouched and `connTxState.End()` drops it via `executor.ReleaseTableLocks` at COMMIT/ROLLBACK (and on teardown). `NOWAIT` contention → `55P03`, lock cycle → `40P01`. The `pg_locks` display registry is unchanged. Verified: `TestPort_IsolationLockNowait` PASS byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3; `-race` over lockmgr + the lock-spec batch green; executor/server/lockmgr suites green; CSV `failed`→`pass`, inventory/coverage regenerated (isolation pass 51→52). |
| 0118-0004 | [Simple (lock-upgrade) deadlock: synchronous early detection (M0118-0003 slice 16)](0118-0004-simple-deadlock-early-detection.md) | accepted | Promotes the `deadlock-simple` isolation spec. Two sessions each take `ACCESS SHARE` on a table then each attempts a lock *upgrade* to `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE`; neither upgrade can complete until the other releases its `ACCESS SHARE`, so the second upgrader closes a deadlock cycle. PostgreSQL's `JoinWaitQueue` (proc.c) detects this **simple** deadlock *synchronously* the instant the second upgrader joins the queue — it returns `PROC_WAIT_STATUS_ERROR` (the requester is the victim) **without waiting for `deadlock_timeout`** — so the victim errors with `40P01` and *no* `<waiting ...>` marker. goopg's `tableLockMgr` (slice 15) routed the upgrades through `lockmgr`, but `lockmgr` only had the **timeout-driven** detector (`time.AfterFunc(deadlockTimeout, …)`), so it parked *both* upgraders, the runner observed both `<waiting ...>`, and the error surfaced late — diverging on marker + timing even though victim *selection* (youngest backend) was already correct. Fix: new `lockState.hasSimpleDeadlock(b, m)` mirrors the `JoinWaitQueue` scan — when `b` already holds a lock here and would queue behind a conflicting waiter `w` whose held locks also conflict with `b`'s request, it is a simple deadlock; `Acquire` checks it after `canGrantImmediately` (mutually exclusive at the deciding waiter) and before enqueueing, then `ReleaseAll(b)` (mirroring the timeout victim path so the survivor's wake-pass fires) and returns `ErrDeadlockDetected` (→ `40P01` via `acquireRelLockTxn`). Scope: simple single-object lock-upgrade deadlock only — multi-object cycles, soft-deadlock queue reordering, and the row-lock `xmax`/`WaitForXID` wait graph remain on the timeout detector / future slices. Verified: `TestPort_IsolationDeadlockSimple` PASS byte-for-byte vs PG 18.3; `-race ./internal/lockmgr/...` green (incl. linear-chain false-positive guard); `TestPort_IsolationLockNowait`/`TuplelockConflict`/`LockCommittedKeyupdate` still PASS; CSV `failed`→`pass`, inventory/coverage regenerated (isolation pass 52→53). |
| 0118-0005 | [General (timeout-driven) deadlock detection for LOCK TABLE (M0118-0004 slice: deadlock-hard)](0118-0005-general-deadlock-timeout-detection.md) | accepted | Promotes the `deadlock-hard` isolation spec — an 8-session/8-relation `LOCK TABLE` cycle where every session sets `deadlock_timeout='100s'` except s8 (`'10ms'`), so s8 runs the detector first and is the victim (`40P01`), per upstream's "rollback the session that first discovers it". goopg already had the general wait-for-graph detector (M0012-0002) and routed `LOCK TABLE` through `tableLockMgr` (slice 15), but three gaps blocked it. (1) `deadlock_timeout` was not a GUC — `SET deadlock_timeout='10ms'` failed at session setup; now registered (`TypeInt`/`UnitMs`, `BootVal 1000`, range `[1,INT_MAX]`, `ContextSuset` per `guc_tables.c` `PGC_SUSET`) with the matching `postgresql.conf.sample` entry. (2) The detector always picked the *youngest* backend; PG rolls back the backend that *runs* the check (timer fired). New `lockmgr.AcquireWithTimeout(ctx,b,t,m,timeout)` (Acquire wraps it via a `useConfiguredTimeout` sentinel) lets `executor.acquireRelLockTxn` pass the session's `Context.deadlockTimeout()`; the parked-acquire timer now fires `runDeadlockCheckFor(b)` → `checkDeadlockLockedFor(prefer)` which selects `prefer` as victim when it is in the cycle, else youngest-in-cycle. `checkDeadlockLocked()`/`CheckDeadlocksNow` delegate with `prefer=0` so youngest-victim unit tests are unchanged. (3) The runner ignored the `(*)` `BlockerStar` marker; `hasStarBlocker` now renders such a step in `<waiting ...>`/`<... completed>` form even when it completes immediately (the victim's fast `40P01`), then `drainWithTimeout` so `s7a8` (gated on `s8a1`) surfaces in upstream order — no passing spec uses `(*)` so blast radius is nil. Scope: hard multi-object cycles only — soft-deadlock queue reordering (`deadlock-soft{,-2}`), the row-lock `xmax`/`WaitForXID` wait graph (`tuplelock-upgrade-no-deadlock`, `multixact-no-deadlock`), and `deadlock-parallel` remain future slices. Verified: `TestPort_IsolationDeadlockHard` PASS byte-for-byte; `-race ./internal/lockmgr/...` + executor `Lock|Deadlock` green; config tests green; `DeadlockSimple`/`LockNowait`/`TuplelockUpdate` still PASS; CSV `failed`→`pass`, coverage/inventory regenerated (isolation pass 53→54). |
| 0118-0006 | [Soft-deadlock wait-queue reordering (M0118-0004 slice: deadlock-soft, deadlock-soft-2)](0118-0006-soft-deadlock-wait-queue-reordering.md) | accepted | Promotes the `deadlock-soft` and `deadlock-soft-2` isolation specs — deadlock cycles PostgreSQL resolves by **rearranging a wait queue instead of aborting anyone**. `deadlock-soft`: a 4-cycle with two hard edges (`e1→d1`, `e2→d2`: an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE waiter behind an ACCESS SHARE holder) and two soft edges (`d2→e1`, `d1→e2`: an ACCESS SHARE waiter queued behind a conflicting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE waiter); reversing the `d1→e2` edge (moving `d1` ahead of `e2` in `a2`'s queue) lets `d1`'s compatible request be granted and unblocks everyone. `deadlock-soft-2`: `s1` must jump over **both** `s3` and `s4` (a topological reorder of a 3-waiter queue). goopg's detector ([0118-0005](0118-0005-general-deadlock-timeout-detection.md)) only built **hard** edges and only ever cancelled a victim, so the hard-only graph was acyclic and both blocked waiters parked forever (`<... timed out waiting>`). Fix mirrors upstream `deadlock.c` (lock groups omitted): `findLockCycle` now records **soft** (queue-order) edges; `deadLockCheck`/`testConfiguration` try reversing them; `expandConstraints`/`topoSort` rebuild the affected queues (waiter-before-blocker, minimal disturbance); `applyWaitOrders` rewrites `lockState.waiters` (preserving `*Waiter` pointers) and `wakePassLocked` grants the newly head-of-line waiter. Runs on the timer path (`prefer != 0`) only; `CheckDeadlocksNow` (`prefer == 0`) keeps the legacy hard-only youngest-victim path (factored into `checkDeadlockHardOnlyLocked`) so unit tests are unchanged. Scope: hard multi-object cycles still roll back the firing backend; the row-lock `xmax`/`WaitForXID` graph (`tuplelock-upgrade-no-deadlock`, `multixact-no-deadlock`) and `deadlock-parallel` (lock groups) remain future slices. Verified: `TestPort_IsolationDeadlockSoft{,2}` PASS byte-for-byte; `DeadlockHard`/`DeadlockSimple`/`LockNowait`/`TuplelockUpdate` still PASS; `-race ./internal/lockmgr/...` green; CSV `failed`→`pass`, coverage/inventory regenerated (isolation pass 54→56). |
| 0118-0007 | [Multixact no-deadlock: re-acquiring a self-held row lock (M0118-0004 slice: multixact-no-deadlock)](0118-0007-multixact-no-deadlock-self-relock.md) | accepted | Promotes the `multixact-no-deadlock` isolation spec — `s1` takes `FOR SHARE`, `s2` also takes `FOR SHARE` (the row's `xmax` becomes a SHARE **multixact** `{s1,s2}`), `s3` requests `FOR UPDATE` and **waits** behind the SHARE multixact, then `s1` re-requests `FOR SHARE` (a lock it already holds). The invariant: `s1`'s re-request must **not** queue behind the waiting `s3` (which would deadlock — `s3` waits for `s1`'s SHARE, `s1` waits behind `s3`); it returns immediately, and only after `s2`+`s1` commit does `s3` complete. **No new engine work** — goopg's existing tuple-lock path already holds the invariant: the wait branch in `stampLockInner` is gated on `tupleLockConflicts` *first* (re-`FOR SHARE` vs a SHARE multixact does not conflict, so the wait/NOWAIT/SKIP branch is skipped entirely); `activeLockHolders` filters the current backend out of the wait set (`m.Xid != Tx.XID`); `stampMultiLock` drops+re-appends self when re-forming the multixact; and `multixact.MembersConflict` (port of `DoesMultiXactIdConflict`) skips self (`m.Xid == reqXid`). `s3`'s `FOR UPDATE` is parked outside the tuple's `xmax` (a waiter, not yet stamped), so `s1` sees only the compatible `{s1,s2}` members and has nothing to wait on — the detector is never consulted. This slice adds `TestPort_IsolationMultixactNoDeadlock` and documents the path so the guarantee is regression-protected. Scope: only the self-relock no-deadlock invariant; `tuplelock-upgrade-no-deadlock` (row-lock upgrade retry algorithm) and `deadlock-parallel` (lock groups) remain future slices. Verified: `TestPort_IsolationMultixactNoDeadlock` PASS byte-for-byte; `DeadlockHard`/`DeadlockSimple`/`DeadlockSoft{,2}`/`LockNowait`/`TuplelockUpdate` still PASS; `-race ./internal/lockmgr/...` green; CSV `failed`→`pass`, coverage/inventory regenerated (isolation pass 56→57). |
| 0118-0008 | [Row-lock chain-follow: committed-DELETE chain-tail sentinel (M0118-0004 slice: tuplelock-upgrade-no-deadlock, partial)](0118-0008-rowlock-chain-tail-sentinel.md) | accepted | Fixes an `ERROR: short read at block` crash in the `tuplelock-upgrade-no-deadlock` spec (perm `s1_keyshare s2_for_update s3_keyshare s3_delete s1_rollback s3_commit s2_rollback`): when `s2`'s waiting `FOR UPDATE` wakes after `s3` has DELETEd+committed the row, `lockRowsOp.stampLockInner` follows the committed updater's `t_ctid` chain to find the live successor. (2) Exposed a latent split — `AllocateSubXid` registered the sub-XID into the in-memory fallback map while `TopLevelXid`/`IsAborted` read the *attached* pg_subtrans `SubxactMap` (real-server path); fixed by routing `AllocateSubXid` through `RegisterSubXid`. | 0118-0013 | [Subtransaction-scoped DELETE/UPDATE xmax for savepoint-rollback visibility (M0118-0009 slice: delete-abort-savept)](0118-0013-subxact-scoped-xmax-savepoint-rollback.md) | accepted | **`delete-abort-savept` PASSES all 7 permutations byte-identical vs PG 18.3.** A DELETE inside a SAVEPOINT over a row the same xact already locked `FOR KEY SHARE` is a lock upgrade; `ROLLBACK TO` must restore the outer KEY SHARE lock. goopg returned `(0 rows)` because three pieces ignored the live sub-XID. **(1) Write side:** new `effectiveWriterXID(ctx)` (storage-op twin of `lockRowsOp.writerXID`) — heap DELETE/UPDATE now stamp the old tuple xmax **and its WAL record** under the current sub-XID inside a savepoint (was always the top-level `ctx.Tx.XID`, which is rebuilt per-Query from the connection txn and so never reflects a savepoint); wired at all 24 old-tuple-xmax stamp + paired-WAL twins (HOT, index/seqscan UPDATE delete-half, DELETE, `UPDATE…FROM`/`DELETE…USING`, MERGE, upsert) — strict no-op outside a savepoint. **(2) Producer:** `stampUpdaterXmaxPreservingLockers` now preserves an **outer-level self** locker (`TopLevelXid==ourTop` but `≠ourXID`) into `{outer-keyshare + subxid-updater}` so dropping the rolled-back subxid member leaves the KEY SHARE alive (only the exact current sub-XID is dropped/re-added as updater). **(3) Reader:** `lockRowsOp.stampLockInner`'s "updater rolled back" test became `HasAbortedXID(xmax) || IsAborted(xmax)` — a `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` lives in the pg_subtrans map (`IsAborted`), not the top-level aborted set, so the row is now treated as live-at-original-ptr not committed-deleted. Pre-commit permutations wait on the restored outer lock then proceed on `s1` COMMIT. Gates: `-race` mvcc/multixact/executor + storage/wal; full M0118-0003 row-lock + M0118-0004 deadlock + MERGE/insert-conflict batch PASS; pgbench smoke 0-failed; CSV promoted failed→pass + coverage/inventory regenerated. Deferred: `delete-abort-savept-2` (FOR NO KEY UPDATE pure-lock upgrade restore), `aborted-keyrevoke` (new-tuple xmin under sub-XID), `multixact-no-forget` (whole-txn ROLLBACK locker retention). |
| 0118-0014 | [Eager top-level XID materialization at SAVEPOINT (M0118-0009 slice: aborted-keyrevoke)](0118-0014-aborted-keyrevoke-savepoint-xid-materialization.md) | accepted | **`aborted-keyrevoke` PASSES all 14 permutations byte-identical vs PG 18.3.** Root cause: `SAVEPOINT` issued before the txn's first write (`BEGIN; SAVEPOINT f; UPDATE …`) ran `AllocateSubXid(sess.tx.XID)` while `tx.XID` was still lazily-unassigned (0), registering the sub-XID with **parent = 0** in the pg_subtrans `SubxactMap`. A zero parent breaks cross-session resolution: another backend's `TopLevelXid(subxid)` returns 0, so its snapshot can't map the sub-XID to a running top-level xact and wrongly treats the savepoint's uncommitted NEW tuple as visible (s2's `FOR KEY SHARE` returned phantom `key=2` instead of waiting), and `xidActiveWithSubxact` reports it dead so the row-lock wait never fires. `delete-abort-savept` escaped this only because its `FOR KEY SHARE` assigned the top-level XID before the savepoint. Fix: `execSavepoint` calls `MaterializeWriterXID()` before `AllocateSubXid` when `sess.tx.XID` is unassigned, so the subxid→parent link is non-zero from birth (strict no-op once a top-level XID exists; nested savepoints inherit it). Supporting twins (same loop): sub-XID-scoped NEW-tuple xmin in `writeHeapRowReturning{,PG}` + HOT `tryApplyHOTUpdate` so a rolled-back savepoint's new version disappears; `HEAP_KEYS_UPDATED` on the single-xid old-tuple stamp in `stampUpdaterXmaxNonHOT` (multixact path already encoded it) so a concurrent `FOR KEY SHARE` sees the key conflict and waits; descendant-direction subxact self-visibility in `isCurrentTxXID`. Gates: `-race` mvcc/multixact; executor/storage unit PASS; `aborted-keyrevoke` 14/14 + siblings `delete-abort-savept`/`tuplelock-upgrade-no-deadlock`/`lock-update-delete` no regression; pgbench smoke 0-failed. Deferred: `delete-abort-savept-2`, `multixact-no-forget`. |
| 0118-0015 | [Self lock-upgrade inside a SAVEPOINT preserves the outer lock as a MultiXact member (M0118-0009 slice: delete-abort-savept-2)](0118-0015-self-savepoint-lock-upgrade-multixact.md) | accepted | **`delete-abort-savept-2` PASSES all 4 permutations byte-identical vs PG 18.3.** The funkier `delete-abort-savept` sibling: s1 holds `FOR KEY SHARE` at the top level, opens `SAVEPOINT f`, upgrades to `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` under the sub-XID, then `ROLLBACK TO f` (must revert to KEY SHARE). A concurrent s2 `FOR UPDATE` must keep waiting until `s1c`; s2 `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` may proceed. goopg let s2's `FOR UPDATE` complete immediately after the rollback. Root cause: `lockRowsOp.stampLockInner` combined a lock-only xmax into a `MultiXactId` (preserving the prior holder via `stampMultiLock`) **only for a foreign holder** (`!isSelfXID(xmax)`); a SELF upgrade fell through to the single-xmax stamp under the current writer XID, discarding the outer top-level KEY SHARE member, so `ROLLBACK TO` left the row with no surviving lock. Fix: new predicate `hasOuterSelfLockMember(hdr)` (true iff the lock-only xmax holds an active self member stamped under a level ≠ the current `writerXID()` — an outer savepoint/top-level lock) widens the producer gate to `!isSelfXID(xmax) || hasOuterSelfLockMember(hdr)`. `stampMultiLock` already keeps every member whose xid ≠ `writerXID()` as a survivor, so s1d now builds `{top-level KEY SHARE, sub-XID NO KEY UPDATE}`; the rollback drops only the sub-XID and `conflictingLockHolders` then waits s2 on the surviving KEY SHARE. Same-level self re-lock yields no survivor → `combined=false` → unchanged single-xmax stamp (hot path untouched). Strict no-op outside a savepoint. Crash-safe (lock-only multi membership is transient in-memory; WAL persistence deferred per [[0118-0002]]). Gates: `TestPort_IsolationDeleteAbortSavept2` 4/4 + siblings `DeleteAbortSavept`/`AbortedKeyrevoke`/`TuplelockUpgradeNoDeadlock`/`LockUpdateDelete`/`SkipLocked*`/`Nowait*` no regression; `-race` mvcc/multixact; executor/storage unit PASS; pgbench smoke 0-failed. Deferred: `multixact-no-forget`. |
| 0118-0016 | [Don't-forget-the-lock: conflict-filtered wait + lock carry-forward on UPDATE (M0118-0009 slice: multixact-no-forget)](0118-0016-multixact-no-forget-lock-carryforward.md) | accepted | **`multixact-no-forget` PASSES all 9 permutations byte-identical vs PG 18.3.** s1 holds `FOR KEY SHARE`; s2 no-key-`UPDATE`s (forming `{s1-keyshare + s2-no-key-update}`); then s2 aborts or commits, and s3 probes. Two divergences. **(1) Over-conflict after ABORT:** s3 `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` waited on s1's surviving KEY SHARE even though the two are compatible — `stampLockInner`'s real-updater branch built its co-member wait set from `activeLockHolders` (every active member) instead of `conflictingLockHolders` (MultiXactIdWait semantics: only conflicting members). Fixed to conflict-filter (excluding the separately-resolved updater); `activeLockHolders` removed (no other caller). `stampAtPtr` now preserves survivors via `stampMultiLock` so the aborted-updater stamp keeps s1's lock instead of overwriting it. **(2) Under-conflict after COMMIT:** s3 `FOR UPDATE` proceeded immediately because goopg inserted the new tuple version with no inherited xmax — the lock was forgotten across the version boundary. Fixed by carrying the old tuple's non-conflicting lockers forward onto the new HOT tuple (`carryForwardLockersToNewTuple`, the new-version half of `heap_update`'s `compute_new_xmax_infomask`, sharing the extracted `survivingLockersForUpdate` with the old-tuple `stampUpdaterXmaxPreservingLockers`); s3 `FOR UPDATE` then waits on the inherited KEY SHARE until `s1c`. Same narrow gate as the producer (pre-existing foreign lock-only holder) so the pgbench hot path is untouched; lock-only multi membership transient in-memory (WAL persistence deferred [[0118-0002]]). Gates: `TestPort_IsolationMultixactNoForget` 9/9 + row-lock/savepoint/multixact sibling batch no regression; `-race` executor/multixact/mvcc; executor/storage unit PASS; pgbench smoke 0-failed. Deferred: non-HOT-path lock carry-forward (delete+insert/`UPDATE…FROM`/MERGE/upsert). |
| 0118-0017 | [`lock_timeout` and statement-timeout-aware lock waits (M0118-0009 slice: timeouts)](0118-0017-lock-timeout.md) | accepted | Implements the `lock_timeout` GUC and fixes the cancel-message for lock waits. Previously **all** lock-wait cancellations (statement_timeout, lock_timeout, client cancel) emitted "canceling statement due to user request", and `lock_timeout` armed no timer; row-level waits (`epqWait`) swallowed the cancel entirely and spun into a spurious `40001`. New leaf pkg `internal/lockwait` carries the lock-wait budget down the request ctx (a **duration**, re-armed per wait like upstream's `ProcSleep enable_timeout_after(LOCK_TIMEOUT)`) plus the `ErrLockTimeout` sentinel. `lockmgr.acquire` gains a lock-timeout `select` case (sharing the new `unparkWaiter` splice-and-repair with `ctx.Done()`); `mvcc.WaitForXID` arms a cond-broadcast timer and checks the lock deadline after `ctx.Err()`. `dispatch.go` attaches the budget when `lock_timeout>0` (independent of statement_timeout). Error mapping: `context.DeadlineExceeded`→"statement timeout" (the only deadline source), `ErrLockTimeout`→"lock timeout", `context.Canceled`→"user request"; `epqWait` now returns a `timeout *ExecError` that all ~11 write-path call sites surface (plain client cancel still swallowed → historical retry). Hot path untouched: `lock_timeout` defaults off, no timer/ctx-value when unset. Gates: `TestPort_TimeoutsRowLevel` 4/4 (statement/lock/lock-wins/statement-wins, message + ~300ms timing) + `TestLockManagerLockTimeout*` `-race`; full row-lock/savepoint/merge/multixact/deadlock/skip-locked/nowait isolation-port batch no regression; `-race` executor/mvcc/lockmgr; pgbench smoke 0-failed. Table-level half landed in [[0118-0018]]. |
| 0118-0018 | [Scan-time ACCESS SHARE so LOCK TABLE conflicts (M0118-0009 slice: timeouts table-level half)](0118-0018-scan-access-share-lock-table-conflict.md) | accepted | Completes `timeouts.spec` (promoted `failed`→`pass`). The four table-level permutations need a plain `SELECT` (`rdtbl`) to hold a transaction-scoped ACCESS SHARE lock so a later bare `LOCK TABLE` (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, `locktbl`) conflicts, parks, and is cancelled by the shorter of `lock_timeout`/`statement_timeout` (messages already correct after [[0118-0017]]). goopg had kept ordinary scans off `tableLockMgr`, so `LOCK TABLE` was granted instantly and never timed out. New `Context.acquireScanReadLockTxn` reuses the LOCK-TABLE machinery (`acquireRelLockTxn` on `tableLockMgr`, keyed by `TxnLockBackendID`, released at txn end) wired at the three relation-read scan-open sites (seqscan/index/index-only). Blast radius bounded: no-op outside an explicit txn (`TxnLockBackendID==0`) and for system catalogs (`RelOid<16384`); ACCESS SHARE conflicts only with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE so it grants instantly absent a concurrent `LOCK TABLE`/DDL; lockmgr is idempotent so re-scans within a txn are mask-check no-ops. No WAL/on-disk change. | 0118-0019 | [`inplace-inval` passes by construction — virtual pg_class immunity (M0118-0009 slice)](0118-0019-inplace-inval-virtual-pg-class-immunity.md) | accepted | Promotes `inplace-inval.spec` `failed`→`pass` with **no code change** — goopg is immune to the upstream inplace-update-revert hazard by construction. The spec checks that a `CREATE INDEX`-set `pg_class.relhasindex=true` (an `heap_inplace_update`) is not reverted when a later `heap_update` (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`) uses a stale catcache *oldtup*. goopg serves `pg_class` from the **virtual** catalog builder and recomputes `relhasindex` live on every read (`len(c.byTable[oid])>0`), so there is no heap tuple, no catcache oldtup to go stale, and no inplace-update byte to clobber — the entire hazard chain is absent. Both permutations observe `relhasindex=t`, byte-identical to PG 18.3. Adds dedicated sequential test `TestPort_IsolationInplaceInval`; regenerates coverage + oracle inventory md.
