| 0118-0031 | [`multiple-cic` isolation spec: const-folded partial-index predicate + CIC drain (M0118-0008)](0118-0031-multiple-cic-const-fold-and-cic-wait.md) | accepted | **Fifth M0118-0008 promotion.** Promotes `multiple-cic` to pass-required (byte-identical to PG 18.3) — two simultaneous `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` builds whose partial-index predicates call IMMUTABLE advisory-lock functions on **empty** tables. Two engine fixes plus one runner fix. (1) **Const-fold** — `execCreateIndex` now evaluates a partial-index `WHERE` predicate that references no table columns **once** at build time (new exported `planner.ExprContainsColumnRef` guard + `evalExpr(pred, nil, ctx)`), mirroring PG's `eval_const_expressions` in `BuildIndexInfo`; the IMMUTABLE function's advisory-lock call now fires despite zero rows, so `s1i` blocks. The stored predicate is untouched (pg_get_indexdef/pg_dump unaffected). (2) **CIC drain** — `CreateIndexStmt.Concurrently` is now recorded by the parser; a concurrent build captures the active-transaction slot set at **start** (`mvcc.Manager.SnapshotActiveOtherSlots`, refactored out of `WaitForOlderSlotsToCommit`) and drains it after the build (`WaitForSlotsToCommit`), so the newer build `s2i` completes only after the older `s1i` — snapshotting at start (not wait time) avoids a mutual wait between two simultaneous builds. (3) **Runner** — the `(*)`-star branch now drains *ungated* pending steps before reporting the star step's own completion (`partitionGatedOn` keeps steps gated via `BlockerStepComplete`, e.g. deadlock-hard's `s7a8(s8a1)`, reported after), matching isolationtester's dispatch-order completion reporting. Gated on `Concurrently`, so plain CREATE INDEX is unaffected; only `multiple-cic` + deferred `prepared-transactions-cic` use CIC in the suite. Gates: strict test PASS; every strict `(*)` spec (deadlock-{hard,soft,soft-2}, classroom-scheduling, project-manager, serializable-parallel{,-2}, temporal-range-integrity, multixact-no-deadlock, tuplelock-upgrade-no-deadlock, timeouts) PASS; lock-sibling regression PASS; `-race` mvcc/lockmgr; parser/planner/executor units; pgbench smoke. **Rest of DDL/VACUUM group still deferred** (alter-table-* constraint locks, `*-conflict` role/ACL infra, reindex-toast, partition specs, vacuum-{skip-locked,concurrent-drop,no-cleanup-lock}, inherit-temp, plpgsql-toast). |
| 0118-0032 | [`alter-table-3` isolation spec: ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER lock + abort-time lock release (M0118-0008)](0118-0032-alter-table-3-enable-disable-trigger-lock-and-abort-release.md) | accepted | **Sixth M0118-0008 promotion.** Promotes `alter-table-3` to pass-required (byte-identical to PG 18.3, all 48 permutations) — mixes `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER` with a concurrent `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and a duplicate-key `INSERT`. Two engine fixes. (1) **ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER lock** — the parser arm (previously a pure no-op) now flags `AlterTableStmt.EnableDisableTrigger` for a `TRIGGER` target, and `execAlterTable` acquires a transaction-scoped `ShareRowExclusiveLock` via the existing `acquireDDLLockTxn` (mirrors PG `AlterTableGetLockLevel` → `ShareRowExclusiveLock` for `AT_EnableTrig`/`AT_DisableTrig`); it conflicts with a concurrent `INSERT`'s `RowExclusiveLock` (waits) but not with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`'s `RowShareLock` (proceeds). The enable/disable is otherwise a semantic no-op (RULE/other variants keep the old no-op). (2) **Abort-time lock release** — verified against PG 18.3 that a statement error leaves **zero** locks in `pg_locks` even while the transaction sits `idle in transaction (aborted)`: PG's `AbortTransaction` drops heavyweight locks at abort, not at the explicit ROLLBACK. `connTxState.Fail()` now releases the transaction's `tableLockMgr` locks (`ReleaseTableLocks(LockBackendID)`) so a later conflicting `ALTER` in another session does not wait on the dead `RowExclusiveLock` of a failed `INSERT`. Gated on `SavepointDepth() == 0` — subtransaction abort (`ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT`) retains locks per PG; idempotent with `End()`. Only `tableLockMgr` locks are released (relation/advisory left to `End()`), bounding blast radius. Gates: strict test PASS; lock-sibling + savepoint/abort + SSI regression PASS; `-race` lockmgr/server; parser/executor units; pgbench smoke. |
| 0118-0033 | [`vacuum-skip-locked` isolation spec: conditional maintenance lock + severity-aware runner (M0118-0008)](0118-0033-vacuum-skip-locked-conditional-lock.md) | accepted | **Seventh M0118-0008 promotion.** Promotes `vacuum-skip-locked` to pass-required (byte-identical to PG 18.3, all 16 permutations) — `VACUUM`/`ANALYZE (SKIP_LOCKED)` against a partitioned table while another session holds `part1` in `SHARE`/`ACCESS EXCLUSIVE`. Three fixes. (1) **Conditional maintenance lock** — new `(*Context).tryAcquireMaintenanceLock` (mirrors PG `ConditionalLockRelationOid`): `TryAcquire`s `ShareUpdateExclusiveLock` (or `AccessExclusiveLock` for `VACUUM FULL`) under the active backend and releases immediately, returning `false` on contention so the relation is skipped not waited on. (2) **Skip semantics + expansion** — `expandVacuumTargets`/`expandAnalyzeTargets` tag each relation explicit (user-named ⇒ `WARNING: skipping vacuum/analyze of "X" --- lock not available` via `AddWarning`) vs expanded (partition child ⇒ silent skip), and record partitioned parents; `ANALYZE` of a partitioned parent then reads each leaf partition under a **blocking** `AccessShareLock` (`analyzeInheritanceWait` → `acquireRelLockMaybeTransient`), reproducing the inheritance-stats read that makes ANALYZE wait under `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` but not `SHARE` (plain `VACUUM` never waits). (3) **Runner severity** — `isolation_runner.go` now echoes each captured server message with its real protocol severity (`pq.Error.Severity`) instead of a hard-coded `NOTICE:`, so `WARNING:` lines render; strictly more faithful (NOTICE-emitting specs unchanged). Gates: strict test PASS; full `TestPort_Isolation*` suite PASS; framework + executor vacuum/analyze units; `-race` lockmgr; pgbench smoke. **Rest of DDL/VACUUM group still deferred** (alter-table-{1,2,4}, `*-conflict` role/ACL infra, vacuum-{concurrent-drop,no-cleanup-lock}, detach/partition specs, reindex-toast, inherit-temp, plpgsql-toast). |
| 0118-0034 | [SELECT-list set-returning function nested in an expression (M0118-0008 enabler)](0118-0034-select-list-srf-nested-in-expression.md) | accepted | **Planner/executor correctness fix (not a spec promotion).** A set-returning function nested inside a larger SELECT-list scalar expression — e.g. `generate_series(1,1000) % 4` — silently collapsed to a **single** row holding the SRF's start value instead of one row per element (so `INSERT INTO b SELECT generate_series(1,1000) % 4` inserted 1 row, not 1000). `buildSelectSrfProjectSet` only expanded an SRF that *was* the bare target (optionally one cast); a nested SRF fell through to the scalar `generate_series` fallback. Fix: detect a nested generate_series, assign it a temp eval-row slot (`ChildWidth + k`, beyond the visible columns), and record a **wrapper** = the resolved target with the SRF `FuncCall` replaced by a `ColumnRef` to that slot (new `findFirstNestedSRF`/`replaceExprNode` helpers; `SrfCol.Wrapped`, `ProjectSet.{Wrappers,ChildWidth,EvalRowWidth}`). The executor builds a per-step eval row (child row in `[0:ChildWidth)`, wrapped-SRF values in temp slots above) and evaluates each wrapper against it. Bounded: `generate_series` only when nested; bare/FROM-clause SRFs and the no-wrapper path are byte-for-byte unchanged. Unblocks the `alter-table-1`/`alter-table-2` data setup (still deferred on FK `NOT VALID` parse + `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` + lock semantics). Gates: `TestSelectListSRFInsideExpression`; planner+executor unit suites; `TestPort_RegressSuite`; pgbench smoke. |
| 0118-0035 | [`vacuum-concurrent-drop` isolation spec: blocking maintenance lock + post-lock existence re-check (M0118-0008)](0118-0035-vacuum-concurrent-drop.md) | accepted | **Eighth M0118-0008 promotion.** Promotes `vacuum-concurrent-drop` to pass-required (byte-identical to PG 18.3, all 6 permutations) — `VACUUM`/`ANALYZE` of partition targets while a concurrent session holds `part1` in `SHARE` then DROPs `part2` and commits. Two fixes mirroring `vacuum.c` `vacuum_open_relation`. (1) **Blocking per-relation lock (non-SKIP_LOCKED path).** Previously VACUUM/ANALYZE took a heavyweight lock only on the SKIP_LOCKED path; without it neither op locked, so `s2` never waited behind `LOCK part1 IN SHARE MODE`. The per-target loop now acquires `ShareUpdateExclusiveLock` (or `AccessExclusiveLock` for `VACUUM FULL`) via `acquireRelLockMaybeTransient` — blocking during acquisition (so `<waiting ...>` fires), released immediately in autocommit. (2) **Post-lock existence re-check.** After the lock the target is re-checked against the live catalog via the new `relationStillExists` helper (`catalog.InMemory.LookupTableByOID`, the `try_relation_open` analog); a target dropped by the transaction that committed during the wait is skipped — emitting `WARNING: skipping vacuum/analyze of "X" --- relation no longer exists` only for an **explicit** (`vacuumTarget.explicit`) target, silently for an expanded partition child. Gates: strict `TestPort_IsolationVacuumConcurrentDrop` PASS; `TestPort_IsolationVacuumSkipLocked` PASS (no regression); executor vacuum/analyze units; `-race` lockmgr; pgbench smoke. **Rest of DDL/VACUUM group still deferred** (alter-table-{1,2,4}, `*-conflict` role/ACL infra, partition ATTACH/DETACH, vacuum-no-cleanup-lock, reindex-toast, inherit-temp, plpgsql-toast). |

A faithful fix is multi-site (planner SELECT + UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/FK/MERGE expansion) and must land atomically per the sibling-paths discipline; this loop lands the zero-blast-radius central pieces: `catalog.Table.TempOwner`, the shared filter `catalog.AccessibleInheritanceChildren(children, owner)` (the single chokepoint the wiring loop calls everywhere), a stable `config.SessionRegistry.UniqueID()` per-connection identity, and `executor.sessionTempOwner(ctx)` deriving `"s<id>"` + stamping it at both `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE` sites. | 0118-0038 | [`INSERT … SELECT` fewer source columns: crash fix + default-fill (M0118-0008 enabler)](0118-0038-insert-select-fewer-columns-default-fill.md) | accepted | **Server-crash correctness fix (not a spec promotion).** `INSERT INTO t SELECT …` with no explicit column list, where the `SELECT` is narrower than the table, panicked the backend (`index out of range` in `insertOp.Next` — `ColumnIndex=[0,1,2]` indexed a 2-col source row) instead of filling the trailing columns with their `DEFAULT`. `planInsert` now reconciles the source arity with `colIndex`: over-wide source → `42601` *"INSERT has more expressions than target columns"*; explicit-list under-wide → `42601` *"…more target columns than expressions"*; implicit-list under-wide → truncate `colIndex` to the source width so the executor's `applyDefaultsForMissing` fills the rest. | 0118-0040 | [`vacuum-conflict` / `cluster-conflict`: ownership-based maintenance privilege (M0118-0008)](0118-0040-vacuum-cluster-conflict-ownership.md) | accepted | **Eleventh M0118-0008 promotion; second/third `*-conflict` members.** Promotes `vacuum-conflict` (16 perms) and `cluster-conflict` (2 perms) to pass-required, byte-identical to PG 18.3. Four changes. (1) New `catalog.Table.Owner` (role name; empty = bootstrap superuser; pg_class.relowner output unchanged). (2) `ALTER TABLE … OWNER TO role` now records the owner — parser captures it into `AlterTableStmt.OwnerTo` (was discarded), executor sets `tbl.Owner` + takes a txn-scoped `AccessExclusiveLock` (`AlterTableGetLockLevel`, no-op in autocommit). (3) New `maintenancePermitted(ctx, tbl)` helper wired into the explicit-target loop of `expandVacuumTargets`/`expandAnalyzeTargets` **before any lock** (mirrors `expand_vacuum_rel`'s no-lock `pg_class` ACL check): an unprivileged explicit target is skipped with `WARNING: permission denied to vacuum/analyze "<name>", skipping it` and **no wait**; after `ALTER … OWNER TO` the role owns the table so the command is permitted and blocks on the conflicting `LOCK … IN SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE MODE` until commit. (4) `clusterOp.Next` now takes a blocking `AccessExclusiveLock` (`acquireRelLockMaybeTransient`) so CLUSTER waits behind the same `SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE` holder then completes. | 0118-0039 | [`truncate-conflict` isolation spec: TRUNCATE privilege model + role-DDL batch fix (M0118-0008)](0118-0039-truncate-conflict-privilege-model.md) | accepted | **Tenth M0118-0008 promotion; first of the `*-conflict` family.** Promotes `truncate-conflict` to pass-required (byte-identical to PG 18.3, all 8 permutations). Three problems solved. (1) **Batch-swallow root cause** — the setup `CREATE ROLE …; CREATE TABLE …;` arrives as one batch; the parser doesn't recognise `CREATE ROLE`, so the parse-failure recovery handed the *whole* batch to `tryHandleRoleDDL` which handled only the `CREATE ROLE` and dropped the `CREATE TABLE` (so `truncate_tab` never existed). New `splitLeadingRoleDDL`/`firstTopLevelSemicolon` peel the leading role statement off, handle it via the existing intercept (keeps `Server.roles` populated for connection-time `roleExists`), then **recurse** on the remainder so `CREATE TABLE` runs; standalone role DDL untouched. (2) **TRUNCATE privilege model** — new catalog ACL store (`tableACLs`, `GrantTablePrivilege`/`HasTablePrivilege`/`DropTableACL` on the `Catalog` interface); `SET ROLE`/`RESET ROLE` now track `connTx.NonSuperuserRole`; an autocommit table-level `GRANT … ON … TO …` is recorded (`grant_ddl.go`); `execTruncate` does a **pre-lock** check — `NonSuperuserRole != "" && !HasTablePrivilege(oid, role, "TRUNCATE")` ⇒ `42501 permission denied for table <name>` immediately, no wait (superuser/owner bypass). (3) **Autocommit TRUNCATE wait** — `execTruncate` switched from `acquireDDLLockTxn` (no-op in autocommit) to `acquireRelLockMaybeTransient` so a granted autocommit TRUNCATE blocks behind `s1`'s open `SELECT` (AccessShare held to commit) and proceeds after commit; preserves `inherit-temp` (its TRUNCATE is in an explicit txn → identical hold-to-commit). Gates: strict test + `-race` PASS; all sibling M0118-0008 specs PASS; createuser/dropuser/amcheck PASS; catalog/parser/server/executor units; pgbench smoke 0-failed ~15.2k TPS. **`vacuum-conflict`/`cluster-conflict` still deferred** (need ownership-based checks, not a grantable privilege); rest of group unchanged. **Follow-up (2026-07-05, M0097-0040):** the same `tableACLs`/`HasTablePrivilege` store now also gates plain INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (`dmlPrivilegePermitted`, `internal/executor/operators_storage.go`, owner-bypass + grant-lookup, checked pre-lock in `insertOp`/`updateOp`/`deleteOp.Open`) — previously only TRUNCATE/MAINTAIN consulted it, so a `REVOKE INSERT` under `SET ROLE` incorrectly still allowed the INSERT. FK-cascade deletes and the logical-replication apply worker write heap pages directly and are unaffected. **Follow-up (2026-07-05, same day): SELECT enforcement.** `seqScanOp.Open`/`indexScanOp.openPrep`/`indexOnlyScanOp.Open` now also gate `SELECT` via `dmlPrivilegePermitted`, with a `catalog.IsSystemRelation(tbl.OID)` carve-out that always permits SELECT on pg_catalog/information_schema (goopg has no pg_init_privs-style default-ACL seeding, so without the carve-out every non-superuser catalog read — psql `\d`, pg_dump, information_schema queries — would newly 42501). Verified no regression in `truncate-conflict`/`intra-grant-inplace` isolation specs + full executor/planner/catalog/server suites + tpch-spotcheck. **Follow-up (2026-07-06, M0122-0008): view-owner privilege check.** Closes the remaining gap just above. `execCreateView` now stamps the creating role as `Owner` (previously every view was silently "owned" by the bootstrap superuser); new `planner.tagViewOwnerScans` (`internal/planner/view_privilege.go`) tags every scan inside an inlined view's plan tree with `PrivilegeCheckRole` = the view's owner (skipped when `WITH (security_invoker = true)`, PG 15+'s escape hatch, now actually enforced for the first time); `dmlPrivilegePermitted` became a thin wrapper around new `dmlPrivilegePermittedAs(ctx, tbl, priv, checkRole)`, which the three SELECT-gated scan operators call with the tagged role via `selectPrivilegeCheckRole`. Nested views keep their own owner (depth-first `Plan()` recursion tags innermost-first). **Still open:** the view's own ACL is never checked against the querying role (no plan node represents "scan the view itself"), a pre-existing gap not caused by this fix — ledger row filed. Tests: `internal/planner/view_privilege_test.go`, `internal/executor/storage_dml_test.go`'s `TestScanOperatorsUseViewOwnerPrivilegeOverride`, `internal/executor/view_owner_privilege_test.go`. |
| 0118-0044 | [Dollar-quote-aware step splitter in the isolation harness (M0118-0008 enabler)](0118-0044-isolation-splitter-dollar-quote.md) | accepted | **Test-harness correctness fix, not a spec promotion.** The isolation runner's `splitSQLStatements` (used by `execStep` to break a multi-statement step into individual statements) handled single-quotes and `--` comments but **not dollar-quoted strings**, so a step like `plpgsql-toast`'s `do $$ ... commit; ... $$;` was split at the first `;` *inside* the `$$` body — goopg received the truncated `do $$\n declare x text` and replied `lex error … unterminated dollar-quoted string`, a harness artifact (goopg lexes `$$…$$` fine). Fix: new `dollarOpener` helper recognises a `$tag$` opener (empty/identifier tag, no `$` inside per PG manual §4.1.2.4, rejects `$1` positional params); the splitter tracks an active `dollarCloser` and copies bytes verbatim until the exact closer. Setup blocks (dollar-quoted `CREATE FUNCTION`) were unaffected — they bypass the splitter via `execGlobalSetup`/`execConnSetupCapture`. The one already-strict spec with a dollar-quoted step (`merge-update`, whose `$$` wraps an `EXPLAIN…MERGE…RETURNING` with no top-level `;`) is byte-identical under both splitters. With correct splitting, `plpgsql-toast`'s first divergence moves to the **real** blocker — `unsupported PL/pgSQL statement` (`COMMIT` inside a `DO` block) — so the deferral now records the true gap. Test-harness only; no engine change; cannot regress any spec. Gates: new unit `TestSplitSQLStatementsDollarQuote`; `internal/testport/framework` tests PASS; `TestPort_IsolationMergeUpdate` strict PASS (no regression); `go vet` clean. Deferred: `plpgsql-toast` itself (PL/pgSQL transaction control + advisory locks + detoast-across-commit) and the rest of the M0118-0008 tail. |
| 0118-0045 | [`vacuum-no-cleanup-lock`: pg_class reltuples/relpages from VACUUM (M0118-0008)](0118-0045-vacuum-no-cleanup-lock-relstats.md) | accepted | **Spec promotion — `vacuum-no-cleanup-lock` → `pass`.** The spec asserts `pg_class.relpages|reltuples` track what a non-aggressive `VACUUM` observes even while a cursor pins the table's only heap page (no cleanup lock). Two gaps: (1) the `vacuumer` setup `SET vacuum_multixact_freeze_min_age = 0` hit `unrecognized configuration parameter` — registered the GUC (`config/defaults.go`, BootVal `5000000`) + its `postgresql.conf.sample` line (parity gate). (2) The virtual `pg_class` builder (`catalog.VirtualRows`, the live read path) hard-coded `relpages`/`reltuples` to `0` and nothing updated them on VACUUM. New `catalog.(*InMemory).UpdateRelStats` (the `vac_update_relstats` analog) overwrites `Pages`/`RowCount` while **merging** into any existing `Stats` so a prior ANALYZE's per-column `pg_statistic` survives; the builder reads `t.Stats` (nil ⇒ `0|0`, so untouched tables are unchanged); `vacuumOp.Next` publishes after a successful vacuum. Load-bearing subtlety: `reltuples` is published from `vacuum.Analyze`'s **fresh-snapshot visible-tuple count**, NOT the prune's surviving-line-pointer count — a recently-dead tuple (deleted+committed but not removable because the pin holder holds `OldestXmin` back) survives the prune yet must be excluded from `reltuples` (PG counts `HEAPTUPLE_LIVE`, not `RECENTLY_DEAD`), which the visible count gets right (`22`→`21` in the pinholder permutation). Heap `pg_class` write-once DDL row left at `0` (not the read path). Gates: `TestPort_IsolationVacuumNoCleanupLock` strict PASS; `TestUpdateRelStatsPreservesColumns`; `TestSampleConfigCoversRegistry`; sibling vacuum/freeze specs PASS; `-race` vacuum/mvcc; executor/catalog/config PASS; pgbench smoke. Deferred: rest of M0118-0008 tail (alter-table NOT VALID/VALIDATE, partition ATTACH/DETACH, reindex-concurrently-toast, plpgsql-toast). |
| 0118-0046 | [`alter-table-2`: ADD FOREIGN KEY … NOT VALID lock semantics (M0118-0008)](0118-0046-alter-table-2-add-fk-not-valid.md) | accepted | **Spec promotion — `alter-table-2` → `pass`** (48 perms, byte-identical to PG 18.3). Two changes: (1) the `ALTER TABLE … ADD FOREIGN KEY …` parser now accepts the `NOT VALID` trailer (in any order with `[NOT] DEFERRABLE [INITIALLY …]`) — new AST field `AlterTableAction.NotValid`, surfaced as `pg_constraint.convalidated='f'` via new `catalog.ForeignKey.NotValid`; (2) the `AlterTableAddForeignKey` executor case now takes a transaction-scoped `ShareRowExclusiveLock` on the altered table via the existing `acquireDDLLockTxn` (PG `AlterTableGetLockLevel` → `AT_AddConstraint`). The standard lock matrix then drives every permutation: a concurrent `INSERT` (RowExclusiveLock) **conflicts** so one of `s1b`/`s2d` waits until the other commits, while `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` (RowShareLock) and plain reads (AccessShareLock) proceed. Confined like its DDL-lock siblings (`create-trigger` 0118-0027, `alter-table-3` 0118-0032): **no-op in autocommit / for system catalogs**, so the pg_dump-restore / HammerDB-load path and pgbench TPC-B are untouched. Only the altered table is locked (the spec cannot distinguish the referenced-table lock; `s2e INSERT INTO a` always follows `s2d INSERT INTO b`). Deferred: `alter-table-1` (adds `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` + ShareUpdateExclusiveLock) + the rest of the M0118-0008 tail. Gates: `TestPort_IsolationAlterTable2` strict PASS; sibling alter-table-3 / create-trigger / sequence-ddl PASS; parser + executor + catalog units; `go vet` clean; pgbench smoke 0-failed. |

Builds directly on 0118-0046: the `ADD CONSTRAINT … FOREIGN KEY … NOT VALID` half already parses and locks; the only new piece is `ALTER TABLE … VALIDATE CONSTRAINT name`. (1) Parser: new `AlterTableValidateConstraint` action kind; `parseAlterTableAction` matches `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT name` (`VALIDATE` is an identifier-keyword). (2) Executor: the new dispatch case takes a transaction-scoped `ShareUpdateExclusiveLock` via `acquireDDLLockTxn` (PG `AlterTableGetLockLevel` → `AT_ValidateConstraint`, the *minimum* lock) and flips the named FK's `convalidated` from `'f'` to `'t'` (`ForeignKey.NotValid = false`); an unknown name raises `42704`. `ShareUpdateExclusive` does **not** conflict with `AccessShare` (reads), `RowShare` (FOR UPDATE), or `RowExclusive` (INSERT) — so VALIDATE never blocks `s2` and the only wait in the spec is the `INSERT` behind the still-uncommitted `ADD CONSTRAINT`'s `ShareRowExclusiveLock`, exactly as in `alter-table-2`. No engine change beyond parse + lock + flag (VALIDATE emits no rows; parity rides on the wait/no-wait timing). No-op in autocommit / for system catalogs, so the dump/load + pgbench path stays lock-free. Gates: `TestPort_IsolationAlterTable1` strict PASS; sibling alter-table-2 / alter-table-3 strict PASS; parser + executor units; `go vet` clean; pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook. |

| 0118-0050 | [PL/pgSQL `SELECT … INTO` statement form (M0118-0008 enabler)](0118-0050-plpgsql-select-into.md) | accepted | **Enabler, NOT a promotion.** Implements PL/pgSQL `SELECT … INTO [STRICT] target[, …] FROM …`, which goopg previously mis-handled by capturing the whole statement verbatim as embedded SQL and letting the planner read `SELECT … INTO x` as SQL's *CREATE-TABLE-AS* spelling (treating `x` as a new table). The parser (`parseSQLStmt`) now special-cases a leading `SELECT`: it detects a top-level (`depth==0`) `INTO` keyword, peels off the optional `STRICT` + comma-separated target list (dotted names allowed for record fields), reconstructs the query text with the `INTO` clause excised, and returns a new `*SelectIntoStmt{SQL, Targets, Strict}` AST node (a SELECT with no top-level INTO still yields a verbatim `*SQLStmt`). The runtime plans/builds the stripped query, captures the **first** result row, and binds via new `bindSelectIntoRow` mirroring the `FOR … IN SELECT` conventions: single target+single column → scalar; single target+multiple columns → record `_<target>_<colname>` sub-fields; multiple targets → positional scalar binding. No matching row sets target(s) to NULL (schema captured from `op.Schema()` before the first `Next()` so the no-row case still binds the right column count); `STRICT` raises `P0002`/`P0003` on zero/>1 rows. Lifts `plpgsql-toast`'s next blocker after 0118-0049: a probe shows `assign1` now executes and emits `length(x) = 6000`; the divergence advances to subquery-valued assignment (`assign2`), expanded record/detoast paths, and the `<waiting ...>` concurrency marker — all deferred (Effort-L). | 0118-0049 | [PL/pgSQL transaction control (`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` in a DO block) (M0118-0008 enabler)](0118-0049-plpgsql-do-transaction-control.md) | accepted | **Enabler, NOT a promotion.** Implements PL/pgSQL `COMMIT;`/`ROLLBACK;` in a **non-atomic** routine (top-level `DO` / procedure outside an explicit txn block): the statement commits/rolls back the current transaction and continues in a **fresh** one; in an *atomic* context (a `DO` inside `BEGIN … COMMIT`) it raises SQLSTATE `2D000` *invalid transaction termination*, as in PG. The transaction lifecycle is server-owned (`connTxState`/dispatch), so a new optional `Context.PLpgSQLCommitChain func(rollback bool) error` callback bridges the layers: the parser emits a `TxControlStmt` node, the runtime invokes the callback (nil ⇒ `2D000`), and the dispatch installs it **only in auto-commit mode** — the closure commits/rolls back the current `tx`, releases only xact-scoped advisory locks (session locks survive), begins a fresh RC tx + snapshot, and reassigns the outer `tx`/`snap` + `ctx.Tx`/`ctx.Snap` so the trailing auto-commit and per-statement RC refresh follow the chained tx. Blast radius nil (only the new `TxControlStmt` case ever calls the callback). This lifts `plpgsql-toast`'s first blocker; its divergence advances to the next gap — PL/pgSQL `SELECT … INTO var` / record handling (deferred, separate Effort-L slice). Gates: `TestParseTransactionControl`; `TestPlpgSQLDoCommitChainDurability` / `…RollbackChain` / `…CommitInExplicitBlockRejected`; `TestPort_IsolationSubxidOverflow`/`FreezeTheDead` strict PASS (no regression); `internal/executor`+`internal/server` units; `go vet` clean; pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook. |

| 0118-0057 | [`DETACH PARTITION … CONCURRENTLY` waits for concurrent table users (M0118-0008 enabler)](0118-0057-detach-partition-concurrently-wait.md) | accepted | **Enabler, NOT a promotion.** `ALTER TABLE … DETACH PARTITION … CONCURRENTLY` completed synchronously in goopg's executor, so the isolation runner never rendered the `<waiting ...>` marker the `detach-partition-concurrently-{1,2,3,4}` specs require — the first divergence after the 0118-0048/0055/0056 enablers. | 0118-0078 | [INSERT enforces the DEFAULT partition constraint (M0118-0008 `partition-concurrent-attach` enabler / piece (c))](0118-0078-default-partition-insert-constraint.md) | accepted | **Enabler, NOT a promotion — piece (c) of `partition-concurrent-attach`.** PG attaches an implicit *partition constraint* (the negation of every sibling's bounds) to a DEFAULT partition and enforces it on **every** leaf insert via `ExecPartitionCheck` — routed or direct. goopg had no per-row partition-constraint expression and never performed this check, so a direct `INSERT INTO tpart_default` of a sibling-owned value wrote the row (spec perm 2 showed 6 rows, not 3 + the missing `ERROR: new row for relation "tpart_default" violates partition constraint`). Fix: `insertOp.Next` now calls new `checkDefaultPartitionInsertConstraint(ctx, leaf, leafCols, leafRow, pos)` at both heap-write sites (routed-leaf path on `partTable`/`partRow`; non-partitioned path on `o.plan.Table` for a direct insert into a leaf default). It walks the target's partition ancestry via `Table.PartitionParentOID` and, for every ancestor that **is** a default (`isDefaultPartitionChild`), re-routes the row's parent partition-key value through the parent's scheme one level (`routePartitionKeyToImmediateChild` → `FindRangePartitionForDatums`/`FindPartitionForValue`); if it lands on a **non-default** sibling, raises `23514` naming that ancestor default. A partition child always carries every ancestor key column by name, so a leaf-ordered row resolves any ancestor's key without re-mapping. Concurrency-correct: the check reads the **live** catalog *after* the INSERT's `RowExclusiveLock` on the default is granted (post-0118-0076/0077 wait), so the re-route sees the just-committed `tpart_2` and fails — PG's "route pre-commit, check post-commit". No-op in ordinary operation (if a sibling owned the value, routing would have picked it, so the re-route returns the default itself); bounded to simple-column RANGE/LIST (expression-key/HASH skip → never a false positive). Probe: **permutation 2 now matches PG byte-for-byte** (`<waiting ...>`/`<... completed>`/23514). **Spec stays `defer`** — perms 1 & 3 need INSERT routing-path `RowExclusiveLock`s on each partition along the path (so the wait happens *before* the re-route), the milestone-shared `alter-table-4` work. This lands the standalone, plain-SQL-testable core of `partition-concurrent-attach`; the spec stays `defer` — its remaining blockers (deferred-until-commit attach visibility so a concurrent INSERT routes to the default, ATTACH locking the default partition so that INSERT `<waiting ...>`, and constraint re-validation after the wait) are the milestone-sized per-session MVCC-catalog work shared with `alter-table-4` (ledger). | 0118-0099 | [`predicate-hash.spec` PROMOTED: page (bucket) level predicate locking in a hash index (M0118-0009)](0118-0099-predicate-hash-bucket-locking.md) | accepted | **`predicate-hash.spec` `failed`→`pass`, all 40 permutations byte-identical; promoted to `runIsoSpecStrict` in `TestPort_IsolationPredicateHash`.** PG's hash AM takes a PAGE-level predicate lock on the probed bucket (`hashgettuple`/`_hash_doinsert` → `PredicateLockPage`/`CheckForSerializableConflictIn`), so same-bucket scan+insert form an rw-conflict while different-bucket ones do not. goopg has no native hash AM (a hash index is built on the B-tree substrate) so it seq/index-scanned with a **relation-grain** SIREAD against which *every* insert conflicts → it emitted 30 serialization failures where PG emits 18 (over-aborted the 12 different-bucket interleavings). Same-bucket conflict edges still form (read-before-write via the bucket SIREAD; write-before-read via conflict-out against the invisible inserter); different buckets exercise neither → both commit. Blast radius bounded to SERIALIZABLE equality scans/INSERTs on `DeclaredHash` indexes: the six pass-required btree/seqscan SSI specs (`project-manager`/`total-cash`/`two-ids`/`receipt-report`/`read-only-anomaly*`/`read-write-unique-4`) + `predicate-lock-hot-tuple`/`partial-index`/`simple-write-skew` PASS no regression. Gates: strict PASS (18 failures matching PG, was 30); `internal/executor`+`internal/mvcc`+`internal/planner`+`internal/catalog` units + `-race` SSI/predicate tests PASS; `go build ./...`+`go vet` clean; pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook. Follow-ups: `predicate-gin`/`predicate-gist` need AM-specific granularity; `DeclaredHash` not WAL-persisted (reverts to relation-grain after restart); UPDATE/DELETE on a hash column not yet bucket-locked. |

| 0118-0106 | [`eval-plan-qual.spec` PROMOTED: EPQ recheck over a join (M0118-0007/0009)](0118-0106-eval-plan-qual-over-join-epq-recheck.md) | accepted | **`eval-plan-qual.spec` `failed`→`pass`, all 50 permutations byte-identical; promoted to `runIsoSpecStrict` in `TestPort_IsolationEvalPlanQual` — closing the M0118-0007 planner/output-format group.** goopg approximates EvalPlanQual (no subplan re-run) by following the locked tuple's CTID chain to the live successor and re-applying a recheck predicate built from the locked table's own columns. For an index scan it folds the index key condition into that predicate (so a committed key-UPDATE is caught). The last divergence was `selectresultforupdate` — `SELECT … FOR UPDATE OF jt` over a join whose locked `jt` is the **inner index scan**, with key condition `jt.id = y`: `y` is another join input's column whose `ColumnRef.Index` lives in the **join output coordinate space**, but `epqRecheckFilter` evaluates the folded predicate against only the 2-column `jointest` tuple, so `ColumnRef{1}` (meant `y`) was misread as `jointest.data` → `jt.id(7) = jt.data(42)` → false → the post-update row was wrongly dropped (`0 rows`). The `filterPredMaxColRef` guard missed it because index `1` coincidentally falls inside `[0,2)`. **Fix:** fold the index key condition into the EPQ recheck **only when `ix.Key` is row-local** (a constant) via new `exprRefsColumnOrOuter` guard — a join/correlated key is a join condition, not a local filter, and for a non-key UPDATE the join key is preserved on the successor so skipping its recheck yields the correct re-projection (key-column changes stay caught by the CTID-chain logic; the `lock-update-delete` constant-key fold is unchanged). **Sibling fix:** a lazy hash join now preserves build-side heap ctids (`markJoinPreserveCTID`/`preserveCTIDRel`/`lazyHashCTID`/`buildHashRightWithCTID`, stamped by `nextLazy`) so `FOR UPDATE` over the **hash-join variant** (locked relation on the drained+closed build side) recovers the TID via the `ms.hasCTID` fallback instead of silently returning the stale pre-update row — `nil`/no-op for every query without a `FOR UPDATE` above the join, so the TPC-H hash-join hot path is untouched. Gates: strict PASS (50/50); `TestPort_IsolationEvalPlanQualTrigger`+`LockUpdateDelete`+row-lock family PASS; `-race ./internal/executor/…`; TPC-H Q12/Q13 spot-check; `go build`+`go vet` clean; pgbench smoke = pre-commit hook. |

Blast radius nil: `execTwoPhaseStmt` returns `handled=false` for all other statements, so existing paths are byte-identical; no `port` spec uses these statements. A `prepared-transactions-cic` probe confirms the mechanism end-to-end — the held prepared txn keeps its MVCC slot active so `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` correctly waits for it and unblocks at `COMMIT PREPARED`; first divergence advanced from "parse error at `p1`" to the final `cic2`/`c1` timing, the **only** residual gap being that goopg's CIC active-slot wait does not yet honour `lock_timeout` (PG cancels with `55P03`). | 0118-0137 | [`predicate-gist.spec` PROMOTED: GiST page-level predicate locking via grid-cell SIREAD (M0118-0002)](0118-0137-predicate-gist-grid-cell-ssi.md) | accepted | **Promotion** — `predicate-gist.spec` `failed`→`pass`, all 36 permutations byte-identical to PG 18.3; `TestPort_IsolationPredicateGist` strict; isolation tally 119 pass / 2 failed. The spec tests page-level GiST predicate locking: SERIALIZABLE scans with spatial half-plane filters (`p << / >> point(k,k)`) + point INSERTs must conflict on the SAME spatial region but NOT on disjoint regions. goopg has no native GiST AM (a `USING gist` index is catalog-only), so the queries fall back to a seq scan that took a **relation-grain** SIREAD against which every insert conflicts → over-aborted all 18 disjoint-region permutations. Fix emulates GiST leaf-page granularity with a synthetic **grid cell**: `ssiGistGridCell(x,y)` = FNV-1a of `(floor(x/256), floor(y/256))` → 31-bit pseudo-page; a SERIALIZABLE seq scan of a GiST-indexed table takes a per-matching-tuple grid-cell SIREAD on the *index* (`ssiRecordGistGridRead`) **instead of** the relation lock (suppressed), and an INSERT conflicts-in on its point's cell (`ssiRecordGistIndexInsert`, the `ssiRecordHashIndexInsert` twin). The heap per-tuple SIREAD is skipped (would coarsen to a heap-page lock and re-introduce false positives, same as the hash index-only scan); the invisible-tuple conflict-out is gated by spatial match (`gistTupleMatches`) so an out-of-region concurrent insert forms no spurious edge. Both rw-edge directions confirmed against the permutations. The `Filter`-over-`SeqScan` predicate is threaded down in **both** build paths (`Build` + the live `buildRec`/`BuildFastIterator`, `pattern_sibling_paths_must_agree`). Blast radius bounded: the per-tuple branch is gated behind `gistSSIIdxOID != 0` (0 for every non-gist scan), catalog `Method`/pg_am/pg_dump/WAL unchanged. Gates: strict PASS (36 perms); non-gist SSI regression (`predicate-hash`, `partial-index`, `index-only-scan`, `simple-write-skew`, `project-manager`, `classroom-scheduling`, `read-write-unique`) PASS; `-race` executor+mvcc + full executor/planner units PASS; `go build ./...` clean; pgbench smoke 0 failed; TPC-H spot-check infra-timed-out on WSL2 (gated path structurally unaffected). |

| 0119-0004aw | [owner-side function REVOKE (`pg_proc.proacl`) round-trip in pg_dump (DU-002 slice 347)](0119-0004-owner-side-function-revoke-proacl-pgdump.md) | accepted | **Implementation** — the owner-side counterpart of slice 346's PUBLIC-side function REVOKE. A function's `acldefault('f', owner)` grants `EXECUTE` to **both** the owner and `PUBLIC`, so the two single-role revokes diverge: `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM PUBLIC` → `{postgres=X/postgres}` (slice 346), `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM postgres` → `{=X/postgres}` (PUBLIC's implicit EXECUTE **survives**), both → `{}` (verified vs real PG 18.3). Unlike a table/sequence — whose default grants only the owner so `REVOKE ALL FROM owner` empties to `{}` (slices 341/343) — the function owner revoke leaves a surviving non-owner aclitem. goopg got this wrong two ways: (1) `recordFunctionRevoke` (slice 346) seeded only the owner's implicit EXECUTE, so revoking the owner emptied the array → pg_dump wrongly also emitted a `… FROM PUBLIC;` line, stripping PUBLIC's surviving default on restore; (2) `relaclTextLockedFor` re-added the absent owner as `postgres=<default>/postgres` whenever the owner key was missing from a non-empty array and `relACLEmptied` was unset, so `{=X/postgres}` rendered as `{postgres=X/postgres,=X/postgres}` (owner resurrected → pg_dump dropped the owner REVOKE). The pre-existing `relACLEmptied` flag is too narrow — it fires only when the owner revoke *also empties the whole array*. Fix: new OID-keyed catalog flag `relACLOwnerRevoked` (the broader "owner's implicit default was explicitly revoked, regardless of surviving grantees"; `relACLEmptied` is its whole-array-empty special case): `RevokeTablePrivilege` sets it whenever the owner entry is fully removed; `relaclTextLockedFor` suppresses the leading owner entry when `relACLEmptied \|\| relACLOwnerRevoked` and the empty-`byRole` early-return renders `{}` for either (covers revoking every grantee in one statement, where the last-removed entry is a non-owner so `relACLEmptied` stays unset); `MaterializeOwnerACL` never resurrects a revoked owner; an owner-side `GrantTablePrivilege` clears both flags; `DropTableACL` clears both. `recordFunctionRevoke` now seeds **both** owner + PUBLIC implicit EXECUTE, but only while `proacl` is still NULL (detected via the newly interface-exposed `Catalog.ProcACLText(oid) == ""`) — re-seeding on a second REVOKE would resurrect an already-revoked grantee, so `… FROM PUBLIC` then `… FROM postgres` must reach `{}` not `{=X/postgres}` (PG expands `acldefault` exactly once). Slice 346 stays byte-identical. The flag is OID-keyed/object-type-agnostic and additionally fixes a latent table bug (`REVOKE ALL ON TABLE FROM owner` while a grantee survives now correctly suppresses the owner instead of re-adding the default). Dump-fidelity only; near-zero blast radius (recorder only removes bits already present; flag fires only on a full owner revoke; prior table/sequence/schema slices set it together with `relACLEmptied` → rendered identically). | 0118-0134 | [`BEGIN; LOCK …` in one simple-query message must be transaction-scoped (regression fix, M0118-0009)](0118-0134-multistatement-begin-lock-txn-scope.md) | accepted | **Regression fix** — restores two pass-required (`runIsoSpecStrict`) specs, `vacuum-concurrent-drop` + `vacuum-skip-locked`, to green. Test: `TestDropOperatorSurvivesAcrossRestart` (`internal/executor/create_operator_test.go`) registers an operator via `RegisterUserOperatorDuringRecovery` only (simulating the exact post-restart state, bypassing the live-CREATE compat registry) and asserts DROP succeeds, the registry entry is gone, and a second DROP on the same operator still 42883s. Protocol-independent, applies to every `compatNoopCommandTag` prefix, not just these four keywords; fixing it touches the shared matching logic across all ~12 prefix cases, out of this loop's bounded "verify + correct the follow-up plan" scope. |
| 0121-0002 | [IndexOnlyScan promotion: residual Filter ColumnRef remap (M0121-0002)](0121-0002-indexonly-scan-residual-filter-remap.md) | accepted | **Implementation (2026-07-04)** — fixes the WordPress backend-crashing bug seeded from M0120-0002 (`.ralph/deferral_ledger.md`, 2026-07-04 M0120-0002 row): `wp_set_object_terms`'s `SELECT term_taxonomy_id FROM wp_term_relationships WHERE object_id = ? AND term_taxonomy_id = ?` panicked `Slot.Get` (`internal/executor/opnode.go:99`, `index out of range [1] with length 1`) whenever `object_id` matched a real row. Root cause: `tryPromoteIndexOnlyScan` (`internal/planner/planner.go`) narrows `Project(Filter(IndexScan))` to `Filter(IndexOnlyScan)` using only the `Project`'s target list to size the covered/output schema, never checking whether the surviving `Filter.Predicate` also referenced a column, and never remapping that predicate's `ColumnRef.Index` values off their pre-promotion (full-row) positions — a residual filter left pointing one past the end of the narrowed scan's row. Root-caused directly (no WordPress/PG4WP needed): a fresh single `psql` connection with a matching `object_id` reproduces it deterministically (the earlier "not reproducible via a single connection" ledger note was because the tested `object_id` had since been deleted from seed data, so the scan probe never yielded a row for the filter to evaluate). Fix: `tryPromoteIndexOnlyScan` now walks the surviving `Filter.Predicate` (`walkColumnRefs`) to extend `covered` with any column it needs that the index carries (abandoning the promotion, falling back to the pre-existing correct `IndexScan`+`Filter`+`Project` shape, if the filter needs an uncovered/non-indexed column or an outer/subquery ref), then remaps the predicate's `ColumnRef.Index` values via new `remapColumnRefsToSchema` — a name-keyed rewrite kept in lockstep with `shiftColumnRefsBy`'s case list — and reinstates an explicit `Project` only when the filter pulled in a column beyond the original `SELECT` list. Tests: new `TestIndexOnlyScanResidualFilterColumnRemap` (`internal/executor/indexonly_residual_filter_test.go`, a minimal 3-column composite-PK table; confirmed it panics with the same signature when the fix is reverted). Gates: `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./internal/planner/... ./internal/executor/...` PASS (no regressions); live end-to-end confirmation against the running `goopg-wp` (`:5544`) instance (both the exact WordPress query and a fresh probe table return correct rows with an `Index Only Scan ... Filter:` plan, no panic); `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` PASS (Q12=2/Q13=33). No new deferrals. |

A later loop closed the `I/O Timings` line: `nodeStats` (`internal/executor/instrument.go`) gains `bufReadTimeNs`/`bufWriteTimeNs` (the latter folding `ExtendTimeNanos()` in alongside `WriteTimeNanos()`, matching upstream's single shared write-time bucket for `IOOP_EXTEND`); `formatIOTimingsLine` (`internal/executor/operators_explain.go`) renders `"I/O Timings: shared read=X.XXX write=Y.YYY"` in TEXT and `"Shared I/O Read/Write Time"` in JSON, both omitted when zero — see the doc's new "Follow-up: EXPLAIN `I/O Timings` line" section for the one accepted GUC-vs-nonzero gating simplification (ledger row appended). Reuses/writebacks/fsyncs and the `CTEDMLPrefix` residual remain open. A later loop closed `fsyncs`/`fsync_time`: `wal.Writer` gains `fsyncCount` (a `walBufferCounters`-shared `stats.Counter`, incremented once per real `dataSync` call in `state.flushUpTo`) and `sharedFsyncTimeNanos` (`AddFsyncTimeNanos`/`FsyncTimeNanos`); `internal/initdb/open.go`'s pre-existing `OnWALSync`/`OnWALSyncDone` hooks (which bracket `FlushUpTo` using a fixed `walProcNum` slot for `pg_stat_activity` display) now also gate `AddFsyncTimeNanos` on the *calling backend's own* `track_io_timing` via a separate `act.LookupTrackedGoroutine()` check, since `walProcNum`'s own flag is never set by any session; `fetchIOStatRows` gains a second instrumented cell, (client backend, wal, normal), rendering `fsyncs`/`fsync_time` — see the doc's new "`fsyncs` / `fsync_time` counters" section. Reuses/writebacks and the `CTEDMLPrefix` residual remain open (each needs a buffering mechanism goopg does not have — ring-buffer strategy / async-writeback issuance). A later loop closed `writeback`/`writeback_time`: new `internal/storage/writeback.go` adds `Pool.accountBackendWrite`/`accountBgwriterWrite`/`accountCheckpointerWrite`, called from `evictVictim`'s dirty flush, `WriteDirtyPages` (bgwriter), and `flushBatch`/`FlushAllPaced` (checkpointer) respectively; each tracks a running pending-page count against a new GUC-driven threshold (`checkpoint_flush_after`=32/`bgwriter_flush_after`=64/`backend_flush_after`=0, upstream's exact defaults) and, on crossing it, calls a new `Manager.SyncFileRangeHint` (real Linux `sync_file_range(2)` via `internal/storage/writeback_linux.go`, `ErrWritebackUnsupported` stub on other platforms), incrementing per-context `writeback`/`writeback_time` counters only on a real successful hint; `fetchIOStatRows` renders these into 3 rows — (client backend|background writer|checkpointer, relation, normal) — the first real instrumentation for the latter two rows. Only `reuses` and the `CTEDMLPrefix` residual remain open, plus 4 named simplifications vs. upstream (single-relation-per-hint instead of coalesced ranges, `backend_flush_after` applied process-wide not per-session, bgwriter/checkpointer writeback timing gated on boot-time `track_io_timing` via plain `time.Since` rather than the activity-registry wait-event clock, and bgwriter/checkpointer `writes`/`write_bytes`/`write_time` still zero) — see the doc's new "`writeback` / `writeback_time` counters" section. A later loop (2026-07-06) closed the `CTEDMLPrefix` nested-node residual: `cteDMLPrefixOp` (`internal/executor/operators_cte_dml.go`) implements a new `instrumentScopeCarrier` interface (`internal/executor/instrument.go`, mirroring the existing `heapFetchCounter` hand-off) so `maybeInstrument` hands it the `*instrumenter` active on its own `Build()` call; its two lazy `Build()` sites (the DML plans and the outer body, both Built inside `Open()` after CTE write-then-snapshot-restore ordering, well after the top-level `withInstrumentation` scope has already exited) now run through a new `buildUnderScope` helper that reinstates that instrumenter around them, so nested nodes (e.g. `Insert on t`) land in the same `nodeStatsTable` the renderer already walks — see the doc's new "`CTEDMLPrefix` nested-node instrumentation" section. A later loop (2026-07-06) closed `EXPLAIN (BUFFERS)` without `ANALYZE`: `internal/executor/operators_explain.go` gains `planningBufferUsageJSON()`, an always-present all-zero `"Planning"` group (`Shared {Hit,Read,Dirtied,Written} Blocks`) set on both non-TEXT render paths whenever `opts.Buffers` is true, independent of `ANALYZE` — matching upstream's `peek_buffer_usage`, which shows this group for any non-TEXT format regardless of ANALYZE while TEXT keeps its existing positive-only gate (correct as-is here since goopg's planner never touches `storage.Pool` during cost estimation, so the value is genuinely always zero, not an approximation) — see the doc's new "`EXPLAIN (BUFFERS)` without `ANALYZE`" section. A later loop (2026-07-06) closed the local/temp-buffer terms: `planningBufferUsageJSON()` and `planToJSONWithStats`'s per-node `opts.Buffers` block both now also set `Local Hit/Read/Dirtied/Written Blocks` and `Temp Read/Written Blocks` to constant `0`, the same "always present, unconditionally, once BUFFERS is requested" rule the `Shared *`/`Planning` fixes already implement — goopg has no local-buffer-manager or temp-buffer concept, so these are genuinely always zero, not a narrower stub — see the doc's new "Local/Temp `* Blocks` terms" section. A later loop (2026-07-06) closed the Local/Temp/Planning-time I/O timing terms: `planningBufferUsageJSON` gained a `trackIOTiming bool` parameter (both `explainOp.Open` call sites now pass it) adding all six `Shared/Local/Temp I/O Read/Write Time` keys as `float64(0)` constants to the `"Planning"` group when the GUC is on, and `planToJSONWithStats`'s existing `trackIOTiming` block gained the `Local I/O Read/Write Time`/`Temp I/O Read/Write Time` pairs (constant zero) alongside the pre-existing real `Shared I/O Read/Write Time` values — same "no local-buffer-manager/temp-buffer concept, so genuinely always zero" rationale as the Blocks terms — see the doc's new "Local/Temp/Planning-time I/O timing terms" section. A later loop (2026-07-06) closed writeback simplification (2): `backend_flush_after` is now genuinely per-session — `activity.ActivityRegistry` gains a per-backend `BackendFlushAfterBlocks` field (`UpdateBackendFlushAfter`/`BackendFlushAfterOverride`, no fast-path gate since `evictVictim` is far rarer than the buffer-pin hot path), seeded at connection setup and kept live by a new `backend_flush_after` `OnChange` hook in `server.New()` (mirrors `track_io_timing`'s own runtime-`SET` wiring exactly); `storage.Pool` gains a `BackendFlushAfterOverride` hook wired in `initdb.Open`, consulted by `accountBackendWrite` before falling back to the pre-existing process-wide default — see the doc's new "Per-session `backend_flush_after`" section. A later loop (2026-07-06) closed writeback simplification (3), finding a real bug along the way: the checkpointer's activity-registry registration (`cmd/goopg/main.go`) used `act.Register(&Backend{PID: "cp-0", ...})` — the regular, numeric-PID-keyed path, where `procNumForPID` maps every non-numeric PID to `r.bgBase`, the same fixed slot `RegisterBackground(WalWriterIdx, ...)` already claims for the WAL writer — so the checkpointer's registration was silently clobbering the WAL writer's `activitySlot` every server run. Fixed by adding `activity.BgwriterIdx = 3` and registering both the checkpointer (`internal/initdb/open.go`, via `RegisterBackground(CheckpointerIdx, ...)`) and, when enabled, the bgwriter (`RegisterBackground(BgwriterIdx, ...)`, `backend_type = "background writer"` matching upstream) in their own reserved slots; `wal.CheckpointerConfig` and `storage.Bgwriter` each gain `OnLoopStart`/`OnLoopEnd func()` fields (mirroring `wal.Config`'s pre-existing pair for the WAL writer) so `initdb.Open` can track each goroutine's identity for the duration of its own `Run`/`run` loop; `OnBgwriterWritebackWait/Done`/`OnCheckpointerWritebackWait/Done` are now textually identical to `OnBackendWritebackWait/Done` (`act.LookupTrackedGoroutine()` → real `WaitEventStart`/`WaitEventEnd`), replacing the previous `time.Now()`/`time.Since` pair — see the doc's new "Registered bgwriter/checkpointer background slots" section. Only `reuses` and writeback simplification (4) remain open in this cluster.  A later loop (2026-07-06) closed writeback simplification (4): `storage.Pool` gains `sharedBgwriterWrittenCount`/`sharedBgwriterWriteTimeNanos` and `sharedCheckpointWrittenCount`/`sharedCheckpointWriteTimeNanos`, incremented in `WriteDirtyPages` (bgwriter) and `flushBatch`/`FlushAllPaced` (checkpointer) respectively — deliberately separate from the backend-scoped `sharedWrittenCount` these two paths never touch — bracketed by new `OnBgwriterWriteWait/Done`/`OnCheckpointerWriteWait/Done` hooks wired in `internal/initdb/open.go` the same `act.LookupTrackedGoroutine()` → `WaitEventStart`/`WaitEventEnd` way every other `On*Wait/Done` pair in that function follows; `fetchIOStatRows` renders the new counters into the `(background writer|checkpointer, relation, normal)` rows' `writes`/`write_bytes`/`write_time` cells, previously a hardcoded `0` — see the doc's new "Background writer / checkpointer `writes` counters" section. Only the feature-sized `reuses` op counter remains open in this cluster. A later loop (2026-07-06) fixed an independent, unrelated `planChildren` gap discovered via `unimplemented_feat.json`: `*planner.Update`/`*planner.Delete` had no case at all (unlike `*planner.Insert`'s `p.Source`), so every `EXPLAIN`/`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on an UPDATE/DELETE silently dropped the target scan (and any `FROM`/`USING` join scans) — confirmed against real PG 18.3, which always nests them under `Update on t`/`Delete on t`. Added cases returning `p.Child` + `p.FromScans`/`p.UsingScans`; ANALYZE actual-stats for that child remain absent (the executor drives it via `extractScan`, not a nested `Build()`+`maybeInstrument`'d operator) — degrades gracefully to a cost-estimate-only line, not a crash. Tests: `internal/executor/explain_update_delete_children_test.go`. See the doc's new "Follow-up: `Update`/`Delete` plan-tree children" section. |
| 0122-0003 | [`pg_stat_all_tables` / `pg_stat_user_tables` / `pg_stat_sys_tables`](0122-0003-pg-stat-user-tables.md) | accepted | Adds the three per-table access-statistics system views (upstream `system_views.sql`). `catalog.PGStatTablesRowsForDBOid(dbOid, scope)` + `StatTableScope` (`All`/`User`/`Sys`) build the 26-column row set under the catalog `RLock`, reusing `PGClassRowsForDBOid`'s exact relation filter (relkind `r`/`m`/`p`; sequences/plain-views/foreign/system-catalog virtual tables skipped) and applying upstream's `schemaname IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') OR ~ '^pg_toast'` split via `isSystemStatSchema`. Like `pg_class`/`pg_stat_io`, the views must list the *connecting* database's tables, so `executor.fetchStatTablesRows` (`internal/executor/pgstat_tables.go`) unwraps `ctx.Catalog` to the concrete `*catalog.InMemory` and scopes to `ctx.CurrentDatabaseOid`, swapped in at `valuesOp.Open` (three new `pg_stat_{all,sys,user}_tables` branches mirroring the `pg_stat_io` case); the static `VirtualRows` fallback registered in `registerSystemTables` scopes to `DefaultDBOid`. goopg has no incremental pgstat mutation counters (no `PgStat_StatTabEntry`), so — following the `pg_stat_io` honest-0/NULL precedent — `relid`/`schemaname`/`relname` are real, `n_live_tup` is the ANALYZE `reltuples` estimate (`TableStats.RowCount`), every other counter is a faithful `0` and every `last_*` timestamp is NULL. Because system catalogs are storage-less virtual tables with no `TableStats`, `pg_stat_sys_tables` is effectively empty (documented deferral). Tests: `internal/catalog/pgstat_tables_test.go` (row shape, scope filter, non-table-relkind exclusion) + `internal/executor/pgstat_tables_e2e_test.go` (full SELECT resolves the view, per-connection branch fires, schemaname split). Deferral-ledger row recorded for the missing per-table counter subsystem. **Sibling (2026-07-12):** the per-index views `pg_stat_all_indexes` / `pg_stat_user_indexes` / `pg_stat_sys_indexes` land the same way — `catalog.PGStatIndexesRowsForDBOid(dbOid, scope)` enumerates `AllIndexes(dbOid)`, filters each index's parent table through the identical relation predicate, and emits the 9-column upstream row (`relid/indexrelid/schemaname/relname/indexrelname/idx_scan/last_idx_scan/idx_tup_read/idx_tup_fetch`) with the five identity cells real and the three scan counters `0`/`last_idx_scan` NULL; `executor.fetchStatIndexesRows` is the per-connection twin, wired at `valuesOp.Open`'s three new `pg_stat_*_indexes` branches. Tests: `internal/catalog/pgstat_indexes_test.go` + `internal/executor/pgstat_indexes_e2e_test.go`. Same `PgStat_StatIndEntry` counter gap deferred. **I/O sibling (2026-07-12):** the buffer-pool I/O views `pg_statio_all_tables` / `pg_statio_{user,sys}_tables` (11 cols) and `pg_statio_all_indexes` / `pg_statio_{user,sys}_indexes` (7 cols) land the same way — `catalog.PGStatioTablesRowsForDBOid` / `PGStatioIndexesRowsForDBOid` reuse the identical relation filter + `StatTableScope` split and emit real identity cells with every heap/idx/toast/tidx block counter a faithful `0` (goopg has no per-relation buffer-pool attribution — the `pg_stat_io` counters are pool-wide); `executor.fetchStatioTablesRows` / `fetchStatioIndexesRows` are the per-connection twins, wired at `valuesOp.Open`'s six new `pg_statio_*` branches (OIDs 9087–9092). Tests: `internal/catalog/pgstatio_test.go` + `internal/executor/pgstatio_e2e_test.go`. **Sequence sibling (2026-07-12):** the `pg_statio_all_sequences` / `pg_statio_{user,sys}_sequences` trio (5 cols `relid/schemaname/relname/blks_read/blks_hit`) completes the `pg_statio_*` family — `catalog.PGStatioSequencesRowsForDBOid` is the only `pg_statio_*` builder whose filter *selects* sequences (`t.IsSequence`, relkind `'S'`) rather than skipping them, same `StatTableScope` split, block counters a faithful `0`; `executor.fetchStatioSequencesRows` is the per-connection twin wired at `valuesOp.Open`'s three new `pg_statio_*_sequences` branches (OIDs 9093–9095). Per-relation block attribution remains deferred (ledger). **Function sibling (2026-07-12):** the two function-statistics views `pg_stat_user_functions` / `pg_stat_xact_user_functions` (6 cols `funcid/schemaname/funcname/calls/total_time/self_time`, OIDs 9096–9097) are the last per-object views in the family — upstream filters on `pg_stat_get_function_calls(oid) IS NOT NULL`, never true under the default `track_functions = none`, so both views are empty on a stock cluster out of the box; goopg has no per-function call/time tracking, so `catalog.PGStatUserFunctionsRows()` returns no rows unconditionally and the views are registered purely so a client gets `0` rows instead of an unknown-relation error (always-empty ⇒ no per-connection twin needed). Tests: `internal/catalog/pgstat_functions_test.go` + `internal/executor/pgstat_functions_e2e_test.go`. A cumulative per-function statistics subsystem (`PgStat_StatFuncEntry` analog) remains deferred (ledger). **Transaction sibling (2026-07-12):** the per-transaction table views `pg_stat_xact_all_tables` / `pg_stat_xact_{user,sys}_tables` (12 cols `relid/schemaname/relname/seq_scan/seq_tup_read/idx_scan/idx_tup_fetch/n_tup_ins/n_tup_upd/n_tup_del/n_tup_hot_upd/n_tup_newpage_upd`, OIDs 9098–9100) are the transaction-scoped counterpart of the cumulative `pg_stat_*_tables` views — same relation filter + `StatTableScope` split, but a narrower shape carrying only the nine `pg_stat_get_xact_*` delta counters (no `n_live_tup`/`last_*`/`vacuum_count`). goopg has no per-transaction pgstat accumulator (`PgStat_TableXactStatus` analog), so every delta counter is a faithful `0`; `catalog.PGStatXactTablesRowsForDBOid` + `executor.fetchStatXactTablesRows` (per-connection twin, three new `pg_stat_xact_*_tables` branches at `valuesOp.Open`). Tests: `internal/catalog/pgstat_xact_tables_test.go` + `internal/executor/pgstat_xact_tables_e2e_test.go`. Per-transaction accumulator deferred (ledger). **Global cluster views (2026-07-12):** the two remaining unregistered stat views are *global* single-row cluster summaries, so they follow the `pg_stat_wal` precedent (static `VirtualRows` with honest zeros/NULLs, no per-connection twin): `pg_stat_bgwriter` (PG 17+ 4-col `buffers_clean/maxwritten_clean/buffers_alloc/stats_reset`, OID 3406 — goopg's bgwriter runs but has no counter accumulator wired to these columns, so all `0`) and `pg_stat_archiver` (7-col `archived_count/last_archived_wal/last_archived_time/failed_count/last_failed_wal/last_failed_time/stats_reset`, OID 3407 — goopg has no WAL archiver, so counts `0` and both `last_*` cells NULL via `VirtualNull`, matching `archive_mode=off`). Both registered in `registerSystemTables` right after `pg_stat_wal`. Tests: `internal/catalog/pgstat_global_test.go` + `internal/executor/pgstat_global_e2e_test.go`. Live bgwriter/archiver counter subsystems deferred (ledger). **`pg_stat_database` (2026-07-12):** the headline per-database cluster view (30 cols) is *global* — it lists every database plus a leading shared-objects row (`datid=0`, `datname=NULL`), independent of the connected database, so like `pg_stat_bgwriter` it needs no per-connection twin; `catalog.PGStatDatabaseRows` enumerates the live registry (`c.ListDatabases`) at query time (`CREATE`/`DROP DATABASE` reflected immediately), OID 9101. Every counter is a faithful `0`, `numbackends` honest `0`, and `checksum_last_failure`/`stats_reset` NULL — matching a fresh real PG 18.3 cluster (verified). `datid` uses a new shared `catalog.databaseDisplayOID(name)` helper that `pg_database.VirtualRows` now also routes through, so the two views' oids join byte-for-byte (resolving the old "keep this switch in sync" comment on `ResolveDatabaseOid`). Tests: `TestPGStatDatabaseViewRegistered` + `TestPgStatDatabaseEndToEnd`. `PgStat_StatDBEntry` accumulator deferred (ledger). **`pg_stat_database_conflicts` (2026-07-12):** the per-database recovery-conflict view (8 cols `datid/datname/confl_tablespace/confl_lock/confl_snapshot/confl_bufferpin/confl_deadlock/confl_active_logicalslot`, OID 9102) is *global* like `pg_stat_database` — one row per database via `catalog.PGStatDatabaseConflictsRows` (`c.ListDatabases`, live) — but UNLIKE it has NO leading shared (`datid=0`) row (upstream is a bare `FROM pg_database D`). Every `confl_*` counter is a faithful `0`: these only ever bump on a *standby* via `pgstat_report_recovery_conflict`, and goopg is a primary with no recovery-conflict accumulator, so all six read `0` exactly like a real PG 18.3 primary (verified byte-identical). `datid` reuses the shared `catalog.databaseDisplayOID` helper. Tests: `TestPGStatDatabaseConflictsViewRegistered` + `TestPgStatDatabaseConflictsEndToEnd`. Live recovery-conflict accumulator deferred (ledger). **`pg_stat_progress_*` (2026-07-12):** the six command-progress views `pg_stat_progress_vacuum`/`analyze`/`cluster`/`create_index`/`basebackup`/`copy` (OIDs 9103–9108) land as static ZERO-row virtual views via a local `mkProgressView(name, oid, cols)` helper in `registerSystemTables`, right after `pg_stat_database_conflicts`. Upstream each is a projection over `pg_stat_get_progress_info('<CMD>')` returning one row per backend with an active progress-report slot (`pgstat_progress_start_command`); goopg has no command-progress instrumentation, so every view is empty — byte-identical to an *idle* real PG 18.3 cluster with no such command in flight. Column names/types transcribed verbatim from `system_views.sql` (CASE-mapped `phase`/`command`/`type` text, `paramN` counters int8, `pid` int4, `delay_time` float8, `*id` oid); no per-connection twin. Tests: `TestPGStatProgressViewsRegistered` + `TestPgStatProgressViewsEndToEnd`. Live per-backend progress feed deferred (ledger). **`pg_stat_ssl` / `pg_stat_gssapi` (2026-07-12):** the two per-client-backend auth-transport views — unlike every stat view above these are *per-backend*, so they belong with `pg_stat_activity` in `internal/initdb/` and are backed by the SAME `activity.Registry`. Upstream both project `pg_stat_get_activity(NULL)` filtered `WHERE client_port IS NOT NULL` (real client backends, not background workers): `pg_stat_ssl(pid,ssl,version,cipher,bits,client_dn,client_serial,issuer_dn)` and `pg_stat_gssapi(pid,gss_authenticated,principal,encrypted,credentials_delegated)`. goopg has neither TLS nor GSSAPI, so the `ssl`/`gss_authenticated`/`encrypted`/`credentials_delegated` flags are a faithful `false` and every detail column NULL — byte-identical to a real PG 18.3 cluster with `ssl=off` built without GSSAPI. `registerPgStatSslView`/`registerPgStatGssapiView` (`internal/initdb/pg_stat_ssl_gssapi_view.go`) walk `reg.Snapshot()`, skip backends whose `ClientPort==""` (the `client_port IS NOT NULL` filter), emit one row each; wired in `initdb.Open` after `registerPgStatActivityView`, no per-connection twin (the registry snapshot is already global). Column types from `pg_stat_get_activity`'s `proallargtypes` (`bits` int4, `client_serial` numeric, flags bool). Tests: `TestPgStatSslView`/`TestPgStatGssapiView` (`internal/initdb/pg_stat_ssl_gssapi_view_test.go`) — exact shape, empty-registry 0-row, client_port filter, all-false/NULL rendering; verified end-to-end against a throwaway goopg server this loop. **`pg_stat_subscription_stats` (2026-07-12) — completes the `pg_stat_*` family:** the per-subscription error/conflict-counter view (12 cols `subid/subname/apply_error_count/sync_error_count/confl_insert_exists/confl_update_origin_differs/confl_update_exists/confl_update_missing/confl_delete_origin_differs/confl_delete_missing/confl_multiple_unique_conflicts/stats_reset`) is driven by the *subscription catalog* not the apply-worker registry — upstream joins `pg_subscription s` with `pg_stat_get_subscription_stats(s.oid)`, so it emits one row per subscription (a subscription with no live worker still appears), unlike the sibling `pg_stat_subscription` (per worker). It therefore lives in `internal/initdb/replication_views.go` next to `registerStatSubscriptionView` and is backed by the same `*catalog.PubSub` registry (`registerStatSubscriptionStatsView`, wired in `initdb.Open` after `registerSubscriptionViews`). goopg has no cumulative-stats accumulator for apply/sync errors or the seven per-conflict-type counters (PG's `PgStat_StatSubEntry`, populated by `pgstat_report_subscription_error`/`pgstat_report_subscription_conflict`), so every counter is a faithful `0` and `stats_reset` is NULL — byte-identical to a real PG 18.3 subscription that has applied cleanly and never been reset. Column types transcribed from `pg_stat_get_subscription_stats`' `proallargtypes` (`subid` oid, counters int8, `stats_reset` timestamptz; `subname` name). Test: `TestStatSubscriptionStatsRendersPerSubscription` (`internal/initdb/replication_views_test.go`) — empty-registry 0-row, per-subscription row shape, all-zero counters, NULL stats_reset; verified end-to-end against a throwaway goopg server this loop (correct 12-column shape/order). `PgStat_StatSubEntry` accumulator deferred (ledger). **`pg_stats` (2026-07-12):** the human-readable per-column planner-statistics view — unlike every `pg_stat_*` runtime-counter view above, this projects the `pg_statistic` catalog (populated by `ANALYZE`) not a live counter subsystem, one row per analyzed non-dropped column (17 cols `schemaname/tablename/attname/inherited/null_frac/avg_width/n_distinct/most_common_vals/most_common_freqs/histogram_bounds/correlation/most_common_elems/most_common_elem_freqs/elem_count_histogram/range_length_histogram/range_empty_frac/range_bounds_histogram`, OID 9160). goopg has no SQL evaluation over the `pg_statistic` heap in the virtual path, so `catalog.PGStatsRowsForDBOid(dbOid)` (`internal/catalog/pgstats.go`) reproduces the projection directly from the same in-memory `Table.Stats.Columns` (`ColumnStats`) that `buildUserPGStatisticRow` writes to the `pg_statistic` heap — the two are **sibling consumers of `ColumnStats` and must agree** (same MCV/histogram order, same `SET STATISTICS 0` skip). Per-database like `pg_stat_all_tables`: `executor.fetchStatsRows` swaps in the `ctx.CurrentDatabaseOid`-scoped twin at `valuesOp.Open`; static `VirtualRows` scopes to `DefaultDBOid`. The array columns (`most_common_vals`/`histogram_bounds` `anyarray`, `most_common_freqs` `float4[]`) are emitted as PG array text literals via `ArrayTextLiteral`, routed verbatim by `TypedVirtualCell`. goopg's `ANALYZE` collects only MCV (kind 1) + histogram (kind 2), so `correlation`/element/range columns (kinds 3–6) are always NULL — matching a real PG 18.3 cluster whose `ANALYZE` computed no such slots. Tests: `internal/catalog/pgstats_test.go` + `internal/executor/pgstats_e2e_test.go`. Simplifications (ledger): text-rendered `stavalues`, placeholder `avg_width`, no `has_column_privilege` filter. |
| 0122-0004 | [GROUP BY GROUPING SETS / ROLLUP / CUBE](0122-0004-grouping-sets-rollup-cube.md) | accepted | Previously the parser discarded `ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`GROUPING SETS` into a plain `GROUP BY` over the listed columns (an `IntegerConst(0)` sentinel silently skipped in `buildAggregateStage`) — no subtotal/grand-total rows were ever produced. Now implements SQL:1999 §7.9's literal definition: the parser expands the clause into `SelectStmt.GroupingSets *GroupingSetsSpec`, a fully materialized `[][]Expr` set list (ROLLUP's n+1 prefixes, CUBE's 2^n subsets, an explicit GROUPING SETS list verbatim, cross-multiplied against any plain columns in the same clause); the planner's `rewriteGroupingSets` (hooked into `planSelect` before anything else runs) expands this into a synthetic `UNION ALL` chain of plain-GROUP-BY branches, reusing the pre-existing N-ary set-op planning machinery (segment flattening, per-branch casts, `wrapSetOpSortLimit`) completely unmodified. `substituteGroupingExpr` NULLs out excluded-dimension references per branch and resolves the new `GROUPING(...)` pseudo-function (`*parser.GroupingCall` AST node, analyzer-typed `int4`) to a literal bitmask, since its value depends only on which branch produced the row. No executor change was needed. Deferred: the substitution walker doesn't cover every `parser.Expr` variant (`InExpr`/`ExistsExpr`/array exprs) or window-function `PARTITION BY`/`ORDER BY` — see the doc's Deferred section and the 2026-07-05 ledger row. |
| 0122-0004 | [Zero-column result sets over the extended query protocol](0122-0004-extended-zero-column-rows.md) | accepted | Closes `unimplemented_feat.json` "goopg does not emit a blank data row for 0-column SELECT results". PostgreSQL treats a zero-column read (`SELECT FROM t`, `SELECT;`) as a real result set — one zero-column `DataRow` per source row, and `Describe` replies with a `RowDescription` of **0 fields**, not `NoData`. The simple-query path (`dispatch.go`) already handled this via `schema != nil` guards; the extended path (`dispatch_extended.go` + `extended.go`) diverged (a sibling-path bug like `0119-0004-extended-protocol-type-format-parity`), gating `res.Fields`/`res.Rows` and the Describe RowDescription-vs-NoData choice on `len(schema) > 0`/`== 0` — so a zero-column read via Parse/Bind/Execute dropped every row (`SELECT 0`) and Describe returned NoData. Fix: use the same nil/non-nil discriminator at all four sites (nil ⇒ write/DDL/txn ⇒ NoData; non-nil zero-length ⇒ zero-column result set). Verified vs PG 18.3 (`\bind \g`). Tests: `internal/server/extended_zero_column_test.go` (`TestExtendedZeroColumnSelectEmitsRows`, `TestExtendedZeroColumnSelectWithFilter`); non-vacuousness confirmed by reverting the row-emission guard. No PG behavior left unimplemented → no ledger row. |
| 0122-0004 | [RANGE window frame mode (non-offset bounds)](0122-0004-range-window-frame.md) | accepted | `RANGE` was the last unimplemented window frame mode — the analyzer rejected any `RANGE` clause with `0A000`, so even the default frame (`RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`) could never be spelled explicitly. `RANGE` differs from `ROWS`/`GROUPS` only for *value offset* bounds (`RANGE BETWEEN n PRECEDING`), which need a type-aware `+`/`-`/`<` operator lookup on the single ORDER BY column (deferred, ledger row). The **non-offset** bounds (`UNBOUNDED`, `CURRENT ROW`) need no value arithmetic: in `RANGE` mode `CURRENT ROW` means "the current row and ALL its ORDER BY peers", exactly the peer-group semantics `GROUPS` and the default frame already compute. Change: analyzer `validateWindowFrame` accepts non-offset `RANGE` (still rejects RANGE+offset with `0A000`; unlike GROUPS, non-offset RANGE needs no ORDER BY); executor `frameBounds` dispatches `FrameModeRange` to the existing `frameBoundsGroups`, and the two group-bounds gates (`needsValueGroupBounds`, `evalExplicitFrameAggFuncs`) were extended to precompute `peerGroupBounds` for RANGE — no new arithmetic. Every expectation cross-checked against a real PostgreSQL 18.3 instance. Tests: `TestAnalyzeWindowFrameRangeOffsetRejected`/`TestAnalyzeWindowFrameRangeNonOffsetAccepted` (analyzer), `TestCompatWindowExplicitRangePeers`/`TestCompatWindowRangeUnboundedPrecedingCumulative` (executor). RANGE-with-offset is now the only open window-frame item. |
| 0122-0004 | [RANGE value-offset window frame bounds](0122-0004-range-offset-window-frame.md) | implemented | Closes the last window-frame gap: `RANGE BETWEEN n PRECEDING AND m FOLLOWING`, where a row is in-frame when its ORDER BY value is within `current±offset` (PostgreSQL's `in_range`). Analyzer `validateWindowFrame` now requires exactly one ORDER BY column for a RANGE value offset (`42P20`, mirroring `parse_clause.c`'s `transformFrameOffset`) instead of rejecting with `0A000`. Executor: `frameBounds` gains a RANGE-value-offset branch delegating to new `frameBoundsRange`, which scans the (already sorted) partition for frame head/tail exactly like `nodeWindowAgg.c`'s `update_frameheadpos`/`update_frametailpos` — including the NULL branches (a non-null current row never frames a null row; a null current row frames its null peer block). The boundary `current±offset` reuses the existing tested `evalBinary` (numeric/interval/date arithmetic = the `in_range` type coverage) and the comparison reuses `compareDatum`; `frameBounds` and its four call sites now thread an `error`. Offsets keep their native type via `resolveRangeOffset` (null → `22004`, negative → `22013`). All three frame modes (ROWS/RANGE/GROUPS) + exclusion are now complete. Every expectation cross-checked byte-for-byte vs live PostgreSQL 18.3. Tests: `TestAnalyzeWindowFrameRangeOffsetOrderByCount` (analyzer); `TestCompatWindowRangeValueOffset`/`…PeersAndFrameFuncs`/`…Nulls`, `TestWindowRangeOffsetNegative` (executor). Deferred (ledger): no per-type `in_range` catalog (unsupported type surfaces as `0A000` lazily at execution, not parse time). Follow-up (2026-07-12): interval-offset negativity now matches PG's `interval_sign` (linear-span) test exactly instead of a per-component heuristic — `INTERVAL '1 mon -10 days'` (+20-day span) is correctly accepted (`TestRangeOffsetNegativeIntervalSign`). |
