| 0122-0006 | [Index column order (ASC/DESC/NULLS) restart persistence](0122-0006-index-column-order-restart-persistence.md) | accepted | Three independent gaps meant a `CREATE INDEX ... (col DESC, col2 NULLS FIRST)`'s ordering never survived past the creating session: the live `pg_index` virtual builder and the heap-persisted shadow row's `indoption` column were both hardcoded to all-zero (`internal/catalog/catalog.go`, `internal/executor/pg18_user_catalog_rows.go` — fixed by computing the real `INDOPTION_DESC`/`INDOPTION_NULLS_FIRST` bitmask from `catalog.Index.ColDescending`/`ColNullsFirst`; `catalog.DecodePGIndexPhysicalRow` gained the ability to decode it back, walking past `indcollation`/`indclass`'s varlena columns), and — the actual crash-durability bug, only reproducible via a genuine uncheckpointed `SIGKILL`, not a graceful `Runtime.Close()` — `createBTreeIndex`'s CREATE INDEX WAL record was emitted before `execCreateIndex`'s separate post-call block set `idx.ColDescending`/`ColNullsFirst`, so a true crash restart's `wal.CreateIndexPayload` replay always defaulted to ascending/NULLS-LAST regardless of the declared ordering, even though the heap row (resynced afterward by the pre-existing `resyncIndexHeapRow`) was correct. Fixed by moving the ordering computation before the `createBTreeIndex` call and threading it in as new parameters, set on the index immediately after creation and before WAL emission. `wal.CreateIndexPayload`'s new `ColDescending`/`ColNullsFirst` fields are encoded as two trailing append-only blocks (not interleaved with column data) so pre-existing on-disk WAL history — discovered when the naive interleaved-bytes version broke `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` against `bench/tpch/runtime_goopg/data`'s WAL — still decodes. Tests: `TestBuildUserPGIndexRowIndoptionRoundTrip` (executor), `TestEncodeCreateIndexRoundTrip`/`TestDecodeCreateIndexBackwardCompatNoOrderBlocks` (wal), `TestCreateIndexColumnOrderingSurvivesRestartViaWAL` (initdb, using the true-crash flush-WAL-then-drop-buffers pattern, not a graceful `Close()`, since that masks the WAL-only bug via its own shutdown checkpoint). Live-verified against the real `cmd/goopg` binary with an actual `kill -9`. **Deferred (ledger row):** `wal.CreateIndexPayload` still doesn't carry predicate/INCLUDE columns/opclass/collation/fillfactor/dedup — those revert to defaults on the same kind of uncheckpointed crash, a wider pre-existing gap this task's investigation surfaced but did not fix (out of scope; see the doc's Non-goals). **2026-07-08 follow-up: this deferred gap is now fixed.** `wal.CreateIndexPayload` gained `HasPredicate`/`PredicateString`/`IncludeColumns`/`ColOpClasses`/`ColCollations`/`Fillfactor`/`DeduplicateItems`/`NullsNotDistinct`, encoded as a new optional, self-describing trailing "extension" block (omitted entirely for a plain index, so pre-existing WAL/tests are byte-identical/unaffected) appended after the ColDescending/ColNullsFirst blocks; `createBTreeIndex` gained an optional `btreeIndexProps` struct parameter (replacing the old bare `predExpr` variadic) set on the index before WAL emission, exactly mirroring the ColDescending/ColNullsFirst fix; `RegisterIndexDuringRecovery` gained the same fields. Only the two call sites that actually declare these properties (`execCreateIndex`'s direct statement path, `createPartitionChildIndexes`) needed updating. Tests: `TestEncodeCreateIndexExtensionRoundTrip`/`TestEncodeCreateIndexOmitsExtensionBlockWhenDefault`/`TestDecodeCreateIndexBackwardCompatOrderBlocksOnlyNoExtension`/`TestDecodeCreateIndexRejectsTruncatedExtension` (wal), `TestCreateIndexExtendedPropertiesSurviveRestartViaWAL` (initdb, same true-crash pattern, confirmed non-vacuous). Live-verified against the real `cmd/goopg` binary with an actual `kill -9`: `pg_get_indexdef`/`pg_index` correct post-restart for a `WHERE`/`INCLUDE`/opclass/collation/fillfactor/dedup/`NULLS NOT DISTINCT` index. **Still deferred (as of the first follow-up):** the heap-recovery driver (`loadUserIndexesFromHeap`) still can't restore these fields after a *checkpointed* restart — `pg_index`'s `indclass`/`indcollation`/`indexprs`/`indpred` heap content is never decoded, and there's no `indnullsnotdistinct` heap field either — a separate, pre-existing residual only a genuine uncheckpointed crash (this follow-up's WAL path) avoids. **2026-07-08 follow-up 2: 3 of those 5 fields now fixed for checkpointed restarts too.** `buildUserPGIndexRow` now writes real `indnatts`/`indnkeyatts` (INCLUDE columns are appended to `indkey` instead of being silently dropped) and writes `indpred` as the predicate's SQL text when `HasPredicate` (`indexprs` stays NULL — goopg has no expression-index support, so nothing can ever populate it). `catalog.PGIndexRow`/`DecodePGIndexPhysicalRow` gained `IndNKeyAtts`/`IndNullsNotDistinct`/`IndHasPred`/`IndPred`; `indpred`'s NULL-vs-present state is inferred from data length alone (safe because `indexprs`, the column before it, is proven always NULL, and goopg's physical tuple encoder writes zero bytes for NULL columns) via a new `decodePGIndexVarlenaText` helper. `loadUserIndexesFromHeap` splits the decoded `indkey` at `indnkeyatts` into key columns vs `IncludeColumns` and threads `HasPredicate`/`PredicateString`/`NullsNotDistinct` through to `RegisterIndexDuringRecovery`. Test: `TestCreateIndexPredicateAndIncludeColumnsSurviveCheckpointedRestart` (initdb, graceful `Close()`, confirmed non-vacuous via `git stash`). Live-verified against the real `cmd/goopg` binary with a graceful `stop`/`start`. **2026-07-08 follow-up 3: the opclass/collation registry is built and both write-side renderers fixed.** `internal/catalog/catalog.go` gained `builtinColumnOpclassOIDs` (oracle-verified against a real PostgreSQL 18.3 instance's `pg_opclass`), `defaultColumnOpclassNameForType`, and exported `*InMemory` methods `ResolveIndexColumnOpclassOID`/`ResolveIndexColumnCollationOID` (added to the `catalog.Catalog` interface) that check user-created classes/collations before the builtin tables. Both the live `pg_index` `VirtualRows` builder and `buildUserPGIndexRow` (the heap-row writer) now call these same two methods instead of each having independently-wrong logic. Test: `TestPgIndexIndclassIndcollation` (catalog). Live-verified against the real `cmd/goopg` binary via `psql`: explicit `text_pattern_ops`/`varchar_pattern_ops COLLATE "C"` and the plain-`int4` default case all match a real PostgreSQL 18.3 oracle. **2026-07-08 follow-up 4: the heap-row READ/decode side is now fixed too.** `DecodePGIndexPhysicalRow` now decodes `indclass`/`indcollation` (new `decodePGIndexOIDVector` helper); `catalog.go` gained the reverse-lookup siblings `ResolveIndexColumnOpclassName`/`ResolveIndexColumnCollationName` (added to `catalog.Catalog`), and `loadUserIndexesFromHeap` now threads the resolved `ColOpClasses`/`ColCollations` name strings through to `RegisterIndexDuringRecovery` instead of always passing `nil, nil`. Test: `TestCreateIndexOpclassAndCollationSurviveCheckpointedRestart` (initdb, graceful `Close()`, confirmed non-vacuous via `git stash`). **The M0122-0006 index-restart-persistence cluster now has no known open residual** (column ordering, predicate/INCLUDE/nulls-not-distinct, opclass/collation — both the WAL-crash and checkpointed-restart recovery paths). |
| 0122-0007 | [REINDEX physical rebuild (plain REINDEX INDEX / TABLE / SCHEMA)](0122-0007-reindex-physical-rebuild.md) | accepted (partial) | Plain (non-`CONCURRENTLY`) `REINDEX INDEX`/`REINDEX TABLE` physically rebuild their btree index(es) from a fresh heap scan instead of the pre-existing unconditional no-op — `reindexOp.rebuildIndex`/`rebuildTableIndexes` reuse CREATE INDEX's own bulk-build path (`ddlOp.bulkBuildBTree`/`bulkBuildBTreeWithPredicate`, whose underlying `btree.BulkCreateWithOptions` already truncates + repacks the target relation). Non-btree access methods (gist/spgist/gin/brin) are catalog-only in goopg (same as CREATE INDEX) so they're a no-op. New `reindexOp.acquireReindexLocks` genuinely HOLDS — not the file's pre-existing wait-then-release pattern — a `ShareLock` on the parent table plus an `AccessExclusiveLock` on the index for the rebuild's duration, mirroring `reindex.sgml`'s real locking. Tests: `TestReindexIndexPhysicallyRebuilds`/`TestReindexTablePhysicallyRebuildsAllIndexes` (direct `btree.RangeScan` proof after deliberately truncating the index's storage) and `TestReindexIndexBlocksBehindConcurrentIndexReader` (a concurrent `AccessShareLock` holder blocks REINDEX until it releases), all confirmed non-vacuous via `git stash`. Live-verified against the real `cmd/goopg` binary: zero-byte-truncated a live index's on-disk relfilenode, confirmed the query then failed (`short read at block`), ran `REINDEX INDEX`, confirmed the query and its Index Scan plan both recovered. Gates: `go build ./...`/`go vet ./internal/executor/...` clean; `go test ./internal/executor/... ./internal/access/btree/... ./internal/catalog/... ./internal/planner/...` PASS; `go test ./internal/testport/... -run 'TestPort_IsolationReindex\|TestPort_IsolationMultipleCic'` PASS (no regression); `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` PASS (Q12=2/Q13=33); `RALPH_PRECOMMIT_SCOPE=smoke scripts/ralph-precommit-test.sh` PASS (0 failed, all 3 workloads). **2026-07-09 follow-up: `REINDEX SCHEMA` (non-`CONCURRENTLY`) now physically rebuilds too**, calling the same `rebuildTableIndexes` per table instead of only reproducing the schema-wide lock/wait timing; `schemaTableNamesByOID` (renamed from `schemaRelsByOID`) returns qualified names re-resolved via `LookupTable` immediately before each use (not `Table`/`RelFileNode` captured once up front), so a table concurrently dropped while REINDEX SCHEMA still waits on an earlier table's lock is detected and silently skipped, matching `reindex-schema.spec`'s tolerate-concurrent-drop expectation. Test: `TestReindexSchemaPhysicallyRebuildsAllTables` (two tables, each with a truncated btree index, confirmed non-vacuous). `go test ./internal/testport/... -run TestPort_IsolationReindexSchema` re-confirmed PASS after the change (concurrent-drop-tolerance behavior unaffected). **2026-07-09 follow-up 2: every `CONCURRENTLY` form (INDEX/TABLE/SCHEMA) now physically rebuilds too**, via a shadow-file build-then-swap: `buildIndexShadow` builds the replacement btree into a fresh, catalog-invisible `RelFileNode` (`Catalog.AllocOID()`-minted, never registered) while the LIVE index keeps serving every reader/writer; the pre-existing `waitForRelationLockers` call is unchanged in position/semantics (so `reindex-concurrently.spec`'s interleaving timing holds); `swapRelationPhysicalFile` then atomically `os.Rename`s the flushed shadow file over the live index's file under a brief `acquireReindexLocks` hold (the same lock plain REINDEX holds for its *entire* rebuild, here only for the swap) — the index's OID/RelFileNode never changes, so no catalog mutation or WAL record is needed for durability. `REINDEX DATABASE`/`SYSTEM` and the synthetic `pg_toast.*` form are still catalog-only no-ops. Deliberately not implemented (same simplification `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` already makes): no second validation scan, so a write racing the shadow build's heap scan may not appear in the rebuilt index. Tests: `TestReindexIndexConcurrentlyPhysicallyRebuilds`, `TestReindexTableConcurrentlyPhysicallyRebuildsAllIndexes`, `TestReindexIndexConcurrentlyDoesNotBlockConcurrentIndexReader`. Live-verified against the real `cmd/goopg` binary: zero-byte-truncated a live PK index's file, confirmed `short read at block`, ran `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, confirmed the same relfilenode, a working query, and survival across a restart with no orphaned shadow file. Gates: `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./internal/executor/... ./internal/access/btree/... ./internal/catalog/... ./internal/planner/...` PASS; `go test ./internal/testport/ -run 'TestPort_IsolationReindex\|TestPort_IsolationMultipleCic'` PASS (all 4 specs, no regression); `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` PASS (Q12=2/Q13=33); `RALPH_PRECOMMIT_SCOPE=smoke scripts/ralph-precommit-test.sh` PASS (0 failed, all 3 workloads). |

Materialized views still error FeatureNotSupported (their heap-backed data needs its own clone path). New E2E `TestCreateDatabaseTemplateViewCopiesQueryAndSurvivesRestart` proves a copied view's query still resolves against the copied table after a full restart. **Follow-up 43 (2026-07-10, this loop):** extended again to materialized views — unlike plain views, a matview's pg_class row is NOT `Virtual` (real heap storage), so it already surfaces via `AllTables` with no new registry method needed; new `copyTemplateMatViews` combines `copyTemplateTables`' physical relation-file copy with `copyTemplateViews`' AST/`ViewDef`/`IsPopulated` field copy. `resolveCreateDatabaseTemplate` gained a 5th return `matViews []*catalog.Table`. | 0122-0019 | [pg_index.indexprs / indpred rendering (node-tree columns)](0122-0019-pg-index-node-tree-columns.md) | accepted | Fixes the live `pg_index` renderer `catalog.InMemory.PGIndexRowsForDBOid` (`internal/catalog/catalog.go`), which hardcoded the `pg_node_tree` columns `indexprs`/`indpred`/`indcoloptions` to `""` — a non-NULL empty string for a `text` column, not SQL NULL. This diverged from the on-disk heap-row twin `buildUserPGIndexRow` (`internal/executor/pg18_user_catalog_rows.go`, already correct) and broke two live-SQL behaviors: `indpred IS NOT NULL` (the canonical partial-index probe) matched every index, and `pg_get_expr(indpred, indrelid)` returned `''` instead of the `WHERE` predicate on a partial index (and `''` instead of NULL on a plain one). Tests: `internal/executor/pg_index_indpred_test.go` (`TestPgIndexIndpredPartialVsPlain` end-to-end through `pg_get_expr`, `TestPgIndexRowsIndprIndexprsNullSentinel` direct row-cell guard). Follow-up (2026-07-10): the live-path expression-index `indexprs` gap is now closed via shared `catalog.IndexExprsText` (joins `idx.ColExprStrings` for expression key columns, verbatim, comma-separated — byte-matched to PG 18.3: `lower(b)`, `(a + c), upper(b)`, `(a * c)`), wired into `PGIndexRowsForDBOid`; tests `internal/executor/pg_index_indexprs_test.go`. Follow-up (2026-07-12): the heap-persisted twin now populates `indexprs` too — `DecodePGIndexPhysicalRow(data, bitmap)` is null-bitmap-aware (probes bits 19/20 to disambiguate the two trailing nullable `pg_node_tree` varlenas), `buildUserPGIndexRow` emits the same `IndexExprsText` output, and the recovery caller (`internal/initdb/open.go`) passes `ht.Bitmap`; backward-compatible (legacy rows always carried a bitmap since `indexprs` was always NULL). Test `TestBuildUserPGIndexRowExprPredNullBitmapRoundTrip` covers all four NULL/non-NULL combinations. This closes unimplemented_feat #135. |
| 0122-0017 | [DROP DATABASE guard checks (M0122-0007)](0122-0017-database-ddl-drop-guards.md) | accepted (partial) | `tryHandleDatabaseDDL`'s `databaseDDLDrop` branch (M0054-0001) was a bare catalog map-delete with no guard checks at all. Added, mirroring `dbcommands.c`'s `dropdb()` order: (1) **ownership check** (2026-07-09 follow-up) — `catalog.InMemory` now tracks `pg_database.datdba` per database (`databaseOwner` map + WAL owner suffix), and DROP DATABASE rejects a non-owner/non-superuser `actingRole` with 42501 "must be owner of database %s", inserted right after the existence check per real `dropdb()`'s `object_ownercheck` ordering; (2) template rejection (`template0`/`template1`, 42809 `WrongObjectType`); (3) self-drop rejection when the target is the calling connection's own live database (55006 `ObjectInUse`, "cannot drop the currently open database"); (4) other-backends-busy rejection via the pre-existing `activity.ActivityRegistry.CountByDatName` (55006 `ObjectInUse`, "is being accessed by other users"). (5) **`WITH (FORCE)` connection termination** (2026-07-09 follow-up 2) — `dropDatabaseHasForce` detects the trailing `WITH (FORCE)`/`(FORCE)` clause; when present, `terminateOtherDBBackends` fires the same process-wide `cancelReg.terminateByPID` path a peer `pg_terminate_backend(pid)` call uses against every backend connected to the target database, then `waitForDatabaseBackendsToDrain` polls up to 5s (mirroring `CountOtherDBBackends`'s own retry loop) before the busy check runs — live-verified terminating a real busy `psql` session and completing the drop. (6) **physical-storage-isolation slice 1** (2026-07-09 follow-up 3) — `CreateDatabase` now allocates a real, distinct `pg_database.oid` from the cluster-wide OID counter (previously every non-template database rendered the SAME hardcoded `"16384"` placeholder — a correctness bug and the blocker for ever allocating a `base/<dbOid>` directory), persisted through a new WAL `oid` suffix and `DatabaseOid` getter; the live `"postgres"` row's placeholder is deliberately left unchanged (subscription/datacl compat). (7) **physical-storage-isolation slice 2** (2026-07-09 follow-up 4) — `CreateDatabase` now creates a real `base/<dbOid>/PG_VERSION` on disk (`initdb.CreatePerDatabaseScaffolding`, exported from the Init-time-only helper), created BEFORE the WAL append (crash-safety mirrors `relocateRelationPhysicalFile`) and re-created idempotently by WAL replay on every restart (`replayDatabaseDDLRecords` gained a `dataDir` param). The original plan's template-copy half is explicitly NOT implemented and re-scoped: goopg still has one shared table/index namespace for the whole process, so there is no way to enumerate "template1's relations" distinct from any other database's — that mechanism needs slice 4 (per-database catalog namespace) first, not the other way around. Slice 4 (per-connection catalog routing) remains untouched. Tests: `TestTryHandleDatabaseDDLCreateCreatesPhysicalDirectory`, `TestTryHandleDatabaseDDLCreateNoPoolIsNoop` (`internal/server/database_ddl_test.go`), `TestDatabaseDDLRecoveryRecreatesMissingDatabaseDirectory` + an assertion added to `TestDatabaseDDLRecoveryReplaysCreate` (`internal/initdb/database_ddl_recovery_test.go`). Live-verified against a real `cmd/goopg` binary: directory created matching the live `pg_database.oid`, survived a restart, and was recreated by WAL replay after being manually deleted. (8) **physical-storage-isolation slice 3** (2026-07-09 follow-up 5) — `DROP DATABASE` now removes `base/<dbOid>` (new `initdb.RemovePerDatabaseScaffolding`, the create-side's symmetric counterpart) once the drop is durable (after `WAL.Append` succeeds, or immediately if no WAL configured); the oid is captured via `DatabaseOid(name)` before `DropDatabase` erases the name→oid mapping. WAL replay of `RecordKindDropDatabase` now removes the directory too, looking the oid up from the still-live registry immediately before `UnregisterDatabaseDuringRecovery`. `base/<dbOid>` is no longer permanently orphaned after a drop. Tests: `TestTryHandleDatabaseDDLDropRemovesPhysicalDirectory` (`internal/server/database_ddl_test.go`), an assertion added to `TestDatabaseDDLRecoveryReplaysDropAfterCreate` (`internal/initdb/database_ddl_recovery_test.go`). Live-verified: `CREATE`/`DROP DATABASE` removed `base/<oid>` immediately, and it stayed gone across a real server restart. Tests: `TestTryHandleDatabaseDDLDropGuards`, `TestTryHandleDatabaseDDLDropRequiresOwnership`, `TestTryHandleDatabaseDDLDropForceTerminatesOtherBackends`, `TestDropDatabaseHasForce` (`internal/server/database_ddl_test.go`), `TestDecodeCreateDatabaseDefaultsOwnerForPreM01220007Payload`, `TestDecodeCreateDatabaseDefaultsOidForPreSlice1Payload` (`internal/wal/database_ddl_test.go`), `TestCreateDatabaseAllocatesDistinctDisplayedOid`, `TestRegisterDatabaseDuringRecoveryAdvancesNextOID` (`internal/catalog/database_test.go`). | 0122-0009 | [`pg_subtrans` truncation](0122-0009-pg-subtrans-truncation.md) | accepted | `SubxactMap`'s in-memory `parents`/`aborted` maps and its on-disk `SubtransSLRU` mirror (`pg_subtrans/` segment files) grew without bound — no removal primitive existed on either store, the M0117-0003 follow-up gap. | 0119-0004db | [Object-privilege ACL grantor tracking (`pg_class.relacl` and siblings)](0119-0004-table-acl-grantor-tracking.md) | accepted | Every rendered aclitem's trailing grantor component was hardcoded to the object owner ("postgres"), regardless of who actually ran the `GRANT` — a real, reachable divergence via a `WITH GRANT OPTION` delegation chain (`SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION bob; GRANT ... TO charlie` → real PG's `charlie=r/bob`, not `/postgres`), which `pg_dump`'s `buildACLCommands` wraps in `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION`/`RESET` once the grantor differs from the owner. New `catalog.InMemory.tableACLGrantor` + `GrantTablePrivilegeAs` record the true grantor per grantee (shared by `pg_class.relacl`/`pg_namespace.nspacl`/`pg_proc.proacl`/`pg_type.typacl`/`pg_database.datacl`/`pg_parameter_acl`/`srvacl`/`fdwacl` via the common `relaclTextLockedFor` renderer); `internal/server/grant_ddl.go`'s `tryRecordTableGrant` stamps the session's current effective role (`connTx.NonSuperuserRole`) as grantor and now validates the previously-discarded `GRANTED BY <role>` clause against it, raising `0A000`/"grantor must be current user" on a mismatch — matching real PG's `aclchk.c ExecuteGrantStmt` exactly (verified live: the clause is real grammar but restricted to naming the current user only). Live-verified end-to-end with the real, unmodified PostgreSQL 18.3 `psql`/`pg_dump` binaries: no goopg-side dump-rendering change was needed at all, since `pg_dump` reconstructs the `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION` wrap client-side from the raw `relacl` string. Tests: `TestRelaclTextGrantor` (catalog), `TestTryRecordTableGrantStampsActingRoleAsGrantor`/`GrantedByCurrentUserIsNoop`/`GrantedByOtherRoleErrors` (server). **2026-07-06 follow-up:** column-level `pg_attribute.attacl` grantor tracking landed too — new `attrACLGrantor`/`GrantColumnPrivilegeAs` mirror the table-level mechanism onto the separate `attrACLs` store, and `internal/executor/operators_ddl.go`'s `execAttrACLChange` (the column-GRANT applier, a different call site from `grant_ddl.go`'s string recorder) now stamps `o.ctx.NonSuperuserRole` as grantor. Test: `TestAttrACLTextGrantor` (catalog). Deferred (ledger row): column-level `GRANT ... GRANTED BY` is parsed-and-discarded (not validated, unlike the object-privilege path), `TYPE`/`DATABASE`/`PARAMETER` ACL grantor stamping (executor-routed, separate call sites), and full grant-option delegation-chain resolution (`select_best_grantor`). **2026-07-06 (later) follow-up:** `TYPE`/`DATABASE`/`PARAMETER` ACL grantor stamping landed too — `execTypeACLChange`/`execDatabaseACLChange`/`execParameterACLChange` (`internal/executor/operators_ddl.go`, `operators_ddl_database_acl.go`, `operators_ddl_parameter_acl.go`) now call `GrantTablePrivilegeAs(..., o.ctx.NonSuperuserRole)` instead of the grantor-blind `GrantTablePrivilegeWithGrantOption` wrapper — no new store was needed since `typacl`/`datacl`/`paracl` already share `tableACLs`/`tableACLGrantor` with `relacl`. Tests: `TestExecTypeACLChangeStampsActingRoleAsGrantor`/`TestExecDatabaseACLChangeStampsActingRoleAsGrantor`/`TestExecParameterACLChangeStampsActingRoleAsGrantor`. **2026-07-06 (loop #45) follow-up:** `GRANTED BY` validation for these three statement kinds landed too — `parser.TypeACLChange`/`DatabaseACLChange`/`ParameterACLChange` now carry a `GrantedBy` field (captured by a new shared `scanGrantTrailingClause` helper, `internal/parser/parser.go`, which also fixed a latent bug where `GRANTED BY` following `WITH GRANT OPTION` was never reached), validated by a new `checkGrantedByCurrentUser` (`internal/executor/operators_ddl.go`, a duplicate of `grant_ddl.go`'s check since executor cannot import server) called first by all three exec functions, rejecting a mismatched grantor with `0A000` before any ACL mutation — matching real PG 18.3's `InternalGrant` check (`aclchk.c:394-412`). Tests: `TestExecACLChangeGrantedByCurrentUserIsNoop`/`TestExecACLChangeGrantedByOtherRoleErrors`, plus `GRANTED BY` parser cases in all three `op_grant_*acl_test.go` files. Still deferred: column-level `attacl`'s `GRANTED BY` clause remains parsed-and-discarded (`buildAttrACLChange`), and grant-option delegation-chain resolution (`select_best_grantor`) for all four object kinds. **2026-07-06 (loop #46) follow-up:** column-level `attacl`'s `GRANTED BY` validation landed too, closing the last of the four — `AttrACLChange` gained a `GrantedBy` field, `buildAttrACLChange` now shares `scanGrantTrailingClause` (its fourth and final caller) instead of its own copy of the stop-token loop, and `execAttrACLChange` calls `checkGrantedByCurrentUser` first, rejecting a mismatched grantor with `0A000` exactly like the other three. Tests: `TestExecAttrACLChangeGrantedByCurrentUserIsNoop`/`TestExecAttrACLChangeGrantedByOtherRoleErrors`, plus `GRANTED BY` parser cases in `op_grant_attracl_test.go`. **This closes every named `GRANTED BY` validation gap across all four object-privilege ACL kinds.** Only remaining deferred item: grant-option delegation-chain resolution (`select_best_grantor`), a feature-sized item for all object kinds. |
| 0118-0141 | [pg_stat_activity dynamic updates silently no-op'd (procNum identity-space conflation)](0118-0141-activity-procnum-identity-space-conflation.md) | accepted | Nightly batch 20260715-010036 regressed three previously-`pass_required` isolation specs (`partition-drop-index-locking`, `insert-conflict-specconflict`, `detach-partition-concurrently-4`) with `pg_stat_activity.query`/`state`-derived output diverging. Root cause: `ActivityRegistry.Register(b)` assigns a backend's slot via `procNumForPID(b.PID)` (a PID hash), but every dynamic call — `UpdateState`, `WaitEventStart/End`, `PIDForProcNum` — is keyed off `connTx.ProcNum`, which `internal/server/server.go` assigns from `s.cfg.TxnMgr.AcquireConnSlot()` (an unrelated MVCC proc-array slot, introduced to fix a separate PID-wraparound clobbering bug). The two index spaces silently diverged for most connections: every per-statement `UpdateState(connTx.ProcNum, …)` wrote to the wrong (usually unregistered) slot, while `Snapshot()` kept reading the backend's real registered slot, frozen at its `Register()`-time defaults — a wiring gap, not a regression in 0118-0073's idle-retention fix (still correct, still unit-tested). Fix: new `ActivityRegistry.RegisterAt(procNum, b)` (mirrors the existing `RegisterBackground(idx, b)` pattern) lets the server register at its own already-computed `procNum` instead of the PID hash; `Register(b)` now delegates to `RegisterAt(procNumForPID(b.PID), b)` so every other caller is unchanged. Verified live via a manually started server + raw `psql`: `pg_stat_activity.query`/`state` now update correctly both mid-statement and on return to idle. All three regressed specs pass again; full isolation battery 0 `--- FAIL`. Also records (deferral ledger, not fixed this loop): the same nightly run's `regress/errors`/`portals_p2`/`select` and four `units` package timeouts (`cmd/goopg`/`amcheck`/`initdb`/`mvcc`) all reproduced clean locally — consistent with host contention during the nightly window, not real regressions. Gates: `go build ./...` clean; `go test` PASS across `internal/activity`/`internal/server`/`internal/executor`/`internal/initdb`; full `TestPort_Isolation*` battery 0 FAIL; `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` PASS (Q12=2/Q13=33); `RALPH_PRECOMMIT_SCOPE=smoke scripts/ralph-precommit-test.sh` PASS (0 failed, all 3 workloads). |
| 0122-0009 | [WAL segment recycling (min_wal_size/max_wal_size/CheckPointDistanceEstimate)](0122-0009-wal-segment-recycling.md) | accepted | `Writer.RemoveOldSegments` previously unlinked every obsolete WAL segment; upstream instead recycles some of them (rename into a future segment slot) so a later `openSegment` skips its own create+zero-fill+directory-fsync. New `Config.MinWALSize`/`MaxWALSize` (wired from `min_wal_size`/`max_wal_size` via `initdb.OpenOptions.WALMinSize`/`WALMaxSize`) plus new `Checkpointer.CheckPointDistanceEstimate()` (an EMA of inter-checkpoint WAL volume, ported from upstream's `UpdateCheckPointDistanceEstimate`) drive the new `computeSpareSegments` formula — a segment-count-relative port of upstream's `XLOGfileslop` — via the new `Writer.RemoveOldSegmentsWithEstimate`/`SlotAwareRetainer.CheckPointDistanceEstimateFn`; `RemoveOldSegments` (distance=0) still reproduces the original `min_wal_size`-only floor exactly. Diverges from upstream by zero-filling the recycled segment (upstream leaves old content in place) because goopg's `reader.go` graceful-EOS heuristic checks for an all-zero tail rather than relying solely on per-record CRC — a recycled-but-unzeroed segment's leftover well-formed old record would otherwise be misread as live WAL. Tests: `TestRemoveOldSegmentsRecyclesUpToMinWALSize`/`TestRemoveOldSegmentsRecycleCapExceedsObsoleteCount`/`TestComputeSpareSegments*`/`TestRemoveOldSegmentsWithEstimateHonoursDistanceAndMax`/`TestSlotAwareRetainerUsesCheckPointDistanceEstimateFn` (`internal/wal/retention_test.go`), `TestCheckpointerUpdatesCheckPointDistanceEstimate` (`internal/wal/checkpointer_test.go`). No further known gap in this sizing bucket (timeline-aware recycling and a `wal_recycle` opt-out GUC remain separately out of scope, see doc's Non-goals). Gates: `go build ./...`/`go vet ./...` clean; `go test`/`go test -race` PASS across `internal/wal`; `go test ./internal/initdb/... ./cmd/goopg/...` PASS; `scripts/tpch-spotcheck.sh` PASS (Q12=2/Q13=33); `RALPH_PRECOMMIT_SCOPE=smoke scripts/ralph-precommit-test.sh` PASS (0 failed, all 3 workloads). |

| 0124-0001 | [TPC-DS SF=1 dual-engine re-sweep at HEAD (M0124-0001)](0124-0001-tpcds-sf1-head-resweep-protocol.md) | draft | Protocol for the sweep that turns §13.3's *projection* into a measurement: one sweep, one 600 s budget, one recorded commit (M0125's delta baseline). Codifies four hazards that already corrupted round-2 reporting — budget-incomparable headlines (the false "TIMEOUT 14 → 16": Q88 merely exceeded a new 180 s budget), sweep-tail collapse, PG backend orphans (**`reap_pg_orphans` exists only in the SF0.5 script, so the SF=1 harness needs it ported**, with a MATERIALIZED victim set), and multi-statement row counting. Requires an S-cold proof before starting, records that `env_tpcds.sh` exports `GOGC=off` so TPC-DS and TPC-H numbers are taken under different GC policies, corrects §1.4's stale pre-reorg ports, and reports confirm/refute for 13 named projections at SF=1 values only. **Updated 2026-07-28: `reap_pg_orphans` is LANDED in the SF=1 harness, and two measured corrections were added — D5's S-cold proof was vacuous (`'public'::regnamespace` matches nothing on goopg, so "zero reltuples" held by construction), and D4a replaces the chunked sweep's same-SHA invariant with same-`engine-tree` + same-`engine-binary`, because `server.sh start` rebuilds from the working tree at every `RESTART_AFTER_TIMEOUT` bounce while `git log -1` stays put. D6 now splits the timeout class in two after Q18 measured `OK 626 s` in set A and `TIMEOUT 627 s` in the re-sweep: a **budget-marginal** query (some run finished it within ~5 % of the budget) carries no signal when its verdict flips, unlike one whose runtime is *unbounded above* by the cut, so the two must never be reported as one class.** **Updated 2026-07-29 (M0124-0006): new rule D6a — a matching row count is not agreement.** Q16 was recorded `OK / 1 row` in chunk 2 while returning `0` against PG's `45` and went unnoticed for ten chunks; restricted to cells `OK` on both engines with equal row counts, **23 of 99 disagreed by value**. D6a makes value comparison mandatory for such cells and defines the graded normalisation that makes it usable (`scripts/tpcds-value-diff.py`): field-strip absorbs `char(n)` blank-padding, numeric canonicalisation absorbs the exactly-zero-quotient scale gap, and a 1e-14 relative tolerance absorbs float8 accumulation order — each pass compared positionally *and* as a sorted multiset, so the pass a cell survives IS its classification. Records the two traps that motivated it: `length()` is not a padding check (PG's `bpcharlen` ignores trailing blanks, so it agrees on both engines — `octet_length` is the discriminator), and diff size is uncorrelated with defect size (Q98's 5068-line diff is pure rendering; Q97's one-line diff is impossible-by-construction wrong). **CLOSED 2026-07-29 — the sweep ran 99/99 and its D7 deliverable landed as [`analysis/tpcds-sf1-goopg-20260728.md`](../../analysis/tpcds-sf1-goopg-20260728.md).** All 13 §13.3 projections tested at SF=1: **11 confirmed as stated, 2 (Q50, Q46) confirmed on rows and refuted on values, 0 refuted outright**. §13.3's projected **21** goopg-only defects measure **40** — the difference is 18 queries that complete with PG's exact row count and a wrong answer (the class D6a exists to find; root causes M0125-0009 ×10, the newly-found M0125-0010 ×4, M0125-0007 ×3, M0125-0006 ×1) plus Q18 joining the timeout class (17, split 15 unbounded / 2 budget-marginal). The engine-commit freeze lifts with this deliverable. |
