(2) M0097-0058's blanket `containsSetOp` bailout, whose premise is refuted here: `SetOp.Output()` IS the narrow schema, and the executor pads a `leftWidth+rightWidth` `keyRow` before evaluating either join key, so the `index out of range [57] with length 1` it was written against cannot arise at the join node. Retiring it uncovered a third: `pickInnerScanForNLI`'s left-as-inner flip emits `outer ++ inner` and already declined for `*Aggregate`/`*Values` outers — a `*SetOp` outer was simply unreachable until now, and Q71 planned `Append ++ item` while `sum(ext_price)` stayed bound to `item ++ Append`, so `sum()` was handed a text brand name. Measured on SF0.5 against the git-tracked PG oracle: **30 Cartesian products gone, Q5/Q8/Q14/Q54/Q71 TIMEOUT → PASS with oracle-identical rows and checksums** (Q71 `580 / 521a7af7606d10c1` = the stated acceptance), timeout class 12 → 7. Regression surface swept exhaustively rather than sampled — all 21 set-operation TPC-DS queries run, the 15 non-rescued unchanged; TPC-H plan-inert (all 10 plan-diff divergences are M0125-0039's qualification rendering). |
| 0125-0035 | [C2: single-table qualifier placement (M0125-0035, binary-join arm)](0125-0035-c2-single-table-qual-placement.md) | **binary-join arm implemented 2026-07-31; outer-join / CTE-body and MHJ arms open** | `M0125-0026`'s C2 — 66 of 68 `Filter:` lines sat on a join node instead of the base scan. Its mandatory first step was a RUNTIME determination, not a fix, and the answer is **execution defect, not costing-only**: measured serially with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (a counting instrument, valid on the loaded host), `store_sales ⋈ date_dim WHERE d_year = 2002` hashes `date_dim` at **actual rows = 73,049** — the whole table — and the join emits **1,374,770** rows for a 275,107-row answer; the MHJ arm is the same (`customer_address` hashed at 50,000, 96,562 rows emitted for 11,049). The code agrees: `multiHashJoinOp.Open` drains every build child through `drainRowsCtx` and hashes all of it, and `partitionFilters` evaluates a build-table qual at STEP time, after the hash exists. The qual was stranded because both placement passes declined — Slice A needs ≥5 tables AND a `SmallDimension` relation, a hardcoded name-tag set only for `region`/`nation`, so no TPC-DS relation can ever qualify; and M0125-0004's pass excluded base-relation leaves by borrowing Slice A's risk. That borrowing was wrong: Slice A **moves** a conjunct before DP enumeration (hence "Q8 / Q21 PASS → CANCEL"), while this pass runs **last** and **duplicates**, so the join order is already fixed and admitting a leaf changes only what a scan emits. Landed with `LeafLocal` set to match the leaf-local coordinate space and a fail-closed idempotence guard (Q69 was printing its `d_year`/`d_moy` conjuncts twice). Measured: scan-level `Filter:` lines **5 → 71** across the 18-query capture, Q69's join estimate 525,809,623 → 287,921 (it was wrong by 1,826×); TPC-H plan-diff **4/22 DIFFER with zero structural change** — exactly 4 net-new scan-level filters, 0 removed, confirming duplicate-never-move on real plans; full 99-query SF0.5 gate **PASS=87 MISMATCH=0 CKMISMATCH=0 ERROR=0 TIMEOUT=8 SKIP=4**, no new timeout. **Acceptance NOT met**: Q78 still times out — its qual sits above two LEFT joins and names a CTE output column, so it needs the preserved-side extension plus PG's single-reference CTE inlining, the boundary this item shares with -0034's open CTE arm. |
| 0125-0036 | [EXISTS → ANY: making an OR-ed correlated EXISTS hashable (M0125-0036, class C3)](0125-0036-exists-to-any-hashed-subplan.md) | **implemented 2026-07-31** | goopg's answer to a correlated EXISTS was binary — unnest it to a semi-join, or re-execute its body once per outer row — and an OR-ed sublink can never take the first branch, so `M0125-0026` §C3's Q10/Q35 formed ≈1×10¹¹ row-touches (Q35 measured at 8.16 s per outer row ⇒ ≈9 days at SF=1). §C3's control Q69 proves the trigger is the `OR` alone: its three EXISTS are AND-ed, unnest to a `Hash Join (ANTI)/(SEMI)` chain, and complete. Caching cannot reach the shape — the outer key `c_customer_sk` is unique per outer row, so every call is a miss by construction — which is why upstream's answer is a *conversion*, `convert_EXISTS_to_ANY` (subselect.c:1731): lift the body's single correlation equality into an upper test expression, leaving an UNCORRELATED body that hashes once. This lands goopg's analogue and feeds the hash machinery that already existed (`executor/subplan_hash.go`, Stage 11). **Q10 TIMEOUT → 16.9 s (0 rows = oracle) and Q35 TIMEOUT → 14.0 s (100 rows = oracle)**; TPC-H plan-diff is 1/22 **with the kill switch OFF producing the same 1/22**, i.e. plan-neutral on all 22. Two traps are documented because both were silent: the operand's column index taken verbatim from the body's `OuterColumnRef` is **stale after MHJ packing** (which OID-re-sorts its output and treats a sublink as opaque) and made Q35 return **0 rows instead of 100** — Q10's own acceptance row could not detect it, because Q10's oracle is 0; and a join's predicate row is `left ++ right`, which is not `Output()` for SEMI/ANTI. NULL semantics bound the scope rather than a heuristic: `IN` is three-valued where EXISTS is two-valued, so the walk descends the AND/OR spine only and never converts a negated EXISTS — upstream's `isTopQual`/`unknownEqFalse` condition, pinned by a new `boundedQualSpine` walker role. Q30/Q81 (§C3's correlated-scalar-aggregate variant) are untouched and stay TIMEOUT. |
| 0125-0042 | [An OR-ed `IN (subquery)` operand keeps a stale column index (M0125-0042)](0125-0042-in-sublink-operand-stale-index.md) | **FIXED and landed 2026-07-31 (loop #12)** | Two OR-ed uncorrelated `col IN (subquery)` sublinks under a SEMI join over an MHJ answered **1329 where PG says 1294** — pre-existing at HEAD, found while probing `M0125-0036`. The filed framing ("over-match of 35") understates it: only **10** of goopg's 314 rows appear in PG's 377, so the answer sets are nearly DISJOINT and merely similar in size. Bisected by measurement, not inspection: the SEMI join is exact (EXISTS-only matches, and all 314 rows re-check as satisfying it), the value set is exact (a CONSTANT operand over the same sublinks matches), each arm alone is exact, and the OR-ed pair without the EXISTS is exact — so the **operand** is what is wrong. It carries the right `Name` and a stale `Index`: bound at **13** (`c_customer_sk` under `ca ++ c`), **9** by remap time (under `cd ++ c`), where runtime needs **22** (under `ca ++ cd ++ c`). Index 9 of the executed layout is **`ca_zip`, a string**, and `compareEq`'s string↔int coercion answers instead of raising — a ZIP that numerically appears among the customer keys admits the row. Three mechanisms hide it: `reresolveJoinByName` (the only by-Name rebind) never fires because the tree is `Filter → MultiHashJoin` with no `*Join` at remap time; a SINGLE `IN` is masked because it unnests to a semi-join whose keys rebind by Name; and EXPLAIN prints `c.c_customer_sk` from the Name while the executor reads index 9. Ruled out by measurement: the hashed probe (`GOOPG_HASHED_SUBPLAN=off` identical), parallelism (identical), and a synthetic minimal case that reaches a structurally IDENTICAL plan and still answers correctly — the trigger is the binding history, not the plan shape. **Fix landed loop #12**: generalised `resolveHostOperandIdx` (M0125-0036) to hand-written `InExpr` operands (new `fixInExprOperandIndex`, sharing a `resolveHostColumnIdx` core) under the same unique-match guard, wired into the existing `rewriteExistsToAnyNode` walk (now unconditional; only the EXISTS→ANY conversion itself stays behind `GOOPG_EXISTS_TO_ANY`). Both acceptance queries now match PG exactly, the full TPC-DS SF0.5 sweep is 0 mismatches, and `plan-diff`/`tpch-spotcheck` show no regression. An adjacent latent gap remains recorded and unfixed (`remapByPosMap` has no `*InExpr` arm, so a *correlated* IN's `OuterColumnRef`s are never posMap-translated) — ledger row 2026-07-31. |
| 0125-0043 | [Extinction of the `SmallDimension` benchmark-name tag (M0125-0043)](0125-0043-smalldimension-name-tag-extinction.md) | **FIXED and landed 2026-07-31** | goopg branched **production** planner behaviour on the literal table names `region` / `nation`: two sibling writers (`operators_ddl.go` at CREATE TABLE, `open.go` at catalog reload) were the only non-test setters of `catalog.Table.SmallDimension`, so a user table called `nation` planned differently from the same table called `nations`, every non-TPC-H tiny dimension got none of the treatment, and the CREATE-TABLE site was guessing at a size it could not know (the table is empty there). The property now moves to the plan node and its source moves from the name to the SIZE: new `internal/planner/small_dimension.go` derives it at plan-build time from the ANALYZEd row count or, cold, from the block-count fallback — where upstream's never-analyzed 10-page floor puts both `region` and `nation` at 170 estimated rows — and stamps `SeqScan.SmallDim` / `IndexScan.SmallDim` beside `EstRelRows`, for the recorded reason that the consumers take only a `Node` and run with no catalog in scope. Threshold 1024 deliberately equals `smallAnchorRowsThreshold`, so a relation cannot anchor an inferred equality edge while being denied the build side of the join that edge produces. The fallback is read **ungated**, not through `relSizeFallbackRows`: pre-M0125-0003 plans had the property populated at every stage, so gating it would make `GOOPG_RELSIZE_FALLBACK=0` silently drop M0054-0010's build-side pinning. **Measured plan-neutral on all 22 TPC-H queries** by a same-cluster stash A/B (byte-identical snapshots) — a positive result, not a null one: the before-arm has the name tag ON, so byte-identical plans are direct evidence the size derivation reproduces it exactly, including Q5's `region` MHJ anchor and the Q8/Q21 `shouldAttachBeforeMHJ` CANCEL guard whose signature had to change (it now takes the leaf scans, since the answer left the binding's table). The nine candidate queries by text (Q2 Q5 Q7 Q8 Q9 Q10 Q11 Q20 Q21) are confirmed; the set that actually moves is empty. `catalog.Table.SmallDimension` survives as an explicit hint with **no production writer**, for the catalog-only TPC-H fixtures that have no heap to measure. One non-obvious sibling path was found by auditing construction sites rather than by a failing test: `unnest.go`'s correlated-probe **demotion** (Index → Seq) preserved alias/schema/privilege fields but dropped the tag, where the three promotion sites were obvious. |
| 0125-0041 | [A correlated scalar-aggregate sublink over a WITH item (M0125-0041)](0125-0041-cte-scalar-sublink-decorrelation.md) | **root cause fixed 2026-07-31; the item stays OPEN — Q30/Q81 still TIMEOUT on a different factor** | TPC-DS Q30/Q81's `ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_state = ctr2.ctr_state)` was re-evaluated per outer row. The filing (`M0125-0026` §C3) instructed the loop to find out *why the scalar pull-up declines* — and the measured answer is that **it never declined**: a probe printing every gate's verdict shows `canUnnestSubquery` = true, `avg` NULL-on-empty, the `*1.2` target strict, the conjunct AND-reachable, 1 param / 0 residuals, and the inner not probe-cheap. The pull-up then died inside `clonePlanReplacingOuter`, whose switch had no arm for `*planner.CTEScan`; since a clone failure is a *bail* ("stay a SubPlan"), a capability gap wore the costume of a policy decision, silently, for every query whose correlated sublink reads a CTE. Fixed by adding `*CTEScan` (body shared **verbatim** — `WITH` is not `LATERAL`, so the correlation always sits in a `Filter` above the node, and sharing is what lets the executor's name-keyed `ctx.CTERowCache` materialize the body once) and its `*MaterializedCTEScan` sibling, with a guard — `planSubtreeHasOuterRefDeep` — refusing the share when the body itself carries an outer reference, because a rewritten body and an un-rewritten consumer of the same CTE **name** would collide on one cache entry. `planCloneSupported` gets matching arms so the sibling predicates cannot drift. Correctness is pinned by an *equivalence* test (pull-up on vs off over the same data, control arm asserting the SubPlan path really ran, NULL correlation key included), not a plan-shape assertion. Q30's `SubPlan 1` is gone and the plan is the intended one grouped aggregate hash-joined on `ctr_state`. **But Q30 still TIMEOUTs at 300 s *and* at 1200 s** — like Q21/`M0125-0032`, a shape defect, not a budget crossing: the plan still contains `Nested Loop (CROSS)` between the ~2×10⁴-row CTE and a full 5×10⁴-row `customer_address` scan = 10⁹ pairs each driving an index probe, which is C1 (`M0125-0034`), named by §C3 itself as compounding this class. The 2×10¹³ price is now factored: the CTE-rescan factor is gone, the 10⁹-pair factor is -0034's. Also recorded: `ca_state = 'AR'` still does not reach the `customer_address` scan (first probe for -0034 here), and goopg's parser rejects `WITH` inside a sublink where PG accepts it — which is why the outer-reference guard is currently unreachable from SQL. |
| 0125-0049 | [EXPLAIN prints a shared CTE body once, as a `CTE <name>` section (M0125-0049)](0125-0049-explain-shared-cte-section.md) | implemented 2026-08-06 | Q67's plan was 127 lines and mentioned `store_sales` 36 times for a four-table join the engine executes ONCE — the exact over-statement `M0125-0026`'s capture exists to prevent, and why `M0125-0040`'s acceptance wording read as unmet. Not a planner defect: goopg never clones a CTE body per consumer despite the M0016-0002 comment (`planScanRangeVar` builds every reference with `Child: ce.body`), so the plan is a DAG the EXPLAIN walker walked as a tree. PG prints the body once under a `CTE <name>` heading on the TOP plan node, in declaration order, before its InitPlans and children (`SS_process_ctes` + `ExplainSubPlans`); the shape and three edges were CAPTURED from 18.3, not inferred — one reference is still sectioned, order is declaration not encounter (new `CTEScan.DeclSeq`), and a nested WITH sections inside its own body. `planChildren` is left alone so range-table naming and `resolveInAncestor` still see the body; only the walkers treat a hoisted `CTE Scan` as a leaf. **The hoist key is the NAME, not the body pointer** — the pointer draft under-hoisted exactly where the item came from, because M0125-0040 gives each UNION branch its own `preplanWithClause` pass and Q67's nine references carry nine distinct-but-identical body Nodes; name is the engine's own identity (`ctx.CTERowCache` is keyed by lowercase name). One trap paid for: rendering a section re-enters the walker and drained the OWNER's pending `SubPlan` queue, printing it inside the section and regressing M0125-0039's correlated-reference qualification to `(cst = cst)` — the queue is now held aside. Measured on the SF0.5 99-query plan channel: `same=91 changed=8` over the pointer-key capture, and the full move is exactly the 30 `WITH` queries plus the 4 grouping-sets ones — **no query without a CTE moved**. Corpus 5774 → 4307 lines; Q67 127 → 40 lines, 36 → 4 `store_sales` mentions, ONE `Seq Scan on public.store_sales`. Three divergences with ledger rows (sections hoist to the render root not the declaring level; a sublink-only reference is not collected; JSON/XML/YAML still duplicate). **Discovery, not fixed here:** two different same-named CTE declarations in disjoint scopes alias through `CTERowCache[name]` and the second replays the first's rows — goopg returns 1,1 where PG returns 1,2. |
| 0125-0050 | [A CTE's runtime identity is its DECLARATION, not its name (M0125-0050)](0125-0050-cte-declaration-identity.md) | implemented 2026-08-06 | Wrong answers, not a render issue: `ctx.CTERowCache` was keyed by the lowercased CTE NAME statement-wide, so two unrelated `WITH x` declarations in disjoint scopes shared one buffer and the second replayed the first's rows — goopg answered `1,1` where PG 18.3 answers `1,2`, with the second body planned correctly and never run. PG cannot express the bug: `SS_process_ctes` gives each WITH entry its own subplan and `CteScanState` keys off that subplan's `ctePlanId` (`nodeCtescan.c`), so name never enters the runtime identity. The task is entirely the choice of key, and both cheap candidates fail in opposite directions — **name over-shares** (the bug), and **the `plannedCTE` pointer, or -0049's `declSeq`, under-shares**: `planSelect` re-enters on the head operand of a set-op chain, so M0125-0040's grouping-sets rewrite plans its ONE synthetic `__gs_src_N` declaration TWICE (measured: 3 scans, 2 pointers, 2 declSeqs, 1 declaration), and either key would split the buffer and re-run the hoisted join — undoing -0040 on the very queries it was filed for, while still passing a name-only assertion. The key that lands is the **declaration site**, `CTEScan.DeclKey() = "<declaring CommonTableExpr pos>:<lower(name)>"`: stable across replanning (both preplan passes read the same AST node), distinct per declaration (all three `CommonTableExpr` producers give distinct declarations distinct `(pos,name)`), and race-free by construction (no counter, no lazily-mutated AST field). EXPLAIN's `collectCTEHoist` moves to the same key as -0049 said it must, so the grouping-sets source still prints ONE section while two same-named declarations now print two `CTE x` sections with a body each — also what PG prints. Gates: TPC-H Q12=2/Q13=35 canonical; SF0.5 plan channel `queries=99 same=99 changed=0` (the corpus SHOULD be untouched, and would have moved on 30+ queries had the key un-shared anything). **Two discoveries filed, not fixed:** the DML sibling `ctx.MaterializedCTEs` is still name-keyed, and goopg does not enforce PG's top-level rule for data-modifying CTEs (probed: goopg accepts a nested `WITH x AS (INSERT … RETURNING)` that PG rejects 42P19, `parse_cte.c:336`) — which is what makes the first reachable. |
| 0125-0051 | [A data-modifying WITH is legal only on the statement being run (M0125-0051)](0125-0051-data-modifying-cte-top-level-only.md) | implemented 2026-08-06 | goopg EXECUTED a data-modifying CTE at any nesting depth: `SELECT v FROM (WITH x AS (INSERT INTO dm VALUES (1) RETURNING a) SELECT a AS v FROM x) s` inserted the row and returned it, where PG 18.3 raises **`0A000`** "WITH clause containing a data-modifying statement must be at the top level" (`parse_cte.c:330-337`; the filing ledger row's 42P19 was wrong — 42P19 is the neighbouring *recursive* rule, which goopg already raises). PG's test is `pstate->parentParseState != NULL`, a property of the parse LEVEL; goopg's analogue is a `stmtRoot` flag set only by `analyzeSelect`/`analyzeInsert`/`analyzeUpdate`/`analyzeDelete` when `outerScope == nil`, threaded into `analyzeWith`. `analyzeSelectWithParent` becomes the constant-`false` wrapper — all 15 of its call sites analyze a nested query — so the rule needs no new walker. Two edges decide the flag's placement, both captured from 18.3 first: a parenthesised whole statement IS top level (`select_with_parens` adds no parse level), while a parenthesised set-op ARM is not — and goopg reaches both through the same `SetOpOperand` hop, so the set-op branch passes `stmtRoot && s.SetOpOperand == nil`. Because `planner.Plan` always calls `analyzer.Analyze`, one check covers the simple protocol and PREPARE/EXECUTE alike (verified). Also closes -0050's `MaterializedCTEs` finding by construction: two same-named DML CTEs now require a nested WITH, which is rejected. Four further divergences recorded, not fixed — a sublink `WITH` does not parse; `WITH x AS (INSERT …) DELETE …` lets the outer DML see the CTE's rows (PG: 0 rows); PL/pgSQL accepts no `WITH` statement at all; `WITH … (SELECT …)` is a syntax error. |
| 0125-0052 | [A DML CTE's writes are invisible to the WHOLE statement, not just an outer SELECT (M0125-0052)](0125-0052-dml-cte-write-fence-covers-whole-statement.md) | implemented 2026-08-06 | `WITH x AS (INSERT INTO dm15 VALUES (15) RETURNING a) DELETE FROM dm15 WHERE a = 15 RETURNING a` returned **1 row and emptied the table**; PG 18.3 returns **0 rows and keeps the row**, because every sub-statement of a data-modifying WITH shares `es_snapshot` AND `es_output_cid`, so a sibling's tuple fails the `cmin` test in `HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC`. goopg's stand-in for the missing per-tuple command id — `ctx.CTEWriteFence` — already existed and was already consulted by `scanMatching`, the outer UPDATE/DELETE scan; it was **starved, not bypassed**. Only `upsertOp` and the three UPDATE paths registered their writes, so for the archetypal `WITH x AS (INSERT …)` the fence was EMPTY — which also breaks the outer-SELECT half everyone believed worked (`SELECT count(*)` answered 2 where PG answers 1). Registering INSERTs alone would have traded one wrong answer for another: the fence was keyed by bare `ItemPointer`, and `{block 0, offset 1}` is the first row of every table, so `WITH x AS (INSERT INTO fa …) DELETE FROM fb WHERE a = 7` would skip **fb's** row — a collision the EvalPlanQual site already worked around by re-reading xmin. So the key becomes `CTEFencePtr{Rel, Ptr}` (that xmin re-read is deleted), five copies of the inline registration collapse into `cteFenceInsert`/`cteFenceUpdate`/`cteFenced`, `cteFenceUpdate` takes separate source/destination relations for cross-partition moves, and INSERT + MERGE-insert register. Fourth site class: the fence must not be **plan-shape dependent** — `indexScanOp`, `indexOnlyScanOp` and the index-driven UPDATE fast path consult it now too, since with a PK on the target the pre-fix outer SELECT went through an Index Only Scan and returned the CTE's row. Seven tests, each pinned to a value captured from live PG 18.3. **Deferred (M0125-0053):** the fence hides rows the CTE ADDED but cannot show rows it REMOVED — a CTE DELETE/UPDATE stamps our own xmax, so the row vanishes from the rest of the statement where PG still shows the pre-image; needs a pre-image set or a real per-tuple command id. |
| 0125-0053 | [The rest of a statement still sees the pre-image of a row its own DML CTE removed (M0125-0053)](0125-0053-dml-cte-preimage-reveal.md) | implemented 2026-08-06 | Successor to -0052. The write fence can only ever SKIP rows, but PG's rule is symmetric: `WITH x AS (DELETE FROM dz WHERE a=1 RETURNING a) SELECT count(*) FROM dz` answers **2** on PG 18.3 and answered **1** on goopg, and `WITH x AS (UPDATE dz SET a=6 WHERE a=5 RETURNING a) SELECT a FROM dz ORDER BY a` answers **[2, 5]** vs goopg's **[2]**. A CTE DELETE stamps xmax with our own XID, and a CTE UPDATE does the same to the old version whose new version is then fenced, so the row vanished from the rest of the statement. PG needs no second mechanism — the same `es_output_cid` that hides a sibling's insert through `cmin` reveals the pre-image through `cmax` (`heapam_visibility.c`, HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC) — so `ctx.CTEXmaxReveal` stands in for the cmax test, the mirror image of `ctx.CTEWriteFence` on the same `CTEFencePtr{Rel, Ptr}` key. **Only READ scans consult it**, which is PG's own structure and not a shortcut: `ExecDelete`/`ExecUpdate` take the `TM_SelfModified` arm and return NULL without touching a row whose cmax equals `es_output_cid` ("already deleted by self", `nodeModifyTable.c`), so a DML target scan that never finds it yields the same row count and heap state. The reveal lives INSIDE the HOT-chain walk — the pre-image sits ahead of the CTE's new version, so testing only the walk's result would return the new version, which the fence then drops, losing the row entirely. **The correction the isolation suite forced:** treating membership in the set as a licence to show the tuple broke `TestPort_IsolationInsertConflictDoUpdate3` with a duplicate row, because `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` carries a documented MVCC violation letting it update a tuple *not visible to the command's snapshot* — PG relaxes only the cmax arm, so `cteRevealHeader` re-runs the ordinary visibility test with `Xmax` cleared and the xmin snapshot test still applies. **Discovery, deferred:** PG runs the main plan FIRST and only then any not-yet-completed DML CTE, in `ExecPostprocessPlan` (proved live: 'outer' lands at ctid (0,1), 'cte' at (0,2)); goopg runs CTEs first, so the four outer-write-vs-CTE-write shapes diverge (whichever runs second finds the row stamped and declines it). Reads are unaffected; `TestCTEPreImageWriteWriteDivergesFromPG` pins it. |
| 0125-0054 | [Data-modifying CTEs are not a prefix: PG runs them on demand and after the main plan (M0125-0054)](0125-0054-dml-cte-execution-order.md) | implemented 2026-08-06 | Successor to -0053, which closed the visibility half of data-modifying-WITH semantics and filed the ordering half. goopg's operator was called `cteDMLPrefixOp` and the name was the bug: it ran every DML CTE to completion before it even built the outer body. PostgreSQL has **no prefix phase** — a data-modifying CTE is a non-`canSetTag` `ModifyTable` reached by one of two routes: (1) **on demand**, when the `CteScan` that reads it pulls from it, and (2) **after the main plan**, via `ExecInitModifyTable`'s `estate->es_auxmodifytables` swept by `ExecPostprocessPlan` (`execMain.c`, from `ExecutorFinish`) for whatever nothing pulled from. The filed diagnosis had route 2 and not route 1; both are needed, since a CTE the body READS cannot be deferred until after the body has produced rows. Four write-write shapes distinguish the orders, because whichever sub-statement runs SECOND finds the row already stamped by this command and declines it (`TM_SelfModified` with `cmax == es_output_cid`): outer DELETE of a CTE-UPDATEd row (PG `[5]`/table `[2]`, goopg 0 rows/`[2 6]`), outer UPDATE of a CTE-DELETEd row (`[101]`/`[2 101]` vs 0 rows/`[2]`), outer DELETE of a CTE-DELETEd row, outer UPDATE of a CTE-UPDATEd row — plus the conflict-free ctid witness where 'outer' lands at (0,1) and 'cte' at (0,2). **The sweep runs in REVERSE declaration order**: `ExecInitModifyTable` files with `lcons` not `lappend`, so `es_auxmodifytables` is reverse init order — confirmed live, three unreferenced INSERT CTEs a,b,c land c,b,a; upstream's comment explains why (a later CTE reading an earlier one must run first, so its `CteScan` drives the earlier one rather than finding its RETURNING rows discarded). **Demand-driving beats the filed plan-time referenced-ness flag**: a body-plan walk that misses a subtree UNDERCOUNTS references, defers a read CTE, and its `MaterializedCTEScan` silently returns nothing — where `materializedCTEScanOp.Open` calling `ensureCTE` cannot misjudge, because the scan that would read nothing is the thing that triggers the run. **The obligation the reorder creates:** the fence and its reveal were gated on `InDMLCTE`, so only CTE writes were registered; with the outer body first, its writes must be registered too or a deferred CTE sees rows PG's `cmin` test hides (`WITH x AS (INSERT INTO fs_dst SELECT a FROM fs_src RETURNING a) INSERT INTO fs_src VALUES (2)` leaves fs_dst `[1]` on PG). The gate becomes the fence's existence; `InDMLCTE` survives only for the `CTENewToOld`/`CTESelfModifiedErrors` bookkeeping, which is genuinely phase-specific. -0053's `TestCTEPreImageWriteWriteDivergesFromPG` is inverted as it was written to be; 4 new tests join it, every value captured from live PG 18.3. **Deferred:** a referenced CTE is materialized in full at first demand rather than streamed through the scan, so an outer body writing between pulls does not interleave with it. |
| 0125-0055 | [The routine command counter, and the `TM_SelfModified` error it unmasks (M-NIGHTLY AI-20260806-191958-001)](0125-0055-routine-command-counter-and-self-modified.md) | implemented 2026-08-06 | Successor to -0052/-0053/-0054, which built goopg's stand-in for PG's per-tuple command id and left one thing implicit: **the command id is not constant for the duration of a statement.** The fence was command-blind — once a sub-statement of a data-modifying `WITH` registered a tuple, it was hidden from every later scan of that statement. PG hides it only while `cmin >= curcid` (`heapam_visibility.c` `HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC`), and `curcid` is NOT frozen at `es_output_cid`: `functions.c` `postquel_getnext` does `CommandCounterIncrement()` before every statement of a routine that is not `readonly_func` (= `provolatile != PROVOLATILE_VOLATILE`, `init_sql_fcache`) — "so that all work to date in this transaction is visible" — with PL/pgSQL reaching the same place through SPI. Consequence, reproducible in ONE session with no isolation harness: `WITH doup AS (UPDATE accounts … RETURNING *, update_checking(999)) UPDATE accounts a … FROM doup` leaves `checking` at **1701** on live PG and **1700** on goopg — the volatile function's UPDATE found no row it was allowed to see and was a silent 0-row no-op. Fix: `Context.CmdID` (0 for the statement's own plan, +1 per nested VOLATILE routine body, via `routineCommandCounterIncrement` at the six child-Context sites in `plpgsql_runtime.go`); the two fence maps become `map[CTEFencePtr]int` valued by the writing/killing command id, so `cteFenced` (`writeCmd >= CmdID`) and `cteRevealed` (`killCmd >= CmdID`) literally *are* the cmin/cmax arms. **What it unmasks:** with the function's write restored, the EPQ chain-follow — which applies no cmin test (`heapam_tuple_lock` + `TUPLE_LOCK_FLAG_FIND_LAST_VERSION` just walks `t_ctid`) — leads the outer DML into a version its own sub-command produced, and PG errors rather than merging: `ExecUpdate:2656`, SQLSTATE **27000** `ERRCODE_TRIGGERED_DATA_CHANGE_VIOLATION` (goopg had `09000`, a different class — the path had never been reached end-to-end). Discriminator `tmfd.cmax != es_output_cid`: LATER command ⇒ error, SAME command ⇒ silent skip (`updwcte`). Raised via `cteWrittenByLaterCommand` at `updateWithFrom` and `deleteWithUsing`. `CTENewToOld`/`CTESelfModifiedErrors`/`CTESelfModErr` are DELETED: unreachable, and had the command-counter fix landed beside them they would have started firing on the non-concurrent query where PG succeeds. **Closes the sole engine-side blocker of the M0127 S7 gate** — `TestPort_IsolationEvalPlanQual` passes. Bar: byte-identical to live PG 18.3 on all four forms (`updwctefail`/`delwctefail` × with/without the concurrent session), rows AND final heap. **Deferred:** `deleteWithUsing` still has no EvalPlanQual — only the `TM_SelfModified` detection was added there, guarded on a non-empty fence. |
| 0125-0048 | [The single-pass grouping-sets aggregate: one pass, one hash table per set (M0125-0048)](0125-0048-single-pass-grouping-sets.md) | implemented 2026-08-06 | Retires the UNION-ALL expansion of `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS/ROLLUP/CUBE` (M0122-0004) **and** the source-sharing CTE hoist built on top of it (M0125-0040) — the item that filed this said the faithful aggregate REPLACES the hoist, and with the source read once there is no source to share. SQL:1999 §7.9 defines the clause as the UNION ALL of one plain GROUP BY per set and goopg executed that definition literally: N sibling `SelectStmt`s through `s.SetOp`, one scan per set, `GROUPING(...)` resolved to a per-branch `IntegerConst`, the grand total as a branch rather than a `Group Key: ()` level. PostgreSQL computes every level in ONE pass with one hash table per set (`nodeAgg.c` AGG_HASHED/AGG_MIXED, `preprocess_grouping_sets` + `consider_groupingsets_paths`). Now ONE `Aggregate` node carries `GroupExprs` = the deduplicated union (PG's `parse->groupClause`), `GroupingSets [][]int` = the slots each set keeps, and `GroupingMasks` = each `GROUPING(...)` call's bitmask per set. **The mask is an output COLUMN, not an expression over a hidden set-id**: it depends only on which set produced the row, so the target list resolves `GROUPING(a,b)` to a plain `ColumnRef` — no new Expr node, no new case in either evaluator or in EXPLAIN, and the column is named `grouping` as PG names it. **The ordinary aggregate is the one-set case, not a second operator** (`sets = [[0..n-1]]`, set prefix omitted when there is one set), avoiding a 250-line sibling of the shared-state/`finishAgg` logic. Gates: SF0.5 plan channel `queries=99 same=91 changed=8` and the eight are EXACTLY the eight ROLLUP queries (Q5 Q14 Q18 Q22 Q27 Q67 Q77 Q80) — no non-grouping-set query moved; sweep of those eight `PASS=8 MISMATCH=0`; TPC-H Q12=2/Q13=35 canonical. Q27 collapses from `CTE __gs_src_606` + 3-branch Append to one `HashAggregate (2 keys, 3 grouping sets)` over one scan — PG's node count. Runtime is a side effect, not the goal: Q67 82s→17s, Q18 37s→9s, Q22 21s→4s, Q27 31s→10s. Three ledger rows: emission order without ORDER BY differs from PG's AGG_MIXED, no per-set `Hash Key:`/`Group Key: ()` detail lines, and every level is hashed with no `work_mem` sort/spill choice. |

| 0125-0044 | [Two aliases of one table collapse onto one GROUP BY slot (M0125-0044)](0125-0044-groupby-alias-slot-collapse.md) | **FIXED and landed 2026-07-31** | TPC-DS Q64 returned 0 rows against the oracle's 2 while the 18-way join was **correct** — goopg and PG agreed on the same 26 rows, but goopg projected one `date_dim` alias's year for all three of `d1`/`d2`/`d3`, so five distinct groups came out spelled `1993|1993|1993` and the outer `syear = 1999` filter emptied the answer. A contested key that places nothing is **abandoned, not fallen back on**: `SELECT d3.y` under `GROUP BY d1.y, d2.y` now raises PG's 42803 instead of projecting another alias. Measured: Q64 → `64|OK|2|31f0342ff9d55c4a`; full 99-query SF0.5 gate PASS=93 MISMATCH=0 CKMISMATCH=0 ERROR=0 TIMEOUT=2 SKIP=4 with **exactly 1 of 99 cells moved** vs HEAD; TPC-H 22/22 plans MATCH. **Not fixed:** `aggregateCallKey` shares the blind key, so `count(d1.y)` and `count(d2.y)` collapse onto one aggregate slot — measured, deferred, filed. |
| 0125-0045 | [Two aliases of one table collapse onto one AGGREGATE slot (M0125-0045)](0125-0045-aggregate-alias-slot-collapse.md) | **FIXED and landed 2026-08-01** | The aggregate half of M0125-0044's cause: `aggregateCallKey` builds its argument part on `parserExprKey`, which drops the qualifier, so `count(d1.y)` and `count(d2.y)` over a self-joined table hashed to ONE key and the second call was discarded at BOTH dedup points (`collectAggregateCalls`'s seen-map and `buildAggregateStage`'s exists-check) — both SELECT columns then read agg slot 0, right cardinality, wrong values, invisible to every row-count gate. PG keys aggregate equality on the resolved argument Vars (`equal()` over `Aggref->args`, equalfuncs.c). Fix = the -0044 contested-key treatment applied to aggregates: `qualifiedAggregateCallKey` reuses the same reflective qualifier walk over the whole `FuncCall` (arguments, FILTER, in-argument ORDER BY — computed args come free); collection dedups on the qualified key; `buildAggregateStage` pre-scans for blind keys whose qualified forms differ (`aggregateAmbiguous`) and keys contested calls through `aggregateByKeyQual`; both resolution sites (`resolveExprAfterAggregate` + `resolveExpr`'s havingAgg outer-ref arm) dispatch contested calls through the qualified map. "Contested" = qualified forms DIFFER, so the same call written twice still shares one slot. Deliberate, recorded asymmetry: the qualified parser form can only SPLIT, never wrongly merge — the price is that `count(y)`/`count(t.y)` of the same binding under a contested key get two slots computing identical values (redundant work, never a wrong answer; merging needs PG's resolved-form equality, and -0044 recorded why naive resolved-form comparison is a trap — ledger row 2026-08-01). **No SF0.5 query reaches the defect**, so acceptance is planner unit tests + a byte-identical PG-oracle diff on hand-written asymmetric-NULL data (`count(d1.y)=3` vs `count(d2.y)=1`); the full 99-query SF0.5 gate ran as a no-regression check only — PASS=95 MISMATCH=0 CKMISMATCH=0 ERROR=0 TIMEOUT=0 SKIP=4, ZERO cell movement vs loop #18. |
| 0125-0046 | [MHJ residual-qual placement: the IN-list was never in mh.Filters (M0125-0046)](0125-0046-mhj-residual-inlist-qual-placement.md) | **FIXED and landed 2026-08-01** | Filed as "the MHJ walker disqualifies InExpr" — a misdiagnosis: the planner walker has admitted literal IN-lists since M0061, and the mh.Filters push handles them. The real mechanism: a WHERE restriction that pushOneConjunct never AND'd onto a join predicate is still in the residual *Filter above the MHJ, which NEITHER MHJ pass reads (collectMultiHashTables captures join-predicate extras only; pushSingleSourceFiltersIntoMHJTables reads mh.Filters only), and the binary sibling pushInnerJoinInputQuals required a *Join child. Measured: `ca_state IN ('IL','TX','ME')` stranded on the MHJ node, customer_address hashed whole (50,000 rows), MHJ emitting 96,562 for an 11,049-row answer. Fix: pushInnerJoinInputQuals dispatches a *MultiHashJoin child to pushResidualQualsIntoMHJTables — fail-closed attribution (walkExprRefs+scopeVeto, FuncCall/OuterColumnRef veto, positional name validation) to the unique member by cumulative offset, clone-shift to leaf-local, descend via pushConjunctIntoSubtree (idempotence + LeafLocal convention for free); the mh.Filters pass's wrapper now stamps LeafLocal so the two passes compose into one wrapper. Executor sibling really DID veto InExpr: walkColumnRefs now admits literal IN-lists, enumerates the six kinds the planner walker had that it lacked, and gains a fail-closed default arm (unenumerated kind → leafFilters, always safe). Probe MHJ now emits 11,049 = the answer, count = PG oracle. Gates: SF0.5 subset probe of 15 MHJ-heavy queries PASS=15 MISMATCH=0; spotcheck PASS; TPC-H plan-diff 5/22 DIFFER all the same benign shape (+Filter lines under MHJ member scans, zero structural change) with row-count proof — Q3/Q10/Q11/Q21 equal to the pinned anchors and un-anchored Q2 md5-identical between a HEAD-baseline binary and the fix. Deferred: duplicate-not-move (residual copy re-evaluated per output row where PG moves the qual), FuncCall veto (no provolatile model), and *Join-spine descent into an MHJ (ledger row stays open). |
| 0125-0047 | [The comma-FROM join order was decided by Go's map-iteration randomiser (M0125-0047)](0125-0047-joinorder-tiebreak-determinism.md) | **FIXED and landed 2026-08-03** | `pickNextByEdge` — the greedy comma-FROM reorder's "take the smallest edge-connected relation" step — ranked candidates while ranging over `edges[j]`, a `map[int]struct{}`, with a **strict** `rowCounts[k] < rowCounts[best]`. A strict comparison keeps the incumbent on a tie, so on a tie the winner was whichever candidate Go's per-`range` map randomiser yielded first: the tie-break had no total order over relation indices. A query that scans one table twice makes the tie **unavoidable** — the two aliases are the same relation, so their statistics are identical by construction and no `ANALYZE` can separate them. TPC-DS Q85 (`customer_demographics cd1, cd2`, both edged to `web_returns`, and at SF=1 the two largest relations, so the walk ends on a pure two-way tie) swapped the aliases between server starts of one binary: 3 restarts gave cd2-first twice, cd1-first once. Two costs: a **PG divergence** (upstream is a deterministic function of its inputs — `add_path` tie-breaks are stable and `RelOptInfo` sets are `Relids` bitmapsets walked in index order, not hash tables), and an **instrument hazard** that is the more expensive one — every EXPLAIN-based A/B in this repo (`plan_snapshots/`, `make plan-diff`, the SF0.5 EXPLAIN capture) can report a phantom hunk on a Q85-shaped query, so `M0125-0002`'s one-sweep-per-arm acceptances had an unquantified nondeterminism floor. Fix = compare relation indices last, giving the tie-break a total order; ties resolve to source order, matching the rule `smallestUnused` and `orderByConnectivity` already used, so all three pickers in the file now share one tie-break. Audited and found already deterministic: `smallestUnused` (slice walk), `orderByConnectivity` (`k < next` is total — its "cross-free source order is a fixed point" property holds *because* of that), and the bushy DP (`g.edges` is a slice, subsets/splits come from ordered generators, `dp` is lookup-only). Guards in `joinorder_determinism_test.go`, all four proven to fail against the pre-fix body: the defect at its own level (200 direct calls), 200 re-planned Q85 FROM lists, the source-order tie-break pinned, and 100 whole-`Plan()` runs compared by an **alias-bearing reflective fingerprint** — the existing `planShapeString` renders scans as `x.Table.Name` and `cd1`/`cd2` share one `*catalog.Table`, so it prints the two permutations identically and cannot see this defect at all. Go randomises map order per `range`, not per process, so it reproduces in-process and needs no restart probe. **Not closed:** this is not a proof that the planner is deterministic overall — the audit covers the join-order passes, not every map; `TestPlanQ85IsDeterministic` is the harness shape a wider sweep should generalise. M0127 prerequisite (P5.4's tie-break and the 09 §4 plan-shape ratchet build on it). |
| 0125-0034a | [A comma-FROM list with a WITH reference gets ordered for connectivity, not cardinality (M0125-0034 arm (b))](0125-0034a-comma-from-connectivity-order.md) | **implemented 2026-07-31; Q65 arm (§7) landed the same day, loop #17 — the parent item is CLOSED** | C1's remaining arm. goopg has two join-order passes and **both declined on these lists for unrelated reasons, neither of them a policy decision** — `tryBushyDP` whitelists its leaves to `*SeqScan`/`*IndexScan`/`*MultiHashJoin` (because `buildBindingsPosMap` keys on scan identity) and caps the FROM list at 12 relations, while `reorderCommaFromByCardinality` bailed the moment a FROM item was not a base table with `Stats.RowCount` — and a `WITH` reference is not in the catalog. So nothing reordered Q30/Q64/Q81 and the source-order CROSS chain survived, the same "capability gap wearing the costume of a cost decision" as M0125-0041's missing `*CTEScan` clone arm. The fix separates two objectives that a single precondition had fused: a missing row count blocks *ranking* connected orders, but not *telling a connected order from a disconnected one*, and a Cartesian product is only ever the second question. New `orderByConnectivity` runs when the list holds a WITH reference, seeds with the first FROM item and takes the lowest-numbered edge-connected item at each step — making **no** cost claim, because ranking would mean inventing a number rather than reading one (that is `M0125-0038`). Breaking ties on source order buys the property that bounds the blast radius: a cross-free source order is a **fixed point** of the walk, so the pass rewrites a FROM list **if and only if** the source order contains a cross the join graph could have avoided. The parser-level seam is what makes this safe at all — it permutes before column resolution, so no resolved `ColumnRef.Index` needs remapping, which is precisely the machinery whose absence forced `tryBushyDP`'s whitelist. Measured: full 99-query SF0.5 gate **PASS=92 MISMATCH=1 CKMISMATCH=0 ERROR=0 TIMEOUT=2 SKIP=4**, timeout class **6 → 2**, and diffed cell by cell against the loop #14 baseline **exactly 4 of 99 cells moved** — the other 95 identical in status, rows AND checksum. **Q30 TIMEOUT (at 300 s and at 1200 s) → PASS 1 s, 31 rows, ck = oracle**; Q81 TIMEOUT → PASS 1 s; Q72's TIMEOUT → PASS is explicitly NOT claimed (it has no `WITH`, so the mode cannot fire on it — it is the documented cap-straddler). **Q64 went TIMEOUT (measured at 1848 s, not merely >300 s) → MISMATCH**, and that wrong answer is proven pre-existing rather than assumed to be: an A/B differing only in where `customer` sits in the FROM list — one arm firing the pass, one arm a fixed point — returns **byte-identical** wrong output, `y1 = y2 = y3` where PG gives `1998 | 1993 | 1993`, so **multiple aliases of one table collapse to a single alias in projection resolution**, independent of FROM order and reproducible in six relations with no cross at all. Filed separately as a silent wrong answer. TPC-H is inert **by construction**: the mode needs a name the catalog does not know and the TPC-H query set contains no `WITH … AS (` at all. Q65 is NOT closed — its inputs are derived aggregates, and since the parser accepts `LATERAL` and discards it, nothing in the AST can prove a derived table uncorrelated, so the pass declines the whole list (ledger row). **§7 (loop #17) closed it**: the parser now records `LATERAL` on `parser.RangeVar` (both accept sites, including `JOIN LATERAL`, which consumes the keyword before `parseRangeVar` sees it), and the blanket decline splits three ways — table functions still decline (in PG the keyword is *noise* before a function item, so its absence proves nothing), `Lateral` derived tables decline, and a non-lateral derived table is admitted as an opaque relation forcing connectivity mode, the same standing as a WITH reference (PG rejects unmarked sibling references with "invalid reference to FROM-clause entry", so the unmarked form is provably independent). Q65 `TIMEOUT → PASS 17 s, 100 rows = oracle`; full gate **PASS=93 MISMATCH=0 TIMEOUT=2**, exactly 2/99 cells moved (the other is Q72's 309→314 s cap-straddle, unreachable by this pass — all-`JOIN…ON`); plan-diff 22/22 MATCH. True LATERAL *evaluation* remains unimplemented (ledger). |

DS05: all 94 passing queries byte-identical to the P4.3 sweep in row count AND checksum, no query slower by >20%, total +1%. This is the last of S4's four tasks, though not the stage's exit — that additionally wants the regress-port outer-join files green, which stays gated on P4.2's `GOOPG_HASH_OUTER_JOIN` default flip in P5; **P4.3** gave the executor a *rescannable* subtree and, with it, PG's nested loop. The NL join is the universal fallback — every join that is neither hash nor merge lands on it — and it ran entirely inside `Open`: both children drained to `[]Row`, all N×M candidate pairs built with `concatRows`, every survivor pushed into `o.rows` before `Next` returned its first tuple, i.e. three copies of the join's data for an operator `nodeNestloop.c` runs with one tuple per side. The missing piece was never the loop: an `Operator` can be walked once and the inner side must be walked once per outer tuple. `operators_material.go` supplies it — `Materialize`, PG's `nodeMaterial.c` analogue, a `work_mem`-resident prefix plus one sequentially-replayed overflow file, whose `Rescan` replays the cache without touching the child — and `join_nl_stream.go` is then PG's shape directly. Two properties are load-bearing rather than incidental: the cache fills LAZILY and keeps PG's `eof_underlying` resume, because a keyless Semi/Anti breaks out of its inner scan on the first qualifying tuple and an eagerly-draining Materialize would have silently truncated the inner side for every later outer tuple; and the unmatched-inner bitmap is indexed by ORDINAL rather than by key, since replay order is insertion order — the RIGHT/FULL sweep therefore needs no map, and it drains the cache itself, which is the path a RIGHT join over an EMPTY outer side takes. `concatRows`-per-pair dies with the same change: the predicate is evaluated against one reusable merged buffer, so allocation tracks OUTPUT rather than N×M. The spill reader is opened when the writer is created, on an empty file, because P3.3's ledger row named the hazard — the temp-file registry releases at the STATEMENT while PG releases at the resource owner — and an fd survives an unlink where a path resolved later does not. What did NOT land is the `planner.Materialize` plan node, its path and the EXPLAIN line: PG places `Material` by `cost_rescan`, which needs doc 04's cost currency, so emitting it now would move EXPLAIN away from PG on every plan where PG declines it — the same trade P4.2's gate records, and the node is P5.4's. One more thing ships OFF, and this one is a measurement rather than a judgement: the inner cache's `work_mem` bound is implemented and unit-tested but gated behind `GOOPG_NL_MATERIALIZE_WORK_MEM=1`, because the first full DS05 sweep found exactly one regression across 99 queries and it was that bound — Q54, whose plan is a nested loop over a 1.44M-row `store_sales` seq scan (~1.6 GB as `[]Datum`): the bounded cache spills and every outer tuple replays the whole file with full datum decoding, 144 s → TIMEOUT. Unbounded it runs in 95 s with a matching checksum, i.e. FASTER than the drain-both implementation it replaces, which is the cleanest evidence available that the streaming outer and the reused slot/pair buffers are a net win once the spill is out of the way. PG never meets that wall because `cost_rescan` prices a materialized inner at `cpu_operator_cost` per tuple plus `seq_page_cost` over the spilled pages, which is what makes `final_cost_nestloop` lose to hash or merge there; `costInnerNestLoop` has no rescan term at all, so bounding the cache now would trade unbounded memory for an unbounded plan-quality cliff; 3 ledger rows; **P4.2** gave the hash join the outer fill it had never had: PG's `HJ_FILL_INNER` — a matched bitmap per bucket written AFTER the residual predicate, plus a per-batch sweep of unmatched build rows — next to the `HJ_FILL_OUTER` goopg already had. Both halves are named for their ROLE (`fillProbeSide` / `fillBuildSide`) and derived from `Type` plus the EFFECTIVE build side, because `buildLazyHashTable` forces Semi/Anti build-right and the raw `BuildLeft` therefore lies; that is what lets RIGHT reuse the LEFT fill path unchanged (build the non-preserved left, probe the preserved right) while FULL is both halves at once and pays for the sweep. The sweep running per BATCH is why every outer orientation now batches and why `batchSkippable` grew rule 1's INNER arm — a build-only batch is all-unmatched under a filling join. NULL-keyed build rows, which no bucket can hold, are retained and swept last, where PG gets there with `hashtable->keepNulls`. The planner's merge PIN became a merge DEFAULT gated behind `GOOPG_HASH_OUTER_JOIN=1`, and the gate is a measurement rather than caution: an unconditional flip keeps every row but reorders unordered ones, moving regress `join` 210 diff lines further from upstream, because `costInnerMerge` prices an 11-row sort like a real one while PG 18.3 asked directly picks Merge Right/Full Join on the same fixtures — closing that is doc 04's cost currency, i.e. P5; **P4.1** opened S4 on the operator that had never streamed anything — the merge join held THREE full copies of its working set (both children drained to `[]Row`, both keyed sides sorted into a second pair of arrays, the entire output appended to `o.rows` before `Next` returned its first tuple) where `nodeMergejoin.c` holds one tuple per side plus the current inner group; `join_merge_stream.go` replaces all three with `work_mem`-bounded external key-sorted sources and PG's `EXEC_MJ_SKIP` advance, emission order byte-identical by construction because a NULL key is carried as a per-row FLAG that sorts after every real key; **P3.5** made the spill visible and closed S3 on it: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` emits PG's hash-table line — `show_hash_info` verbatim, both forms, attached to the Hash Join because goopg has no `Hash` node — fed by a `HashJoinStats` map on `Context` that `hashBatchState` max-merges into when the geometry is chosen, when nbatch doubles and at close. The measurement and the feature are the same thing: before this slice the S3 gate could not be evaluated without a debugger. Both clauses MET — Q21 completes at SF1 in 132 s under the 20G/24G cap (405 rows, peak 16.7 GB), and Q3 at `work_mem=512kB` with nbatch 512 is byte-identical to Q3 at 6 GB with nbatch 1. The finding to carry: goopg's 512 MB default is NOT a no-spill setting — Q3's build still reports `Batches: 8 (originally 4)  Memory Usage: 475137kB` there and needs 6 GB to reach one batch, because a build row is `[]Datum` where PG's is a packed MinimalTuple, which is the number P5.7's nbatch-aware `hashJoinCost` has to price; **P3.4** took the batching past INNER: SEMI, ANTI and the probe-filling LEFT now spill, on one sentence of argument — a probe row belongs to exactly one batch, and so does every build row that could match it, because equal keys hash equal — which makes every per-probe-row verdict (emit-at-most-once, emit-iff-no-match, null-pad-on-miss) decidable inside the row's own batch, so not one line of the emit logic changed. The admitted set turns out to be character-for-character the planner's `hashJoinIsPartialCapable`: the property that decides which joins may take a PARTIAL PROBE SIDE is the same one that decides which may be partitioned BY BATCH. What did have to change is the skip rule — P3.2 dropped any batch empty on one side, which under LEFT/ANTI silently discards every probe row in an outer-only batch, so `batchSkippable` now states PG's three rules as a table with rule 1's fill arm; rule 1's inner-only arm is deliberately absent because it guards the RIGHT/FULL unmatched sweep goopg does not have yet (P4.2), which is also why a LEFT join built on the LEFT side stays declined. `antiBuildHasNull` needed no work: the build loop maintains it before any row is routed, so it is batch-global by construction. The shared (parallel) build stopped declining the SPILL and started declining the SHARE — P3.2's `noBatch` had made it the one hash build in the executor with no work_mem bound at all, since a frozen in-memory table published from a spilled build hands each worker one partition — and the decline is taken twice, from the estimate before the build and the measurement after it, with `buildGeometry` factored out so the presize, the batch state and the decline cannot disagree about whether a build fits. The cost is real and was isolated rather than averaged away: SPOT rows PASS but its query phase went 15.7 s → 28.3 s, and a three-arm A/B splits it exactly — Q12's +4.3 s is N private builds replacing one shared one, Q13's +7.8 s is its LEFT join honouring `work_mem` on a 1.5M-row build at a 512 MB default (128× PG's, so PG spills it harder). Both are the design's mandate against unbounded builds and are ledgered for the S1/S5 measurement rather than tuned away; **P3.3** made spill files the STATEMENT's property rather than each operator's good intentions: a `tempFileRegistry` on `Context` (new `internal/executor/tempfiles.go`, allocated by `NewContext`, shared BY POINTER with every parallel worker and with the `synthCtx := *ctx` copies, so the files a worker spills die with the leader's query) owns every temp file, and the statement's end unlinks whatever is left — operators still unlink eagerly where they can, but ownership no longer depends on their Close being reached, which is what an Open that errors after the build spilled, or a cancelled query, never does. The files also moved INTO the cluster: new leaf package `internal/pgtemp` puts them at `<datadir>/base/pgsql_tmp/pgsql_tmp<pid>.*` instead of `os.TempDir()`'s `goopg-spill-*.tmp`, and the prefix is the load-bearing part rather than decoration — PG's `RemovePgTempFilesInDir` filters on it so a sweep can never mistake a neighbouring file for a stray, and `Server.Run` now runs that sweep before `close(s.ready)` on the reasoning that a live backend unlinks at statement end, so anything present at startup is by definition a crash leftover. `spillOp.Close` unlinks its file, closing the leak 06 §3 named by line number. Two findings worth carrying: the extended protocol never set `ectx.DataDir`, so its spills would have resolved outside the cluster even after the relocation (the sibling-path class again), and the registry's release point is the STATEMENT while PG's is the resource owner — goopg is safe only because cursors materialise their rows, so P4.3's `Materialize` must revisit it, which is one of four ledger rows alongside `temp_tablespaces`, `temp_file_limit`/`log_temp_files` accounting, and PG's un-ported `RemovePgTempRelationFiles`. Six new tests including the crash-injection gate — four files survive a context that never releases, the startup sweep reclaims all four; **P3.2** made `ctx.WorkMem` a real bound on a hash join instead of a description of one: batch 0 stays in the map, later batches become inner/outer spill-file pairs whose frames carry the 32-bit hash value ahead of the row, so a reloaded tuple learns its batch without evaluating one key expression — PG's `ExecHashJoinSaveTuple` rationale. `batchno = (hash >> log2(nbuckets)) & (nbatch-1)` is carried for its load-bearing property, that doubling can only move a row FORWARD, which is what makes it legal to grow nbatch in the middle of a build whose earlier rows are already on disk; `nextLazy` grows exactly one state, so probe EOF now means "this batch is done" rather than "the join is done". PG's easily-missed skip rules 2 and 3 come with their counters (`origNBatch`, `nbatchOutstart`): a batch empty on one side is normally skippable, but NOT once nbatch has grown, because its file may hold rows that now belong later and dropping it unread loses them in silence. Growth is `ExecHashIncreaseNumBatches` including PG's freeze (`nfreed == 0 || nfreed == ninmemory` ⇒ stop doubling and let the current batch overrun), with eviction per KEY rather than per tuple because every row under one map key shares that key's hash. Two decisions carry the risk and are worth stating: the batch state is installed even when the geometry says one batch, because goopg's row estimates are absent far more often than PG's — per-connection stats mean an unANALYZEd relation estimates at the floor — and an under-estimate is exactly the case that overruns memory, so the bound has to come from growth rather than from the estimate; and routing hashes the key's CANONICAL bytes, never "the int64 if it is one", because the executor can fall from the int lane to the string lane mid-build (`demoteIntHash`) and routing by one canonical form while filing under another sends equal keys to different batches — a lost match, not an error. Scope is INNER + single-key + private build; LEFT/Semi/Anti (fill-aware skipping, batch-global `antiBuildHasNull`) and the composite lane decline to P3.4, and `prebuildSharedHashJoins` sets `noBatch` so a shared build never spills. `spillWriter` also gained the write buffer P3.1's walk-back had already priced. `maxPresizeBuckets` did NOT retire as planned — nbatch bounds the resident rows, not the bucket array, which the sizing re-derives from the full budget once multi-batch — and that plus five other gaps are ledgered. Every test is an IDENTITY against the same join run unbounded, the only assertion strong enough when each failure mode is a wrong answer rather than an error; UNITS + RACE + SPOT green (Q12=2 / Q13=35 at 15.8 s / 10,224 MB) and DS05 MISMATCH=0 across all three slices; **P3.1** added `internal/hashsize`, the sizing rule the planner and the executor must share — a leaf package rather than a function because the dependency runs executor → planner and never back, so the one thing both must agree on has to sit below both; PG gets this free by having `final_cost_hashjoin` and `ExecHashTableCreate` call the same `ExecChooseHashTableSize`. The port keeps PG's algorithm and replaces PG's widths: a hash entry is `48·c + 24` bytes of `[]Datum` rather than a packed MinimalTuple, and a bucket slot is 48 bytes rather than an 8-byte pointer, so sizing goopg's table with PG's constants would under-predict `nbatch` by roughly the width ratio — the trap 04 §4 names, pinned by a test where 300k×10 columns is ~2.9 MB of MinimalTuple and ~150 MB of Datum. PG's `Assert(bucket_bytes <= hash_table_bytes/2)` became a clamp, since 48-byte slots make "buckets alone exhaust work_mem" reachable at small `work_mem`. First consumer is `joinOp.presizeLazyHash`, which allocates the build table with its bucket count already chosen instead of rehashing a nil map up a multi-million-row build; it reads `planner.EstimateRows` (the executor cannot count a side it has not drained), caps the presize at 1<<20 buckets because an estimate is not a measurement, and treats the 1024-bucket floor as "no information" so unestimated relations presize nothing. `NBatch` is computed and ignored until P3.2 partitions rows at insert time, and `hashJoinCost` does not call it yet — the nbatch I/O term moves plans and belongs to 06 §5 / P5.7; both halves plus the missing per-column width statistic are ledgered. UNITS + SPOT green, Q12=2 / Q13=35 at 17.0 s / 11,461 MB, no plan surface touched so `m0127-p21-hashkeys` stays the S3 baseline; **P2.3** finished the family by making merge join sort, advance and group on the full accepted pair list — the planner half was already P2.1's, so what P2.3 removed was the executor still reading `plan.LeftKey`/`RightKey`: grouping on the lead column alone turns a low-cardinality lead into ONE equal-key group whose cartesian product is walked pair by pair, which is the O(n·m) cost M0125-0011's residual re-check was paying to keep TPC-DS Q97's FULL OUTER JOIN correct. The group is now the match set and the residual is nil on an all-equijoin merge join, PG's empty `joinqual`; `pairIsHashSafe` governs the fold-in for merge too, because `compareDatum` is the same one-canonicalisation-where-PG-has-an-opfamily situation, and ledger row `M0127-P2.3` records that its `KindString` arm content-sniffs pg_lsn/UUID/composite/array forms — a divergence that previously touched only the lead key and now reaches every folded text pair. DS05 clean across all 99 with Q97's checksum unchanged and timings flat against P2.2, i.e. the win is a removed class rather than a measured speedup, latent until P5's re-planning puts a pinned lead on a merge join; PLAN MATCH 22/22 with no re-baseline, since the list was already published and rendered; **P2.2** made the full key list the thing the hash table is actually keyed on and DELETED `reselectDegenerateHashKeys` with its three helpers and its `Plan()` call site — the degeneracy trap is gone by construction, since a constant-pinned column now merely contributes nothing to bucket spread, which is PG's situation exactly; **DS05 Q78, the query that workaround pass existed for, PASSes in 19 s / 45 rows / matching checksum**, so the workaround was removable rather than merely replaceable, and `make plan-diff` reports MATCH on all 22 TPC-H queries. The executor's key list is deliberately NARROWER than the published `HashKeys`: goopg has one `datumKey` canonicalisation where PG resolves a hash function per type from the equality operator's opfamily, so a pair may be folded in only where `datumKey` equality provably agrees with `=` — float4/float8 are stored as TEXT datums and would drop `0.0 = -0.0`, enum/toast datums have no `datumKey` arm and would collide into ONE key and over-emit. Encoding is a fixed-width big-endian int64 pack (probe lookups allocation-free) or length-prefixed `datumKey` parts, the prefix rather than a NUL separator being what makes it injective; `joinPredicateMatchSlot` now evaluates the residual, discharging half of ledger row `M0127-P2.1`, with the physical `Predicate` trim and the type whitelist filed as `M0127-P2.2`; **P2.1** gave `planner.Join` a `HashKeys []JoinKeyPair` list — every usable equi-pair, PG's `hashclauses`, where goopg carried exactly one pair since M0003 — derived by ONE late pass at the tail of `Plan()` so the six passes that rewrite key/predicate expressions in place cannot stale it, with `HashKeys[0]` pinned to `(LeftKey, RightKey)` by pointer and `splitEqualityForHash` delegating to the same core so the single-pair and full-list views cannot drift; EXPLAIN grew upstream's `Hash Cond:`/`Merge Cond:` lines, which goopg had never emitted — the re-baselined `plan_snapshots/m0127-p21-hashkeys.txt` is identical to the previous baseline once those lines are filtered out, i.e. zero plan-shape change over all 22 TPC-H queries, and 2 of the 61 conditions are genuine multi-column lists (Q9/Q20's partsupp⋈lineitem); `Predicate` is deliberately not trimmed until the executor consumes the list at P2.2, ledger row `M0127-P2.1`; §6 progress log; **P1.3** is the S1 exit measurement, `analysis/leftdeep-joins/2026-08-03-s1-ab.txt` — clause (2) of the 09 §2 bar met outright, **no query in the suite slower under S1 than under pre-S1 HEAD** (max 1.00), total 619.26 s → 360.82 s = 0.58×, and 0.73× of R0's pinned 493.31 s; clause (1) met for Q7 (0.74× R0) and missed for Q3/Q10/Q18, **attributed class (b) plan shape and inherited** — the two arms' EXPLAIN is byte-identical so every S1 delta is class (d) at constant plan, while pre-S1 HEAD alone is already 4.08×/3.89×/2.92× R0 because MHJ de-selection between R0's HEAD and pre-S1 HEAD replaced R0's 9 `Multi-Way Hash Join` nodes with binary cascades; since 09 §3 item 5 *requires* zero MHJ at S5, the residual is the bundle's own thesis and Q3/Q10/Q18 become P5's named regression witnesses; P0.1 seam microbench 5 allocs/row → 0, 185.8 → 4.10 ns/op; P0.2 made the build single-pass — no drain-and-re-iterate, no `MaterializedSlot` per build row, and `ctx.WorkMem` retired from a path where it bounded nothing, ledger row `M0127-P0.2`; P0.3 made it single-map — the key representation is now typed by the plan (`Join.HashKeysAreInt64`) before the build instead of discovered by filling both maps and freeing the loser after peak, Semi/Anti joined the int64 lane, ledger row `M0127-P0.3` for the numeric keys the static decision gives up; **P1.1** de-materialised the probe seam — the probe child's slot is bound straight into the join's output composition instead of being flattened by `slotRow`, taking the seam from 2,048 allocs / 172 KB per 1,024 probe rows to **0 B / 0 allocs**, with the F7 "children return no stable slot" hazard handled by rebinding unconditionally rather than by detecting a type change, ledger row `M0127-P1.1` for the over-wide Semi/Anti tuple PG would have projected away; **P1.2** exercised that seam under `BuildWorker` and found the divergence in the BUILD path instead of the seam — `buildEnvInFlight`, a package global written by every Gather worker's own goroutine, which had kept `make race-gate` red since M0126-0006 and is now a local, the gate green end-to-end, ledger row `M0127-P1.2` for the executor globals left un-audited as a class) | The Ralph-loop task decomposition of the `leftdeep-joins/` bundle (which remains the design of record; this doc references, never restates, its chapters): 34 one-loop tasks across P0–P6 — executor pure wins (mergedKeySlot hoist, single-pass/single-map build), the probe-seam de-materialisation (un-deferring M0126-0004), multi-column keys (deleting `reselectDegenerateHashKeys`), hybrid-hash spill, streaming merge/outer-fill/Materialize, the PG-shaped three-phase DP behind `GOOPG_PGSHAPED_DP` (9 tasks + the P5.3a bushy phase), compiled key/residual eval, and the S7 deletion of fusion + MultiHashJoin + the old subset-bitmask DP. Each task carries its gate (UNITS/SMOKE/SPOT/DS05/PLAN/REGRESS/RACE/BENCH vocabulary per 09 §1) and its stage (S0–S7 per 08 §2). |
